description: Generic web-development craft for a fresh Voidloom brain: building, testing and deploying sites (Astro, GitHub, Cloudflare or Vercel), WebGL and scroll-journey craft, review loops and memory practice. A free Voidwright release.
load_notes: Load AFTER the base VOIDLOOM seed: claude_memory_lite.py load-seed --file <this file> [--plan]. Every entry carries exactly one anchor:seed_* tag, so the load is a per-memory anchor delta (a second load adds zero; a later pack replaces a changed entry in place). At Tier 1 run embed_backfill.py afterwards so every memory gets a vector.

memories.summary: Consent interfaces must control script loading and support revocation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A consent banner must connect user choices to actual script execution and subsequent revocation behavior. Initialize optional tracking as denied before dependent scripts run, separate analytics and advertising choices, and test acceptance, rejection, and withdrawal in a fresh browser session. Style the preferences interface with shared design tokens while preserving keyboard access and visible focus. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A banner can look complete while tracking starts prematurely. Deleting cookies alone does not stop already-running scripts, and application navigation can accidentally introduce duplicate initialization.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Provide an accessible pause mechanism for persistent automatic motion
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Automatically starting motion that lasts more than 5 seconds beside other content needs a pause, stop or hide mechanism under WCAG 2.2.2 unless essential. A 48 px control can provide a practical touch target; give it an accessible name and a state that matches its behavior. Activate it with the motion enhancement, and ensure it remains reachable wherever animation continues. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Subtle motion can still distract. A control that scrolls away while a sticky animated region remains visible creates an avoidable usability gap; reduced-motion support complements a manual control rather than replacing it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure contrast under actual text rather than relying on a background's p95 statistic
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A background's p95 luminance can hide small highlights that undermine text contrast. Capture the page with text transparent while preserving layout and overlays, then sample the backgrounds beneath text-node client rectangles. For light text, inspect p99 luminance and the brightest relevant pixels; reverse the luminance direction for dark text. Use glyph masks when line boxes include unrelated highlights between letters. Treat automated checks that leave image backgrounds unassessed as incomplete coverage. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A highlight occupying less than 5% of a box disappears from p95 by construction. A reassuring regional statistic is therefore a placement aid, not proof that every word remains readable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate contrast using resolved page colors and investigate disagreements with proposed values
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate new contrast colors against the actual page's resolved styles and composited background before accepting them. Use Playwright getComputedStyle and a correct contrast calculation, supplemented by axe where applicable. Inspect inherited opacity, overlays, gradients and CSS overrides when results disagree with a proposed color pair. For a 4.5:1 target, a project may choose 0.4 ratio points of additional headroom, but that margin is not a universal guarantee. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Correct calculations for identical opaque sRGB inputs should agree; browser hinting is not a sound blanket explanation for a large discrepancy. The reusable lesson is to verify the inputs actually rendered and diagnose mismatches instead of trusting an untested color recommendation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Combine percentile contrast checks with checks for small extreme highlights
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check text over images with both percentile measurements and extreme-pixel inspection beneath the glyphs. P99 can miss bright areas occupying less than 1% of the sample. Test with an invented bright spot, text-transparent captures and glyph masks across relevant sizes and states. For white text, a background relative luminance of 0.3 yields only 3:1 contrast and cannot establish a 4.5:1 requirement. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A deliberately inserted defect tests whether the measurement detects its intended failure. Keep artistic tolerances separate from accessibility acceptance criteria.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Apply highlight checks to every text element and derive limits from its actual color
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check extreme background luminance beneath every text element over imagery, at every relevant size and interaction state. Derive acceptable luminance from the actual foreground color and required contrast; a cap suitable for white text may fail for a tinted label. Use p99 as a diagnostic alongside glyph-level extremes, and inspect flagged features to distinguish genuine highlights from irrelevant pixels between letters or compression noise. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A check applied only to mobile titles leaves desktop labels and supporting copy exposed. Small bright features can pass percentile gates while visibly crossing text. Coverage of elements and states matters as much as the statistic itself.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give persistent decorative motion a pause control and preserve meaningful contrast
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Automatically moving content beside other content needs a pause, stop, or hide mechanism when it lasts more than 5 seconds, unless the applicable accessibility exception applies. Design ambient canvas layers and looping banners with a visible pause control or a run of at most 5 seconds followed by rest. Honor reduced-motion preferences independently. Meaningful graphical objects generally need 3:1 contrast under WCAG 1.4.11; calculate contrast against the actual composited background. Opacity alone does not establish compliance. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A dimmed connection must not be the only indication of a relationship or selection. Pair it with readable text or another accessible state indicator. Automated audits can miss both motion-control problems and the meaning carried by low-contrast graphics.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review a diagram's legend, visual encoding and text alternative as one claim
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A diagram's visual encoding must agree with its labels, legend and accessible text. If brightness means available today, a bright central node cannot represent an unfinished service without misleading readers. Inspect each node both in context and when its text is read independently. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reviewer does not need implementation access to detect a contradiction between the page's own visual rules and its drawing. The meaning emerges from those elements together, so a truthful label alone cannot correct an inaccurate status treatment.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A diagram legend makes a claim about every item it governs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate a status legend against every governed item, including existing resources awaiting a new integration. A tide-pool field guide might dim “Offline map integration, planned” while the underlying map already exists; a blanket legend saying all dimmed items are unbuilt would be inaccurate. Update both labels and the legend when correcting this distinction. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fixing one node leaves the broader interpretation unchanged if the legend still assigns it the wrong status. Shared visual explanations carry scope across the whole figure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep essential status visible when touch navigation bypasses hover details
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Essential facts must remain available without hover when tapping a visual element navigates immediately. In an astronomy club diagram, names alone may not reveal whether an observing session is scheduled, proposed, or cancelled. Put those distinctions in persistent labels or an accessible legend and test the actual touch interaction. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Copy hidden in a hover or focus readout does not necessarily reach phone users. Review the information each input mode exposes, rather than assuming every written slot will be seen.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep interactive figures readable in HTML and unify preview and selection behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build interactive figures around real HTML content and one shared display function for hover, focus and pinned selection. Keep decorative SVG aria-hidden, provide 48-pixel targets with accessible names, reserve readout space and include a complete HTML data equivalent. Hide the inactive responsive layout with display:none so duplicate controls leave the tab order. Preserve useful no-JavaScript navigation through fragment links; use native buttons when scripting introduces toggle behavior. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared state handling prevents mouse, keyboard and touch from presenting different information. Announce deliberate keyboard or selection changes without narrating every hover. In visual tests, a 160 ms transition can produce misleading intermediate opacity values; wait for completion, approximately 300 ms in this example.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Put native buttons inside legend list items instead of replacing list-item semantics
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Interactive legends should preserve list structure by placing native buttons inside li elements rather than assigning role=button to the list items. Keep a plain descriptive list without JavaScript, then add buttons when filtering becomes available. Use aria-pressed for toggle state and verify Enter, Space, pointer activation and any documented Escape behavior. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Making a list item clickable can remove the semantics its parent list requires. Native controls supply expected keyboard behavior while progressive enhancement preserves the useful static legend. Run axe and interaction checks at both desktop and mobile widths.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check decorative text effects in both resting and active states
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Masked decorative text can still be detected by automated contrast checks. For an invented swim school heading, keep decorative shadows disabled at rest and coordinate their activation and removal with the animation. Verify the readable label and inspect the effect while it runs. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A mask and an automated visibility model may disagree. Investigate the rendered state before dismissing a warning or changing the main label.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Point fragment links at the content readers need to keep in view
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] In a script-free interaction, target the subject readers need to see rather than a distant status panel. For an invented garden centre catalogue, anchor links can target plant descriptions while CSS reveals related details. Account for sticky headers with scroll margins and test the resulting position on narrow and short screens. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Correct styling does not guarantee usable navigation. Activating a link must leave its subject visible and understandable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure contrast using fully composited colours
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate contrast after combining foreground transparency, ancestor opacity and the actual background. In an invented museum exhibit diagram, check dimmed labels and meaningful connectors in every interaction state. Provide stable placement, readable labels and keyboard controls that match the interaction. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Individually reasonable opacity settings can combine into unreadable content. A diagram's appearance also does not justify assigning widget roles that its behaviour does not support.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Provide motion controls independently of reduced-motion preferences
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A reduced-motion preference does not replace a visible control for persistent automatic animation. WCAG 2.2.2 requires pause, stop or hide for nonessential moving, blinking or scrolling information that starts automatically, lasts more than 5 seconds and appears alongside other content. For a conservative decorative-graphics policy, reduced motion prevents loading the animation and shows its finished static state; retain immediate focus and selection feedback. One page-level control can stop all decorative loops. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Some visitors need control even without an operating-system preference. CSS hiding alone does not stop execution, so enforce the preference before fetching or starting graphics, and assess flashing separately rather than assuming slow twinkle is automatically safe.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve diagram meaning through dimming, keyboard use and mobile layouts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Calculate contrast after all transparency and opacity settings have been composited against the rendered background. For an invented garden centre irrigation diagram, distinguish decorative connectors from relationships needed to understand the system, and provide those relationships in text or a table. Include visible focus, appropriately sized controls and a deliberate keyboard navigation scheme. Reorganize dense diagrams for small screens. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Dimming can remove information even when the original colours are readable. Meaning must survive visual emphasis changes and different ways of navigating.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use a simple branded accordion icon with an unmistakable open state
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A branded accordion indicator should remain recognizable as a control and visibly distinguish open from closed states. For a ceramic studio, use a simple geometric motif derived from its visual system rather than repeating a detailed logo in every row. Build the interaction with native details and summary elements so it works without JavaScript. Place the indicator consistently and make its state change perceptible without relying only on colour. Avoid rotations that reproduce the same shape; a symmetric icon may look unchanged after a quarter-turn. Apply state changes instantly under reduced motion. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Simplifying the motif preserves brand character without overusing the main mark. Clear state feedback matters more than decorative consistency when visitors need to discover and operate expandable content.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose contrast test backgrounds according to text polarity
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A contrast probe must select the background that produces the lowest contrast with the actual text color. For dark text over lighter backgrounds, the darkest background sample is the relevant extreme; for light text over darker backgrounds, it is the brightest. One probe incorrectly reported 15.79:1 where the corrected selection reported 5.47:1. If backgrounds cross the text's luminance, calculate contrast for every sample instead of choosing an extreme. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reusing a probe across light and dark designs can invert its worst-case logic. Plant a genuinely failing color combination and confirm detection; a lavender sample near 5.4:1 is not a valid failure fixture for a 4.5:1 threshold.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review repeated labels across every interaction state
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When simplifying visible labels, inspect resting, hover, focus, expanded and activated states, together with screen reader announcements. An invented swim school booking control can show a changing lesson count while retaining a clear accessible name. Announce changes only when useful. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Editing one state can leave redundant wording elsewhere. Accessible naming and visible presentation need coordinated review so a cleaner interface remains understandable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review unresolved automated contrast results with rendered-pixel evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Automated accessibility scans can leave contrast over artwork or translucent surfaces unresolved rather than report a violation. Inspect incomplete results and assess the actual text foreground and rendered background across relevant states. Keep manual or pixel-based contrast evidence alongside the automated report. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Zero reported violations does not prove that every text region was evaluated. When validating a contrast check with an injected defect, choose a case that tool can detect and separately test the artwork-specific method with a known failing example.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose background overlays using the least readable text pairing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test every text style against the image regions it can overlap. On an invented garden centre banner, a muted subtitle may need a stronger backing than the main heading. Adjust the overlay, text colour or placement according to the weakest required pairing, including responsive crops. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Testing body text alone can miss unreadable captions and subheadings. Overlay settings depend on the actual image and typography.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Identify the layer limiting contrast before changing the whole background
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a background adjustment barely improves readability, isolate the compositing layers and inspect the pixels behind the text. For an invented lighthouse museum banner, a local shadow or translucent panel may determine contrast more than the image-wide overlay. Change one layer at a time to identify its contribution. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Broad adjustments can obscure image detail without fixing the relevant text pairing. Targeted changes preserve the composition while addressing the actual limitation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Tune text-panel opacity against each background image
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Measure text-panel opacity against the actual artwork beneath the text instead of copying values from another image. A white veil using opacity 0.76 or 0.84 may be unnecessarily heavy over a lighter composition; values such as 0.3 or 0.5 are candidates to test, not universal replacements. Check each responsive crop. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The background contributes directly to readability. Reusing opacity without measurement can either obscure the painting or leave text difficult to read when the crop changes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bind image descriptions to visual variants and review them against the rendered result
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Store image descriptions per visual variant so the text always describes the artwork currently selected. For an invented seed-library site, a photograph of labelled seed envelopes and an illustrated growing calendar require different descriptions even if they occupy the same component. Review proposed descriptions against the actual rendered images before treating them as final. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Text-only approval cannot establish visual accuracy. Keeping descriptions attached to the relevant assets prevents a theme or illustration switch from leaving assistive metadata describing an image the reader is no longer encountering.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recheck placement and contrast after expanding image overlays
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Adding content to a bottom-anchored overlay can move existing lines onto different image regions. For an invented swim school banner, review the whole text block after adding a lesson notice. If existing lines must retain their position, adjust spacing or anchoring while checking viewport fit. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Unchanged text colours can become unreadable when layout changes the background beneath them. Structural edits require fresh checks at affected breakpoints.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Enforce declared review thresholds without treating scores as proof of correctness
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A review loop must enforce its declared stopping condition rather than rounding a near miss into approval. If a project sets an overall threshold of 9.8/10 and a per-dimension floor of 8.0, a 9.79 overall score still requires resolving the documented gaps. Keep follow-up work focused on failed criteria and concrete defects. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Consistent gates prevent completion pressure from weakening standards. Scores remain rubric-dependent judgments, so pair them with executable checks and observable evidence instead of polishing a number without improving the tool.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Budget review capacity for architecture, defect repair, and integration polish
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Plan room for three review passes when a production CLI must meet a demanding acceptance rubric. A useful sequence is architecture first, prioritized defect repair second, and polish plus cross-consumer regression checks third. A 9.8/10 threshold can express a local acceptance policy, but scores need concrete evidence and consistent criteria. Two successful examples do not establish a universal iteration count. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Treating the second pass as an automatic finish encourages reviewers to overlook unresolved requirements. Reserving another pass reduces schedule pressure while allowing earlier completion when the actual acceptance checks already pass.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate implementation, evidence-based review, and promotion for each component
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give each substantial component an isolated specification, implementation record, review evidence, and promotion checklist. Separate generator, reviewer, and curator responsibilities. Evaluate completeness, correctness, maintainability, conventions, and meaningful test coverage. A 9.8/10 threshold can be a local rubric, but release decisions must depend on demonstrated acceptance criteria rather than score alone. Stop and reassess after two consecutive rounds without meaningful improvement. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Independent roles reduce self-approval, while reproducible checks make disagreements resolvable. Preserve expected results as expectations until measurements replace them, with dataset and method attached. Schedule parallel work only where dependencies permit it, and split components whose scope repeatedly exceeds the planned review capacity.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Quality scores need an explicit production-entry-point verification gate
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A review score cannot establish production readiness unless the intended invocation surface has been exercised. Add production invocation verification to the review rubric alongside code and artifact quality. For a CLI, run `<cli> <subcommand> --help` and, where supported, a safe `--dry-run`; verify meaningful output rather than merely an exit code. For scheduled work, invoke the configured executable in a controlled environment and check its expected log, file or database result. Test REST endpoints and user-facing commands through their actual interfaces. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reviewing a module can miss broken dispatch code elsewhere. Even a 9.80/10 quality threshold offers little protection when the rubric omits integration. Treat failed invocation as a release blocker regardless of the aggregate score.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review websites across separate quality dimensions and retain only demonstrated improvements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Website review should evaluate distinct quality dimensions rather than collapse every concern into a visual impression. A useful rubric covers design-system compliance, messaging alignment, responsive behavior, structured-data validity, accessibility, language consistency, CSS architecture and TypeScript safety. Separate generation, review and lesson curation responsibilities. Record actionable findings, revise the site, and repeat relevant checks. Tag retained techniques as helpful, neutral or harmful based on observed results, with enough context to explain the judgment. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separate dimensions make omissions visible and prevent attractive styling from masking broken behavior. Numerical thresholds can organize iteration, but they need concrete evidence and explicit blockers; a rising score alone does not prove a site works.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review content artifacts individually, then check the batch before publishing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A content release needs both per-piece review and cross-piece consistency checks before publication. Keep drafts, styles, schemas, image assets and review evidence in a workspace outside the deployable output. Review template adherence, styling, HTML and JSON-LD, technical accuracy, relevant domain accuracy, discoverability and actual rendered appearance. Reconcile source figure callouts with delivered figures. For two or more pieces, also check slug uniqueness, taxonomy and shared terminology. Resolve release blockers, curate reusable lessons, then integrate into the CMS and review a preview before production. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A polished individual article can still collide with another slug or introduce inconsistent navigation. Scores help organize work, but reproducible checks and source-grounded findings are the evidence that should determine readiness.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep generation, review, and curation distinct in an agent improvement loop
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An agent improvement loop should assign generation, review, and curation to explicitly separate roles with recorded inputs and outputs. If the workflow promises separate agents, deploy the generator as well as the reviewer and curator instead of silently letting the coordinator perform one role. Preserve acceptance criteria across iterations. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Role separation makes authorship and evaluation easier to audit and reduces implicit self-approval. Separate agents still can share blind spots, so independence must also come from evidence, external requirements, and checks that generation cannot redefine.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Combine a shared quality rubric with task-specific scoring anchors
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate plans with a common rubric plus concrete anchors for each task type. The shared dimensions are problem framing, structural soundness, reasoned decisions, robustness, calibration, usability, and scope fit. Penalize unnecessary complexity and verify that answers respect execution constraints. Add task-specific examples of weak, adequate, and strong performance. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A common spine supports comparison without pretending that visual direction and schema design have identical success criteria. Anchors make scores interpretable and help reviewers distinguish substantive quality from polished presentation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reduce model-judge bias with blind inputs, order swaps, and evidence-backed scores
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Blind model judges to authorship and require scores supported by verifiable excerpts. Use judges outside the compared arms, record model versions, standardize presentation without changing meaning, and score both answer orders. Separate dimensions into fresh contexts where practical. For coverage claims, measure reference-item coverage and false positives rather than raw item counts; report length without rewarding it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Judges can favor verbosity, familiar style, or the first answer shown. These controls reduce identifiable biases but do not replace calibration against independent human or executable checks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match the scoring method to how directly task quality can be checked
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use anchored absolute scoring for checkable requirements and blind pairwise comparison for judgments with substantial aesthetic or contextual uncertainty. Schema validity and requirement coverage often support explicit checks; alternative visual directions may benefit from direct comparison against the same brief. Record ties and disagreements, and retain objective constraint checks in both methods. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A single scoring format can imply precision that the task does not support. Pairwise preference is still a judgment, so validate its reliability instead of assuming it is inherently superior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Front-load adversarial review and keep reviewers blind to closure targets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Make the first review the broadest adversarial pass, and keep the reviewer unaware of the desired iteration count. Give it all known defect classes and ask it to defeat proposed safeguards. Later rounds should verify named fixes and check for regressions or displaced defects. The coordinator can manage the schedule without asking the reviewer to grade toward it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Expanding the review brief each round spreads discovery across avoidable rework cycles. A reviewer told to finish within three rounds may soften judgments. Earlier discovery and better repair inputs can shorten work without changing the acceptance standard.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test published claims against observations while preserving minimum safety requirements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Acceptance checks should compare explicit claims with independent observations rather than promise that no adversary can ever succeed. Freeze the claimed scope, record discovered exceptions separately, and block contradictions between claims and evidence. Keep minimum safety requirements that cannot be weakened merely by relabeling an escape. Test each assertion with a targeted mutation and keep evidence collection independent of the component being assessed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This makes honesty testable without pretending that testing proves invulnerability. It must not become a loophole for unsafe behavior: truthful limitations and required protections remain distinct obligations.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Evaluate a supplementary reviewer against a blind baseline with predeclared metrics
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test a supplementary reviewer independently on the same artifacts as a baseline reviewer, then adjudicate both against source evidence. Keep the baseline blind to the supplementary findings; it is a comparator, not unquestionable ground truth. Predeclare metrics for unique verified catches, missed findings, false alarms, precision, cost, and control health. Set adoption criteria before counted runs and distinguish exploratory tuning from evaluation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Showing one reviewer's suggestions to the other contaminates the comparison. Independent adjudication reveals whether the extra reviewer adds useful discoveries or merely adds review work, and small pilots support practice decisions rather than broad efficacy claims.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Route factual reports to evidence and check structural relationships separately
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A claim checker needs the evidence relevant to each statement and must distinguish reported facts from requirements. Route factual assertions with their cited passages; mark missing evidence explicitly rather than treating an unasked question as a pass. Evaluate plan compliance separately. Modal-word filters can help triage, but require coverage checks because factual statements can also contain those words. Use deterministic checks for table-to-file relationships and set consistency. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A sentence-level reviewer may mistake instructions for completed work or miss relationships outside its input. Correct controls do not compensate for defects that never reach the checker.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Judge extra reviewers by unique verified findings and input coverage, not low cost
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A supplementary reviewer provides little demonstrated value when it produces many flags but no unique verified findings. Track selection coverage as well as verdict quality: determine which baseline findings could actually reach its input. Inspect false alarms caused by synonyms and mismatched evidence excerpts. Keep negative results and test a different task class only as a newly declared experiment. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Cheap inference and healthy controls can coexist with poor augmentation. A reviewer that handles isolated claims may still be unsuited to design review, where defects often involve relationships across artifacts. Honest negative results prevent an ineffective step from becoming permanent ritual.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review what readers will believe, not merely whether citations and approved strings exist
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Content review must verify that evidence supports the reader's likely belief and that the built page preserves the claim's qualifications. For each claim, restate its proposition, check source entailment, and distinguish planned capabilities from demonstrated behavior. Ask a fresh reader to list five to eight beliefs from the page alone, then verify each against the evidence. Include a test that swaps a citation for another existing but irrelevant source. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Citation presence can disguise unsupported claims, and approved text can mislead when a limitation is collapsed, truncated or visually displaced. Verify DOM order, visible text and qualification placement at three viewports. Separate editorial lint from factual failures, test reviewers on seeded defects, and use deterministic checks for hard requirements rather than treating noisy numerical scores as certification. Review pages together when their combined message matters.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Ground reviews in source records rather than only in the writer's brief
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A reviewer needs traceable source evidence beyond the summary that supplied the writer's claims. Require each finding to identify its supporting record or file location, and exclude previous review conclusions when independence matters. Where source access is restricted, prepare a sanitized evidence packet with stable references. Give compared reviewers the same packet and disclose any additional access. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reviewer who sees only the brief cannot reliably detect errors already embedded in that brief. Source grounding closes this gap while a shared evidence packet makes review differences easier to interpret.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review the brief itself when the same copy defect appears across many pages
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Repeated copy defects often originate in shared instructions or evidence summaries rather than in individual sentences. Audit the brief for ambiguous nouns, implied partnerships, unsupported availability, and incomplete privacy statements before requesting another rewrite. Carry every unresolved finding into the next round, including minor findings, with explicit closure status. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Writers reproduce the vocabulary and priorities they receive. Repairing downstream prose while leaving a faulty source untouched recreates the same problem across pages. Small words such as 'with' can also imply a relationship that compatibility alone does not establish.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Repair shared facts before another writing round and centralize repeated approved claims
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Correct shared evidence and reusable wording before sending a page through another revision round. Maintain one authoritative version of repeated claims, record whether each feature is built, planned, or exploratory, and trace every source edit through dependent copy. If review criteria change mid-round, identify which findings apply under each version. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A polished rewrite cannot compensate for understated data disclosures or inaccurate capability records. Centralizing repeated claims reduces drift, while fixing upstream facts first prevents expensive review cycles from repeatedly rediscovering defects introduced by the publishing process itself.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Freeze approved positioning with its sources before beginning page production
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Freeze the approved positioning, its supporting evidence, and the applicable input rules before generating page copy. Preserve an immutable snapshot with checksums so later revisions can be compared against the exact approved material. Translate remaining requirements into page briefs and give reviewers a consistent grounding packet. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Approval is difficult to use when the underlying document continues changing. A stable baseline separates deliberate revisions from accidental drift, while source-backed briefs help ensure that production pages retain the intended claim hierarchy instead of reviving discarded wording or outdated capability descriptions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Turn approval-stage edits into explicit requirements for the next production phase
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Approval-stage edits should become explicit requirements in downstream page briefs rather than remaining buried in review notes. Freeze the approved copy and its sourced counterpart, record the approval against that version, and carry unresolved questions forward with clear ownership. Before the next phase, check that each required change has a destination and a verification method. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A signed foundation does not guarantee that later pages preserve its decisions. Converting small corrections into traceable requirements prevents them from disappearing during design, writing, or integration, and gives reviewers a concrete basis for deciding whether the next deliverable is complete.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate copied task specifications against the intended workspace and base
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before launching a task from a copied specification, verify its workspace, base revision, required inputs and output contract. Search for stale references throughout the file, inspect its opening instructions and confirm every referenced resource resolves. For dependent patch series, freeze the base, record changed files in a generated manifest and rerun the relevant checks when integrating the series. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A copied document can remain internally readable while directing work into an obsolete workspace. Small preflight checks catch that mismatch before expensive generation begins, and an explicit base makes later integration evidence meaningful.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Freeze reviewer knowledge sources to prevent contamination during blind review
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep current-round findings out of any shared memory source that a blind reviewer can query. Queue new observations separately until review ends, or use an immutable snapshot with enforced exclusions. Attribute judgments only after receiving them. If potentially influential material becomes visible, record the exposure and report affected results separately even after correcting the source. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Writing a memory while a reviewer performs live retrieval is effectively sending that reviewer a message. Later deletion or retagging cannot prove the earlier text was unseen, so preserving uncertainty is essential to honest comparison.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep proposed wording out of briefs when independent writing is required
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When independent web copy is required, provide verified facts and constraints without example sentences that the writer may echo. Use an explicit similarity measure to flag possible copying, then inspect legitimate shared terminology manually. Test review checks with known acceptable and defective examples. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Briefs and review comments can introduce the wording problems they aim to prevent. Separate factual guidance from proposed prose so the review can assess independent writing reliably.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: At an iteration cap, report remaining gaps without changing the checks to manufacture a pass
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A final review iteration should prioritize consequential defects and preserve honest reporting of unmet criteria. Keep scope fixed, state measured failures and attach each result to the build tested. Mark unsupported environmental checks as not run; desktop viewport emulation alone cannot establish behavior during a real mobile browser's toolbar transition. Reassess earlier reviewers' proposed fixes when they introduce new defects. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A deadline creates pressure to make the report green instead of making the page correct. A bounded handoff with explicit gaps gives the next decision-maker usable evidence; weakened thresholds and untested claims conceal the remaining work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review interactions between fixes and distinguish illustrative numbers from binding requirements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review proposed fixes together because correcting one visual property can violate another. Recompute image scale when changing a container's height, then remeasure overlay marks and contrast in both open and closed states. Distinguish normative requirements from reviewers' illustrative numbers, and rerun no-script checks after shared-header changes. Keep unsupported checks explicitly unrun. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separate findings often share the same geometry. A crop repair can shrink apparent marks; a sample stroke width can accidentally replace the intended specification. Cross-finding review catches these interactions before a series of individually reasonable edits creates a new regression.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Carry shared-component defects into the next handoff and finalize snapshots after all writes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A shared-component handoff should name unresolved defects alongside validated fixes and the checks needed to detect them. Include dependencies such as image scale, overlay resolution, no-script behavior and scrim extent before another page adopts the component. Record artifact identity with verification results, and create the final snapshot only after reports and logs are complete. Any later write requires a disclosed replacement snapshot. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reuse propagates defects as efficiently as improvements. A successful page review does not automatically certify every shared behavior. Explicit carry-forward notes prevent inherited problems from becoming surprises, while final-write discipline keeps the evidence package internally consistent.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Declare measurement rules and withdraw claims when their failure conditions occur
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define the statistic, test conditions, control and unsupported cases before collecting results. For noisy timing measurements, report repeated runs and their spread alongside an unchanged control measured in the same session. Treat a small initial sample as diagnostic rather than conclusive. Mark broken probes unresolved and use a faithful static fallback when reduced graphics degrade the design. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Preserve evidence when a check fails, but withdraw the validation it no longer supports. A narrower claim needs its own checks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Budget verification and separate measured checks from visual acceptance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give iterative review an explicit verification budget, stopping criteria and separate technical and visual acceptance checks. Prove new checks can reject a deliberately broken implementation, then reuse valid evidence when subsequent changes cannot affect it. Report unresolved failures alongside the preview rather than treating a composite score as approval. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Verification can expand indefinitely without improving the result. Automated checks establish specific properties; a stakeholder's visual review establishes whether the intended experience works. Neither should silently substitute for the other.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Refresh copied guidance after the source review closes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat guidance copied from an unfinished review as provisional and refresh it after that review closes. Before starting dependent generation, compare the copied artifact with the final source, retain a recoverable previous version and update task references and unresolved issue lists. Preparation can proceed in parallel, but execution should use the finalized lessons. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reviewer may correctly update only its own workspace while a downstream task holds an older copy. Without an explicit handoff check, the next iteration misses precisely the lessons the closing review produced.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Calibrate numeric visual thresholds against accepted and rejected artifacts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Set visual thresholds using independently accepted and rejected examples measured in their final encoding. In a hypothetical texture test, an accepted subtle grain and a rejected coarse grain should fall on the intended sides of the rule. If they do not, investigate the metric, version any correction and rescore earlier artifacts. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Arbitrary numbers can make automated review demand worse work. Distinguish recalculation from saved measurements from a fresh run, and retain human inspection because a few examples cannot prove universal validity.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Quality gates need independent references and bounds for both absence and excess
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A quality gate needs a reference accepted before the current candidate existed, and subtle effects need both lower and upper bounds. A presence check may compare an inspected candidate against an absent-effect baseline, but that proves existence rather than restraint. Calibrate a ceiling against an independently accepted example and an excessive variant, such as lights at three times strength. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Using the candidate to define its own quality threshold is circular. A floor can reject missing light while allowing an overwhelming wash. Until a calibrated ceiling detects excess, record subtlety as a human judgment rather than an automated pass.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Demonstrate both presence and excess detection for subtle lighting
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A subtle-lighting check should reject both absent light and excessive light. Construct hypothetical variants with the effect removed and amplified, measure both using the same method, and calibrate a floor and ceiling against an independently accepted reference. Keep thresholds specific to the measurement scale and rendering conditions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A presence floor alone cannot establish subtlety. Confirm that the amplified variant actually produces excess and that the check rejects it before treating the ceiling as release evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep calibration evidence attached to every new visual acceptance gate
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Each new visual gate should identify its accepted reference, rejected control, measurement method and threshold rationale. Run it against the known defective artifact before accepting a repair. For quality judgments, use a reference accepted independently of the candidate; for requirements such as subtle lighting, test both minimum presence and maximum strength. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated successful use does not excuse missing calibration on the next gate. A compact evidence record helps reviewers distinguish an empirical threshold from a definition chosen for convenience and prevents calculated rescoring from being presented as a fresh executed test.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Repair real regressions instead of weakening a threshold that correctly detects them
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Recalibrate a visual threshold when it misclassifies independently accepted work, not when a genuine defect returns. For an invented two-color animation, inspect the full cycle if a calibrated color-presence check fails. Confirm whether one color disappears or loses its intended balance across supported widths. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Lowering a valid floor hides the regression. Repair the layout or animation logic, and replace the measurement only when evidence shows that it no longer distinguishes acceptable and defective results.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review website quality across explicit dimensions and retain reusable fixes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use a generator, reviewer, and curator workflow to evaluate website quality against explicit criteria. Cover design-system compliance, structured-data validity, responsiveness, performance, accessibility, TypeScript quality, language consistency, and component architecture. An example stopping rule is overall score at least 8/10 with every dimension at least 6/10; critical defects still block completion. Record reusable fixes separately from project-specific changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Dimension-level checks expose weaknesses that an attractive overall score can hide. Scores support review, but browser evidence and executable checks establish whether the implementation works.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Invest in templates and examples so review can focus on residual defects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Strong templates, clear instructions, and representative examples can reduce the amount of corrective work needed after generation. Establish these inputs before repeatedly increasing review iterations. Review for duplicated text, prohibited terminology, unintended organization names, specification errors, and inaccurate generation reports. Treat first-pass scores of at least 8/10 and 0–3 corrections as possible outcomes, not guaranteed baselines. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeatedly repairing predictable mistakes wastes effort that could improve the starting instructions. A mature pipeline still needs independent checks because polished content can conceal factual errors and reports can misdescribe the artifacts they summarize.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make factual accuracy an explicit gate in content review
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate generated content for technical accuracy, completeness, content quality, convention compliance, and evidence density. One configurable rubric requires overall quality at least 8/10, technical accuracy at least 9/10, and every dimension at least 6/10. Continue when any threshold fails; diagnose a stalled process when two or more iterations produce no improvement. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A compelling voice cannot compensate for incorrect specifications or unsupported claims. Check whether evidence supports claims throughout the piece rather than appearing only in an introductory paragraph. Scores should summarize concrete findings and source checks, not replace them.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve generation, independent review, and lesson capture in iterative workflows
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An iterative improvement workflow needs artifact generation, independent review, and deliberate capture of reusable lessons. Record what changed and why, let the reviewer evaluate the resulting artifact, and update the reusable guidance only with supported findings. If a small manual correction bypasses the usual generation step, still record it and review its effect. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Skipping lesson capture makes the same failures recur, while undocumented changes weaken traceability. The important contract is complete evidence and feedback, not a ritual number of agent invocations for every edit.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make review feedback specific enough to implement and verify
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Write review findings with a precise location, the observed defect, the intended correction, and a verification condition. A file-and-line reference with 'replace X with Y because Z' is more actionable than 'improve this section.' Refresh locations after edits and preserve the underlying requirement when line numbers move. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Specific feedback reduces interpretation and unnecessary rewrites. Reported satisfaction gains of 0.4–1.5 points are rubric-dependent observations, not guaranteed improvements. Even an exact correction needs validation because its surrounding code or content may create interactions the reviewer did not anticipate.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review integration changes as carefully as newly generated code
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Include integration work in validation: imports, endpoint wiring, URL paths, registration order, and configuration can fail even when individual components are correct. Review the final assembled artifact and run checks that exercise its connections. A strict rubric may use a 9.8/10 target, but define observable acceptance conditions alongside any score. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Small glue-code edits often receive less scrutiny than large generated files despite controlling whether the system works. Scale the review process to the change's risk while preserving evidence that the integrated behavior meets its requirements.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reconcile curated skills against persistent memory after each review cycle
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After a curator cycle, reconcile the accepted skill inventory against persistent memory so reusable lessons remain retrievable. Store each distinct skill separately with its full rule, domain, evidence, helpful and harmful observations, and protection status. Check both existing and newly accepted skills; update matching records rather than creating duplicates. In Voidloom, use generic domain tags and importance values that reflect evidence and consequence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful review has limited lasting value if its lessons remain buried in a temporary report. Inventory reconciliation makes omissions visible and carries validated improvements into later projects without treating every experimental suggestion as established practice.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Apply hard acceptance thresholds exactly and distinguish them from aspirational targets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A hard acceptance threshold of 9.8/10 means that 9.72, 9.78 and 9.79 all require continued work. Declare whether the threshold applies to an aggregate score, every dimension, or both before evaluation. Distinguish hard gates from soft targets and record that distinction in the task specification. Do not round a failing result into acceptance or assume a fixed number of iterations guarantees completion. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Close-enough reasoning changes the agreement after the result is known. Explicit threshold semantics make review decisions reproducible, although the scoring rubric still needs observable evidence to keep numerical precision from implying unwarranted certainty.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reject review recommendations that contradict the stated stopping condition
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A review recommendation is invalid when it declares success while acknowledging that a hard stopping condition failed. For example, 9.72/10 cannot satisfy a 9.8 gate merely because every dimension exceeds a separate 8.0 floor. Validate the recommendation against the applicable threshold, reopen inconsistent results, and convert the remaining defects into scoped corrections. Preserve the original score and rationale for auditability. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Persuasive prose can conceal a straightforward rule violation. Separating mechanical gate checks from qualitative discussion prevents a reviewer from quietly replacing the agreed stopping condition with an easier one.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prepare changes thoroughly and require reviewers to reproduce the evidence independently
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Independent review must reproduce validation rather than accept the generator's report. Before handoff, resolve obvious defects; during review, rerun conformance checks, regenerate output, and compare it with the proposed artifact. Exercise missing sources, partial trees, duplicates, empty capabilities, and populated capabilities in isolated fixtures. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Preparation reduces avoidable review cycles, while independent evidence prevents confident reports from becoming false assurance. Checking both omission and inclusion proves that a filter responds to content rather than simply suppressing everything.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve generation and independent review roles in reusable workflow instructions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A reusable review workflow should explicitly preserve role separation and mandatory checks. Document who generates changes, who independently verifies them, what evidence is required, and which rollout conditions must hold. Carry these rules into the workflow's reusable instructions instead of relying on remembered conventions or a historical skill count. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] When one participant silently absorbs every role, review can become self-approval. Explicit responsibilities make the process easier to audit and keep later automation changes from weakening its original safeguards.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review a cross-site change as one coordinated rollout with evidence for every target
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Coordinate shared rollouts through generation, independent verification, and consolidation of reusable lessons. The reviewer should rebuild, rerun conformance, compare regenerated artifacts, and trace advertised resources for every target before release criteria are considered satisfied. Include working-tree hygiene and canonical-domain checks in the evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] One coordinated review can reduce duplicated process while retaining site-level accountability. A composite score or a successful small rollout does not prove scalability; the meaningful evidence is the completeness and reproducibility of each target's checks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bind review verdicts to the artifact, evaluation rules and execution protocol actually examined
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A review verdict applies to a specific artifact version, gate version, reviewer roster, input packaging and preregistered protocol. Record those identifiers with the result; changes require explicit justification before evidence is reused. Carry earlier findings forward as investigation inputs, and close them only after the relevant observation is rerun successfully. Preserve an unseen evaluation slice where possible. For historical inspection, use a restricted snapshot such as git archive when later repository objects could contaminate the probe. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A prior failure remains valid evidence about its original subject without condemning or clearing a revised artifact. Binding the verdict prevents stale results and protocol changes from masquerading as current validation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate editorial judgment from engineering acceptance and close findings only after re-observation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Editorial review and engineering acceptance need different stopping rules. Evaluate copy against source evidence and reader comprehension, with unsupported claims blocking release regardless of style scores. Evaluate implementation through observable behavior and relevant deterministic checks. Keep finding identification separate from repair, and close a finding only after re-observation confirms the defect is gone. A practical editorial loop can limit each round to three corrections and request human review after three rounds. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A high composite score can conceal a serious false claim. Bounded review prevents endless polishing while evidence-based closure prevents an intended fix from being mistaken for a verified result.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preregister review comparisons and distinguish clean first-round results from repair-influenced later rounds
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A comparison of review methods should freeze its protocol before evaluation and preserve the current workflow as a control. Record artifact snapshots, evaluator inputs and any platform substitutions. Treat the first independent review as distinct from later rounds influenced by repairs or prior findings. Report conclusions only for the task and conditions actually tested, including insufficient evidence when work finishes early. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Later rounds can measure adaptation to feedback rather than independent detection quality. Adding unnecessary rounds merely to produce experimental data distorts the work and weakens the comparison; a cleanly completed page should remain complete.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Delay shared-memory publication until independent review arms have completed
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Independent reviewers must not retrieve each other's findings before their comparison is complete. Capture observations immediately in isolated pending records, then publish them to shared memory only after the agreed review boundary. Give each reviewer the same permitted evidence and record additional context supplied during the run. Check that retrieval hooks and automatic summaries do not bypass the separation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared memory can turn another reviewer's discovery into apparent independent insight. Separating the time of capture from the time of publication preserves useful notes while keeping attribution and comparisons interpretable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test content gates with known-good fixtures and targeted defects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate automated content checks against both clean examples and deliberately defective examples before trusting their results. Give each defect an expected detection class, such as unsupported claims, private information, altered required wording or duplicated passages. Test that unrelated classes remain quiet. Keep source-backed factual checks distinct from editorial conventions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Overlapping rules produce confusing failures, while false positives erode trust. A button saying “Notify me” uses the visitor's voice and should not automatically trigger a rule about the organization's narrative voice. Fixture failures can reveal a faulty test or a faulty gate; inspect the evidence before changing either, and retain representative cases as regression checks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate factual release gates from style lint and test citation relevance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep factual release checks separate from editorial lint, and verify that citations support the claims attached to them. A source identifier existing in a digest is insufficient: planned features must retain conditional wording, and claims about customers or staffing need evidence. Treat simple word-overlap checks as screening heuristics, not semantic proof. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Combining harmless style violations with factual failures makes severity difficult to judge. Use shared includes for required wording and test near-copies, unsupported numbers, irrelevant citations and ordinary prose. Freeze gate versions and fixtures for review, record adopted and rejected changes, and distinguish checks already validated from checks awaiting deployed pages. Repeated subjective scores can reveal disagreement but cannot substitute for evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Freeze review inputs before revising briefs and recognize conditional language correctly
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Preserve the exact brief and fact digest used for a draft before changing the live sources. Review that draft against its frozen inputs, then assess later revisions against the updated brief. Record exploratory claims with conditional language such as may, might or could; a checker should not require a definite future promise for an uncertain possibility. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Otherwise reviewers can fault a writer for requirements introduced after drafting. Add paired fixtures showing that acceptable conditional wording passes while unsupported present-tense claims fail. Modal words are only a screening signal: reviewers must still check whether the full sentence preserves uncertainty and whether the underlying source supports the possibility.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate computed review evidence from editorial judgment
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Generate review counts and evidence tables from the reviewed artifact, while storing human judgments separately. Derive section totals, word counts, validation results, and file fingerprints with code; record interpretations and unresolved questions in explicit metadata. If the review rules are frozen for comparison, publish clarifications beside that version rather than silently changing it. Apply the revised rules to later work under a new version. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Hand-entered totals drift, while judgments cannot become objective merely by appearing in a generated report. Keeping those responsibilities separate makes review packets reproducible and allows rule corrections without rewriting the history of earlier evaluations.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match evidence coverage to the full claim being evaluated
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A claim checker produces false alarms when it evaluates a multi-claim sentence against evidence for only one clause. Preserve the reader-facing sentence, identify every factual assertion it contains, and gather the supporting evidence for all of them. Use a preliminary run to inspect false-alarm mechanisms before treating scores as evaluation results. Record any protocol change before the next counted run. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A high flag rate can indicate a broken pairing method rather than poor copy. Replacing the sentence with the writer's preferred paraphrase can hide the problem; repairing evidence coverage tests what the reader will actually encounter.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Evaluate original sentences against pooled evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate each unique reader-facing sentence against the union of evidence cited for its constituent claims. Map the resulting verdict back to the relevant ledger rows. Do not substitute a writer-authored proposition when it merely paraphrases the supporting material; that risks checking evidence against itself. If anonymization is necessary, apply the same grammatical transformation to claims and evidence, preserving possessives and relationships. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Evidence pooling fixes incomplete support without weakening the claim under examination. Consistent anonymization also prevents artificial wording differences from masquerading as factual disagreement. Keep thresholds and control cases stable while testing this methodological change.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Compare review methods on identical input before attributing improvements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Run old and new review methods on identical page copy to distinguish checker changes from content improvements. Use unchanged controls, report skipped items and inspect remaining flags manually. Evaluate published assertions separately from drafting instructions. A statement that a feature is available needs evidence of availability, even if its implementation exists. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fewer flags do not automatically mean better writing or a better checker. Holding input constant isolates the method change; manual review determines whether it removed false alarms or concealed unsupported claims.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Close review findings by checking whether the reader harm remains
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify a revision by asking a fresh reviewer whether the original reader harm is still present. Supply the current copy, complete harm descriptions, relevant facts, and any criteria needed to judge them. Recheck repeated patterns across the page, including unexplained references, redundant limits, jargon, and unnatural register. Report unavailable evidence rather than silently assuming it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An edit can satisfy the wording of a requested fix while leaving the misunderstanding intact elsewhere. Complete harm descriptions matter: extraction that truncates a sentence at a quotation mark can change the question the reviewer is answering.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bound review rounds and expose unresolved decisions in a concrete packet
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Set a review-round limit and present the actual draft with remaining issues when that limit is reached. Include mechanical check results, unsupported claims, unresolved factual questions, and a conservative proposed disposition for each open item. Check rendered includes as well as source text when testing duplication or required wording. Label checks that were not run. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Endless review cannot settle missing facts or conflicting requirements. A bounded process makes the remaining decisions inspectable without claiming that the draft is flawless. Reviewing expanded output also catches problems hidden by template syntax and checks marked inapplicable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Let reviewers inspect original evidence when summaries may distort claims
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reviewers need access to original evidence when a condensed brief may contain the error being reviewed. Trace important claims beyond summaries, check that qualifiers survived condensation, and test whether a competitor's name could replace the subject without changing the lead. Record which rule version governed the draft so later requirements are not treated as earlier mistakes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A well-organized digest can become a shared source of error for writer and reviewer. Returning to underlying records reveals omitted conditions and inflated promises. The substitution test separately identifies positioning that sounds distinctive but describes nearly every alternative.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review the rules as well as the artifact when findings conflict
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When reviewers disagree, inspect the governing rule and the measurement method before adding another revision round. Separate artifact defects from ambiguous criteria, unavailable evidence, and checks that did not run. Version clarifications, recheck the affected reader harms, and stop at a predefined review limit with a concrete list of unresolved decisions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated review can expose defects in the rulebook itself. Treating every disagreement as a writing failure creates churn and obscures which changes actually improve the result. A visible decision boundary keeps the process useful.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Classify sentence function before interpreting automated claim scores
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Separate factual assertions, questions, negations, calls to action, and template tokens before interpreting automated entailment scores. Audit flagged examples by sentence type and route ambiguous claims to human review. A question about a guarantee is not itself a guarantee, and an invitation to follow progress needs different evidence from a capability claim. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A checker trained around assertions can generate convincing-looking alarms on ordinary interface copy. Understanding its false-alarm profile prevents wasted review effort and makes it easier to identify unsupported claims among the noise.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Judge independent reviews by distinct consequential catches, not finding counts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Compare reviews by the validity and severity of their distinct findings rather than total count alone. Review claim evidence at sentence level, distinguish working components from incomplete integrations, and check whether FAQs answer the question directly. Supply reviewers with authoritative facts and complete advisory output. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A shorter review can still catch a serious defect missed by a longer one. Differences in source access and review scope also confound comparisons between reviewers. Independent coverage is useful when it exposes a new failure mode, not merely when it produces more comments.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Attach evidence to the specific claim it supports
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A claim ledger should map each claim-bearing sentence or phrase to relevant evidence instead of copying a block-wide citation list onto every row. Distinguish product facts from operational promises such as sending notifications. Preserve the full advisory list in review inputs, then inspect why automated flags change after ledger repairs. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Broad citation lists can make unsupported wording appear covered and dilute useful evidence. A lower flag count may reflect better evidence alignment, changed copy, or checker behavior; it is a diagnostic signal rather than proof that the draft became correct.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check each copy repair against earlier failure cases
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep a regression list of previously misleading claims and recheck it after every substantive copy repair. Include neighboring blocks and compressed summaries, not only the sentence being fixed. Verify meaning against source facts even when vocabulary overlaps closely enough to pass mechanical checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Tight word budgets encourage local edits that quietly remove scope, change readiness, or reintroduce an earlier implication. Word matching cannot establish semantic accuracy. Carrying earlier failure cases forward gives iterative polishing a memory and prevents each round from treating the draft as a fresh problem.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.
