memories.summary: Independent review should probe behavior beyond the builder's passing checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Independent review should test user-visible behavior and alternate execution paths even when every existing gate passes. Compare first and repeat submissions, send malformed JSON, inspect error logs for submitted content, measure menu bounds, and exercise a manual production build. Malformed input should produce a controlled client error without logging body excerpts. Check that production safeguards do not depend exclusively on a CI branch variable. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Builders tend to test the failure modes they anticipated. A separate review can expose contradictory privacy behavior, unsafe defaults, or hidden deployment paths that the original suite never modeled. Critical correctness defects should block release before polish receives further attention.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review proposed wording for cross-document effects, including the reviewer's own suggestions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reviewer-proposed wording needs the same consistency checks as the original draft. When a revision changes the definition of a phrase, inspect every sentence that relies on that definition. Describe the harm and acceptance condition clearly, leaving room for the writer to choose wording that fits the whole document. Track closure separately for copy, implementation, and unresolved decisions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A locally elegant sentence can introduce a global contradiction, especially when adopted verbatim from a reviewer. Separating responsibilities also prevents a clean copy review from being mistaken for proof that the promised behavior is already implemented and tested.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test creation and update paths separately and tie acceptance to observable requirements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful creation-path test does not prove that updating an existing resource applies the same configuration. Exercise both paths, including authenticated form submission rather than page loads alone. Use explicit pass/fail requirements and a privacy statement-to-behavior table to assess release readiness. If scoring criteria change, do not interpret the score difference as measured improvement without calibration. Redact authorization headers and session cookies from diagnostics. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fresh resources can inherit settings that older resources lack, leaving a polished preview unable to submit forms. Concrete acceptance checks expose that gap more clearly than a composite score, while sanitized evidence avoids creating a second incident during diagnosis.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Divide acceptance responsibilities without duplicating live side effects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Independent acceptance reviewers should share core checks while dividing live tests that send messages or alter data. Give each reviewer a separate workspace and port, keep their findings blind until adjudication, and assign one reviewer to challenge assumptions and deletion behavior. Permit only one authorized contact-email smoke test, then delete its exact test records. Verify rollout using a build-specific marker on the intended route. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeating the same review prompt adds less coverage than assigning distinct investigative responsibilities. Coordinating side effects preserves realistic testing without duplicate messages, while independent execution still exposes shared infrastructure failures.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate application correctness from live infrastructure readiness
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Passing application checks does not establish deployment readiness when live infrastructure checks fail. Record code, configuration, and end-to-end results separately, and bind each verdict to the deployed revision. After an infrastructure-only repair, verify application artifacts remain unchanged before selectively rerunning affected checks. Prove persistence with a second CI push. Keep residual findings explicit, including incomplete cleanup, lint bypasses, and test-value normalization gaps. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Agreement between independent reviewers helps localize a failure, but it does not prove that every untested risk is absent. Separating evidence prevents an infrastructure repair from being mistaken for a new application review.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Acceptance needs explicit residual risks and automated checks that actually run
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An acceptance verdict should distinguish passing release criteria, residual defects, and checks that exist only as instructions. Verify any claimed unchanged build by comparing artifacts or meaningful source differences. Prioritize residuals that undermine production guards, such as whitespace allowing a test credential through validation. Move critical post-push checks into CI rather than relying indefinitely on a runbook reminder. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Independent acceptance strengthens evidence for the tested release, but it does not erase known limitations. A written checking procedure offers no protection on a push where nobody runs it, and a small input-normalization bug can defeat an otherwise convincing guard.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use executable release criteria when subjective scores stop resolving remaining risks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Near release, translate remaining requirements into binary executable checks and require independent reviewers to pass every blocking check. Freeze the criteria before repair, keep reviewers blind to each other's findings, and provide separate ports and scratch directories. Treat numeric quality scores as supporting observations rather than substitutes for acceptance. Coordinate any live side effects explicitly, and record nonblocking findings in a residual list. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Small score changes can reflect reviewer variability rather than meaningful improvement. Concrete checks expose the remaining failure and make a later acceptance attributable to a verified fix rather than optimism or iteration pressure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate review checks against actual document formatting and known false positives
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A review check must detect faults in the document formats it will process. Preserve continuation and nested bullets when extracting facts so headings retain their qualifications. Test status detection with planned, in-development, available and explicitly unavailable features. Run changed rules against known-valid copy and confirm that new controls expose the previous implementation's defect. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A passing test may only show that a fixture matches the detector. During a predefined evaluation, record extraction faults and version repairs separately so results remain comparable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat clustered review flags as hypotheses until checked against complete evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check automated review flags against complete supporting documents before turning them into revision instructions. Include positive and negative controls, record skipped items and errors, and identify flags that depend on the same extracted fact. Inspect nested bullets for lost qualifications. Where practical, assess findings without knowing which reviewer produced them. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Several similar flags may reflect a recurring content defect or a shared extraction failure. Scores can prioritize inspection, but evidence determines whether a claim needs correction.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Evaluate review methods by confirmed usefulness rather than falling flag counts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Track confirmed findings, false alarms and repeated flags tied to the same document structure. Assess a reviewer configuration across multiple rounds before making it mandatory, optional or retiring it. Keep conclusions limited to the tasks and settings tested. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated objections to supported claims can reveal missing context or faulty extraction. Editing accurate prose merely to silence those objections can reduce quality. Confirmed usefulness measures whether review improves the page; raw counts measure how often the checker objects.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Shared temporary directories can compromise independent reviews
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Independent reviewers need separate scratch directories as well as separate workspaces. Assign each reviewer a private working area and explicitly exclude shared session directories and other reviewers' scratch locations from permitted inputs. Where independence matters, enforce visibility boundaries through filesystem permissions or isolation rather than instructions alone. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A neutral-looking temporary folder can expose another reviewer's conclusions or a writer's drafts. A reviewer voluntarily declining to open a visible file is helpful conduct, but it is not a reliable blinding mechanism.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Isolated writers can reveal contradictions in the brief before those contradictions become copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A writer working from a bounded source packet can expose conflicts that a context-rich coordinator overlooks. Supply explicit claim sources, wording constraints and an allowed output set, then require unresolved contradictions to be reported. Check all representations of a fact when correcting an input, including tables and explanatory notes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Isolation prevents the writer from silently filling gaps with background knowledge. Questions about contradictory terminology or missing support are evidence that the source packet needs repair, even when the resulting draft passes mechanical checks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Combine source-bounded copy review with a reviewer who can inspect the implementation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Copy review needs both checks against supplied facts and checks that those facts match the implementation. Give one reviewer a bounded source packet and another read-only access to relevant code and execution evidence. Compare findings by claim and consequence rather than treating agreement as the sole measure of validity. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Two reviewers can agree that a sentence follows from an inaccurate fact sheet. A code-reading reviewer can uncover the deeper gap, while a source-bounded reviewer reveals ambiguity and unsupported wording without relying on hidden context.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make a writer's source packet complete without relying on hidden background context
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A writer-facing packet should contain the facts, maturity levels, claim limits and source precedence needed to draft independently. Keep sensitive or irrelevant investigation material outside it, but translate every necessary conclusion into usable guidance. Test the brief with mock copy before relying on it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] If a writer must consult an unavailable dossier to understand a constraint, the packet is incomplete. A self-contained packet makes omissions and contradictions visible early and reduces the temptation to turn intended capabilities into present-tense promises.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use permitted sources to constrain a slot's claims before drafting
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A content slot's permitted-source list constrains what the wording may claim, not just which citations appear afterward. Read that list before drafting headlines, questions and body text, then check that each complete proposition is supported. Flag suggested wording that exceeds the slot's evidence rather than assuming the suggestion grants permission. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Citation bookkeeping cannot repair an unsupported sentence. Establishing the evidence boundary first reduces rework and catches contradictions between a brief's examples and its own source rules.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate genuine unsupported claims from valid paraphrases in automated review
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Automated claim-review flags require adjudication against the actual meaning of the source and sentence. Classify findings such as unsupported tense, expanded scope and valid paraphrase separately. Compare them with independently raised writer questions, but retain the original evidence for each decision. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reviewer can be sensitive to different wording while missing a more consequential implication. Flag counts and agreement are useful diagnostic signals, not proof of correctness; tracking failure types makes the tool's practical strengths and blind spots clearer.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A claim ledger must preserve the sentence's whole proposition
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A claim ledger must restate every material assertion in the original sentence, including actor, tense, scope and implied availability. Review the ledger proposition alongside the exact copy rather than checking the proposition alone. If an approved line fails factual review, reopen it through the normal change process. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An overstated sentence can appear supported when its ledger entry quietly drops the unsupported part. Downstream checkers then validate a weaker statement that readers never saw, creating a false appearance of rigorous grounding.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Universal words require review across the whole page and mechanism
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Claims using only, every or never require evidence across the full scope they assert. Check related facts, rendered includes and secondary descriptions rather than validating one ledger row in isolation. A statement about one component's allowed destination must not silently become a claim about all application traffic. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Individually supported sentences can contradict each other when combined. Universal wording crosses fact boundaries, so row-by-row entailment checks need a separate consistency review of the complete page and the mechanism it describes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define repairs by the affected fact class, not just the sentences named in a finding
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a fact changes, the repair task should require review of every dependent claim, including unnamed and approved slots. Use source references to define the affected set, then rederive each proposition from the amended evidence. Make this sweep compatible with instructions limiting unrelated edits. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A narrow “change nothing else” task can preserve exactly the stale statements the correction invalidates. Naming the dependency class prevents careful compliance from becoming a source of defects and gives reviewers a concrete basis for checking closure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat automated claim-review scores as leads for source inspection
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Automated claim-review flags should prompt inspection of the sentence and its sources rather than serve as final verdicts. Check that the reviewer handles known valid and invalid examples, reports skipped rows and errors, and examines compressed titles as well as body copy. Keep independent reviews separate until their findings are collected. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Titles can introduce tense or scope errors through compression, but a model can also misread them. A numerical score does not replace a reasoned determination of what the source supports.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give source reviewers necessary evidence while keeping private details out of findings
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A source-grounded reviewer needs access to the underlying record, with explicit limits on what may appear in downstream findings. Report sensitive issues by class, such as an unsupported employment claim, rather than reproducing private identifiers. Ensure the review schema permits necessary evidence fields before review begins. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Source access improves factual checking but creates another route for information leakage. Structured findings can preserve the reasoning needed for correction while preventing private source details from flowing into drafts or public artifacts.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Combine source review with a fresh reading of the assembled page
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review the assembled page for composition as well as checking individual sentences against sources. Expand shared content, include the footer, and look for repeated arguments, undefined terms, misplaced descriptions and transitions that change scope. Treat predicted reader confusion as a hypothesis to investigate with unfamiliar readers. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A sentence can be valid in isolation yet become repetitive or misleading beside another valid sentence. Fresh readers reveal comprehension problems, while source review establishes whether the proposed correction remains true.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate source summaries against primary records as well as copy against summaries
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Factual review needs two checks: whether the copy matches its source summary and whether that summary matches the underlying record. Inspect chronology, authorship, causal links and universal claims at the record level. Keep private identifiers out of findings when they are unnecessary to explain the defect. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A writer can faithfully reproduce an inaccurate summary and pass every copy-to-source check. Independent record review catches inherited mistakes and directs corrections to the source so later pages do not repeat them.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check proposed replacement text before presenting it as a fix
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reviewer-supplied replacement copy should pass the same factual, wording and length checks applied to the draft. Scan it for relevant phrase overlap and read it in context before recommending adoption. Label illustrative wording as provisional when it has not been checked. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Review suggestions often become authoritative templates for the next revision. An unchecked example can introduce a new violation and force another round of work, so responsibility for a proposed fix includes validating the proposal itself.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Group review findings by reader harm before assigning revisions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Consolidate overlapping review findings into a small set of concrete harms, such as unsupported claims, unclear offers and contradictory positioning. Preserve individual evidence under each group and specify what successful correction would look like. Separate straightforward factual fixes from decisions that change the actual offer or public positioning. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A long issue list can encourage scattered sentence edits that miss the shared cause. Grouping makes the revision coherent while keeping genuine product decisions from being silently settled by a writer.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep revision scope auditable and inspect new wording for new implications
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A focused revision should preserve unaffected text and make changed claims easy to compare with their sources. Snapshot inputs, identify changed sections, rebuild the claim mapping and inspect assembled output. Pay particular attention to added definitions, broader synonyms and punctuation that changes what a phrase describes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fixing an unclear term can introduce an ambiguous referent or erase development status. Small, reviewable changes help reviewers distinguish resolved defects from new implications without repeatedly reassessing the entire page.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Do not infer reviewer reliability from a few changing scores
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When an automated reviewer changes its verdict on identical text, treat the score as unstable evidence and inspect the source directly. Record unchanged inputs, model settings and controls when comparing runs. Establish any decision threshold on a broader evaluation rather than inferring reliability from a few favorable examples. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A disappearing flag does not demonstrate that a defect was fixed, and a new flag does not prove regression. Small samples cannot support a general claim that one score band is reliable and another is noise.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Close review findings by checking the original harm, not just changed wording
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A finding is resolved only when the misleading implication or reader obstacle has been removed. A new definition can still imply present availability, and replacing a causal phrase can leave the same causal suggestion through sentence placement. Compare revised text with the original harm, its source evidence and its surrounding context. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Pattern checks can confirm that prohibited wording disappeared while the mistaken belief remains. Closure review should also check whether the repair introduced undefined roles, broader claims or unsupported tense.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Judge a repair against the reader misunderstanding, not just the passing check
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A copy repair is complete only when it removes the original misleading interpretation. Replacing a flagged noun phrase can satisfy a regular expression while leaving the same causal implication in the paragraph. Read the revised passage beside a plain statement of the harm, including the sentences immediately before it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Automated checks recognize the patterns they encode. Readers also infer relationships from placement and sequence, so a passing check can hide a defect that merely changed vocabulary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check suggested replacement wording against evidence before accepting it
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Apply the same factual scrutiny to suggested replacements as to the original web copy. Verify chronology, causal links, pronoun references and availability against authoritative project documentation. Close each finding by checking both whether the edit was made and whether the resulting statement is true. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A suggested sentence can introduce an unsupported claim. Agreement between writer and reviewer does not provide independent evidence, so factual verification must remain a separate step.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Do not treat a reviewer's example sentence as verified source material
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Suggested replacement copy is a draft, even when it comes from the reviewer who identified the defect. For a bicycle-repair co-op, changing a history paragraph to say every expansion introduced a new skill would require evidence for every expansion. Verify universal claims and implied timelines against records before adopting them. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A compliant writer can faithfully implement a false suggestion. Checking only whether the finding was addressed misses errors introduced by the finding itself.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test copy guards with paraphrases of the failure class
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A wording guard should be tested against paraphrases that preserve the misleading meaning. If the defect is an unsupported causal link after a list, test demonstratives, gerunds and alternative causal verbs rather than only the original phrase. Include acceptable sentences to expose overbroad matching. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A regular expression built from one example protects that wording. Writers naturally reach for synonyms, so class-based test cases reveal gaps before a superficial rewrite earns a false pass.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Continue independent repairs while unresolved decisions remain isolated
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An unanswered stakeholder decision need not block repairs that are valid under every possible answer. Separate factual corrections from decision-dependent wording, complete the independent work, and reserve a bounded final pass for the unresolved choice. Recheck new definitions and status language introduced by each repair. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This keeps review moving without inventing authority. Smaller edits can indicate convergence, but only if the remaining misunderstandings also shrink; fewer changed words alone do not establish readiness.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define the harm class before writing its automated guard
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Write an editorial guard from the prohibited meaning before choosing matching words. For unsupported causation, consider constructions using “led,” “prompted,” “because” and “as a result,” then test realistic paraphrases and legitimate uses. Run the guard against the reviewer's own proposed repair as well. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repair instructions can reproduce the same faulty reasoning they aim to remove. Class-based examples improve coverage, while semantic review remains necessary because broader expressions can still miss implications or reject truthful sentences.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Track review convergence with scoped changes and remaining defect severity
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Assess revision progress using both the scope of edits and the severity of unresolved defects. Freeze the input set, compare content sections against the prior version, and distinguish intentional changes from incidental drift. Recheck source support and word budgets for changed passages. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A shrinking diff makes review easier but does not prove correctness. The useful signal is that important misunderstandings disappear while previously sound passages remain stable and new wording receives proportionate scrutiny.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Calibrate automated review scores locally before using a cutoff
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Automated review thresholds need task-specific calibration against independently confirmed defects. If scores below 0.3 identify two real errors while scores from 0.4 to 0.5 fluctuate on identical text, treat the lower range as a hypothesis for useful triage, not a validated universal cutoff. Record unchanged-text variability and collect more labelled examples. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Two successes cannot establish reliable precision or recall. Local observations can guide investigation without turning a small, unstable sample into a general claim about the reviewer.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use capped review rounds with a final pass for bounded residual fixes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A capped review process can move to final approval when substantive defects are closed and remaining edits are explicitly bounded. List residual issues, distinguish harmless polish from misleading wording, apply the agreed fixes, and run a focused closure check. Do not let the round limit override unresolved truthfulness problems. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Unlimited full reviews can create fresh wording churn. A narrow final pass preserves scrutiny while directing attention to the few remaining changes and decisions that affect publication readiness.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit supposedly independent copy examples for source echo
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a control example must avoid source echo, measure shared word runs before accepting it. Use the same tokenizer as the final check; a strict task may require zero shared five-word runs outside explicitly permitted fixed terms. Inspect matches, rewrite unintended borrowing and repeat the audit. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Writers trying to preserve factual fidelity often reproduce source phrasing without noticing. An explicit check makes the independence requirement observable, although lexical independence alone does not establish different reasoning or structure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recheck a section's historical failure classes after every constrained edit
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A closure check should revisit all relevant defect classes previously fixed in the edited section. If a short FAQ once needed a definition, verify that later additions have not displaced it to meet the word cap. Keep required meaning and optional wording visibly separate in the brief. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A narrowly scoped amendment can undo an older repair without touching the newest finding. Regression review protects the section's accumulated guarantees rather than checking only the latest request.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure the named defect rather than a convenient proxy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Removing shared word runs does not necessarily remove repetitive content structure. A rewrite can use entirely different vocabulary while presenting the same facts in the same order. When the finding concerns mirroring, compare information sequence, sentence roles and the passage's purpose alongside lexical checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Optimizing an easy metric can worsen the experience it was meant to protect. Review criteria should remain tied to the reader's problem instead of drifting toward whatever the script can count.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify narrow final edits against a frozen approved baseline
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A final copy patch should change only the authorised sections and preserve the rest against a frozen baseline. Compare sections programmatically, update evidence notes for affected claims and disclose any required content that cannot fit. Resolve budget conflicts according to the brief's priorities before accepting the patch. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Every incidental edit adds review burden and can disturb settled wording. A small verified diff supports efficient review, but scope compliance does not excuse removing meaning the answer still needs.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Escalate conflicting editorial constraints instead of endlessly rewording
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When repeated rewrites cannot remove a misunderstanding, inspect whether the governing rules conflict. A ban on body status language may clash with a requirement that an FAQ answer stand alone outside the page. Identify the missing distinction, revise the relevant constraint and test the revised answer independently. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Some failures belong to the specification rather than the writer. Naming the contradiction allows one principled correction instead of another cycle of synonyms that preserves the same ambiguity.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use isolated reader checks to test whether availability distinctions survive
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test availability wording by showing the answer alone to unfamiliar readers and asking which options they believe are open today. Record uncertainty as well as incorrect interpretations. If readers identify the current service but still assume planned alternatives are available, the repair has closed only part of the defect. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A passing self-check verifies compliance with encoded rules, not comprehension. Small reader checks can reveal a concrete unresolved ambiguity without supporting broad statistical claims about all visitors.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Revalidate headings and evidence notes when their section changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A heading's supporting claim can become stale even when the heading text remains unchanged. After adding a route or changing a section's scope, reread its headings, summaries and evidence notes. Write each recorded proposition as a faithful restatement of what readers can actually infer from the published words. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A builder may verify exact text matches and valid source references without checking contextual truth. Section-level changes can invalidate dependent claims that a changed-lines-only review never visits.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Combine open reading questions with explicit availability choices
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review important copy through several reading contexts and ask both open questions and explicit status questions. Show separate readers a search snippet, an extracted FAQ answer, or raw FAQPage JSON-LD. Ask what they believe, then request “available today,” “not yet,” or “cannot tell” for each offer. Include a literal reading of the claims. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Different contexts expose different ambiguities. Agreement among model-based readers is useful diagnostic evidence, but it is not a substitute for representative human testing or a population estimate.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Approve the exact reviewed copy only after checking what isolated excerpts imply
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Final copy approval should identify the exact reviewed artifact and include a fresh check of excerpts likely to circulate independently. Verify availability, identity, and limitations in FAQs and metadata as well as in the full page. Record unresolved minor issues separately from defects that change the reader’s understanding. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful build proves that the page can be produced, not that its claims are understood correctly. Small wording revisions can materially change interpretation, so approval must apply to the final text rather than an earlier review.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Positive controls and error messages must satisfy the same truth checks as published copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A positive control certifies acceptable behavior, so its meaning must be checked independently of the validator it tests. For word-order rules, include an obviously valid sentence and a reversed construction that changes the claim. Read diagnostic messages as instructions a writer may follow literally. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A faulty control can teach a gate to approve the defect it should reject, while a misleading error message steers revisions toward the same mistake. Large test counts cannot compensate for an incorrect definition of acceptable behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A citation must support the predicate of a claim, not merely mention its subject
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check that cited evidence supports what a sentence says about an entity, not just the entity’s identity. A source establishing who runs a bakery does not by itself prove that the bakery manufactures every item it sells. Use automated entailment flags to prioritize source inspection, then distinguish missing support from factual contradiction. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A low model score is a review signal, not a verdict. The remedy may be adding the correct citation rather than changing an otherwise true sentence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate the published sentence against evidence rather than trusting its ledger paraphrase
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Fact-check the exact page wording because a claim ledger can silently repair an incorrect sentence. After rearranging copy to avoid repetition, compare modifier attachment in the published sentence with both the evidence and the ledger entry. Do not move a location phrase or condition while restating the claim for review. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A true-looking paraphrase can conceal a false original. Changes made for a narrow mechanical purpose deserve a fresh semantic check, especially when the supporting record was written by the same author.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review brief wording as potential published copy and fix upstream causes of recurring defects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat slot purposes, examples, amendments, and diagnostic messages as wording that may reach the published page. Check them for factual scope, standalone clarity, jargon, and collisions with approved copy before assigning the draft. When a defect follows the brief faithfully, correct the brief and identify that cause in the findings. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A mock generated from the same instructions can reproduce their blind spots while appearing internally consistent. Accurate attribution also prevents writers from overcorrecting unaffected sections in response to mistakes introduced upstream.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check revision scope and factual meaning separately
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] In a document-review workflow, compare the revised version with the agreed edit list, run relevant checks and inspect the meanings introduced by each change. For an invented museum visitor guide, moving an opening-hours qualifier could accidentally make a seasonal schedule sound permanent. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A focused revision can still introduce a false statement. Scope checks establish what changed; evidence review establishes whether the new wording is supported.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Attach each caveat to the claim it actually qualifies
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Identify the subject and scope of each claim before judging a nearby caveat. In an invented garden centre guide, free admission to the grounds can coexist with a charge for workshops. Neither statement establishes whether special events are free. Check the source wording before accepting an automated warning. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Adjacent statements can concern different services or conditions. Separating their subjects prevents both false contradictions and unsupported generalizations.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check whether moving a modifier changes the claim
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When repairing an ambiguous modifier, list the subjects it could qualify and verify the revised meaning. In an invented swim school guide, a statement about free equipment rental must not become a promise of free lessons. If a wording check rejects an accurate sentence, revise the check or use another accurate construction. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Grammatical clarity can expose a new factual error. Passing a writing rule does not establish truth.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Do not let literal text checks force unexplained jargon into copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Let wording checks accept clear equivalent phrasing when the requirement remains satisfied. If a rule demands an unexplained technical expression, revise the check alongside the page copy and document the changed acceptance criterion. Include valid alternatives and misleading near-matches in test fixtures. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An overly narrow rule can reject readable writing while rewarding jargon. Reviewing the rule change explicitly preserves accountability without confusing a particular string with its intended meaning.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: When suggested fixes keep introducing defects, supply facts and constraints instead
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When reviewer-written replacements repeatedly create new errors, try a revision brief containing facts, prohibited implications and acceptance criteria without example sentences. Ask the writer to derive fresh wording, then assess the result against the same factual requirements. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Suggested prose carries assumptions about actors, locations and capabilities that can survive superficial editing. Removing that prose tests whether it is causing the regressions. Treat improvement as a hypothesis to verify through closure review and reader comprehension, rather than assuming the technique always works.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Evaluate constraints-only briefs through independent closure and reader checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A constraints-only writing brief should be evaluated through factual closure checks and fresh-reader comprehension, not merely successful lint. State the harms to avoid and the verified facts, then inspect whether the writer independently derives wording instead of copying the brief's sentence frames. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Cleaner drafting behaviour is useful process evidence, but it does not establish that the final page is accurate or understandable. Keeping those conclusions separate prevents enthusiasm for a workflow change from replacing evaluation of its actual output.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Close semantic findings by reading the whole claim rather than checking a token
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review the complete sentence when resolving a finding about meaning, even if an automated phrase check passes. Verify the subject, predicates, qualifications and coverage of relevant cases. Record which checks were mechanical and which required judgment. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A required phrase can appear while qualifying the wrong actor or covering only part of the requirement. Making the check's limitations explicit prevents token presence from substituting for factual resolution.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Exact phrase matching misses near-copies formed by a single substitution
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A six-word exact-match check can miss a copied sentence frame when one substituted word splits the shared text into shorter runs. Supplement exact matching with seven-word windows that mask one position, then inspect matches for shared structure and meaning. Treat five-word overlaps as review leads rather than automatic clearance. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Passing a threshold proves only that the tested pattern was absent. A synonym can preserve the entire promise while defeating an exact-run detector, so genuine repair often requires changing the sentence structure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test copy candidates in isolated page copies alongside a known failing control
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate each wording candidate in a separate temporary page using unchanged checks and reference inputs. Inspect overlap with prohibited wording, approved messaging and neighboring sections. Include an invented failing draft that demonstrates the targeted defect, and record why candidates are rejected. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A passing result offers limited evidence unless the checker also rejects the intended failure. Isolated page copies prevent mixed edits, while rejection reasons make the final choice easier to review.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review repairs for defects they introduce elsewhere
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A repair can satisfy its immediate constraints while introducing a near-copy or another defect elsewhere on the page. After noun swaps and reordered clauses, compare the revised sentence against protected messaging using substitution-tolerant matching as well as exact runs. A sentence with 8 of 9 tokens identical deserves inspection even when no six-word run matches. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Literal string bans invite literal compliance through synonyms. Checking the underlying sentence frame catches cases where the defect moved instead of disappearing.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep review thresholds stable and resolve contradictory rubric versions explicitly
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Apply the authoritative review rubric consistently and identify stale summaries before grading. For example, a six-word overlap rule requiring at least two content words must not silently become a five-word rule because an older table says so. Describe the condition that would justify a stronger finding without changing the scale mid-review. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Vivid examples can tempt reviewers to escalate inconsistently. Stable thresholds make results comparable; explicit rubric revisions allow stronger checks without disguising a change in standards.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify structural copy repairs with both the revised page and the defective predecessor
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A copy repair is better supported when the revised page passes and its defective predecessor fails the same targeted check. Confirm that the new sentence changes the relationship being expressed rather than merely replacing a word. Allow genuinely required terminology, and verify that the supporting claim record still matches the revised wording. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A clean result alone cannot distinguish a successful repair from a broken detector. The predecessor supplies a concrete negative control, while claim verification prevents originality edits from introducing unsupported promises.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review briefs and examples as carefully as the copy they produce
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Briefs, amendments, examples and diagnostic messages can introduce the same defects that reviewers later attribute to generated copy. State the reader harm and constraints before prescribing replacement wording. Re-run existing controls whenever a rule expands, check near-copies explicitly, and use fresh readers to assess availability claims on the rendered page. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Writers naturally imitate authoritative examples, including flawed ones. Improving the instruction artifacts removes defects at their source and prevents repeated repair loops that leave the underlying guidance untouched.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use structured fresh-reader tests to reveal misleading first impressions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give fresh readers only the rendered visitor text and ask structured questions about availability, first-screen meaning, confusion and the next action. For an amateur astronomy club, ask whether a visitor believes telescope bookings are open today and where that belief formed. Test standalone FAQ extracts separately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Checklist compliance can miss a page that reveals a decisive limitation only at the bottom. Independent reader responses expose that interpretation problem. Model-based readers provide useful probes, but their agreement is not a substitute for testing with actual visitors.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use automated claim scores to prioritize evidence review, not decide truth
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Automated claim scores should direct attention to evidence rather than determine whether a sentence is true. Inspect whether a citation supports the predicate, not merely the named subject, and separate neighboring caveats from the claim under review. Evaluate the checker across at least three review loops before deciding whether it earns a required role. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A cheap checker can still add little value if it only repeats findings humans already identify. Thresholds are local calibration results, not transferable confidence levels; keep the tool optional until its incremental contribution is demonstrated.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use review caps to control churn while keeping unresolved truth defects explicit
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] End iterative review with a clear list of unresolved findings, separating factual defects from optional wording changes. Track whether successive passes reduce meaningful problems, and define a round limit before revisions begin. If an advertised capability fails for a supported configuration, correct or qualify that claim rather than treating it as taste. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Endless polishing consumes attention, but a review cap does not make a false statement acceptable. A concrete handoff preserves accountability while allowing harmless stylistic choices to remain without another full writing cycle.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prepare content, assets and acceptance checks before starting a design loop
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Resolve content sources, image assets, figure semantics and acceptance checks before asking a design generator to iterate. Require a design brief with layout sketches at 1440 and 390, a token plan and a clear visual priority. Use approved copy keys and a missing-copy list instead of invented claims. Check one meaningful h1, visible FAQ agreement with structured data, an eager hero image and reduced-motion behaviour. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Prepared inputs let iterations focus on design judgement rather than plumbing. A bounded loop can use screenshots at 375, 768 and 1440, axe in resting and active states, and a median of three Lighthouse runs. Example score targets of 90/95/95/90 are project budgets, not universal release criteria. Preserve exit codes and run one heavy job at a time when memory is constrained.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Independent review must inspect visual meaning beyond existing automated checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review diagram grouping, image cropping, text contrast and responsive composition independently of existing tests. In a hypothetical page, different breakpoints for content and imagery could leave an unsuitable crop at intermediate widths. Inspect open disclosures, meaningful edge endpoints, unrelated cluster crossings and decoration that could be mistaken for data. Capture sticky layouts at specified viewport sizes and scroll positions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Automated checks cover anticipated failures. Full-page captures can flatten sticky behavior, and measurements from closed controls cannot establish contrast in active states.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Retire review guidance that teaches generators to predict reviewer scores
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Remove active guidance that treats expected reviewer scores or score trajectories as evidence of quality. Preserve retired text for audit, mark it inactive and replace score-based advice with observable artifact requirements and reproducible checks. Also review copied guidance when a rule is superseded; retiring one copy does not repair every downstream skillbook. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Score-prediction advice encourages optimisation for a reviewer response rather than for the work. Historical reports can remain as records without continuing to influence generation. The useful lesson is the defect, its evidence and its fix, not how many points a particular reviewer once awarded.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reassess earlier advice and compare findings under consistent criteria
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review proposed fixes for regressions as carefully as the original implementation. For an invented museum website, expanding a disclosure may change an image crop, and lightening a text backing may weaken contrast. Record new evidence even when it challenges earlier advice. Track concrete findings and use comparable criteria for any score comparison. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Review is useful when it can correct its own assumptions. Current rendering checks and reproducible evidence are stronger than confidence inherited from an earlier report.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Probe viewport assumptions and measurement precision during final visual review
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Inspect short visible viewports, text scrim boundaries and measurement precision after broad checks pass. Account for browser chrome when judging initial headline visibility. Bound scrims to the text where practical. Do not infer subpixel precision from whole-pixel probes; improve the method or report uncertainty. Verify that assets and validation logs match the current build. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Final review often exposes assumptions in the checks. Describe remaining polish through observable defects, and avoid comparing scores produced by changing criteria.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Cap review loops and present unresolved visible defects as concrete decisions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Stop a design review loop at its agreed iteration cap and present a reviewable result with explicit remaining choices. A strong composite score below the stop threshold can still justify human review when required gates pass. Lead the brief with visible defects, such as a headline clipped at 412x700, and distinguish acceptance from one additional bounded repair round. Verify the preview contains the intended build and state whether production changed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Near-complete work can consume substantial additional effort without resolving subjective choices. A bounded handoff makes the remaining tradeoffs visible and prevents a score from becoming permission for endless iteration.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate measurable visual defects from art-direction decisions during review
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Split visual review findings into reproducible defects and choices that require a design decision. On a seed library's illustrated catalogue, measurable defects might include moving paths retracing permanent ones, a sticky heading wiping artwork, poor text contrast, unnecessary mobile asset downloads or keyboard focus scrolling the page unexpectedly. Record affected widths, scroll positions and rendering modes. Evaluate perceived motion separately: a layer may animate continuously yet look static during a 2-3 s glance. Show controlled alternatives when deciding pace or density. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Technical measurements can establish that geometry collides or assets are wasted, but they cannot decide the desired emotional intensity. Separating these questions lets builders fix objective failures while reviewers make informed visual choices instead of hiding both behind one composite score.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use an early credible preview to guide design effort
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Present a credible first-pass page early enough for visual feedback to influence the next iteration. For a neighbourhood bakery, a working preview of the menu, photography and ordering flow can reveal priorities that a specification leaves abstract. Keep essential technical checks in place, then focus refinement on the areas where viewing the page produces concrete feedback. Separate design acceptance from outstanding correctness defects and record minor polish in a backlog. Reuse successful components while evaluating their fit on each new page. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Review scores cannot fully predict how a page will feel when seen as a whole. An early preview gives decision-makers something concrete to respond to and helps avoid spending several rounds polishing details that do not determine the design.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reuse validated components and checks while making each new experiment deliberate
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Start a related page from validated components and acceptance criteria, then identify the small set of genuinely new behaviours. A tide-pool field guide can reuse its navigation, accordions, figure fallback and image treatment while introducing one new interactive species diagram. Deliver an early preview, write a generation report before the final check run, and preserve reproducible logs. Budget a core verification set, with deeper sweeps assigned according to risk; after a localized fix, rerun the core and affected checks rather than blindly repeating everything. Reuse prior results only when the tested artifact and conditions still match. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reuse reduces repeated decisions only when assumptions remain visible. Deliberate novelty concentrates review effort, while bounded verification and a written handoff prevent an interrupted build from leaving an unexplained preview and untraceable test claims.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reuse traceable test evidence while independently probing new failure modes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An independent review can reuse traceable test results while rerunning previous failures, a representative sample and checks for newly introduced risks. Bind reused evidence to the exact artifact, configuration and environment. Measure startup separately from steady-state frame cost: a smooth animation can still block scrolling while building its caches. Check deep-linked accordions for layout shifts and inspect whether their open-state icon is visibly different. Report shared-component defects separately from page-specific polish so a common fix reaches every consumer. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeating every check is not the only way to review thoroughly, but unqualified reuse can hide regressions. The strongest independent review validates evidence and explores missing dimensions instead of merely reproducing the generator's checklist or treating visual acceptance as proof of correctness.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review new lessons each iteration and update every affected workflow
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review newly learned web-delivery lessons after each iteration, then consolidate them when the work closes. When changing the review cadence, update every workflow that inherits it and clearly mark older instructions as superseded. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Early review can catch faulty checks before they shape later work. Updating only one guide leaves conflicting procedures, so shared workflow changes need the same careful propagation as shared code changes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Close design iterations with evidence while keeping unresolved release checks explicit
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Close a design iteration only after rerunning checks invalidated by its final edits, while tracking unresolved release checks separately. Useful evidence includes responsive label gates, no-JavaScript behavior, accessibility in resting and interactive states, content-security-policy checks and unchanged-mode comparisons. Include deliberately broken variants that the tests must reject. Recheck shared bundle budgets after integration. For CPU-throttled timing checks, use a quiet machine and a control case; a failing control makes attribution uncertain. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Design work can reach a satisfactory stopping point before deployment readiness is established. Separating those decisions avoids endless aesthetic iteration while preventing a strong review score from concealing missing hardware coverage, noisy measurements or integration work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Classify failures and inspect test changes before another visual iteration
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Separate suspected measurement faults, existing defects, marginal passes and newly introduced failures before revising a rendering. Compare questionable failures with an unchanged baseline and inspect changes to verification code. When correcting motion formulas, define the coordinate system and test the expected direction explicitly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A failed check may require repairing the measurement or the rendering. Unexplained test edits can weaken acceptance criteria, making apparent visual progress difficult to assess reliably.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify that a deliberately introduced defect reaches the active rendering path
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A mutation test proves nothing unless its injected defect actually changes the rendering path under test. If an application has multiple shader implementations, introduce the intended fault into the implementation selected by the test configuration and verify that the rendered output changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Editing an inactive shader can make a detector appear robust because the supposed broken case is still healthy. Check mutation activation separately from detector failure so a passing test cannot hide an inert experiment.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use an honest preview to obtain human direction when automated visual review stalls
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A bounded visual-review loop can hand an imperfect build to human preview once engineering checks pass and remaining defects are disclosed. Publish a separate preview, include the current assessment and unresolved issues, and retain the project's production approval boundary. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Another scoring round may provide less useful information than seeing the result on the intended hardware. Preview turns abstract disagreement into something reviewable while keeping a provisional visual assessment distinct from a production release decision.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate a new visual test against an unchanged failing build before editing the artwork
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Run a new visual regression test against an unchanged snapshot of the known failing build before applying the fix. Preserve the built assets, serve them as captured, and record viewport and rendering conditions. Then rerun the same test against the revised artifact. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] If the baseline changes while the test is being designed, a later pass cannot cleanly demonstrate improvement. Establishing the failure first provides evidence that the test detects the original defect under comparable conditions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Calibrate texture checks against accepted and defective examples
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before enforcing a texture threshold, test whether it accepts suitable artwork and rejects visible defects. For an invented garden centre illustration, include intentionally smooth regions, detailed foliage and unwanted speckling in the calibration set. Combine measurements with visual review of the intended style. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A numeric floor can reward noise while rejecting deliberate softness. A useful check measures defects without forcing every region to share the same texture.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Challenge a miscalibrated visual gate with evidence and a reversible comparison
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a visual gate rewards a worse artifact, document the disagreement and provide a reversible comparison before revising the gate. Show the measured result, the visible defect encouraged by the threshold, and the alternative that better matches the intended appearance. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Review criteria can be wrong, including criteria written by the reviewer. A declared deviation with evidence supports correction without hiding failure or silently lowering standards; the revised criterion still needs independent validation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: End capped review loops with the limiting quality dimension and unresolved defects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a review loop reaches its iteration cap, hand off the limiting quality dimension and a concrete defect list rather than only an aggregate score. Distinguish engineering readiness, interaction quality and visual judgment, then identify the next useful reviewer or test environment. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Improving scores can coexist with unresolved aesthetic problems. A bounded loop avoids endless refinement, while a clear handoff preserves uncertainty and lets a human decide whether further iteration, preview feedback or release is appropriate.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Calibrate numeric visual thresholds between an absent effect and an independently accepted example
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Numeric visual thresholds should be calibrated against both an absent-effect baseline and an independently accepted example before they become gates. A threshold selected by intuition can reject acceptable subtle motion simply because the measured signal is smaller than expected. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Numbers make a rule repeatable, but they do not establish that it measures the right thing. Confirm that the metric separates the intended cases, document what its units mean, and avoid treating an uncalibrated cutoff as objective quality.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate effect-presence tests from aesthetic-quality tests
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A test calibrated against the candidate itself can establish that an effect is present, but it cannot independently establish that the effect is good. Comparing absent lights with the candidate's measurable lights supports a presence check; claiming subtlety also needs an independently accepted reference and a limit on excessive intensity or motion. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Self-calibration can turn the current implementation into its own standard. Name the test according to what it proves so a successful presence check is not mistaken for aesthetic approval.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate work by file ownership and schedule heavy execution against available memory
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Separate git worktrees reduce editing conflicts, but they do not isolate CPU or memory consumption. Split work into tracks with clear file ownership and a shared task specification, then run only as many heavy generators or browser jobs as the host can support. Lightweight reviewers can inspect artifacts without launching additional browsers. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Parallel design work can remain useful even when heavy execution must be sequential. Independent tracks can ship once validated, but shared wrappers and metadata still require integration review because apparently unrelated changes may touch the same source line.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Publish machine-readable discovery only for capabilities the site actually provides
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Agent-readable websites need discoverable content and accurate capability metadata, not a collection of unsupported protocol files. Start with robots.txt, a sitemap, stable links, and accessible page content. Add Markdown representations, API catalogs, authentication metadata, or agent discovery documents only when corresponding services exist. The cited Cloudflare readiness framework covered these areas (as of April 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Scanner scores cannot establish interoperability. Validate content types, schemas, endpoints, and advertised permissions against the applicable protocol version. Make training and crawler permissions deliberate policy choices rather than enabling them merely to improve a score.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate OAuth resource identity and issuer reachability beyond a successful HTTP response
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] OAuth metadata can return HTTP 200 and valid JSON while describing the wrong resource. Check that the resource identifier matches the protected service being described and that metadata discovery follows the applicable specification. Confirm authorization-server identifiers against actual issuer metadata rather than guessing a hostname or copying a frontend API address. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A scanner may impose origin-matching checks, but passing those checks does not establish a functioning OAuth relationship. Test discovery and authentication together, and avoid publishing authentication claims solely for a readiness score.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Generate discovery artifacts from shared sources and test them after deployment
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain machine-readable website artifacts alongside the content and services they describe, then validate the deployed responses. Generate Markdown alternatives and any content digests from the same source as the site. Check advertised discovery links, content types, and callable interfaces; omit commerce or authentication protocols when no corresponding service exists. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A collection of individually valid files can still contradict itself. Shared generation reduces drift, while live checks catch middleware, routing, and header behavior that a successful static build cannot demonstrate.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Agent discovery documents must describe real protocol endpoints and return JSON
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An agent discovery document must describe an implemented protocol service and return the expected JSON content type. Check the current protocol version before selecting fields, interfaces, and capability declarations. Where a JSON discovery route is expected, verify that missing-file handling does not return an HTML page with HTTP 200. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A contact form or static skills index is not automatically an agent protocol endpoint. Publishing unsupported interfaces creates false expectations, and scanner-specific field checks should not replace validation against the actual protocol specification.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit agent discovery against real site capabilities rather than filling every metadata slot
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An agent-readiness audit should verify discoverability, content representations, access policy, and genuine integration capabilities separately. Check that robots.txt and sitemap references resolve, and that any advertised Markdown representation returns the promised content type. If the site exposes APIs, authentication, or agent skills, validate their discovery documents against the applicable specifications. One audit checklist included API catalogs, OAuth metadata, MCP descriptions, and skill indexes (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A structurally valid document can still advertise a nonexistent capability. Marketing sites should not invent authorization servers or tools to gain points. Validate behavior and authority as well as JSON shape, and distinguish optional conventions from established standards.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Publish OAuth metadata only for authorization relationships the site actually implements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Do not fabricate OAuth discovery documents merely to satisfy an agent-readiness score. A website using a third-party form service does not thereby become an OAuth-protected resource authorized by that service. Publish protected-resource and authorization-server metadata only when the described resource, issuer, endpoints, and scopes correspond to a real implementation. Otherwise omit the unsupported surface and explain that it does not apply. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Populated fields can pass structural checks while misleading agents about how to authenticate. False metadata is worse than an honestly missing feature because consumers may attempt unsupported flows or trust an unrelated issuer. Audit scores should measure working capabilities rather than reward plausible placeholders.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep skill discovery indexes, documents, and content digests synchronized
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Generate skill discovery metadata from the same documents that a site publishes, including digests computed from the final file bytes. A reported discovery format used an index with a schema identifier and entries containing name, type, description, URL, and SHA-256 digest, with one SKILL.md document per skill directory (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it). Validate the current consumer's schema and fetch every advertised URL during the build. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Migrating from flat descriptors to document-based discovery can leave valid-looking indexes pointing to missing files. Build-time generation prevents stale hashes and mismatched descriptions. Version-specific discovery conventions should not be presented as universal requirements for all agent systems.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat agent-readiness scans as capability inventories rather than universal implementation requirements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Agent-readiness checks should distinguish content discovery, access policy, authentication and actual callable capabilities. Inventory robots.txt, sitemaps, discovery links, Markdown representations, API catalogs and authentication metadata separately. Some scanners also inspect DNS-based discovery, bot authentication, agent cards and skill catalogs; scanner coverage is perishable (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it). Match every published document to an implemented service and validate its format against the relevant specification. Do not fabricate OAuth issuers, tool definitions or agent endpoints to satisfy a score. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A scanner taxonomy is useful for finding gaps, but it blends broadly useful web practices with specialized capabilities. Honest metadata helps automated consumers understand a site; unsupported declarations create false expectations.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate application fixes from DNS changes when auditing agent discovery
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Split agent-discovery findings into application-layer changes and DNS-layer changes before assigning remediation. Application work can include robots.txt, Markdown responses, Link headers and truthful service metadata. DNS work may require separate account access for discovery records and DNSSEC. Record the scanned hostname, failing check, supporting evidence and responsible role; fix applicable findings, deploy, and scan again. Scanner requirements are perishable (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it). Check that discovery records use the namespace expected for the scanned host and that authentication metadata names a real issuer when required by the implemented flow. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Clear ownership prevents an application deployment from being mistaken for a complete infrastructure fix. Mark unsupported capabilities as intentionally absent instead of inventing services to make every check pass.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Evaluate domain-hosted resource catalogs as discovery infrastructure, not guaranteed adoption
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A domain-hosted catalog can describe real agent resources so discovery services can find them without loading every capability into a model's context. A draft approach described publishing an ai-catalog.json manifest beneath /.well-known/ (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it). Verify the current specification, schema, and implementation support before adopting that path. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Searchable catalogs separate discovery from execution and can reduce unnecessary context. Organizational interest does not establish interoperability or future adoption; treat a draft as an experiment with validation and a removal plan.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use agent-readiness scores as diagnostic signals rather than proof of interoperability
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Inspect the individual checks behind an agent-readiness score before using it as a release gate.
