Relevant areas include crawl discovery, accessible content, bot controls, protocol metadata, and authentication documentation. Scanner coverage and weighting are vendor-dependent and change over time (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A local threshold such as 70 out of 100 can flag regressions, but it does not prove a site supports every advertised protocol. Preserve truthful metadata and test real consumers rather than adding fictional services to raise the score.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Generate discovery catalogs from maintained source metadata
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat a discovery catalog as a deterministic compiled view of actual capabilities rather than another hand-maintained inventory. Read existing service and skill metadata, normalize its shapes, and emit only resources that exist. Validate identifiers, required fields, mutually exclusive fields, and examples against the chosen schema version. Provide a --stdout mode that emits only JSON, with diagnostics on stderr. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Compilation reduces disagreement between discovery files. Representative queries should describe real operations; plausible text and nonempty placeholder entries cannot substitute for implemented capabilities.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Unify shared generators while proving unchanged inputs preserve existing output
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain one canonical implementation of a shared metadata generator and verify compatibility before distributing it. Normalize supported input shapes, document precedence between alternative source fields, and exclude discovery artifacts that are not executable APIs. For unaffected fixtures, require regenerated output to match the existing artifact byte for byte. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Multiple nearly identical copies make fixes difficult to track. Compatibility checks let hardening reach additional sites without introducing unrelated output changes, while a shared package or helper can reduce future duplication when its maintenance cost is justified.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Publish truthful authentication metadata and keep signing keys private
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe public anonymous access honestly instead of inventing OAuth infrastructure to satisfy a scanner. Publish OAuth metadata only when the corresponding roles and endpoints exist. For an implemented signature protocol, generate a separate Ed25519 key pair for each site, publish only its public JWK, and derive a thumbprint using RFC 7638 canonicalization. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Discovery metadata is a contract consumers may act on. A published key alone does not implement authentication. Keep private keys in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat, with restrictive permissions and a rotation plan.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate OAuth metadata against protocol semantics before satisfying scanner heuristics
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] OAuth protected-resource metadata must identify real authorization servers using issuer identifiers, not arbitrary metadata-document URLs. Do not populate authorization_servers merely to make a scanner's presence check pass, and do not declare a public resource protected when it is not. Document anonymous access separately when that is the actual behavior. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A lenient scanner can reward a structurally populated field while missing a semantic error. The reliable acceptance test is whether a conforming consumer can discover and use the declared authentication arrangement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Configure authentication-document headers through the mechanism the deployment actually serves
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Serve a Markdown authentication guide with the intended Content-Type and cache policy, then verify the deployed response. Vercel uses header rules in vercel.json, while supported Cloudflare static-asset deployments use a _headers file in the published assets (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it). Runtime-generated responses may need headers set in code. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A configuration file that works on one platform may do nothing on another. Keep Markdown rules separate from JSON metadata rules, and inspect live headers to catch precedence conflicts or files omitted from the build.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Declare an OAuth server only when it authorizes access to the advertised resource
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A marketing site must not advertise a third-party OAuth server unless that server actually authorizes access to the site's advertised resources. A form submission to a CRM or authentication for a separate application does not establish that relationship. Remove false declarations and explain the real access model; do not replace them with a fictional self-issued OAuth service. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Consumers use authentication metadata to decide where to obtain credentials and how to access resources. Honest omission is more interoperable than a scanner-friendly declaration that cannot work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Scope interactive startup notices so they cannot contaminate automated outputs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Global agent instructions should restrict interactive startup notices to the main interactive session. An automated or delegated task may inherit the instruction without receiving the session hook that satisfies it, causing an irrelevant notice to appear in its output. Define explicit exemptions for those contexts and test the instruction with a strict JSON-only task. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A diagnostic message that is harmless in conversation can corrupt machine-consumed output or become published copy. The fix belongs in instruction scope, rather than relying on downstream consumers to strip unexpected prose.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat repeated unsolicited agent notices as an instruction-scope defect
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When independent automated runs repeatedly prepend the same irrelevant notice, inspect shared instructions before changing individual task prompts. Reproduce the behavior with a minimal task, identify the condition that automated runs cannot satisfy, and scope the notice to interactive sessions. Validate the fix with both prose and structured-output tasks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repetition across tasks points to inherited context rather than isolated model behavior. A downstream parser workaround leaves the instruction conflict intact and can fail again when another consumer expects an exact schema or publishes the response directly.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Remove hardcoded audiences and stale year ranges from reusable research prompts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reusable research prompts should derive audience context from configuration and time windows from the current clock. Audit prompt templates for profession-specific framing, inherited examples and fixed years before distributing a general tool. Where no audience profile is available, use neutral instructions instead of silently assuming one. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Hidden prompt defaults can steer every result toward the original builder's interests while appearing personalized. Reviewing implementation alongside public descriptions catches this mismatch and prevents documentation from promising generality that the underlying behavior does not yet provide.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Publish API catalogs using the standard linkset structure rather than custom endpoint JSON
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A standards-based API catalog uses a linkset representation instead of an arbitrary endpoints array. Follow RFC 9727's API catalog profile and RFC 9264's JSON linkset structure, including the top-level linkset array and applicable link relations. Serve the catalog with application/linkset+json and the appropriate profile parameter. Include descriptions and documentation that actually describe the APIs, and verify both the response header and body against the specification. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Human-readable JSON can still be unusable to a standards-aware client. Schema validation catches structural omissions, while semantic review prevents nominally valid links from pointing to unrelated summaries or nonexistent services.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Markdown negotiation must return a real representation of the requested page
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Advertising a Markdown alternate does not implement HTTP content negotiation. For eligible page requests, parse Accept preferences and q-values, honor exclusions such as q=0, and return the corresponding Markdown representation with Content-Type: text/markdown when selected. Set Vary: Accept so caches distinguish representations. Test direct requests, HTML defaults, missing alternates and unsupported routes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A Link header helps discovery but cannot satisfy a request for another representation. Returning a generic site summary under every page URL may pass a superficial content-type check while losing the requested information; preserve page identity rather than merely changing the response label.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep experimental discovery-protocol checks advisory until their contract is stable
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Integrate emerging discovery-protocol validation as an advisory CI check until its requirements and operational value are established. Pin the validator and schema version, validate manifest structure, and probe advertised endpoints separately. Distinguish mandatory failures from unsupported optional features, and preserve machine-readable results with meaningful exit codes. Verify the current specification before copying field names or endpoint assumptions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Experimental conformance tools can expose useful problems without being mature enough to block every release. Separating protocol validity, endpoint behavior, and broader site readiness prevents a changing external score or draft schema from becoming an unexplained production gate.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Monitor authoritative protocol changes and act on verified differences
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain a versioned watchlist of primary sources for agent discovery, authentication, and machine-readable website interfaces. Include official specifications, schema repositories, release notes, and platform changelogs. Record the last reviewed version and compare new material against that baseline before changing a build. Separate adopted requirements from exploratory proposals and document which deployments are affected. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fast-moving guidance can become stale between projects, while blindly following every new proposal creates unnecessary churn. A delta-based review focuses effort on changes that alter an existing contract and provides evidence for why an implementation was updated or deliberately left alone.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Generate discovery catalogs from authoritative artifacts and test for regeneration drift
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat a discovery catalog as a generated projection of authoritative capability metadata rather than a second hand-maintained registry. Read the source artifacts without modifying them, normalize their relevant fields, and emit deterministic output. In CI, regenerate the catalog and compare it with the committed version; unexpected differences should trigger review. Make ordering and formatting stable so the diff reflects real changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Two manually maintained descriptions of the same capabilities eventually disagree. Generation reduces duplicate maintenance, while an empty regeneration diff demonstrates reproducibility from the current sources; separate checks are still needed to prove those sources describe working endpoints.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Derive catalog identity from validated source metadata and fail without partial output
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A portable catalog generator should derive the site's origin and organization from validated source metadata instead of hardcoding host strings. Parse the source URL, validate required identity fields, and stop with a clear diagnostic and nonzero exit status if they are missing or invalid. Emit no partial catalog on failure. Test the generator against unrelated sample sites before reusing it broadly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Hardcoded origins can silently publish another site's identity after copying a script. Fail-fast validation turns missing configuration into an obvious build problem and keeps incomplete output from being mistaken for a valid public discovery document.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Advertise only real capabilities and test both omission and inclusion behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A capability catalog should omit entries with no usable capabilities and include valid entries when capabilities are present. For a catalog derived from MCP-related metadata, inspect the actual supported tools, resources, or prompts according to the selected schema rather than hardcoding a blanket inclusion or exclusion. Log skipped entries and test both empty and populated cases. Verify endpoint behavior separately from metadata. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An advertised but unusable service wastes callers' effort and weakens trust. A bidirectional check also catches the opposite defect: silently hiding a functioning service because an earlier workaround permanently excluded its category.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Publish only verifiable identity and trust claims in discovery catalogs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Omit optional trust attestations when there is no evidence to support them. A schema accepting a trustManifest field does not establish certification, compliance, or workload identity. If using did:web, configure an actual resolvable DID document under a domain you control; a domain-shaped string alone is insufficient. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Discovery metadata becomes input to automated trust decisions. An absent optional claim communicates uncertainty honestly, while fabricated assurance can cause another system to grant access or confidence it should withhold.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Back every catalog capability with a real artifact or callable endpoint
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Every discovery catalog entry must correspond to a real artifact or callable endpoint. Derive capability identifiers from the source index, associate skill records with actual indexed artifacts and digests, and verify that advertised URLs resolve to their intended resources. Exclude capabilities that exist only in descriptive copy. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A catalog is an executable promise to another system. Filling gaps with plausible capabilities creates failed calls and makes an otherwise useful discovery surface unreliable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use consistent domain-scoped identifiers and validate against the target schema
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Scope catalog identifiers to a controlled domain and use consistent resource-kind segments. Where the target schema specifies it, validate identifiers shaped like urn:ai:<domain>:<kind>:<name> against ^urn:ai:[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+(:[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+)+$. Keep agent, skill, api, and mcp naming consistent, and check namespace requirements separately from this local regex. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Predictable names reduce collisions and simplify deduplication across sites. A regex checks syntax; it does not establish namespace registration, ownership, or global uniqueness by itself.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Expose discovery catalogs through the transports supported by intended clients
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Publish a discovery catalog through multiple supported discovery surfaces rather than assuming every client parses HTML. An experimental integration can expose /.well-known/ai-catalog.json, a robots.txt Agentmap directive, an HTML link with rel="ai-catalog", and an HTTP Link header with the same relation. Serve the file as application/json with deliberate caching. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Crawlers, HTTP clients, and DOM readers follow different discovery paths. These conventions require client support, so test the actual consumers instead of treating publication as proof of interoperability.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Gate discovery links consistently while treating authentication as a separate control
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Apply the same public-discovery policy to catalog links and neighboring metadata links. If a layout suppresses discovery on noindex pages, place the ai-catalog link inside that conditional alongside existing api-catalog, describedby, or service-doc links. Preserve those existing links when adding another format. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Consistent gating avoids accidental advertising of internal surfaces. However, noindex is an indexing directive rather than access control: protect private catalogs and endpoints with authorization regardless of whether a page links to them.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe endpoint invocation explicitly instead of presenting POST URLs as artifact downloads
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Distinguish a retrievable artifact URL from an endpoint that requires an invocation method and payload. In catalogs supporting embedded data or references, embed an endpoint description when the URL field means a GET-able artifact. Include the method, request shape, authentication requirements, and supported media type, and enforce exactly one of url or data when required by the schema. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A bare URL leaves consumers guessing whether to fetch documentation or execute an operation. Explicit semantics prevent failed requests and accidental method assumptions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Generate representative queries from real examples and improve them at the source
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Derive representative queries from actual capability examples rather than inventing unsupported intents. For a catalog configured for 2–5 queries per entry, prefer source-card examples, then use clean templates based on a display name and meaningful tags. Avoid truncated-description fragments and internal API jargon. Improve weak examples in the source metadata and regenerate the catalog. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These queries guide retrieval toward capabilities users can actually invoke. Source-level improvements preserve consistency and prevent hand-edited generated files from drifting.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Integrate discovery features into both first-build guidance and ongoing maintenance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A new discovery feature needs build integration, verification guidance, and a maintenance path. Document source-generation order, catalog publication, response headers, and layout discovery links together. Check relevant specification versions before implementation, record meaningful changes, and define when advisory checks become release requirements. Include a handoff for updating existing sites. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful one-off implementation does not improve future builds automatically. Updating reusable instructions and maintenance responsibilities prevents older sites and newly created sites from silently diverging.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Normalize documented source variants before deriving a catalog origin
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Handle known source-schema variants explicitly when deriving a discovery catalog's origin. A documented compatibility chain might inspect agentCard.url, agentCard.endpoint, then agentCard.provider?.url. Validate candidate URLs and confirm that each field represents the intended service origin; a provider's website may describe a different entity. If none qualifies, omit the affected entry and explain why. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Normalization enables shared generators across heterogeneous sites, but blindly accepting any available URL can turn schema compatibility into incorrect attribution.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Normalize string and object capability lists before generating metadata
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Normalize capability inputs before mapping identifiers into a catalog. For sources accepting strings or objects, convert strings with typeof s === 'string' ? {id:s} : s, then validate objects and filter invalid identifiers. Omit an optional capabilities field when no valid identifiers remain. Prefer a real displayName over a slug for human-facing text. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Mapping s.id over string inputs can serialize undefined values as null array entries. Explicit normalization prevents plausible-looking but unusable metadata on sites with different source shapes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Classify API capabilities by documented behavior rather than catalog membership alone
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Advertise an API operation only when its callable behavior is documented and verified. Discovery documents such as sitemaps, skill indexes, and server cards should retain their document semantics instead of being labeled as POST endpoints. Use paths as classification hints, then confirm methods and request contracts; a path prefix alone cannot prove or disprove an API. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Misclassification invites agents to invoke static documents and duplicates existing discovery entries. Accurate operation metadata prevents a catalog from promising behavior that its resources cannot provide.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe actual authentication behavior and update reusable guidance after correcting it
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Authentication discovery documents must describe the access controls a site actually uses. State which resources are public and document genuine authentication requirements for protected operations; do not declare an unrelated identity provider as the site's authorization server. When correcting a misleading template, update both existing outputs and the instructions used for future builds. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Invented authentication metadata sends agents toward unusable flows and creates false expectations about protection. Fixing the reusable source prevents the same error from returning in the next project.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve a static fallback that survives failure of the script responsible for enhancement
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A usable fallback instruction must exist in static HTML even when JavaScript is enabled but the enhancement script fails to load. Store the authoritative command in a data attribute and retain a visible survival copy in the results pane. When initialization succeeds, reconcile the visible copy with the authoritative value. Test script-load failure separately from JavaScript being disabled: noscript does not cover both cases. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Removing duplicate text can remove the only working instruction in a failure branch. Judge duplication against the availability invariant it protects, rather than assuming every repeated string is unnecessary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define clear input and output contracts for each search method
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give different search methods explicit input requirements and validate each independently. In an invented garden centre catalogue, keyword search and photo-based lookup should specify accepted inputs, result limits and understandable matching information. Return usable item links and distinguish an estimated match from a confirmed identification. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Different inputs produce different failure modes. Clear contracts help callers handle results correctly without depending on hidden implementation details.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distinguish unavailable search from a completed search with no matches
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Report a failed or unavailable search separately from a successful search that returns no matches. For an invented museum catalogue, service interruptions and invalid requests should produce explicit statuses with suitable retry guidance. Show a no-results message only after the search has completed successfully. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An empty result should not conceal an operational failure. Clear statuses prevent readers and automated callers from treating a broken search as evidence that an item does not exist.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make exported text self-contained and correct facts at the source
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Include necessary scope and availability information in text that may be read independently. An exported programme from an invented museum should carry relevant dates and booking conditions without relying on the website footer. Correct inconsistent facts in the maintained source, then regenerate and check dependent versions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Exported content loses surrounding context. Shared source corrections prevent different formats from publishing conflicting versions of the same fact.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Label feature availability according to verified user access
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Distinguish implementation status, required configuration and demonstrated user access when describing a feature. For an invented swim school booking site, verify whether online cancellation works for the advertised users and identify any prerequisites. Label planned, limited and available features accurately beside the relevant claim. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The existence of code does not establish that a reader can use a feature. Precise availability wording prevents implementation intent from becoming an unsupported promise.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check dependency behaviour before claiming offline support
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Offline verification must include dependencies that fetch assets or contact services automatically. For an invented museum guide, test startup and visitor actions with network access blocked, including conditions where previously downloaded resources are absent. Describe any required preparation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Application code can contain no direct network requests while a dependency still makes them. Observed behaviour and explicit prerequisites provide stronger evidence than a source-text search alone.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: State network restrictions with their exceptions and evidence limits
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe a network restriction together with its scope, permitted connections and verification status. For an invented swim school booking service, explain any payment-service exception beside the restriction. Distinguish configured access from a connection verified in testing, and describe future controls as planned. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Broad claims become misleading when necessary exceptions are omitted. Nearby qualifications help readers understand both the policy and the strength of its supporting evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe submitted data from the actual request payload
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check the fields actually transmitted before describing what a web form sends. For an invented garden centre enquiry form, account for the message, contact details and any automatically included page information. Update inaccurate disclosures and assess unnecessary fields separately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Interface labels and design notes may omit data added during request construction. Accurate descriptions depend on the implemented payload.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify service location separately from enabled features
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat where a service runs and what it can do as separate properties. For an invented museum website, disabling external content discovery does not establish that its booking service runs on the same server. Verify destinations and feature settings independently before describing deployment or data handling. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A feature toggle cannot prove a network boundary. Precise descriptions prevent convenient labels from becoming unsupported guarantees.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify fallback behaviour stage by stage instead of promising a universal fallback
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check each pipeline stage independently before claiming that unavailable model features fall back to simpler rules. Build a table for configured, unconfigured, failed and capability-limited backends. Record whether each stage completes deterministically, retries, skips, errors or produces no result. Inspect exception handling and actual outputs rather than assuming the whole pipeline shares one fallback. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Model-independent maintenance can continue while generative or web-dependent stages stop entirely. A blanket fallback sentence conceals that distinction and promises continuity the implementation may not provide.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Publish truthful capability metadata even when a readiness scanner rewards unsupported claims
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Agent-readiness metadata should describe implemented capabilities rather than satisfy every scanner check. Publish discovery documents only when their resources and protocols exist; do not invent authentication scopes, token protection, or an MCP server to improve a score. Classify failures as missing implementation, incorrect metadata, or genuinely inapplicable. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A high score obtained through false declarations makes automated clients less reliable. Pair discovery checks with accessibility, links, and actual form rejection tests so metadata quality remains connected to observable site behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Do not invent authentication infrastructure to satisfy a scanner
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Agent-readiness documentation should describe real capabilities, even when an inapplicable scanner check remains red. For a public site without accounts, protected APIs or MCP services, do not advertise registration endpoints, credential issuance or servers that do not exist. Inspect the scanner's current criteria and distinguish missing implementation from an unsupported feature. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Adding misleading metadata improves a score while making discovery less trustworthy. Building a real authentication service solely for a score introduces operational and abuse-management obligations that may have no connection to the site's purpose.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Machine discoverability does not prove that a scroll story's meaning survives text extraction
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Agent-readiness checks should distinguish discovering a page from recovering the meaning of its scroll-driven content. A crawler or Markdown consumer has no human scroll gesture to advance video currentTime. Verify that essential claims, sequence and links remain available in semantic HTML or a text representation independent of animation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Machine-facing discovery endpoints can work while the central explanation remains trapped in motion. This is a risk to test, not proof that every scroll story fails extraction. Compare the extracted content with the intended narrative and add explicit text where visual transitions carry indispensable meaning.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use static rendering by default and add interactive islands only where needed
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build content pages statically and reserve client-side framework islands for features that require interaction. For a ceramic studio, workshop descriptions can remain static while an audio demonstration player becomes an interactive island. Tailwind CSS v4 uses the @tailwindcss/vite integration in this stack (as of March 2026; re-check before relying on it). An 8px spacing grid and 1.25 type ratio are useful starting constraints. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separating content delivery from interaction keeps JavaScript purposeful, while shared spacing and type rules reduce visual inconsistency.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Move branding into configuration and let SVGs inherit semantic colors
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reusable website templates should read branding from configuration rather than hardcoded component values. Use a shared site-name field in navigation and footers, currentColor in SVG strokes, and semantic CSS variables for theme colors. Configure site URLs and contact settings separately for each environment; validate required settings instead of silently falling back to another site's values. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Central configuration prevents partial rebranding and misdirected form submissions. A canonical template also reduces drift between independently maintained copies.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify template portability with placeholder scans and a clean build
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A standalone website template needs both a successful build and a complete customization checklist. Use recognizable placeholders for required substitutions, then scan source files and generated output for unresolved placeholders and residual branding. Test the template with an unrelated example, such as a seed library, and configure its domain independently. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Compilation proves that code can build; it does not prove that contact destinations, metadata, links, and deployment settings are ready for someone else's installation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Upgrade the existing site before combining framework migration with a redesign
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Establish a working framework upgrade on the existing design before beginning a substantial visual redesign. Inspect resolved dependency versions, integration compatibility, runtime requirements, and official migration guides for each crossed major version. Distinguish a static Astro build from server rendering and separately deployed hosting functions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Moving infrastructure and design together makes failures harder to attribute. A green baseline narrows the cause of later regressions, while recording actual package metadata avoids relying on stale memories of which release is current.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate content, styles, and generated assets after a framework migration
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful framework migration must verify the site's content pipeline and generated assets as well as the build exit code. Follow the target release's content-configuration conventions, remove superseded configuration, and check collection discovery, rendered pages, sitemap output, and any Markdown generation. Inspect styling integration before introducing a fallback. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A clean build can still omit content or conceal visual regressions. Keep the existing design during migration so changes remain attributable, and distinguish genuinely empty collections from unexpected discovery failures instead of dismissing every warning.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Adapt scaffold patterns while explicitly configuring routing, headers and dependency boundaries
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build a new scaffold from reviewed patterns rather than copying an existing site's content, integrations and credentials. Pin tested dependency versions, record the runtime, and check type-checking compatibility independently of transpilation. For an Astro site on Cloudflare Workers, explicitly configure the intended account, asset routing, preview behavior and headers. Route only requests needing application logic through the Worker and verify static assets separately. Inspect the installed Wrangler schema before depending on routing options. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Hidden integrations and ambient secrets travel easily with copied scaffolds. Install scripts should receive only necessary environment variables, with secrets kept in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. Explicit routing also prevents redirects or content negotiation from being bypassed by asset handling.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Derive published facts from registered sources and reject ambiguous build environments
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain a fact registry that records each published value, its source and its derivation. Retire obsolete keys explicitly, fail on unresolved required facts and exempt only registered values from prose-specific lint rules. If source data is unavailable to hosted CI, derive and validate the public artifact locally before building. Configure deployment checks against your own intended account, keeping secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Loose placeholders and ambient shell configuration let stale facts or the wrong deployment context survive otherwise successful builds. Explicit sources and environment checks make those failures visible.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Pair Astro builds with static checks and browser runtime probes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful Astro build does not establish that client-side TypeScript runs correctly in the browser. Add an appropriate static check, such as astro check or tsc --noEmit, and visit every changed page with Playwright. Register pageerror listeners before navigation, report console errors, and exercise the interaction that starts each client layer. Save the results with the build evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Transpilation can leave an undefined identifier that throws only when the page runs. A failed animation may leave its poster visible, making the page look plausible while later visual tests report only missing samples. An early runtime probe exposes the cause before expensive visual checks obscure it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Refactor scroll journeys into data while preserving measurable behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A reusable scroll-journey component should take explicit stop data, hold durations, assets and optional behaviors. Derive passage count from the number of stops, and enable special transitions only where their required elements exist. During the refactor, compare text positions, track length and navigation behavior against the baseline at identical viewport settings. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared markup reduces duplication, but hidden page assumptions can spread regressions to every consumer. Geometry comparisons provide useful evidence without claiming to establish complete visual equivalence. Inspect emitted HTML too: a presence-style data attribute rendered as an empty string can behave differently from a literal true value when selectors or tests compare exact values.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review a complete page prototype before extracting reusable Astro components
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] For visually uncertain Astro pages, prototype the complete page before decomposing it into components. Align the content and messaging, produce standalone HTML with embedded CSS, and inspect it with Playwright at widths of 1440, 768, and 375px. Obtain design feedback, resolve review findings, and then extract shared layouts and components. Compare the resulting Astro page against the approved prototype. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reviewing a complete composition makes hierarchy, spacing, and copy problems visible before abstractions make them expensive to change. This is useful for exploratory designs rather than a mandatory replacement for established components.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Place page-specific scripts within the layout's intended document structure
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Put page-specific Astro scripts inside the layout slot or another explicit insertion point within the HTML document. A script written after the closing layout component can appear outside the document structure when the layout emits the complete document. Inspect generated HTML to confirm placement. Astro processes component styles separately, so style-tag behavior does not establish where scripts belong. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Browsers may repair malformed markup and make the page seem functional, hiding a structural defect. Correct placement keeps the generated document predictable and simplifies debugging.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate review workspaces and standalone previews from deployable site output
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep iterative review artifacts and standalone design previews outside the site's generated deployment directory. Define a documented location for each, using relative paths suitable for any checkout. Configure the build so only intended public assets reach the deployment output. Retain enough context to connect a preview with its source version. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Mixing review reports, temporary HTML, and production files creates accidental publication risks and makes cleanup harder. A clear boundary also prevents rebuilds from deleting useful review evidence or stale previews from masquerading as current output.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Generate portable previews that remain readable without scripts or network access
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build standalone HTML previews with embedded styles, visible content, and no analytics or unnecessary external scripts. Override reveal animations so content does not remain hidden when JavaScript is absent. Provide dependable font fallbacks; package fonts locally when offline fidelity matters. Regenerate every affected preview when navigation or shared components change. A script can combine built HTML and CSS consistently. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A preview should expose the design immediately and reliably. External dependencies, stale shared components, and hidden animation states can cause reviewers to judge an incomplete or misleading representation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Randomize related resources in the browser when recommendations must vary between visits
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Random selection during an Astro static build stays fixed until the next build, so visit-level variation requires browser execution or a runtime response. Fetch 8–12 relevant candidates and render three useful initial cards, keeping the remaining candidates hidden. On page initialization, use Fisher–Yates to choose three from the pool. Scope initialization to each component and handle client navigation or restored pages if those count as new visits. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This preserves a useful no-JavaScript experience while varying recommendations. Relevance filtering must precede randomization, and random draws can repeat; guaranteed novelty requires remembering prior selections. Do not assume every crawler ignores JavaScript or sees only the initial three cards.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Generate catalogs after their inputs and before the static build consumes them
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Order generated discovery artifacts after their source generators and before the site build. Generate digests first, compile the catalog next, then run the static build that copies it into deployable output. Provide a standalone command such as build:ai-catalog for inspection, and use consistent logging, path resolution, and error handling across scripts. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Incorrect ordering can publish stale digests or omit a catalog entirely. Explicit dependencies make the build reproducible and let developers diagnose generation without rebuilding unrelated assets.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify build artifacts and rendered metadata according to the active adapter
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Derive artifact checks from the project's active build adapter rather than assuming one output directory. Inspect generated output to locate static discovery files; server builds may separate client assets from server bundles. For dynamically rendered pages, request the rendered route and inspect its HTML for discovery links instead of searching for a nonexistent prerendered file. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A correct deployment can fail a verification script that assumes static output everywhere. Adapter-aware checks distinguish missing artifacts from artifacts located or rendered differently.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit Astro upgrades for compiler, whitespace, integration, and output changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat an Astro major upgrade as a compatibility audit rather than a dependency-only edit. Verify the actual target release and its official migration guide, then inspect runtime requirements, compiler strictness, inline whitespace, Markdown processing, removed APIs, reserved filenames, and adapter behavior. Test invalid nesting, adjacent inline elements, CSS serialization, and rendered output with focused fixtures. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Plausible release summaries can contain unverified or future-version claims. Checking the installed release and observable behavior avoids baking an unreliable version narrative into a reusable migration plan.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use browser-hosted Python for static-site computation without exposing server secrets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Pyodide can execute Python inside a browser tab, allowing a static page to provide computation without a server-side execution endpoint. Connect semantic inputs, a run button, and a results area through a JavaScript controller; consider a worker for computation that could block the interface. Measure download size and loading behavior for the pinned runtime rather than assuming a fixed payload or cache lifetime. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Browser execution simplifies hosting, but client code cannot safely hold private credentials. Network access still follows browser and API rules; protected services need appropriate authentication and, when necessary, a backend.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep injected widget markup declarative and initialize behavior through separately loaded scripts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Widgets embedded through HTML injection should keep behavior in a separately loaded script and expose configuration through data attributes. Scripts inserted through innerHTML do not execute, so an inline script bundled inside an injected fragment is an unreliable initialization mechanism. Distinguish runtime DOM injection from Astro's build-time HTML rendering instead of assuming they have identical execution behavior. Initialize widgets explicitly when their markup becomes available. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separating markup from behavior makes widgets easier to reuse across CMS fragments, MDX and static pages. Script inertness is not sanitization: untrusted HTML still requires appropriate sanitization, and text values require contextual escaping.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make widget discovery repeatable when navigation or lazy loading can introduce new markup
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A single DOMContentLoaded scan misses widgets inserted after initial page parsing. Modal creation, client-side navigation, framework rendering and lazy CMS loading can all introduce eligible markup later. Expose an idempotent rescan function, invoke initialization from the relevant lifecycle event, or observe a narrowly scoped container with MutationObserver. Track adopted elements so repeated discovery cannot attach duplicate handlers; clean up listeners when components are removed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An undiscovered widget often produces no exception and simply remains inert. Explicit lifecycle support prevents a static-page implementation from silently failing when reused in a dynamic site.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify CMS identity and dataset visibility before deciding which build credentials are necessary
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify CMS authentication, project identity and dataset visibility separately before connecting a website build. Run read-only checks from a clean environment and compare the returned project with your intended configuration. Sanity public datasets can support published-content reads without a build read token, while draft access requires appropriate authentication (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Keep any required secret in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful login alone does not prove that a build targets the correct project or exposes only intended content.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Generate deterministic figure data from structural specs and rendered registry text
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep figure structure separate from wording, then generate layout data from registry keys and their fully rendered text. Reject missing keys, include expanded text when measuring labels, and store a source-spec hash with the wide and compact layouts. Provide a --check mode that fails when committed output differs from newly generated output. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Structural specs remain small and reviewable, wording retains its editorial controls, and generated coordinates become deterministic diffs. Drift checks catch stale figures after either content or layout logic changes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate data attributes used as state flags from structural selector hooks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] JavaScript dataset properties can accidentally create attributes already used as structural hooks. Setting root.dataset.figLive creates data-fig-live; if a descendant live region uses the same attribute, a document-wide selector may return the root instead. Use distinct state names such as data-fig-ready and scope queries to the component. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Camel-case conversion hides the collision during review because the JavaScript and markup look different. Search both forms and verify actual consumers before claiming that tests, CSS or other code are affected.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Astro elements created at runtime need styles that do not depend on missing scope attributes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Elements created with document.createElement do not automatically receive Astro's build-time component scope attribute. Style progressively enhanced children through a scoped parent and a global child selector, such as .legend :global(.legend-button), or use a suitable global stylesheet. Measure target size and inspect keyboard focus after insertion. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A generated button can look plausible while missing its reset, padding and focus treatment. In a reproduced case, controls measured 39 px instead of the intended 44 px. A geometry check exposed a defect that screenshots and an automated accessibility scan missed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make portrait art direction a reusable image-component capability
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A reusable image component should accept distinct portrait and landscape sources when their compositions differ. In Astro, construct a picture element with media-qualified portrait AVIF and WebP sources before landscape sources, followed by an img fallback. An example breakpoint is 47.9375rem, but the consuming content should determine it. Request portrait widths such as 480, 720 and 960 while capping outputs at the source width; an 896x1200 source must not be upscaled to 960. Include intrinsic dimensions, alt text and appropriate loading and fetch priority. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Centralising art direction prevents each page from inventing its own crop workaround. Expose object-position as a component option, retain asset provenance and inspect representative widths such as 390 and 1440. Separate compositions preserve meaningful detail that a landscape cover-crop can discard.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Exempt only supplied text from editorial rules while keeping the entire page under validation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Imported content should receive narrow editorial exemptions rather than exemption from every page check. In an Astro site for a bicycle-repair co-op, place externally supplied instructions inside a marked content container while the shared layout, links, accessibility, metadata, and routes remain fully validated. Generate fragments from canonical sources and record a source checksum. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Whole-route exemptions allow stale content and broken integration to accumulate. A build that detects source-checksum drift exposes forgotten regeneration. When replacing standalone files, also test old direct links and downloads so the improved page architecture preserves existing entry points.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify build-time artwork selection in emitted files
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A build-time artwork switch must exclude inactive variants from the emitted asset graph, not merely hide them in the page. Resolve a selected variant through configuration and explicit imports or narrowly scoped aliases, then inspect the output directory for both selected and excluded assets. Broad eager or lazy globs can still include unwanted files depending on the asset pipeline. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A visually correct page can silently ship both collections. An output census establishes whether the switch actually controls delivery rather than only choosing what the visitor sees.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use explicit generated imports when aliased globs silently miss variant assets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] If an aliased import glob silently returns no assets, generate a virtual module with explicit imports and assert the expected asset keys. A reported Vite 8 native import-glob configuration failed for some regex-alias prefixes while direct imports resolved (as of October 2026; re-check before relying on it). Reproduce the issue in the project's exact toolchain before adopting the workaround. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An empty glob can still produce a successful build while omitting the intended figure. Explicit imports and completeness checks turn a silent content failure into a diagnosable build error.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Align page entry points with the build tool's dependency accounting
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Inspect how a build-budget checker attributes shared code and dynamic imports before reorganizing bundles. For an invented museum website, a page-specific gallery effect may need its own entry point to keep ownership explicit. Verify the resulting dependency graph and compressed outputs. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Deferred loading and budget attribution answer different questions. Separate entries can clarify which pages depend on an optional feature, but the actual build must confirm the result.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Render repeated interaction hints through a shared Astro component
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Put repeated interaction hints in a shared Astro component so every relevant figure receives the same affordance. Keep the component responsible for consistent markup and presentation, then verify its presence across the pages and viewport sizes that use it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Copying hints into individual scenes makes omissions and styling drift easy. A shared component turns a repeated interface requirement into one maintainable implementation while leaving scene-specific visual effects independently adjustable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Pair Astro builds with type checks and browser runtime-error checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful astro build alone does not establish that client code is type-correct or free of runtime exceptions. Run the project's type-check command and collect Playwright pageerror events before expensive visual checks, exercising the relevant device-dependent paths. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A missing helper can leave an effect silently absent while the build succeeds. Catching the exception first distinguishes broken execution from a visual detector that reports no samples or insufficient motion.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Pair Astro builds with type checks and browser runtime error checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful Astro build does not establish that application code passes type checking or runs without browser errors. A missing helper can survive the build and prevent an interaction from executing. Run a separate type-checking step and capture browser page errors before starting visual assertions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A screenshot can look plausible even when the code responsible for its interactive layer never ran. Checking runtime health first prevents visual tests from evaluating a broken or incomplete execution as though it were the intended design.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prototype workflows should include customization, verification, setup, and teardown
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A reusable website prototype workflow must cover customization, account setup, review, and eventual teardown. Maintain a checklist for branding, content, navigation, forms, domains, and environment configuration. Identify which infrastructure is shared and which resources belong exclusively to each prototype. Define observable acceptance checks before generation, then document how to remove temporary deployments and credentials. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A template that produces attractive pages but leaves setup or cleanup implicit transfers hidden operational work to its next user.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use a routing guide to connect specialized workflows without duplicating them
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give a multi-tool automation system a routing guide that maps user intentions to the responsible workflow and its entry command. Include a surface inventory, decision tree, common end-to-end examples, composition rules, startup checks, and explicit limits. Separate content production from infrastructure coordination: one workflow creates assets, while another handles distribution, approvals, and operational documentation. Link the guide from a discoverable documentation index. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Specialized workflows become difficult to use when operators must remember every boundary. A routing layer preserves specialization while making handoffs explicit; duplicating implementation instructions inside it would create competing sources of truth.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make onboarding a verified sequence from prerequisites to a working smoke test
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain one authoritative setup guide that takes a fresh workstation from prerequisites to verified operation. Start by distinguishing human, automation, and administrator roles. Then document installation, authentication, configuration, required file synchronization, and a small end-to-end smoke test. Give headless environments their own authentication instructions. Store secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat; restrict local secret-file permissions and avoid sharing machine identities. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Successful installation does not prove that authentication, permissions, or auxiliary files work together. A troubleshooting table and tested commands prevent onboarding from depending on undocumented knowledge. Update the guide whenever tools or authentication flows change.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make integration access a visible onboarding gate and revalidate it at runtime
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Track integration readiness per content source and verify it before running maintenance. Record whether required connectors are available, credentials are configured, and a read-only access check succeeds. Include a last-checked timestamp and a specific remediation message for failures. For Notion, source-sharing and connection setup depend on the current interface and API version (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A registry makes missing setup visible during onboarding, but a stored boolean can become stale after permissions change. Runtime verification prevents repeated partial runs and gives the operator a concrete next step. Keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make approval boundaries enforceable in command behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An approval command should require explicit valid targets and reject ambiguous requests before making changes. Require at least one identifier, validate the complete requested set before execution, and abort with zero side effects if any identifier is unknown. Avoid an unrestricted approve-all shortcut where individual review is required. Keep rejection separate from enactment, and refuse or safely handle attempts to approve an already enacted item. Test each property independently. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Written instructions are easy to bypass accidentally when the command interface accepts broad or empty input. Structural constraints turn approval into a verifiable transition and reduce the chance that a typo, retry or misunderstood flag triggers unintended work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Index reusable procedures by capability, inputs and invocation triggers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe reusable web-development procedures by capability and selection criteria. Record each procedure's domain, expected inputs, outputs, location, prerequisites and useful invocation situations. Distinguish intake, writing, design, maintenance and review responsibilities. State boundaries between a brief consultation and a complete workflow, and keep the registry synchronized with available procedures. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Function-based indexing helps unfamiliar contributors select an appropriate procedure and reveals missing or overlapping responsibilities.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Align analytics account boundaries with the organizations that own the data
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Separate analytics accounts by data owner when independent access and future handoff matter. In GA4, grant a reporting service account access to each required account rather than assuming an organization-wide grant cascades across accounts (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it). Discover accessible accounts dynamically instead of hard-coding one account. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An account boundary can make later human access easier to reason about. A bicycle-repair co-op should be able to inspect its own analytics without gaining visibility into another organization's traffic.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make the analytics reader grant an explicit onboarding step for every new account
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Include a reader-access grant and a discovery check whenever a new analytics account is created. In GA4, an authorized administrator can use Admin → Account access management → Add users to grant a service account Viewer access at account level (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it). Choose that scope only when all properties should be readable. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Creating a property does not automatically make it visible to reporting tools. Verify discovery using the reporting credential itself, and allow for propagation delay before diagnosing a failed grant.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify analytics onboarding with the credential that downstream reports actually use
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Analytics onboarding is complete only when the reporting identity can discover and read the intended property. Create the account, property, and web stream; configure the site's tag according to its consent requirements; grant the reporting identity appropriate access; then verify discovery and a representative read. Confirm collection separately because readable configuration does not prove events arrive. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This checkpoint catches the common gap between creating analytics infrastructure and making it operational. Where an administrator must perform a grant, keep the workflow pending until the verification succeeds.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep reporting-service access separate from each organization's human self-service access
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat automated reporting access and human analytics access as separate permission paths. A reporting service may read several explicitly authorized accounts, while a person receives access only to the account they own or manage. A curated dashboard is another presentation layer and must enforce its own data boundaries. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This separation preserves flexibility without conflating audiences. An amateur astronomy club can receive a simplified report today and direct access later, while neither route requires exposing another organization's data or sharing the reporting service's credential.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distinguish identical policy text from equivalent policy meaning
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check literal equality and semantic equivalence separately when distributing policy across automation guides. An empty diff proves that two blocks contain the same bytes; it does not prove the policy is correct or consistently applied. Different wording may preserve the same requirement while obscuring which version is authoritative. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Maintaining a canonical policy and explicit references reduces reconciliation work. When exact duplication is required, automate that comparison; when local adaptation is allowed, review the obligations and exceptions rather than claiming byte identity.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat design-tool prototypes as handoffs that need a deliberate production port
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use a design prototype to communicate composition and interaction, then deliberately translate it into the production framework. Provide a specific brief, obtain the prototype and its assets, identify the essential visual behavior, and map that behavior onto the real site's components and content. Verify accessibility, responsive layout, and runtime behavior after the port. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A convincing prototype is useful evidence of design intent, but its implementation may not meet production constraints. For a tide-pool field guide, preserve the educational interaction while adapting asset loading, keyboard access, and reduced-motion behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Package local automations with explicit scope and reproducible instructions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A reusable local automation needs a guide, setup instructions, operating rules, and concrete runbooks for its tools and evaluation criteria. State which resources are local, which artifacts are authoritative, and what would need to change before team use. Keep private run data separate from distributable instructions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A collection of scripts is difficult to inherit without its operating context. Explicit scope prevents a personal workflow from being mistaken for a shared service with access controls and collaboration guarantees.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Protect the invariants that keep an evaluation corpus trustworthy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Identify corpus-integrity rules before collection: preserve original prompts, capture outputs verbatim, verify execution metadata, bound retries, and retain anomalous attempts. Replay identical prompts across comparison arms and give one controlled process responsibility for accepting artifacts. Audit these rules independently. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A small procedural defect can invalidate many otherwise useful responses. Explicit invariants make failures detectable and keep convenience changes from silently altering attribution, task equivalence, or the evidence available to later reviewers.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep shared runbook mirrors separate from private execution data
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Share reusable automation instructions through a documented mirror while keeping private transcripts, run registries, and sensitive artifacts outside that publication surface. Identify the authoritative source and track mirror updates explicitly. List unfinished integration steps without implying that they have been executed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A mirror improves discoverability but introduces another copy that can drift. Clear publication boundaries prevent accidental disclosure, and honest completion states help the next maintainer distinguish an installed capability from a proposed follow-up.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Document and verify the full installation surface of an automation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain an installation manifest covering guidance files, configuration entries, startup integrations, retrieval handles, and maintained mirrors. Before updating, back up affected files; apply changes idempotently; verify the live configuration and behavior; document uninstall and rollback steps. Use paths belonging to the reader's own installation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Installation reports can become stale while configuration drifts. A concrete manifest makes upgrades reviewable and prevents partial deployments in which a file exists but its loader, retrieval path, or mirror still points elsewhere.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use durable artifacts and a compact manifest to coordinate large evaluations
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Have evaluation workers save complete outputs to designated artifacts and return compact completion metadata to the coordinator. Maintain a manifest linking prompts, outputs, execution attribution, and validation status. Verify artifact existence and contents before accepting a worker's completion message. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Large responses can overwhelm coordination context without improving oversight. A manifest preserves the information needed to schedule comparisons and prepare blinded review, while full artifacts remain available for inspection and recovery when a worker reports success incorrectly.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate packaged skills against the dependencies their instructions actually reference
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A portable skill package must include every dependency required by its instructions. Extract referenced skills from the package, resolve their transitive dependencies, and compare that closure with the installation manifest. Treat unresolved references as packaging failures. Text search can discover candidates, but ambiguous mentions need explicit dependency declarations. Test the package in a clean installation where undeclared local skills cannot mask omissions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A prose instruction to load another skill can fail silently when that skill is absent. Dependency validation binds the instruction to something the recipient can actually execute.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Tag lessons by the workflows they should improve at capture time
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Attach generic workflow destinations to lessons when they are recorded, then use those labels to assemble maintenance inputs. A deployment discovery may apply to both initial setup and ongoing maintenance; an animation lesson may belong to media production and browser delivery. Track proposed updates through review and incorporation, allowing one lesson to serve several workflows. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] End-of-project reconstruction requires remembering both what happened and where it belongs. Early routing makes follow-up searchable and auditable while preserving the distinction between a captured observation and an accepted workflow change.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Write account setup guides from observed behavior and explicit human handoffs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build novice setup guides around tested actions, expected results and clear responsibility boundaries. Explain which account the reader should see, what each command does, where credentials belong and how to recognize a wrong-account symptom. Describe credential synchronization in one direction from your own key file to the platform's secret store, never through the repo or chat. Include rotation and troubleshooting steps. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A guide becomes trustworthy when it reports measured behavior rather than design intentions. Explicit handoffs reduce guessing, especially when dashboard actions and automated checks belong to different participants.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make novice guides observable, with explicit prerequisites and completion handoffs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A novice setup guide should state prerequisites, explain the purpose, assign responsibilities and provide an expected result after each numbered step. Include a permission table with reasons, a troubleshooting table and a short completion phrase that contains no secrets. Put recommended optional choices, such as credential expiry, in visibly marked decision boxes and verify their resulting state. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers can complete the main task while silently missing an optional-looking safeguard. Observable checkpoints expose that gap, and a simple handoff lets the reader report completion without composing a technical status report.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review guides in execution order and put warnings before consequential actions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Cold-read operational guides as a literal sequence of actions, with every warning placed before the action it constrains. Check login assumptions, ambiguous buttons, expected results and existing-state hazards. A private browser window needs its own sign-in instructions. DNS instructions should inspect existing records before adding anything, and rollback descriptions should account for cached state. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Many dangerous documentation defects are ordering defects. A warning in troubleshooting arrives too late, and an author mentally supplies steps that a first-time reader cannot infer. A cold read helps, but actual dashboard behavior still needs independent verification.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distinguish documented capabilities from verified dashboard click paths
