memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A capability description does not establish the current dashboard path for enabling it. Write instructions using visible tab names, box titles and button labels only when observed; mark uncertain locations as alternatives and date any concrete UI path. Validate the guide against the real screen, then read back the resulting configuration. Place warnings about unrelated production settings before the relevant click. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reviewer can find internal contradictions without noticing that an entire screen description is fictional. The first real execution tests the guide against the vendor interface, revealing assumptions that prose-only review cannot resolve.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate human setup steps by reading back the resulting platform state
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After a reader completes a dashboard step, inspect the resulting configuration rather than assuming the click produced the intended state. Guides should emphasize permission levels as clearly as permission names, display optional choices explicitly, and use short completion handoffs. Tools can tolerate harmless formatting variations while rejecting ambiguous credential selection. Keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reader can follow plausible instructions and still leave a trigger missing or grant Read when Edit was required. State readback catches these differences and turns first-run confusion into concrete documentation improvements.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make background model selection explicit and keep website promises behind verified behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An application's background model choice should be explicitly configured rather than inferred from whichever account or CLI happens to be available. Explain what data the background task sends, which backend it uses, and how the user can change that selection. Test supported backends on disposable data through the real setup path before advertising them. Keep planned capability separate from released behavior. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Foreground model choice can create a false impression that every background operation uses the same provider. A website accuracy review can uncover this product gap, but the copy must retain the limitation until the implementation is verified.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify the execution path before describing a background feature as model-powered
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe a background feature from its observed execution path, including fallbacks, rather than from its intended design. Verify whether model calls succeed, whether rejected calls trigger heuristics, and whether the chosen backend uses an API or a subscription-backed CLI. Record backend selection explicitly and test output compatibility through the actual installer on disposable data. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A scheduled task can complete while its advertised model step never runs. Likewise, access to an interactive subscription does not establish that an integration uses it. These distinctions affect both product accuracy and the user's understanding of data handling and costs.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make delegated editorial decisions within scope and preserve an auditable final version
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When editorial judgment has been explicitly delegated, make bounded decisions and record their reasons alongside the approved text. Preserve the final reviewed artifacts, identify any accepted amendments and rerun relevant checks on the resulting bytes. Keep optional polish separate from corrections required for accuracy. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeatedly returning already delegated choices creates friction without improving oversight. A concise decision record makes the work reviewable while allowing progress. Preserving the actual approved version also prevents later edits from being mistaken for text that received the same review.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make automated insights visible through a real review interaction
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An improvement loop needs a reliable review interaction, not merely another writer or storage table. Reuse existing observations where possible, synthesize at most one actionable candidate per review cycle and allow no candidate when evidence is weak. A useful template is a rule of no more than 120 words, tied to an existing instruction section and supported by evidence spanning at least two days. Treat near-duplicates as reinforcement of an existing candidate. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Stored insights have no operational effect if nobody encounters them. Reducing redundant infrastructure leaves attention for the actual transition from evidence to a reviewed behavioral change.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Budget concurrent agents for their child processes and checkpoint work incrementally
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Agent concurrency must account for duplicated model processes and browser instances, not just the number of visible tasks. Memory retrieval may load an embedding stack in each worker, while browser-based review adds Chromium. Measure available headroom, begin conservatively and serialize expensive retrieval or browser work when pressure rises. Require long tasks to save completed sections incrementally. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Read-only work can still exhaust memory. A fixed agent count is not a portable capacity limit, and incremental checkpoints preserve useful progress when the process or virtual machine fails.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: After repeated crashes, reduce concurrency and recover only from validated artifacts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A second crash under lighter concurrency weakens the claim that agent count alone explains the failure. Consider host memory pressure, stuck child processes and background services, while keeping these as hypotheses until evidence distinguishes them. Temporarily run one background job at a time, save progress frequently and validate recovered files for completeness before resuming. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Surviving filenames do not prove completed work: an empty result file or partial report can look like success. Conservative recovery preserves progress without turning an uncertain diagnosis into a permanent operating rule.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recover interrupted orchestration from durable job state before starting replacement work
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After a controller failure, inspect saved artifacts and surviving processes before launching replacement work. Check revision status, build identity, job handles and progress files. If a detached verification job remains healthy, monitor it and use the supported recovery mechanism. Record its exit status and capture the final state after reporting finishes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A controller can stop while its subprocess continues. Durable progress records support recovery, while duplicate jobs can waste resources or interfere through shared servers and output directories.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Turn inherited lessons into executable task requirements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Carry lessons into the next build as concrete requirements with commands, measurements and expected outcomes. Put shared fixes in shared components, define the core verification set and require an early progress report plus a final artifact snapshot. Keep generation outputs separate from durable lesson curation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An instruction to remember previous mistakes is too vague to execute reliably. A task specification makes those lessons actionable and reviewable, while separating code generation from memory updates prevents tentative implementation choices from becoming permanent guidance.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit running automation through durable artifacts and observable processes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Audit a running build using its progress file, declared step list, artifact fingerprints and process state. Confirm that executed gates match the agreed scope, check for duplicate test chains, inspect temporary-directory placement and compare protected-file changes against the task boundary. Record repository ahead/behind state and whether required reports exist. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Durable evidence reveals stalls, duplicated work and unintended writes without relying on an agent's narrative. A staged script with stamped logs makes the workflow inspectable while it is still running, when correction is useful.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make long build tasks recoverable through early reports and saved checkpoints
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Write progress reports early and save recoverable checkpoints throughout long-running build tasks. Keep implementation files in persistent storage, commit coherent increments and record which gates ran against which artifact. After interruption, inspect the working tree and process state before resuming. Preserve unresolved findings, including tiny mobile typography or rendering failures, in the report. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A restart should require reconstructing execution state rather than recreating the work. Uncommitted files may survive, but checkpoints and durable reports make recovery much less dependent on that assumption.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define complete autonomous build scope and a separate release boundary
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An autonomous site-build specification should cover secondary pages, error states, performance, structured data, accessibility and deployment readiness as well as the main visual experience. State which changes may reach a preview and what authorization production release requires. Require durable progress reports, explicit unresolved defects and periodic capture of reusable lessons. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Broad implementation authority does not remove the need for a clear finish line. A complete checklist prevents visually impressive pages from masking missing operational work, while a stated release boundary keeps execution aligned with the agreed scope.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Batch motion production after aligning storyboards and proving the shared method
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When several pages share a proven motion system, align their storyboards before preparing one consolidated render handoff. Keep ingredients and outputs grouped by page, while providing a single queue of prompts, aspects and expected filenames. For a ceramic studio, classes, firing services and exhibition pages could share production conventions while retaining distinct visual narratives. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A consolidated handoff reduces repeated setup and makes missing assets easier to identify. It also exposes inconsistencies before rendering begins. Batch the expensive work after a representative probe succeeds, then integrate the returned clips with page-specific checks rather than assuming a shared component guarantees that every page fits.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Acknowledge webhook events promptly and deduplicate before starting slow work
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Separate webhook acknowledgement from slow processing and deduplicate incoming event IDs before triggering downstream work. Slack's Events API expects an HTTP 200 within 3 seconds and may retry otherwise (as of October 2026; re-check before relying on it). In n8n, inspect both nested event fields and flattened fields when filtering bot messages, including bot_id, bot_profile, app_id and relevant subtypes. Returning an empty item array stops that execution path. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A job taking 60 seconds can outlast the acknowledgement window and turn retries into duplicate replies. A shared in-memory or workflow-level ID list needs careful concurrency and persistence handling; for reliable multi-worker processing, use an atomic deduplication store with an appropriate retention period. Bot filtering also prevents self-triggered loops.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give each automation one discoverable, portable documentation entry point
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Package each automation with a single documentation entry point linking its guide, executable instructions, setup requirements, agent specifications, and reviewed lessons. Use relative paths and explain manual authentication steps for a newcomer. Record prerequisites, expected inputs and outputs, failure recovery, and validation commands. Link the entry point from the repository's agent instructions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Scattered setup knowledge makes an automation dependent on its original author. A self-contained guide supports repeatable execution across machines. Keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat, and review proposed lesson updates before treating them as established guidance.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Maintain a scoped automation index in repository agent instructions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep a living automation index in the repository's agent instructions, linking each available workflow to its entry point and prerequisites. Update the index whenever an automation is added, moved, or retired. Include only workflows relevant to that repository and describe what each does rather than relying on persona names. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A concise index lets a new agent or maintainer discover supported workflows without scanning the entire filesystem. Scoped entries reduce irrelevant context, while maintained links prevent outdated instructions from sending execution toward missing or inappropriate tooling.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define website automation by responsibilities and observable acceptance checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A website automation role should specify ownership, operating modes and verifiable completion criteria. Separate new builds, maintenance and audits; assign responsibility for the application shell, content operations, deployment and specialist claim review. Follow discovery, environment checks, design, implementation, integration, security, deployment and verification. Capture Playwright screenshots at 3 representative viewports and run accessibility and performance checks. Emit structured data only when it accurately describes visible content. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A calm working style can support careful decisions, but personality descriptions cannot replace acceptance evidence. Clear responsibilities prevent gaps, while relevant checks avoid arbitrary schema counts or scanner scores becoming substitutes for a usable website.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bound migration discovery and stream results outside the model context
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Large site migrations need explicit discovery budgets and incremental artifacts. Begin with the highest-value sources, crawl only deduplicated candidates and write structured results in batches. Keep summaries and unresolved decisions in the working context while retaining full evidence in files. Expand to additional sources when expected value justifies the remaining request, time and token budgets. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Feeding an entire historical crawl into a model can consume resources without improving redirect decisions. Bounded stages make costs visible and preserve progress, while an explicit escalation path allows deeper discovery when the initial inventory proves insufficient.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define an artifact contract between site extraction and implementation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A site-reconstruction handoff should provide a complete, inspectable artifact bundle before implementation begins. Include a page index, captured HTML, per-page media references, notes, screenshots, a shared asset map, and instructions connecting assets to page locations. Record capture limitations and identify missing material. The receiving builder should validate the bundle and load its implementation instructions before starting. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Extraction and implementation solve different problems. An explicit artifact contract reduces repeated discovery and prevents a builder from guessing which image, section, or interaction belongs where. Screenshots establish visual evidence while structured mappings preserve relationships that raw HTML alone may not explain.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Select reconstruction or creative design mode from the supplied source and requested outcome
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use strict reconstruction when the task supplies an approved HTML reference, and creative design when it supplies a brief requiring interpretation. This distinction applies equally to full sites, individual pages, and resource articles. For reconstruction, preserve approved copy, section order, media placement, and intended interactions while adapting implementation to the target framework. For creative work, make and document design decisions against the brief. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An excellent redesign can still fail a reproduction request. Declaring the mode before work starts prevents accidental paraphrasing and invented sections, while ensuring that an open-ended brief receives the design judgment it actually requires.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Handle automated review refusals transparently without retry loops or silent approval
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When an automated reviewer refuses a task, record the refusal and route permitted checks through an appropriate deterministic or human review process. Clarify a genuinely ambiguous review scope once if useful, without disguising the content or attempting to bypass safeguards. Validate structural requirements such as markup, links, and metadata with suitable tools, and record which checks remain incomplete. Identify the fallback reviewer and reason in the verdict. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated identical requests waste time and do not establish review coverage. Transparent fallback keeps a pipeline from silently skipping pages or treating an unavailable automated verdict as approval, while preserving the same acceptance criteria for allowed work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Extract stable generator helpers before repeated copies begin to drift
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Share stable generator boilerplate when multiple sites need the same maintenance behavior. Candidates include path setup, JSON reading, diagnostic formatting, and top-level error handling. Keep the shared module small and its distribution explicit so every consuming repository receives compatible versions. Avoid extracting abstractions solely for a hypothetical second consumer. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated copies make minor fixes inconsistent across sites. A focused shared layer reduces that risk without hiding site-specific source data or turning a simple generator into a general framework.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate reusable automation documentation from private deployment inventories
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep deployment inventories outside publicly shared automation packages. Share generic workflows, validation rules, and examples, while storing account identifiers, production targets, and local repository locations in a separate private configuration. Scan release artifacts and generated documentation for accidental local paths and identifying data before distribution. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reusable automation often needs private operational context to run, but recipients do not need the original operator's infrastructure map. Separating those concerns makes a package safer to publish and easier to configure independently.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Register automation handoffs according to responsibility and keep references consistent
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Connect automations through explicit handoffs that match their responsibilities. A cross-site propagation task needs a link from the workflow that produces shared changes; routine site maintenance may use a separate target registry. Keep documented names, directory slugs, and lookup references consistent, and verify that the receiving workflow can actually be found. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Registering a task everywhere adds noise without guaranteeing execution. A clear handoff establishes who receives the output, what triggers the next step, and which configuration governs its scope.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distinguish a validated automation package from a verified production rollout
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Report documentation readiness and production rollout as separate completion states. Validate that distributed instructions agree, private configuration stays private, and published artifacts contain no local identifying paths. Then identify the remaining execution and deployment checks explicitly rather than describing a packaged workflow as already operational across sites. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Documentation can pass every structural check while no production behavior has changed. Clear completion boundaries prevent downstream operators from assuming that deployment, live verification, or target coverage has already happened.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distribute one canonical generator and express site differences through source data
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain one canonical generator for shared behavior across repositories. Distribute it unchanged and verify byte equality or cryptographic digests for every in-scope copy. Represent site differences through validated configuration and source artifacts rather than hardcoded branches on site identifiers. Record stale copies outside the authorized rollout scope without modifying them incidentally. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Per-site forks multiply maintenance paths and conceal inconsistent fixes. Identical code plus explicit data makes differences explainable and keeps a shared rollout bounded.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test a reusable rollout process on structurally different changes before generalizing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate a supposedly generic rollout process with a second structurally different change. For example, apply the same coordination and review stages to both a generated JSON catalog and an authentication guidance document. Keep platform-specific headers, caching, and output paths within each target's implementation step. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Success on one payload demonstrates one working case, not generality. A different payload exposes hidden assumptions while showing which parts of the process are reusable and which require explicit adapters.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Design local developer tools for portable operation and explicit trust boundaries
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A portable local developer tool benefits from simple installation, explicit capabilities, and recoverable state. Consider a local daemon with a browser interface when headless access matters, short-lived single-use login links, restricted tool permissions, auditable calls, and a movable data directory. Updates should be atomic, authenticated, and reversible; a checksum alone does not authenticate a publisher. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These choices reduce handoff friction while keeping authority visible. Structured CLI output helps automation, but failures should still use meaningful nonzero exit codes so scripts cannot mistake a reported error for success.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Write deployment guides from live configuration and minimize manual transcription
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Generate deployment instructions from current vendor documentation and live configuration wherever possible. For a GitHub-connected Worker, select only the intended repository, specify build and deploy commands, match the configured Worker name and read back branch triggers. Copy DNSSEC DS fields programmatically from the provider rather than retyping a digest. Date dashboard paths and preview feature descriptions (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A useful guide names prerequisites, expected results and verification steps. Batch independent account tasks, then have an unfamiliar reader check whether the instructions assume knowledge they do not provide.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check research deliverables for completeness and distinguish quota failures from content gaps
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate research outputs against a declared structure before using them downstream. Check that each file exists and contains substantive sections, requested comparisons, references and clearly labelled estimates. Record missing reports and whether an independent source was actually obtained. Structural completeness is a prerequisite, not proof of factual accuracy; inspect consequential claims against their sources. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful process exit or a long report can hide an incomplete deliverable. Billing or quota failures require a different response from malformed output. Track actual usage and cost per run because prompt size and output requirements can invalidate an old budget estimate; do not generalize one batch's charges into current vendor pricing.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give writing agents a compact input pack with explicit precedence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define the precedence of writing instructions before asking an agent to produce site content. Put current overrides ahead of general style guidance, distinguish verified facts from examples, and supply a task-specific brief with a clear output contract. Pilot the pack on a small representative section and inspect whether the output reflects the intended rules. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] More context does not automatically produce better adherence. Contradictory or poorly ordered instructions leave the agent to invent precedence. A compact, tested pack reduces that ambiguity and makes failures traceable to a rule, fact, or missing requirement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Frame a repair around observable outcomes and named acceptance gates
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define the repair's observable outcome, current release scope, and acceptance gates before starting implementation. Retrieve relevant investigation notes, isolate changes in worktrees where useful, and test the known failure mechanism directly. For retrieval work, that includes model compatibility, honest failure states, and usable results. Record acceptance evidence and capture decisions during the work, then update dependent documentation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A written route prevents a bounded repair from drifting into an indefinite redesign. Named checks are more informative than a subjective quality score and give the next maintainer a concrete explanation of what completion means.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make cross-session handoffs stand alone and distinguish proposals from requirements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Structure a handoff with the required outcome first, the critical technical trap second, and the supporting evidence path third. Include scope boundaries, unresolved questions, acceptance requirements, and any dependent content update. Label implementation suggestions as proposals so the receiving developer can improve them without accidentally changing the requirements. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A recipient who missed the investigation needs enough context to act without replaying the conversation. Separating obligations from suggested mechanics preserves autonomy while preventing silent changes to the intended result or deployment boundary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Organize a web-development pack around recognizable jobs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Group a web-development pack by the work a builder performs: planning, design, implementation, content, launch checks, and maintenance. Map supporting services such as hosting, DNS, analytics, forms, and email to those jobs. Keep web development a distinct package when its lifecycle and deliverables differ from a broader marketing program. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A flat inventory of tools is difficult to evaluate or use. Job-based grouping helps a reader see what the pack enables, what remains an external dependency, and which parts support ongoing care rather than the first launch.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Scope a web-development pack around delivery work and distilled guidance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Organize a web-development pack around initial site or resource-hub construction, website maintenance and resource-hub maintenance. Include the design, writing, implementation, deployment, accessibility and performance guidance those workflows need. Incorporate useful findings as practical instructions, adding supporting machinery only when delivery requires it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A coherent pack helps contributors build and maintain websites. Clear boundaries between supporting guidance and separate workflows keep the package understandable and easier to maintain.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure whether job output reaches its consumer, not merely whether the job exits successfully
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful background job must be verified at the destination that users actually read. Trace generated output through persistence and the consumer query, comparing produced items with durable records and retrievable results. For a bakery's nightly menu importer, a successful run and populated audit log are insufficient if the ordering page reads another table. Separate confirmed observations from suspected regression causes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Jobs can run for months while delivering nothing useful if a refactor disconnects logging from storage. Monitoring execution alone misses this failure; output-to-consumer checks expose the broken handoff.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Translate public promises into end-to-end acceptance criteria and ongoing alarms
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Derive repair acceptance criteria directly from the behavior promised to users. For a tide-pool guide that generates candidate observations, verify durable storage, explicit uncertainty labels, retrieval through the normal interface, and appropriate ranking below comparable verified observations. Test every claimed processing mode and require a real scheduled run. Add an alarm when eligible output is produced but nothing reaches the consumer-facing store. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Passing a unit test for the repaired function does not prove the whole promise. A claim-to-check contract aligns publication with delivery, and an ongoing yield alarm detects the same broken handoff after future changes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Turn a delivery failure into a consumer-side check for future audits
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a job completes without delivering usable output, add consumer-side verification to future capability audits. Locate each output where users access it and exercise an interaction that retrieves it. Review implementation, published messaging and live behavior separately. Derive displayed counts from the underlying data rather than entering them manually. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Successful execution logs do not establish successful delivery. Verifying arrival catches missing integrations before pages make claims about capabilities users cannot access.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Delegated approval removes repeated permission requests, not verification
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When approval authority is explicitly delegated, complete the authorised work and its required checks without repeatedly reopening the same permission question. Keep the scope clear, resolve material findings before publication, and surface genuinely new decisions separately. Record what was changed and verified. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Delegation saves attention for decisions that require human judgment. It is not evidence that the result is correct, so the quality gate should remain intact even when another approval stop is unnecessary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reuse versioned task instructions and portable workspace links for comparable runs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use a versioned task template, an input manifest, and portable workspace references when comparing repeated writing runs. Record checksums before work begins, define permitted inputs and expected outputs, and use relative symlinks where linked files will move together. Recover prior instructions from their saved source instead of reconstructing them from memory. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Unrecorded changes to the task can masquerade as differences in writer quality. Portable references also prevent a relocated workspace from failing for reasons unrelated to the copy under review.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give every review finding a disposition and route it to the layer that can resolve it
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Record a disposition for every finding, including issues deferred from the current writing round. Route wording defects to copy revision, hidden status to layout work, and unresolved promises to the person responsible for the underlying offer. Carry essential qualifications into Markdown and other machine-readable versions alongside the claims they limit. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A cap on immediate revisions should prioritize work, not erase findings. Corroboration helps rank concerns, but shared reviewer assumptions still need scrutiny before agreement is treated as independent evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A brief’s purpose sentence can act as an unreviewed draft line
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Read prose-like instructions in a brief as candidate copy and challenge any meaning they would communicate incorrectly. Check whether a setup phrase implies public availability, whether a mechanism lacks its object, and whether a heading covers all the material beneath it. Draft a supported version and flag the instruction conflict. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Faithful execution does not protect against a faulty brief. Fixing the instruction at its source prevents the same wording from reappearing in later rounds or spreading to related pages.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate scroll-story structure from the video generation provider
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A scroll-story workflow can reuse an established video-production process while adopting a separate method for stops, passages, seams and browser playback. Define who writes prompts, who renders clips and who reviews them, then hand the web builder finished media and approved HTML copy. Silent website passages need no voice-over, music or narration script unless the design explicitly requires them. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Keeping the production route explicit reduces duplicated process and accidental use of an unsuitable provider. The transferable structure is the handoff contract and review sequence; a particular generation tool should remain replaceable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Put specialized web-video recipes in the workflow where future work will find them
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A reusable web-video process needs discoverable recipes and entry-point instructions, not only a completed example. Add explicit branches for scroll passages and silent loops, specify which narration or music stages to skip, and define a mechanical normalization step before browser integration. Include both prompt review before rendering and seam review in the final page. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Lessons are easy to lose when they remain buried in a project log. Connecting recipes to the main workflow makes the intended route available when a similar task next appears and reduces reliance on someone remembering the previous implementation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make proven web-video checks available in both build and maintenance workflows
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Integrate reusable video guidance into both new-site and maintenance workflows through clear triggers, linked recipes and verified retrieval terms. The shared checklist should cover delivery ranges, still-based stops, normalized encodes, final media verification, motion controls, poster loading and player compatibility with the content-security policy. Builds should consume only the package's finished web assets. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A fix learned during one implementation offers little protection if the next workflow cannot find it. Place guidance where the task begins and test its discoverability, so future work starts with known constraints rather than rediscovering the same failure modes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Agent instructions should reward honest uncertainty and composed correction
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Write agent instructions that favor transparent uncertainty, calm investigation, and evidence-based correction over agreement or rushed completion. When a task stalls, require the next diagnostic step; when a check fails, record the failure and revise the approach. Keep shared behavioral guidance consistent across project templates and instantiated instruction files. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Pressure to appear successful can encourage unsupported claims. These are useful operational rules without assuming that emotion-like language establishes subjective feelings or proves a causal theory of model behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build foundations first and keep verification strict under deadline pressure
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Complex releases become easier to reason about when foundational controls and test harnesses precede dependent features. Record the reasoning behind important decisions, then verify integrations with concrete failure cases rather than relying on review scores. Stage experimental work with real copies when symlinks could escape the intended workspace, and compare expected file contents before promotion. Treat a score below a declared threshold as below threshold: 9.79 does not become 9.8 by convenient rounding. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Calm execution reduces the temptation to waive inconvenient checks. The useful retrospective records which safeguards caught real bugs and which assumptions failed, so later work inherits evidence instead of a celebratory launch narrative.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give creative agents room to explore without framing mistakes as existential failure
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Creative-agent instructions can encourage curiosity, play, and distinctive ideas while keeping error handling calm and concrete. Describe failed attempts as information, require candid uncertainty, and preserve quality checks when an iteration disappoints. Avoid threats, panic, or pressure to succeed at any cost. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Dramatic persona language can compete with the task's actual constraints. A calm baseline is a practical instruction-design choice rather than a proven guarantee against reward hacking; judge its usefulness through observable behavior, including honest reporting and willingness to revise.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Stop repeated paid retries when the latest result defeats the working diagnosis
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Pause repeated paid attempts when the latest result falsifies the working diagnosis and no evidence supports the next change. A three-failure checkpoint is a useful trigger for reassessment, not proof that all failures share one cause. Run available low-cost diagnostics: compare parameters, job histories, input formats, and successful controls. Prepare the next discriminating experiment with its cost and expected outcomes before escalating to the budget holder. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repetition can feel like progress even after diagnosis has become guessing. A ready-to-run experiment preserves momentum while putting the spending decision with the person responsible for it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate model representation claims from claims about subjective experience
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat findings about emotion-related model representations as specific to the tested model and experiment. Before using them to justify a website assistant's behavior, inspect the intervention, baseline and evaluation tasks. Distinguish changes to internal activations from ordinary persona prompts. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An emotional label or composed writing style does not establish subjective experience or reliable conduct. Evaluate a website assistant through observable decisions, tool use and outcomes, including how it handles mistakes and uncertainty.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give agents calm failure procedures and permission to report uncertainty
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Design agent instructions so deadlines, failed tests, and unavailable services lead to bounded recovery rather than pressure to claim success. Specify when to retry, reduce scope, preserve partial work, or report a blocker. Pair warmth with evidence checking and explicit permission to disagree. Encourage accurate uncertainty and composed corrections. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These procedures make honest failure handling operationally useful. Claims that emotional wording directly controls internal model states require separate evidence; a calm persona is not a safety guarantee. Monitor concrete actions and results, and never infer trustworthy behavior solely from reassuring language.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Show only one idle attention cue at a time
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Serialize idle ripple or pulse cues so that only one is visible at a time, and suppress them while a related detail is open. Keep these decorative hints distinct from actual keyboard focus and selection styling. Verify both the calm resting state and a deliberately noisy case with overlapping cues. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Several simultaneous ripples can look like multiple focused controls or competing requests for attention. A single restrained cue helps reveal interactivity without confusing the current state or interrupting someone who is already reading.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use browser measurements and accessibility scans before declaring a web review complete
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Code review and a clean build do not replace Lighthouse runs, axe scans, and manual interaction checks. Capture reports and screenshots for representative routes, mobile viewports, and important UI states. Inspect focus visibility, contrast, heading structure, and touch targets explicitly. Lighthouse lab measurements do not establish field INP or guarantee real-user performance. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Review scores can conceal missing evidence. Repeatable artifacts show what was actually tested and make regressions easier to compare, while manual checks cover interactions automated scans cannot fully assess.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify build, repository security, hosting configuration and HTTPS before production cutover
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A production infrastructure gate should verify the actual build, repository controls and hosting configuration. Run `npx astro build` and resolve failures before pushing release changes. Choose repository visibility deliberately, require strong account authentication, protect the production branch and scan for secrets with Gitleaks. Ignore environment files and confirm none are already tracked. Keep secrets in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. In your hosting account, confirm repository linkage, application root, build settings, preview behavior and production branch. Verify your custom domain, certificate and response headers. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A locally successful page can still deploy from the wrong directory or branch. Explicit checks connect source control to the site that visitors will actually receive.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Initialize consent before analytics and verify requests, events and duplicate collection
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Analytics integration should establish consent defaults before loading tags and then verify actual collection behavior. If using Google Consent Mode v2, configure the relevant storage and advertising consent states before tag initialization, then update them from the consent interface. A `wait_for_update: 500` value is a timing configuration, not a substitute for consent enforcement. Vendor APIs and behavior are perishable (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it). Distinguish a GA4 measurement integration from a GTM container, and check whether the container already supplies GA4 before adding another loader. Inspect CSP violations, network requests, pageviews and form events in both denied and accepted states. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Counting identifiers in HTML or seeing a script return 200 cannot prove correct analytics. Duplicate loaders and incorrect consent ordering can silently distort measurement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prove no-op generator upgrades through both direct generation and the full build
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A generator upgrade intended to leave an artifact unchanged should reproduce that artifact byte for byte through both direct execution and the normal build. Compare output against the committed artifact, confirm the deployed generator matches the canonical implementation, and inspect version-control status for unexpected changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Direct execution checks the generator, while a full build checks its integration, environment, and ordering. Matching output on unchanged inputs is useful regression evidence, but does not prove correctness for newly supported inputs; those need their own representative fixtures.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Assert that a mutation changed bytes before trusting a fidelity test
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A byte-fidelity mutation test must first assert that its mutation actually changed the input. Unicode punctuation, visually similar characters, or normalization differences can cause a naive ASCII replacement to match nothing. Check the mutation count or compare original and mutated bytes before testing whether the validator detects corruption. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An unchanged fixture can produce a false pass that looks like strong protection. Proving the negative example exists is essential before its rejection provides evidence about the validator.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check that each value belongs to the correct entity, not merely that it appears in a source
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Source membership checks cannot detect values assigned to the wrong entities. Keep separate gates for whether a value exists in the source and whether it belongs to the entity named in the output. Test the second gate by swapping two otherwise valid values. Proximity matching can work for well-separated claims; use structured bindings or parsing when both entities fall within the same window. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Two swapped specifications remain valid members of the source set while making the page false. Separate gates preserve useful failure messages and expose a defect that a broad traceability score can hide.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Probe whether validators read generated constants, not just whether verdicts change
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verdict-change tests can miss validators that read generated content without changing their result. Complement them with poison-pill objects that record access and raise on operations such as iteration, indexing, conversion, comparison, and truth testing. Give each probe a positive control using data the validator must read. Compare probes with different detection mechanisms. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A validator can accidentally grade the same constants used to generate its output. A clean probe only supports the behaviors it can observe; swallowed exceptions, cached values, and uninstrumented access require additional structural checks. Agreement improves confidence but does not prove complete independence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recalibrate a faulty check using independent evidence and preserved failure controls
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When independent evidence establishes that an artifact is correct, investigate a failing check before changing the artifact. For example, sentence-level token overlap may misjudge a summary that faithfully condenses several sentences. Model the actual relationship, document the calibration change, and rerun known-valid examples alongside defect controls. Preserve the intended rejection of genuine faults. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Editing correct work merely to satisfy a flawed metric hides the measurement error. Calibration is justified by an independent oracle and retained detection capability, not by a desire to make the current build green.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Turn critical workflow rules into run-stopping checks with positive controls
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Critical rules need executable checks that stop the run when violated. Reject placeholder URLs instead of emitting them, verify that cited files exist, and return a nonzero exit status when required evidence is unresolved. Test each guard with a deliberately invalid input and a valid control. Place the checks on the path that actually emits or publishes the artifact. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A warning that allows publication does not enforce a requirement. Prose remains valuable for explaining intent, but mechanical checks carry repeatable obligations through fatigue, handoffs, and repeated edits.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Derive failure controls from the governing source, not a paraphrased checklist
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A positive control must violate the actual governing rule, not an inherited restatement of it. Read the primary specification, select a definite violation, and verify that the intended gate rejects it. Include an allowed example to detect overblocking. If a planted input passes, first establish whether it was prohibited at all before blaming the implementation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A checklist can silently expand or distort a rule. A control built from that distortion may certify nothing while reporting success. Primary-source derivation separates a broken validator from a test that never exercised the requirement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Run publication gates against generated artifacts inside the deployment path
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Publication safeguards must run on the generated artifacts in the actual deployment pipeline. Cover sourced claims, confidential content, broken interactions, inconsistent facts, structured data, accessibility, and relevant performance budgets. Inspect HTML, Markdown alternatives, JSON-LD, metadata, alt text, and asset names. Give each critical check a planted defect that must fail. Keep sensitive matching data in a protected CI mechanism rather than publishing a private-name denylist. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A local-only scan leaves later edits unchecked. A build followed by a failing gate protects release only when deployment stops on that failure and publishes the exact artifacts that passed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Diagnose secret-scan fragment matches without printing secret values
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Investigate whether a secret-scan hit matches a complete secret or only a fragment before classifying it as a leak. A public identifier and its related secret can share a prefix; verify that possibility through boolean comparisons that reveal no values. Exempt only the proven public-overlap fragment, retain full-secret matching, and add another discriminating fragment where appropriate. Do not assume a naming suffix alone proves a value public. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] False alarms teach maintainers to ignore scanners, but broad exclusions can hide real leaks. A narrow, evidence-backed adjustment improves precision while preserving coverage. Secrets remain in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate test harnesses before trusting remote deployment results
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Exercise test harnesses and build watchers against known fixtures before relying on remote results. Check timestamp placement, strict boolean assertions, branch-and-revision matching and application-level delivery failures. Define expected rate-limit behavior using the service's documented consistency model, and check feature enablement during preflight. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Verification code can fail independently of the website. A watcher matching only a revision can confuse branch builds, while an incorrectly timed timestamp can create a false failure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate generated denylists against both forbidden material and ordinary permitted text
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat a generated denylist as a parser output that needs validation before it can block publication. Derive sensitive names and identifiers from controlled sources, normalize them, and inspect the result for accidental numeric, hardware or generic-language entries. Test known forbidden examples and ordinary permitted prose. Record the rule version used by CI, and separate hard blocks from review warnings. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Extraction errors can turn harmless dimensions or common words into publication failures. Exact term matching also misses a confidential idea paraphrased without its name, so a denylist supports contextual review rather than proving that a page is safe to publish.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate verified claims from production-dependent claims in approval packages
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An approval package should state which claims are verified and which still depend on production changes. List the exact artifacts reviewed, relevant checks, known limitations and launch tasks that remain open. For privacy statements, distinguish configured behavior from observed behavior, including logging, retention and deletion. Investigate apparent documentation gaps before adding duplicate records. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A green review can imply more than its evidence supports when preview results are presented as production truth. Explicit limitations let a reviewer approve the concrete work without accidentally endorsing unfinished operational promises.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inspect the changed artifact before claiming that a fix is complete
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify a fix in the artifact and its behavior before calling it complete. A commit message, review comment or remembered rule describes intent; none proves that the relevant code changed. Reopen the affected file, inspect the diff and run the smallest meaningful check of the original defect. When the same verification failure recurs across sessions, turn it into a concrete workflow rule. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fluent descriptions can create a false sense of completion. Reading the actual result interrupts that substitution and turns retrospective observations into a behavior that prevents the next missed fix.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Report each quality gate independently and treat missing audit output as an unfinished check
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful accessibility scan does not establish that performance or design review passed. Check representative pages at 1440, 768 and 375 px, inspect horizontal overflow and controls, and verify live response codes, content types, redirects and security headers. Record each result separately. If Lighthouse produces no JSON report, its gate remains unfinished regardless of other successes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separate evidence prevents a reassuring collection of green checks from concealing an untested requirement. Human approval can authorize release, but it cannot manufacture missing audit results.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Record release exceptions explicitly and complete missing checks after deployment
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When an authorized release omits a required check, record the exception and follow-up work. List completed checks, omitted checks, the release decision and the steps needed to close the gap. Keep accessibility, visual review, content accuracy and performance findings distinct. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Permission to release does not establish complete verification. An explicit exception record lets the next maintainer finish the missing work without mistaking approval for evidence that every check passed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Point printed QR codes at a short path with a temporary redirect and test the full path
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Point a printed QR code at a short path you control, such as /go/spring-fair, and forward it to the real page with a temporary redirect (302 or 307) so you can re-point it later. Never use a permanent 301 for a printed target. Test the exported image itself: decode it, open the decoded address, follow the redirect and confirm the intended page. Repeat after any change to those routes or to the destination. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Browsers cache permanent redirects, so a printed code tied to one can never be moved. A code that scans is not proof that it lands on the right page; only the full path test shows what a visitor receives.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test design gates at their boundaries and inspect SVG attributes as well as CSS
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Design-system checks should inspect every rendering surface where a forbidden value can appear, including SVG presentation attributes and CSS declarations. For an accessible figure, verify that a semantic HTML alternative represents each unique interactive item and that decorative SVG is hidden from assistive technology only when the equivalent meaning is available. Test caps exactly at the limit and just above it; a local three-accents-per-panel rule should accept 21 accents across seven panels. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Negative mutations prove rejection, while boundary-positive controls prevent overly strict checks from shrinking the permitted design space. Restoring fixtures after mutation tests keeps subsequent results trustworthy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bind verification logs to the exact build they tested
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Every verification log should identify the exact served build it tested. Record a deterministic artifact-tree digest and source revision, then compare them with the handoff build. Complete commit hooks before the final build, run checks against that build and prevent unnoticed artifact changes afterward. Verify that the server actually serves the hashed directory; caches or an incorrect root can invalidate the association. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Timestamps show ordering, not identity. Late edits and hook-driven rebuilds can leave plausible green logs beside different output. Treat the provenance mechanism as provisional until a deliberate artifact change causes the comparison to fail.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prove build-provenance checks fail when the tested artifact changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate artifact provenance by deliberately changing the build after verification and confirming that its old logs are rejected. Stamp each log with the served artifact digest and source revision. Introduce a controlled change that alters output, rebuild, verify the mismatch, then restore and rebuild before rerunning affected checks. Also compare served responses with the hashed artifacts or expose a trustworthy build marker. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A digest printed in a report provides little protection unless comparison is enforced. Timestamp checks may still pass after an unrecorded rebuild. The deliberate mismatch proves the guard detects changed content rather than merely checking that verification happened recently.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Budget verification across roles and rerun checks according to change impact
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verification plans need a runtime budget, clear ownership and explicit rerun rules. Separate a fast core from expensive sweeps, assign each heavy check to a responsible stage and avoid duplicating it automatically across roles. After a late fix, rerun the core and checks reachable through the changed dependencies; record the build identity of any reused evidence. An example escalation threshold is 90 minutes of verification, after which the remaining coverage is reported explicitly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Individually reasonable gates can accumulate into hours when every small change restarts multiple full suites. Budgeting preserves useful rigor by asking who already checks a condition and how often it must be checked.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify deployments with a marker unique to the expected build
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A deployment watcher should identify the expected build using a marker absent from the previous build. Prefer a generated build identifier over a generic class or text fragment that may already exist. Establish the previous value before deployment when possible, then poll for the expected value while accounting for caching. If the first poll already matches a verified unique identifier, the deployment may simply have completed before polling began. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A common marker can report success while the old page is still served. Observing a false-to-true transition is useful evidence, but exact build identity is the essential property; a first-poll match alone is neither proof nor failure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reuse older test evidence only with an explicit dependency-based justification
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Older verification results may support a newer build only when a documented change-impact analysis shows their subject is unaffected. Preserve each log's original artifact digest and revision; never relabel it as a fresh run. Inspect changes and relevant dependencies, including shared components, styles, data and build configuration. Whole-page measures such as Lighthouse, document bytes and layout shift can be affected even by text changes. Rerun reachable checks and retain a small independent sample. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Artifact identity prevents stale claims, while dependency-aware reuse prevents needless full-suite repetition. A diff summary alone cannot establish independence; the reasoning connecting changes to each reused check must travel with the evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reuse test evidence only when a documented change-impact analysis supports it
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After a late change, rerun affected gates and reuse earlier logs only with a written explanation of why their inputs remain unchanged. Stamp logs with the tested build and report each remaining failure independently. Distinguish application boot work from renderer or environment overhead rather than treating all timing failures as equivalent. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Selective verification is defensible when its dependency reasoning is visible. A fast first pass remains useful with named defects; concealing them behind an overall passing score makes the next iteration harder to plan.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prove environment-sensitive fixes with a failing control under production conditions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate an environment-sensitive fix using the deployed policy and a deliberately reverted implementation. For a CSP-related animation failure, the reverted version should fail under the production header while demonstrating why a weaker local setup missed it. Check layer activation, motion, frame-zero appearance and console violations together. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A green local test is insufficient when the environment caused the defect. A discriminating control shows that the new gate detects the actual failure mechanism rather than merely confirming that some animation exists.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate automated release evidence from human review
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A release checklist should distinguish reproducible technical checks from judgments that still require human review. Rebuild from a clean checkout, compare output hashes where builds are deterministic, run lint and build verification, and probe every route at representative widths for console errors and expected HTTP status. Record outstanding checks for physical devices, transitions and copy separately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Passing automation establishes only what those checks observe. An explicit list of unresolved judgments prevents a successful build from being mistaken for a fully reviewed experience.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Confirm test mutations reach the active build before judging the check
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify that an intentional defect changes the code path delivered to the test environment. For an invented museum gallery, a mutation to an unused rendering branch cannot demonstrate whether a visual check detects broken image placement. Confirm the selected variant and inspect the rendered defect before interpreting the test result. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A source edit proves only that text changed. Mutation evidence requires an observable defect in the artifact under test and a corresponding failure from the intended check.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Show an aesthetic check failing on a known defect before using it to accept a repair
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Save a known defective build and confirm that a new visual check rejects it before using the check to accept a repair. For an invented halo effect, use a visibly broken transition as the negative control and calibrate the metric against an independently accepted reference. Repeat repaired runs at each relevant viewport size. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A proposed fix and a convenient threshold can agree without detecting the original defect. Baseline failure and repeatable repaired results provide stronger evidence that the check distinguishes the intended states.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure a mutation's delivered strength before trusting its test result
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A visual mutation must affect the shipped variant at the claimed strength before it can validate a gate. CSS brightness(3) on near-white content can deliver much less than three times the measured light because of clipping. Additive clones using plus-lighter may provide a stronger mutation, but measure their result too. Log the modified layer, active build variant and delivered effect. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An inactive shader edit, a no-op parameter change or a clipped multiplier can leave a sound gate green. Distinguishing a faulty mutation from a faulty gate prevents false conclusions about test sensitivity.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reproduce a measurement before reusing its threshold
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before reusing a visual threshold, run the new measurement code on the accepted reference and reproduce its reading. Preserve crop order, filtering, exclusions, color handling and resampling. If any step changes, recalibrate the threshold for that method. Store the measurement recipe with its results and distinguish recorded readings from approximations. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Applying an old threshold to a changed measurement can reject the very reference that justified it. Reproducibility establishes whether the values are comparable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Calibrate visual thresholds against independently accepted and rejected artifacts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before a numeric visual threshold blocks a change, measure independently accepted and rejected artifacts using the same method on final encoded assets. Use an accepted reference chosen before the candidate. For subtle illumination, establish both presence and excess limits, then confirm that absent and amplified variants fail. Version justified recalibrations and rescore earlier examples. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Arbitrary thresholds can reward inferior output. Investigate the measurement when accepted work fails; repair the artifact when a valid check detects a real defect. Numeric precision cannot substitute for calibration.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build command-line tools incrementally and test real service behavior before release
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Develop service-backed CLIs in stages: establish core commands, extend the architecture, test representative live integrations, and repair observed failures. Use code review and automated checks throughout, but also inspect real outputs for incorrect endpoints, redirects, missing citations, and incompatible response formats. A 9.8/10 review target cannot substitute for these checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Structural review and live execution reveal different failure classes. Start with bounded integration tests before expensive stress testing. Use credentials from your own key file or the platform's secret store, never from the repo or chat, and define cost and request limits before exercising external APIs.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose acceptance gates that match the work each pipeline stage performs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Extraction stages should pass fidelity checks, while implementation stages should pass functional, visual, and accessibility checks. For extraction, verify page counts, asset resolution, intended HTML structure, screenshot correspondence, and handoff completeness. For an Astro build, add rendering checks, Lighthouse diagnostics, axe checks, and requirements specific to the site. Keep subjective review scores separate from executable evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Applying the same numerical score to every stage obscures what success means. A polished review narrative cannot compensate for missing extracted pages, and perfect file counts cannot establish a usable interface. Stage-specific gates make failures actionable and completion claims easier to audit.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate experimental conformance warnings from established release requirements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep experimental conformance checks advisory until their rules and implementation are dependable. Continue enforcing established release checks, and investigate warnings against the specification before labeling them product defects. A media-type allowlist warning may reflect a tool limitation when the relevant schema permits an open media-type string. Record the discrepancy and define promotion criteria for the new check. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An immature validator can block correct releases, but ignoring every warning can hide real defects. Evidence-based classification preserves both delivery and accountability.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate catalog semantics before writing generated output
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A catalog generator should reject invalid output before writing a manifest. Validate identifiers against the selected schema, enforce exactly one of url or data where required, and check configured representative-query bounds such as 2–5. Exit nonzero with actionable diagnostics on failure, and avoid leaving a partially written artifact. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Build-time rejection catches inexpensive, visible failures before they become obscure agent-call errors. Internal checks are a first gate; independent validation still matters because a generator can misunderstand its own contract.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Regenerate and compare derived artifacts independently in every repository
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Prove generated-artifact freshness separately for every repository in a rollout. Run the generator with its stdout mode, if available, against that repository's current sources and compare the result with the committed catalog. Require an empty diff for each site, alongside schema validation. Keep generation deterministic so the comparison is meaningful. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A valid catalog may still be stale. Schema conformance establishes structural acceptability; regeneration establishes that the artifact faithfully represents the sources that future builds will use.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test omission rules with both empty and populated fixtures
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify a capability omission rule in both directions using an isolated fixture. Confirm that empty input emits zero entries, then add one valid capability and confirm that exactly one appropriate entry appears. Include an unrelated discovery document to test classification boundaries. Compare source-tree digests before and after if testing begins from a copied repository. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A passing empty-input test can hide a generator that always skips a site. The populated case demonstrates that the rule responds to actual content.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Ship browser execution widgets only after testing independent failure states and recovery behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Browser execution widgets need explicit failure-state tests alongside successful execution tests. Test a blocked CDN, disabled JavaScript, unavailable WebAssembly and a throttled connection separately. Provide an advisory timeout and a hard timeout, require explicit success before displaying a passing verdict, and preserve a useful static fallback. Verify editor bounds, font and resize refits, keyboard escape paths and visible authoring errors. Use fresh execution namespaces, identify user-code errors clearly, and support rescanning if markup can arrive later. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful demonstration exercises only one branch. These checks target stranded controls, misleading results and inaccessible editors that remain hidden during happy-path testing.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Centralize values whose disagreement causes silent cross-system failures
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Name shared values once when several subsystems must agree for correct behavior.
