For browser Python execution, the reported filename, virtual-filesystem source path and traceback filtering rule should derive from the same constant. Where values necessarily exist in separate systems, such as JavaScript editor bounds and CSS limits, add a consistency check. Escape filenames appropriately if building regular expressions from them. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These mismatches may never throw an exception: they can merely hide source lines, expose runtime frames or truncate an editor. Explicit coupling and focused checks catch failures that ordinary crash monitoring cannot see.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prove environment isolation with observable checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test that a deployment wrapper removes ambient credentials rather than trusting its implementation. Seed harmless sentinel variables matching relevant credential prefixes, execute the wrapper and verify that none survive before the intended credentials are loaded. Inspect variable names without printing values, and check the resulting account identity through a read-only request. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A clean-environment design is only a claim until exercised. A rejected API request can help diagnose credential selection, but an error alone does not establish account identity; combine environment checks with a positive identity or scope check.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give automated preview checks a scoped service identity and test both access outcomes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test protected previews both without credentials and with a dedicated automation identity. Cloudflare Access service-token policies supported authenticated checks using client ID and secret headers (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Store credentials in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat, and avoid exposing them in command arguments or logs. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A login redirect proves denial, while a successful service request proves that automation can reach the application. Both are necessary. Deploy new form behaviour to the protected preview first and require the relevant tests to pass before promotion. Investigate secret-scanner findings rather than routinely bypassing the scanner.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Identify builds by branch and revision, then probe production without creating records
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Match deployment results by branch, revision and environment rather than commit alone. The same commit can finish successfully on preview before its production build has even queued. After deployment, exercise validation and rejection paths that should create no records: invalid fields, missing bot tokens and preview-only dummy tokens submitted to production. Compare database counts before and after. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A watcher that selects the wrong build can report success for work that has not deployed. Negative probes provide useful production evidence without sending unnecessary email or polluting stored submissions. Proving that test credentials fail in production is especially valuable when preview testing depends on them.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Missing lint configuration must produce an explicit outcome
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A conditional lint check must report missing configuration instead of silently declaring success. For editorial checks, define whether absent budget metadata triggers documented defaults or a configuration failure. An example default policy is headlines of 4–12 words, subheads of at most 20 words, and hero headline-plus-subhead pairs of at most 30 words. Print which policy branch ran and which fields it checked. Include a fixture with a 24-word subhead and no explicit budget block. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A green result is misleading when no relevant assertion executed. Visible branch reporting distinguishes a real pass from a skipped check and prevents changes in document structure from quietly disabling quality controls.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test advertised retrieval capabilities through the public interface
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Add a regression test for each advertised retrieval capability through the interface users actually invoke. Audit exposed operations, supported encoders and result confidence alongside storage structure. Include invented searchable images and verify returned results through the public entry point. Image tables alone do not establish image search support. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A feature can remain broken or unreachable when tests exercise only ingestion. Public-interface tests expose missing connections and help preserve usable behavior during refactoring.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate image retrieval coverage, ranking, failure handling and encoder compatibility
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Image retrieval acceptance should cover ingestion coverage, ranking quality, failure states and embedding compatibility. Count eligible files and files with indexed images separately. Use invented images and labeled queries with expected matches, measure recall at a chosen result count, and include unrelated queries that should return no confident match. Test missing indexes, loading errors and incompatible query encoders. Record results in an acceptance report. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Successful indexing does not establish useful search. Explicit compatibility checks catch accidental routing through an encoder that produces plausible but invalid results.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check stored vectors and text-to-image pairing with complementary fixtures
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate image embeddings with both self-distance checks and an invented text-to-image ranking fixture. Re-encode sampled stored images using the indexing metric and normalization, then compare distances against a locally validated tolerance. Separately verify that a caption encoded by the paired text encoder ranks its expected image within the chosen result count. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Self-distance can detect sampled image-encoder drift but cannot establish correct text-to-image pairing. The two checks provide complementary evidence that configuration labels alone cannot supply.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate content rules against each block's destination
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Tag copy blocks by destination and run checks against the rules that apply where each block will appear. Distinguish page body, shared disclosure, footer, and independently exported text. Inspect rendered includes and claim ceilings after editorial rules change, rather than checking only draft placeholders. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A document-wide search cannot reliably distinguish a prohibited repetition from a required disclosure. Destination-aware checks make large content sweeps reproducible and reduce the chance that an apparently clean draft becomes misleading when its fragments are assembled into pages or reused elsewhere.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Require important build gates to detect deliberate defects before trusting green results
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate structural checks by introducing representative defects and confirming that the checks fail. Useful cases include an unsafe redirect, a missing noindex header, an internal note bundled for browsers, and an inaccessible navigation state. After fixing each defect, rerun the same check to establish red-to-green evidence. Production builds should reject unfinished strings and unsafe test configuration regardless of whether deployment starts in CI or a local shell. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A passing gate proves little if its detector never observed the failure it claims to prevent. Deliberate fault injection exposes checks that merely mirror the builder's assumptions, while production guards prevent alternate deployment paths from bypassing those checks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Fix noisy detectors instead of excluding entire asset types from inspection
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Repair a scanner's false-positive rule rather than removing CSS, SVG, or other broad asset classes from its scope. Test externally proposed defects such as an inline visual effect, stale text in generated Markdown, or hidden success content leaking into a text representation. Cover all relevant routes, mobile and desktop widths, panel bounds, repeat submissions, and malformed requests. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Exclusions introduced to silence one nuisance can create much larger blind spots. Independent mutation cases reveal what a check actually observes, while an explicit coverage matrix exposes gaps that a long list of passing assertions can conceal.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test both false positives and true positives when changing leak-detection rules
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Every leak-detector correction needs paired regression cases showing that harmless content passes and representative sensitive content still fails. Distinguish CSS color tokens, font paths, and sitemap names from identifier-like text using context-aware matching. Update both generated configuration and its source so regeneration preserves the fix. Restore previously excluded asset classes and rerun the complete scanner. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reducing noise can accidentally weaken protection. Broadly stripping text is especially risky when the same syntax could carry a real leak. Paired fixtures and whole-corpus checks make the intended boundary visible rather than treating fewer alerts as automatic evidence of improvement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distinguish missing configuration from an unreadable response
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A configuration checker must distinguish a missing requirement from a response it cannot interpret. Validate the response structure before inspecting fields. Treat an absent container or an unexpected list-versus-object shape as a schema error rather than empty configuration. Report separate outcomes for success, missing requirements and unknown structure. Display safe names and types without values, and exercise valid and invalid fixtures. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Parser defects can resemble deployment failures. Reporting what the checker recognized makes its conclusions auditable and prevents confidence in checks that never reached the intended data.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Enforce logging promises across the full application import graph
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Enforce an error-only logging policy across every module reachable from server entry points, including scheduled handlers. Prefer syntax-aware checks that cover dot notation, brackets, optional chaining, destructuring, and aliases. Plant a failing example for each supported spelling and a permitted example to detect overblocking. Audit platform-generated request logs separately, and constrain error payloads as well as logging methods. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Scanning only an entry file misses shared-library logs. Permitting console.error does not itself make logged content private, and application lint cannot establish the behavior of infrastructure logging outside the source tree.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Certify the deployed artifact and configuration for the exact revision pushed
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Declare a deployment ready only after checking its expected artifact and revision-bound configuration. Require a probe route to return 200 with a marker unique to the new build, and inspect required binding names and types on the matching deployment. Use separate outcomes for a mismatched revision, an unfamiliar response schema, and a confirmed missing binding. Record the inspected deployment identifier in the deployment report. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A green push, an old page returning 200, or a configuration check against another revision can all create false confidence. Binding evidence to the actual release prevents those observations from being substituted for proof.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test deployment guards where a failed guard cannot reach production
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test dangerous-action guards in an environment where bypassing them cannot execute the dangerous action. Evaluate the decision function directly across argument variants, use a temporary repository with a fake trigger, or inject a local-only transport. If using a PATH shim, prove that it refuses remote operations before testing the wrapper. Include alternate flag positions and subcommand forms. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Running a real deployment to see whether its guard stops it makes the test's safety depend on the unproven guard. A harmless execution boundary lets a failing test reveal the defect without publishing an unintended build.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define a guard's forbidden class before testing individual examples
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Specify what a guard refuses as a complete class, then derive test cases from the relevant grammar or authoritative value set. Cover alternate CLI argument positions, normalized whitespace, and indirect language references such as aliases and destructuring. Use a parser when syntax matters; a naive comment stripper may mistake a URL inside a string for a comment. Plant one forbidden example per spelling and include valid controls. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Testing only the first suspicious example proves little about coverage. A definition-driven inventory reveals omissions systematically and prevents successive reviewers from rediscovering equivalent bypasses one at a time.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test shared denylists for both missed variants and ordinary-language collisions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Changes to a shared content denylist need both leak-detection tests and site-wide false-positive checks. Registry-derived names may omit shortened forms, aliases, or module names; add supported variants deliberately. Test case folding and word boundaries against ordinary language, and use scoped rules when a term is forbidden only on particular pages. Run the scanner on approved fixtures and generated output before adopting the update. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A rule that correctly catches sensitive vocabulary in one context may block harmless prose elsewhere. Derivation alone guarantees coverage only for the exact forms present in the source registry.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test configuration refusals with isolated simulated inputs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test configuration validation through an isolated decision interface using simulated inputs. For an invented museum media uploader, cover supported formats, unsupported formats, missing settings and malformed declarations without starting real uploads. Confirm that the launcher interprets accepted settings consistently with the validator. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Successful setup does not prove that invalid configurations are rejected. Isolated refusal tests expose missing checks without triggering costly or disruptive operations.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prove offline builds with denied network access and controls that catch missing safeguards
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Prove an offline-build claim by completing a representative build with network access denied at the process boundary. Preinstall required artifacts, run the acceptance suite, and retain its transcript. Separately test loader arguments and environment enforcement so removing a safeguard causes a failure even with a warm cache. List every pinned revision and compare repeated builds under controlled conditions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A configuration diff proves intent, while execution under denied network access proves the tested path works offline. Revision pins support reproducibility but do not establish determinism on their own.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify deployment arrival with a new artifact marker and validate rendered output
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful push does not prove that the intended artifact reached its destination. Before deploying, confirm a release-specific marker is absent; afterward, poll the intended URL until that marker appears and check the response. Also inspect generated output for unresolved includes and verify any intended access restrictions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An old marker can pass against a stale deployment. Pairing a before-and-after probe with build validation distinguishes source control success from actual delivery and catches templates that compiled without producing the expected public content.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate assembled content because defects can cross component boundaries
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Run text checks on the assembled artifact as well as individual content slots. A six-word repetition rule can fail across adjacent slots even when every slot passes alone. Exercise the check with planted boundary cases, and account for claims repeated in diagrams, accessible text alternatives and Markdown exports. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers and downstream gates encounter combined output rather than isolated source fields. Testing only the parts misses interactions introduced during assembly, while checking only one rendering overlooks claims that travel through other surfaces.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test a passing content gate with representative known defects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A content gate's first clean result should be checked against deliberately defective scratch examples. Introduce representative violations such as a missing planned qualifier, a forbidden phrase or a misplaced status label, and verify that the expected checks fail. Keep the valid original unchanged. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Zero findings may mean the content is clean, or that the gate never examined the relevant text. Positive controls establish that specific checks can detect their intended failures without claiming that the gate catches every possible defect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Revalidate a content gate whenever its rules change
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat an amended content gate as a changed validator that needs fresh positive controls. Exercise the new requirements with representative defects, including obsolete wording, missing status qualifiers and unsupported availability claims. Confirm the intended findings rather than accepting any nonzero failure count. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A gate that detected last round's errors may miss this round's revised rule or inspect the wrong field. Targeted controls establish that the updated checks still recognise the failures they were introduced to prevent.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reproduce conflicts between required copy and lint rules before resolving them
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When required wording fails a copy check, preserve a failing control and determine whether the wording or the check is wrong. Test the exact phrase, inspect the rule's intended meaning, and document the conflict. Avoid invisible characters or spelling tricks that merely evade matching. A meaning-preserving rewrite is appropriate only when revision is allowed and the rule remains valid. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Passing a regex is not the same as meeting the requirement. A reproducible example makes the conflict reviewable without silently sacrificing either meaning or approved text.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Report validation coverage and reject unexpectedly empty scans
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A check that unexpectedly matches zero fields must not report successful validation. Report matched counts, compare them with expected coverage and distinguish an empty scan from a clean result. Test wording rules with invented allowed and prohibited examples before applying them to website copy. Keep explanatory annotations separate from publishable text. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] False positives can damage correct copy, while empty scans conceal missing checks. A passing result is meaningful only when the validator inspected the intended fields.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test a rule's examples and exemptions as carefully as the rule itself
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Every example and exemption supplied with a validation rule should be tested against that rule's intended boundary. If future approval language is allowed, test both “would let you approve” and the present-tense twin “lets you approve.” Include punctuation, hyphenation and spelling variants where relevant. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A narrow regex repair can accidentally admit a broader class of false claims. Examples also become templates for later work, so a contradictory example can propagate the very defect the instruction was meant to prevent.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Independently reproduce evidence before marking a cross-team requirement complete
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A completion report should include reproducible checks of stored state, user-visible behavior and operational outcomes. Independently rerun the checks most relevant to the published claim, and distinguish a successful observation from sustained reliability. Record skipped runs or isolation faults alongside successes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A handoff can accurately describe one test while leaving broader behavior unproven. Reproducing evidence in the receiving environment catches mismatches between what another component reports and what the website or integration actually depends on.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Compare measured field counts with expected coverage before trusting budget checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Word and character budget checks should report how many fields were found and how many were validated. If a page expects 37 sections, a result covering zero fields is invalid evidence even when labeled PASS. Check unmatched labels, verify headline and metadata limits independently, and retain the coverage report. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A parser can silently stop recognizing content after a format change. Temporary manual checking can establish coverage for a release, but the broken matcher still needs repair so future runs do not inherit false confidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A clean fixture can share the same hidden defects as the output it validates
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate supposedly clean examples against an independent standard before using them as controls. A fixture and a draft can reproduce the same defect because both echo a flawed source, even when the writer never saw the fixture. Test known-invalid mutations and valid near misses, and examine the fixture's own wording for unsupported implications. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Agreement between outputs from a shared source is not independent evidence of correctness. Controls should challenge inherited assumptions rather than certify them through repetition.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make validation reports describe only the properties actually checked
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A generated report must claim success only for properties its checks measure. If a website validator counts sections but does not measure word limits, report those as separate checks and mark untested limits as unverified. Review report templates whenever checks change, and identify older reports containing obsolete claims. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Boilerplate can outlive the implementation that justified it. Precise reporting prevents readers from treating a narrow check as evidence of broader correctness.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test editorial rules against varied truthful text to expose false positives
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Editorial validators need positive and negative examples spanning different grammatical contexts. A broad spelling suffix rule may flag legitimate words such as “specialist,” while a ranking-word rule may misread “local-first.” Test punctuation boundaries, clause scope and verb objects instead of relying only on isolated keywords. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A rule that works on one page may encode that page's accidents. Diverse truthful examples reveal false positives, and prohibited paraphrases expose omissions before the validator is reused elsewhere.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match the intended meaning of a phrase rather than banning every use
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Editorial guards for ambiguous phrases should consider their grammatical objects. “Takes on repairs” expresses accepting work, while “takes on competitors” expresses rivalry; a blanket ban treats both alike. Run early drafts through the validator and add truthful counterexamples when legitimate wording is rejected. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Even source-approved language can collide with a poorly scoped rule. Early checking exposes the conflict cheaply, while improving the rule prevents future writers from making awkward substitutions solely to satisfy it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Generate reported copy counts from the final file after all editing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Calculate word counts and other reported copy metrics from the final artifact after the last editorial pass. Replacing “be” with “serve as” adds one whitespace-delimited word and can invalidate a previously correct note. Use a script to produce sentence, section, and page counts from the same file that will be delivered. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Stale measurements are small factual errors that undermine confidence in the review record. The reliable fix is ordering the workflow correctly, rather than asking editors to remember every affected number.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Rebuild cross-page checks whenever the approved reference corpus changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Re-run cross-page wording checks after another page becomes part of the approved reference corpus. If a project requires a status phrase while also rejecting repeated six-word sequences, newly approved copy can invalidate previously acceptable wording. Add the discovered collision as a regression case and keep valid alternatives as positive controls. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Individually sensible rules can conflict when applied together. Deriving checks from current approved text reveals those interactions; a brief validated against an earlier corpus cannot guarantee that later drafts still satisfy them.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Exclude the target from its peer corpus and verify fixtures before blaming the draft
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Duplicate-copy checks must exclude the page under test from its own peer corpus, including when testing a scratch copy. Build the peer list explicitly and verify that relative source references resolve inside the test workspace. Recheck these assumptions when a page is added to a shared corpus or moved. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Self-comparison and missing fixtures can produce convincing failures that resemble writing defects. Investigating the test setup first prevents unnecessary edits and keeps infrastructure problems from being assigned to the content author.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check repeated wording across heading and body boundaries
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A page-wide token scanner can detect repeated sequences that cross component boundaries. A heading’s final words and the following paragraph’s opening words may form a prohibited six-word run even when each field passes on its own. Test assembled text in reading order and inspect joins between headings, cards, and body copy. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Component-level cleanliness does not guarantee page-level cleanliness. Knowing how the validator joins fields prevents surprises and helps distinguish an editorial policy violation from a scanner behavior that needs reconsideration.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Install source fixtures with the brief and diagnose missing-reference failures at the resolver
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A source-validation workspace must contain the files that its citation resolver expects. When a check reports missing evidence, inspect how it resolves relative paths before rewriting the cited claim. Install the source digest alongside the brief, verify the expected files, and rerun validation after correcting the setup. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A missing fixture can make many legitimate citations fail at once. Treating that pattern as a writing problem wastes review rounds; making fixture installation part of workspace setup prevents the recurring failure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test both word orders when a copy rule depends on phrase placement
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A text check that searches only after a trigger phrase can miss the same defect placed before it. Include both ordinary and mirrored word order in known-invalid fixtures, such as a location clause preceding or following a construction claim. Check that valid sentences still pass. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A rule built around one observed sentence may recognise its shape rather than its underlying error. Mirrored fixtures expose that limitation before a passing result is treated as evidence of semantic coverage.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Replay known defects to reveal the limits of automated copy checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test an automated copy checker against the full known defect set and record invalid examples that still pass. Use invented website copy covering missing terms, ambiguous pronouns, unexplained jargon and incorrect assumptions about service location. Assign uncovered cases to explicit human review. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] One rejected fixture proves only that a checker can detect that example. A broader regression set exposes blind spots and prevents a passing result from implying comprehensive editorial validation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reject a passing lint result when expected fields were never checked
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat a zero-field lint result as failed validation when fields are expected. Verify the checked-item count, expected coverage and detailed output before accepting the verdict. Confirm that the checker rejects an invented invalid fixture and accepts a valid one. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Empty input can produce a success label without exercising any rule. Counts and contrasting fixtures distinguish a working validator from one that never encounters its targets.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Revalidate supposedly valid fixtures when the defect class expands
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Every fixture labelled valid is itself a factual claim that needs review when a rule changes scope. If a location rule expands from models to agents, reassess examples previously accepted because they avoided the narrower noun. Do not preserve their labels solely to keep the test suite green. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A control can accidentally certify the very defect a reviewer later discovers. A new failure may expose a mistaken oracle rather than an overstrict implementation; determine which explanation is correct before changing either.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Run old valid controls first when broadening a validation rule
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When widening a validation rule, run previously accepted controls before interpreting the new regression results. Investigate each newly rejected control against the underlying requirement, then correct its label or the rule as appropriate. Follow with known-invalid examples and a clean passing fixture. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A broader check can reveal defects that an earlier suite endorsed. Treating every new control failure as a regression in the validator would preserve those mistakes and hide valuable evidence about the old rule's limits.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Detect one-word substitutions with seven-word near-copy windows
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A near-copy heuristic can flag seven-word windows matching a reference in six of seven positions with at least three content words. Index each reference window under seven masked keys, wildcarding one position per key, then look up candidate windows using the same masks. Review matches and explicitly exempt wording shared by design. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Exact six-word matching can miss a sentence frame preserved through one substitution. This heuristic makes that pattern inspectable without proving that every match is bad copy. A recorded 0.09-second run is an isolated observation, not a portable performance guarantee.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Compare old and new checks on the same defect and inspect the actual diagnostic
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] To prove a new validation rule adds coverage, run both the old and new implementations against the same planted defect and compare their exact diagnostics. Equal finding counts do not establish equal detection: one implementation may be reporting an unrelated problem. Keep temporary validator copies outside the scanned input tree. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A failing mutant shows that something failed, not that the intended rule caught it. Inspecting the reported location and reason prevents unrelated findings from masquerading as evidence that the new check works.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Scope page scanners to real pages and check what tight copy budgets remove
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Run page-level checks against actual page directories, and separately review factual coverage when copy reaches its word limit. Keep drafts, messaging notes and review artifacts outside the scanner's page input or exclude them explicitly. After shortening a disclosure, check whether it still answers the reader's central privacy question. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] False collisions from non-page material obscure useful findings. A sentence that exactly meets its budget can also omit a crucial boundary while passing every mechanical check. Correct input scope and semantic review address different failure modes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make storage checks enforce the intended boundary instead of banning every API mention
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A storage policy check should distinguish permitted preference handling from prohibited tracking rather than reject every storage API indiscriminately. Define the allowed API, key, source component and operations narrowly. Use negative fixtures to prove that a different key, file or storage mechanism fails. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Keyword bans are simple but can enforce a broader rule than the written policy. A narrow exception makes the permitted behaviour reviewable. Static checks still cannot establish the full purpose or timing of a write, so browser verification must cover those properties.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test storage allowlists against minified output and real user interactions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Storage allowlists must handle production syntax and verify write timing in the browser. A minifier may replace quoted strings with backtick literals, breaking a scanner that accepts only single and double quotes. Prefer syntax-aware analysis where practical; document comment-related false positives in simple text scanners. Permit a generic motion-preference key only in its designated source component and verify its generated output. Test rejection of the wrong API, wrong key, wrong source file and unexpected built-output access. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Static checks constrain call sites but do not prove user intent. Confirm that initial load writes nothing, pausing writes the preference, navigation preserves it and resuming removes it. Verify session behaviour separately; these observations do not themselves establish a legal exemption.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test citation parsers against supported formats and inspect complete results
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Citation checks must support the paths and identifier syntax used by the website's evidence index. Include invented fixtures with plain, bold and dotted identifiers, plus valid references in different directories. Compare unchanged baseline results with changed results and inspect complete machine-readable output rather than truncated excerpts. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated failures can indicate a parser defect rather than unsupported claims. Repair format coverage and manually verify affected references while the checker is unreliable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A passing check with zero matched fields provides no coverage evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat a word-budget check that inspects zero relevant fields as missing coverage, even if it reports PASS. Confirm that the checker recognizes the field types under review, including bullets rather than only headlines and subheads. For a 70-word limit, count the actual bullet when automated coverage is absent. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful exit status can hide a vacuous check. Review evidence should report how many expected fields were found and assessed, allowing a reviewer to distinguish a genuinely passing result from a check that did no useful work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Version visual test criteria with their tolerances, exceptions and viewport assumptions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A visual acceptance rule must specify its measurement method, tolerance, exceptions and supported viewport conditions. For example, a 5 source-image px target with a written ±1 px tolerance accepts 4.0 px; measure the half-maximum crossing by interpolation. Explicitly exempt intentional selection feedback where appropriate and label physically unattainable cases separately from failures. Sweep visible mobile viewport heights from 540–720 px in 20 px steps across widths of 320–430 px. Bound text scrims to the words they protect and reserve performance headroom before adding effects. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Targets without tolerances let quantisation decide outcomes. Version changes and apply them prospectively so a newly clarified ruler does not silently rewrite earlier evaluations.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate proposed performance targets from measured results
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Label performance budgets as proposed until they have been tested with the intended workload. For an invented swim school website, document the browser, device conditions, viewport and graphics settings used for measurements. Check reduced motion, script-free content access and recovery separately from performance. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An acceptance plan describes intended evidence, not completed results. Separating targets, test execution and observations prevents unverified expectations from becoming published claims.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Fail quality gates when expected reports are missing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A quality gate must verify report completeness before calculating scores or declaring success. If Lighthouse cannot launch Chrome, an empty report collection must fail rather than satisfy an all-pass check vacuously. Require the expected route and run counts, validate report structure, and surface launch errors separately from low scores. Long temporary paths can cause browser socket-path failures; use a short task-specific temporary directory when diagnosing that condition. Ensure reports belong to the current run so stale files cannot fill missing slots. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A green summary over zero inputs creates stronger false confidence than an obvious crash. Input accounting makes the gate prove that testing happened before it claims the tested pages passed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Performance controls must account for every layer active during measurement
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A control run must disable every decorative layer that can activate at the tested viewport and scroll positions. Record which layers initialize at each position, and refresh that inventory when page composition changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Unrelated initialization can be mistaken for a regression in the component under investigation. A control is useful only when its actual state matches the intended comparison.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A planted motion defect must survive existing CSS defenses
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before using an injected defect to validate a reduced-motion check, verify that the defect actually produces motion. An injected infinite animation can be neutralized by an existing reset such as animation-duration: 0s !important. In an isolated test fixture, use sufficient specificity and importance to make the intended violation observable, then confirm its computed animation state. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A passing check against an inactive defect says nothing about detection quality. Existing defenses may be working correctly while the checker remains untested; prove the planted condition before interpreting the result.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distinguish detected defects from failed test setup
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Count a planted defect as detected only when the intended check reports its specific failure. A mutation script that throws because changed markup no longer matches can exit with status 1 without running the relevant assertion. Require evidence that the mutation applied, that the defective state existed, and that the checker rejected it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A nonzero process exit combines many possible outcomes, including setup errors and crashes. Treating every such exit as successful detection rewards broken test infrastructure and creates false confidence in coverage.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Classify budgeted code by responsibility rather than import syntax
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define a rendering feature's code budget through explicit entry points and dependency reachability. List the files included in the calculation, and distinguish feature dependencies from unrelated application controllers. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Dynamic imports serve many purposes and do not identify rendering code by themselves. Classification based on syntax can silently charge unrelated features against a budget as an application grows.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define guards by prohibited behavior and test equivalent spellings
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Specify a validator's prohibited behavior before enumerating the syntax that can express it. For a console restriction, cover dot access, bracket access, optional chaining, destructuring and aliases. For a command guard, parse the complete argument vector, including global flags and alternate command forms. For vendor test values, consult the current published set and handle surrounding whitespace explicitly. Avoid regex comment stripping that mistakes a URL's double slash inside a string for a comment. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A guard written around the first offending example only covers that example's spelling. Plant one isolated defect for each relevant form, confirm that it applied and survived existing defenses, and require the intended assertion to report failure. Setup crashes and inactive mutations do not demonstrate protection.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reference centralized copy by key when source checks also scan comments
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a repository enforces centralized copy across source files, comments should reference registry keys rather than repeat registered display text. A comment quoting a requested title can still trigger a source-wide duplication check even though it never appears in the rendered page. Explain the behavior or reason for the change without embedding another copy of the value. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Centralization is easier to maintain when references remain stable as wording changes. The rule is specific to the repository's checking policy; document whether comments are included so developers understand the failure instead of treating it as an unexplained build error.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Require completed and expected check counts before interpreting test results
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Report completed and expected checks alongside passes and failures. Require an explicit completion signal, identify checks that never ran, and distinguish assertion failures from runner errors. Repair obsolete markup assumptions and rerun the suite when an exception interrupts execution. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A plausible pass tally may describe only an executed subset. Release evidence must establish both what passed and whether the planned checks actually finished.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate dependency fixes with cold asset builds and a clean lockfile installation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate image-processing dependency updates with a cold build and a fresh installation from the committed lockfile. Clear or isolate generated-image caches, rebuild, compare outputs, and verify the resolved dependency version. If a transitive dependency is pinned exactly, deduplication alone may not select the intended fix; evaluate a targeted override and its compatibility. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A warm build can reuse old images and falsely suggest that a new encoder preserves output. Separate dependency fixes where practical, and assess deployment-tool updates against advisory severity and validation evidence rather than assuming either immediate adoption or a fixed waiting period is always safer.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep animation planning pure and verify that the live renderer follows the same plan
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Separate a looping animation's deterministic planner from rendering so many cycles can be checked without waiting through playback. A pure plan(seed, n) function can support structural checks over 50 or 60 cycles, while a small live comparison confirms that the page consumes the plan. Test expectations should independently express the intended constraints. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Observing 50 cycles lasting 10–14 s each consumes many minutes. Pure planning makes broad checks practical, but sharing code alone is not proof of correctness; matching two live cycles establishes integration, not every visual property.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Extract shared animation math unchanged and compare it with an independent reference
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When extracting shared animation logic, move the calculations unchanged before attempting improvements. Compare the old and new implementations with identical inputs across representative states and boundary cases. Keep the reference independent of the extracted code. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A deterministic comparison can reveal behavioral changes that visual inspection misses. Browser checks remain necessary to verify rendering, integration and lifecycle behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate motion metrics and verify that deliberate defects actually execute
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Motion checks need calibrated metrics, independent sampling and proof that injected defects execute. For an invented ribbon animation, compare candidate smoothness metrics against representative continuous and abruptly changing motion before selecting a threshold. Verify the mathematical properties of any easing curve and measure its rendered behavior separately. Record explicit evidence that each injected defect reached the tested path. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Sampling interference and failed code substitutions can create false failures or false passes. A metric earns trust by distinguishing known good and bad motion under controlled conditions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Track deployments by build identity rather than commit alone
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A commit hash does not uniquely identify a build attempt. The same revision can run on different branches or be retried after failure, so a watcher that selects any matching commit may immediately report an old result. Record the build identifier returned when starting a deployment, then poll that build and retrieve its logs. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Commit identity answers which source was used; build identity answers which execution succeeded. Distinguishing them prevents stale failures from hiding successful retries and unrelated builds from supplying false confidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Run build and design checks after each implementation part
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Run build verification after each meaningful implementation part, including checks for design-system rules. Encode restrictions such as an accent colour being reserved for outlines rather than fills, and check them alongside compilation and asset budgets. Repeat the complete suite before release. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A rule violation discovered only at the final build can require rebuilding several dependent sections. Incremental verification catches the mistake near its source, when the affected code and design decisions are still easy to locate and change.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reproduce failing checks on the baseline before calling them regressions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Run a newly failing check against the unchanged baseline before attributing the failure to a proposed change. If it fails there too, determine whether the baseline contains a defect or the assertion describes obsolete behaviour. Update stale assertions against the intended contract and retain a deliberately broken case that must still fail. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Ported tests can carry assumptions from earlier designs. Baseline comparison prevents incorrect blame, while the broken case proves that repairing the test has not removed its ability to detect the relevant fault.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Rebuild the intended variant before serving artifacts to tests
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After building an alternate variant, rebuild the intended variant before running any test that serves the output directory. Record the selected configuration with the artifact and assert it at test startup. If a check used the wrong build, mark that run invalid and repeat it against the correct output. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Changing configuration back does not replace files already emitted to disk. A deliberately broken variant can appear to pass when the browser is actually testing another build, creating false confidence in both the feature and the test.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Update test geometry and asset references when artwork variants change
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Audit visual tests for embedded dimensions and scene references whenever a background image or responsive variant changes. Derive geometry from the selected asset metadata where possible, and assert which variant the test loaded. A hard-coded 768 px phone image width is invalid once a differently sized image replaces it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Tests can report failures against correct artwork because they still map coordinates through an older image or scene file. Checking those dependencies prevents needless rendering fixes and keeps the test aligned with the displayed composition.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure repeated-run variation before trusting statistical visual gates
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use at least three page loads and inspect their spread when a live statistical check changes result between runs. Treat that as an initial noise estimate, not a guarantee of sufficient sampling. For claims that an effect is unchanged, prefer deterministic seeds, structural comparisons or identical-input frame checks where appropriate. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A single baseline/candidate pair can mistake ordinary variation for a regression or conceal a real change. Repeated observations expose unstable thresholds, while deterministic evidence can support narrower claims more directly.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Hash build artifacts after the build succeeds so logs identify the output actually tested
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Generate the artifact fingerprint after a successful build, then attach that fingerprint to its build log and subsequent verification results. Hashing the output directory before invoking the build identifies the previous artifacts. Stop on build failure rather than stamping whatever output happens to remain. Carry the completed build's identifier into every dependent test report. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A correct test result attached to the wrong artifact is weak release evidence. Ordering the stamp after artifact creation makes it possible to establish exactly which output was built, checked and considered for release.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make mutation tests introduce a meaningful change that the gate must detect
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate an unchanged-rendering gate with a mutation that produces a substantial expected effect. If the shipped multiplier is 1, changing it to 1 proves nothing; setting it to 0 can create a useful negative control when that disables a visible layer. Verify that the mutation was applied and that the gate rejects the changed result. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A nominal mutation can leave the artifact identical to its baseline. Requiring a real behavioral change demonstrates that the check can detect the regression it claims to prevent.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Share rendering construction with tests while keeping acceptance criteria independent
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Let a rendering gate consume the same light-chain construction used by the page so it measures the configuration that actually ships. Keep the acceptance criterion independent of that construction, and test it with a deliberately defective chain. A provisional implementation reported that recreating the earlier chain caused the gate to fail as intended. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A separately maintained test renderer can drift from production and validate an imaginary artifact. Shared construction reduces that drift, while an independent criterion and negative control help prevent the test from merely agreeing with the implementation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Fail loudly when a mutation cannot be located or applied in a generated bundle
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Make mutation planting fail explicitly when its target is missing, ambiguous or unchanged. Minified variable names are unstable across builds. A structural pattern involving constants such as =.5, =.55 and =16 can be a temporary locator, but still requires uniqueness checks and confirmation that the intended behavior changed. Prefer a stable source-level hook when practical. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A silently missed mutation leaves the original artifact intact, making the negative control meaningless. Treating successful mutation as a verified prerequisite prevents false confidence in a test that never encountered the defect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Rescore unchanged visuals when revising a measurement method
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Run old and revised visual measurements on the same unchanged artifact before attributing score changes to rendering improvements. For an invented glowing illustration, capture a paused reference with only the measured subject hidden. Compare percentile-based intensity ratios with maximum-to-median intensity, and report differences introduced by the measurement revision. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A changed measurement method can change the score while the artwork stays identical. Measuring that offset separates calibration repairs from visual improvements and prevents misleading comparisons across test versions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Record artifact checksums and working-tree state for exploratory measurements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Exploratory measurement logs need a built-artifact checksum and working-tree status because a commit identifier does not describe uncommitted asset changes. Record the source revision, whether the tree is dirty, the checksum of the measured output, and the relevant variant settings. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Many image trials can occur under one commit while producing different files. Without artifact identity, apparently contradictory measurements may simply describe different variants, making comparisons unreliable and preventing another developer from reproducing the chosen result.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify merged visual work with a clean build, preserved invariants and explicit asset budgets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Merging parallel visual changes requires checking shared data invariants and the combined build, even when each branch passed separately. Resolve overlapping configuration deliberately, retain required module registrations and variant relationships, then run a clean-environment build and verification suite. Measure each affected route against its declared asset budget. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A textual union can still break semantic relationships or exceed a budget. Automated rendering also leaves perceptual questions unresolved, so attach remaining visual defects to the preview for real-hardware review.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reproduce a reference measurement before adopting its threshold
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reproduce an accepted reference measurement with the current procedure before adopting its threshold. For an invented image fixture, compare filtering before cropping with cropping before filtering to reveal boundary effects. Record crop coordinates, filter settings, operation order and measurement version alongside the threshold. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A threshold is meaningful within its measurement procedure. Reproducing that procedure prevents apparent improvements or regressions caused entirely by changes to the test.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recalibrate thresholds whenever measurement regions or masking rules change
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Recompute reference measurements whenever an image metric changes which regions it includes, excludes or fills. Run accepted references and candidate images through the same revised procedure before selecting a threshold. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A threshold belongs to a measurement procedure, not just a named metric. Reusing an old threshold after changing the procedure can reject an accepted reference or approve an unsuitable candidate.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate visual-balance metrics against accepted and rejected compositions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before using a visual-balance metric as an acceptance gate, check that it distinguishes compositions reviewers accept from those they reject. Compare brightness totals with measures of occupied area, placement and visual weight, using consistent crops and scale. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A convenient brightness measure may overlook an obvious imbalance. A useful metric should reflect the intended judgment and remain a supplement to visual review.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Count the intended visual shapes and inspect images even when metrics pass
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A visual gate must count the shapes named by the requirement rather than any bright fragment. A star-density check can pass a defective extension if it counts thread fragments as stars. Restrict detection to compact round points and inspect both the source and extended regions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Automated counts can reward the very artifacts a reviewer rejects. Looking at the measured crop exposes semantic mistakes that a green result cannot reveal.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use count-based acceptance intervals for sparse procedural details
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] For sparse counts, use a suitable count-distribution interval instead of a fixed multiplicative tolerance. With expected star counts around 2–13, a 0.5x–2x rule can change its verdict when a single point appears or disappears. If a Poisson model fits the placement process, derive a 95% acceptance interval from the expected count. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Small counts have large relative variability. State the model assumptions and account for uncertainty in the expected rate rather than treating a ratio as statistical evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure deliberate defects before using them to validate a visual gate
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Confirm the strength of a deliberately defective test image before using it to prove a gate works. One excessive-light variant measured mean 3.39–3.84 and p99 74–87, comfortably beyond ceilings of 1.5 and 30; accepted samples measured 0.86–0.96 and 14–17. A brightness(3) variant saturated too early to provide that test. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A weak defect can make a useful gate look ineffective, while an unmeasured defect provides little evidence about sensitivity.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep image-edge probes inside the region they are meant to grade
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An edge-detection probe must stop before unrelated interface controls enter its sampling region. A probe intended to assess an artwork fade can mistake buttons and radio controls for hard image boundaries. In one correction, sampling ended 1 px before the form and used median aggregation to reduce interference from tiny stars. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Region contamination creates convincing but irrelevant failures. Verify the sampled area visually before changing artwork to satisfy the detector.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test overlay structure separately from the artwork beneath it
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Pixel differences across a text overlay measure both the overlay and its underlying artwork. If the requirement concerns overlay shape, inspect computed styles or mask structure directly and report pixel measurements as supporting evidence. A pixel-step limit of 25 passed a rejected rectangular overlay at 3 of 4 sizes in one calibration. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A weak box over dark art can score better than a smooth halo over bright detail. Structural checks reduce that confounding effect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Assert the intended change in built artifacts before pushing a release
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before pushing a production merge, verify that the built output contains the change the release is supposed to deliver. Check representative metadata filenames, new layout classes or expected interface text. A failed merge followed by a successful build can otherwise validate an unchanged tree. Run dependent steps so failures stop the chain, and verify the resulting revision. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Green exit codes describe the commands that ran, not necessarily the work intended. Supply required public build configuration explicitly; keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Smoke-test deployed journeys for media transport, indexing and runtime failures
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Production verification for a video journey should check the deployed page and media responses as well as the build result. Request the public page, confirm intended indexing behavior, test video byte ranges for 206 responses, and inspect cache headers for duplication. Scroll forward and backward at representative sizes such as 1440x900 and 400x860 while monitoring console errors and Content Security Policy violations. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Build checks cannot prove that production headers, caches and browser media behavior match preview assumptions. Record Lighthouse, accessibility scans and real-phone playback as separate checks; a successful headless smoke test does not imply they were performed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reject missing required fields instead of letting plausible defaults report false success
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate required field names at system boundaries before applying defaults that could imply success. If a producer emits 'round' but a consumer expects 'iteration', silently substituting zero can make unresolved work appear absent. Reject the mismatch or translate it through an explicit, tested adapter. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Plausible defaults are dangerous because nothing fails loudly. The same discipline applies to interaction assumptions: test fast scrolling when duration is being used as a proxy for viewing time. Boundary checks should expose the mismatched assumption before a report or interface confidently presents the wrong result.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build motion from the approved artwork's shapes, colours and textures
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Derive interactive effects from the approved artwork. For an invented garden centre, animated leaves should retain the shapes, colours and soft edges of the illustrated planting beds. Reuse suitable image textures and keep the static fallback visually consistent with the live version. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Motion feels integrated when it preserves the illustration's visual language. Unrelated textures or edge treatments can make an otherwise competent effect appear pasted on.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Confirm approved reference assets before deriving visual rules
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain a small manifest identifying approved reference assets, superseded versions and the components each reference governs. Separate explicit design restrictions from implementation assumptions that remain open to revision. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Measurements from the wrong reference can produce precise but irrelevant requirements. Clear scope also prevents a temporary assumption from becoming an unnecessary restriction across the site.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure decorative details and interactive markers as separate visual groups
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Group elements by visual role before comparing their size and edge softness. On an invented garden centre map, decorative blossoms and selectable location markers need separate targets. Compare corresponding elements at the same display scale and inspect enlarged crops alongside measurements. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An average across unlike elements may describe neither group. An element can also appear oversized because of a hard edge rather than its diameter.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reassess text-protection overlays after repairing the background image
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After changing background artwork to improve readability, compare each text-protection overlay enabled and disabled. Inspect the background beneath text, overlay boundaries and expanded interface states. Remove redundant protection only after verifying readability throughout those states. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An overlay that once helped can become a visible patch after the image changes. Its continued use should follow from its current effect rather than its original purpose.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Evaluate text overlays beneath the words and across surrounding artwork
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use matched captures to assess a text overlay's effect on readability and nearby artwork. Check whether its colour improves the background for the chosen text colour, then inspect how far its feathering alters areas outside the text. Calibrate tolerances against the intended design. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Contrast checks alone do not reveal an overlay that unnecessarily flattens surrounding detail. A translucent fill can also change luminance in the opposite direction from the one intended.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: After resizing a text overlay, recheck contrast and newly exposed image boundaries
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When tightening or removing a text overlay, separately verify its extent, colour and integration with the background. Compare enabled and disabled states, then inspect nearby image transitions that the previous overlay may have concealed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A smaller overlay can preserve more artwork while still harming contrast. Removing a broad shadow may also expose an existing seam, so passing an extent check does not establish that the entire repair is complete.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep interactive targets stable and label availability clearly within animated scenes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build animated scenes around stable interactive targets. For an invented swim school, illustrated water may move while lesson buttons remain fixed and easy to locate. Label each offering's availability explicitly, distinguishing lessons visitors can book now from those that are full or not yet scheduled. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Atmospheric motion should support navigation. Shared visual styling must not imply that every depicted offering is equally available.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Animate extracted artwork from recorded rest positions and verify the reconstructed scene
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Extract moving pieces from an illustration, repair the background behind them and record their rest positions. Verify that the initial composition matches the approved still, that pause stops motion and that text remains readable throughout the animation. Choose text-panel opacity through contrast checks against representative moving backgrounds. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reconstruction checks help preserve the original composition and texture. Readability must hold during motion, not just in the initial frame.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve the illustration's visual language when switching from static to live rendering
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use consistent silhouettes, textures and composition in a static illustration and its animated enhancement. For an invented garden centre, illustrated foliage should retain its grain and shape when movement begins. Keep supporting background layers present through the transition. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful technical handover can still look like a visual downgrade. Shared source textures and restrained motion help preserve continuity without requiring identical layouts everywhere.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Judge texture restoration in the final encoded image
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate texture restoration after exporting with the format and compression settings intended for delivery. Compare the encoded result with the source for retained fine detail, unwanted sharpening and changes to larger shapes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Detail visible in a working image may disappear during compression. Increasing restoration strength can also revive distracting structure, so both texture and composition need inspection in the asset users receive.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use fine-detail metrics to limit speckle in intentionally soft regions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat high-frequency image measurements as possible noise limits when evaluating intentionally soft regions. Calibrate against accepted examples of the same material and inspect the image directly. Do not require a smooth painted surface to match the edge energy of crisp detail. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Noise can increase a sharpness metric without improving texture. Material-specific references prevent a numerical target from rewarding the wrong appearance.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose directional smoothing to match the geometry of an unwanted artifact
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Diagnose an image artifact's orientation before choosing a blur. For an invented swim school illustration with unwanted circular ripples, consider smoothing along the radial direction while preserving variation around the circle. Compare this with simpler smoothing and inspect for smearing or loss of intentional detail. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Directional processing can target a structured defect more selectively, but its coordinate system and strength must fit the image. It is a candidate technique, not a universal repair sequence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recheck removed image defects after every texture-restoration step
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After suppressing unwanted image structure, repeat the relevant checks whenever sharpening or texture restoration is applied. Compare the final encoded result with accepted references and inspect whether the original defect has returned. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Restoration can recover both desirable texture and the structure a repair was meant to remove. Judge each result on the delivered image instead of assuming all restoration is safe or banning it categorically.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Coordinate image fades and tinting to avoid visible bands and corners
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When artwork fades into a page background, inspect whether transparency alone gives a clean transition. If tinting is needed, introduce it gradually and coordinate intersecting edge masks so corners do not receive duplicate treatment. Review the result at actual display sizes and across responsive layouts. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Independently reasonable edge effects can overlap into a visible patch or band. The transition should follow the surrounding page colour and composition rather than a fixed recipe.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Specify spatial scale and depth separately from illustration style
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe spatial scale, depth and movement explicitly in an illustration brief. An invented lighthouse museum's coastal tour could use foreground rocks, middle-distance paths and a distant shoreline to establish a continuous journey. Decide edge treatments according to where the image meets surrounding page content. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A medium such as watercolour does not determine whether the result is a small vignette or an expansive landscape. Clear spatial cues give movement a coherent setting.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure artwork by visual role before translating style into rendering settings
