Trace the intended code, bindings and secret-bearing version through deployment, and verify production afterward; matching source commits alone do not establish identical configuration.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Order a first deployment around prerequisites and verify each connection
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build a first deployment runbook in dependency order, with a read-back check after each configuration change. Verify account identity and feature enablement; create the repository; pin the intended account; configure static assets and routing; establish preview hosting; back up conflicting DNS; attach domains; configure HTTPS and DNSSEC; connect builds; verify production and preview triggers; protect previews; then add databases, bot checks and email. Cloudflare Workers commands and feature behaviour are perishable (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Permissions alone do not establish that a feature is enabled. Sequence prevents failures such as missing preview hosts or secret updates based on the wrong version. Store secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat, and exercise the full path before declaring deployment complete.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify deployment identity and test that unauthorized targets are rejected
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before deploying, verify the intended account and use credentials whose permissions exclude unrelated targets. Create the credential in your own account, store it in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat, and configure the project to use it explicitly. Inspect package scripts before running build or deploy commands. Use a read-only permission check or a controlled sandbox to confirm that an unauthorized target is rejected. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Successful authentication proves identity, not correct scope. A negative check helps demonstrate that an account mix-up cannot silently become a production write.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prove branch-preview behavior before relying on it for review
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify preview deployments with a disposable branch before adopting them as the review workflow. In your own repository and hosting account, identify the production branch, connect the intended project, and configure preview behavior using current platform documentation. Push a harmless visible change on a test branch, inspect its deployment result, and confirm that production remains unchanged. Store deployment secrets in the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A connected repository alone does not establish correct branch routing. A small end-to-end check demonstrates what reviewers will see and catches accidental production targeting early.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build deployment runbooks from verified steps and expected outcomes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A first-deployment runbook should explain each prerequisite, action, expected result, and recovery step using the reader's own accounts. Start with repository ownership and hosting identity, then document the build command, output artifact, deployment configuration, preview access, and production verification. Record where secrets belong: in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. Verify vendor-specific steps against current documentation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A launch log records what happened once; a runbook explains how another person can reproduce it. Explicit checkpoints make failures diagnosable without requiring access to the original developer's environment.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Investigate conflicting preview results as potentially different execution paths
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A working preview URL and a failed dashboard build can describe different deployment paths. Enumerate triggers, commands, branch filters, timestamps, and produced artifacts before deciding which path failed. Cloudflare preview controls and their relationship to custom triggers changed in the observed platform behavior (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Do not assume two visible activities are independently configurable. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A green custom upload can coexist with a failing native preview operation, leaving operators with contradictory evidence. Reconstructing the actual execution path is safer than disabling an apparently redundant setting whose effects have not been measured.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Document which deployment paths a build monitor can actually observe
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful build API response proves only the workflows that API exposes. Cloudflare Workers Builds responses omitted some native preview activity in observed use (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Compare API results with the branch dashboard and a request to the deployed artifact. Confirm a proposed CLI command exists with the installed version's help before making it part of a runbook. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Monitoring can be internally correct yet incomplete. Naming its coverage prevents an all-green response from being interpreted as evidence about invisible workflows, especially after a vendor introduces a new deployment mechanism.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate production and preview deployment paths and prove each independently
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Configure one intended deployment path per environment and give previews separate data resources. For your own repository, identify the production branch, enforce production build guards, and document its deployment command. Select a supported preview mechanism, configure its bindings and secrets, then test a disposable preview before connecting routine branch pushes. Cloudflare native previews required explicit preview configuration in the observed setup (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An early recipe is a hypothesis until both environments have been exercised. Separate databases and credentials prevent successful preview testing from contaminating production.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define deployment success with build, dashboard, artifact, and access checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A protected preview deployment is complete only when the build, operator-visible status, deployed content, and access behavior agree. Before pushing, reproduce the build from a clean checkout. After pushing, inspect the relevant platform view and verify a marker from the intended revision at the preview URL. Test anonymous and authenticated requests against the configured protection policy. Confirm only the intended preview mechanism is active. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Different observers expose different failures. A URL can serve stale content, an API can omit a workflow, and a dashboard can report a separate operation. Put these checks in the recurring deployment checklist so the lesson survives beyond one incident.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Re-read platform state after changing deployment settings
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Inspect deployment state immediately after changing a dashboard switch and before pushing a dependent change. Disabling a Cloudflare preview checkbox removed an API-created non-production trigger in observed behavior (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Record relevant settings beforehand, compare triggers afterward, and verify that the intended preview path still exists. Treat relationships between dashboard controls and API objects as hypotheses until confirmed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A label can suggest a narrower effect than the platform actually implements. A read-only state check catches deleted or altered automation before a push turns a configuration misunderstanding into a missing deployment.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify the deployed artifact when process telemetry cannot establish success
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Deployment monitoring should verify an artifact tied to the intended revision, not just a successful process record. Poll for an identifiable version or a live content marker, with distinct outcomes for success, failure, and timeout. Include bounded waits and retain enough sanitized evidence to diagnose a mismatch. For protected probes, keep credentials in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat; use restricted temporary files only when necessary. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An incomplete build API cannot prove that a push reached the live preview. Artifact checks answer the practical question directly while preserving uncertainty when the expected output never appears.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat missing deployment artifacts as failure evidence without inventing the cause
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] If a preview still serves old content after a bounded wait, report that the new artifact was not observed and obtain the deployment log. Check the installed CLI's help rather than assuming a list command exists. Wrangler 4.140.0 lacked the proposed preview-list command in the observed environment (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Separate observations from hypotheses about ignored commands or rejected configuration. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A stale page can remain healthy and protected while deployment has failed completely. Artifact checks expose that distinction, but only logs or a controlled experiment can establish why the replacement did not arrive.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate build success from deployment-command and binding failures
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful clean build does not validate the deployment command or target environment's bindings. Read the platform log to identify the command actually executed, then compare its configuration requirements with the repository. An observed Cloudflare native preview ran npx wrangler preview and failed because its previews block was missing; cron triggers were also not automatically added (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Rebuilding application code cannot fix a deployment configuration error. Clean-build evidence narrows the investigation, while the executed command and binding diagnostics reveal whether the platform followed the path the operator expected.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use preview-only migration configuration and independent preview secrets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Apply preview database migrations through a configuration that contains only the preview database. Create the separate database in your own account, verify its identity, point a temporary Wrangler configuration at it, and run migrations against that configuration. Give preview signing tokens independent secrets and verify access protection on the resulting URLs. Cloudflare provided preview base-configuration secret commands in the observed tooling (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Removing production from the migration configuration reduces accidental targeting risk. Independent signing material also prevents preview credentials from authorizing production operations.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use a disposable preview to prove access control and database isolation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A disposable preview should prove both successful operation and isolation from production. Deploy a uniquely named test preview, check anonymous and authenticated access, inspect noindex and CSP headers, then submit one clearly identifiable test record. Verify preview rows increase while production rows remain unchanged; delete only the exact test record and confirm cleanup. Cloudflare preview deletion auto-confirmed in a non-interactive run in observed tooling (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Validate the target name before invoking deletion. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful page load proves neither form bindings nor database isolation. A small, reversible end-to-end experiment exercises the dependencies that ordinary build checks cannot reach.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Remove obsolete deployment paths and keep probe credentials outside repositories
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Complete a deployment migration by removing obsolete scripts and verifying the new live artifact through the supported path. Update documentation and review instructions together so future changes cannot accidentally resurrect the old mechanism. A protected URL watcher should check a revision-specific marker, authenticated access, anonymous denial, and timeout behavior. Keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat; any temporary credential file belongs outside the working tree with restrictive permissions and cleanup. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Leftover commands preserve ambiguity. Temporary monitoring code can also create a credential leak if it writes inside a repository and crashes before cleanup.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Label preview success and production dry-run evidence separately
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A verified preview deployment and a successful production dry run establish different levels of confidence. Verify the preview through the real branch pipeline, inspect its content and protection, and record what was exercised. Use a production dry run to inspect bindings and packaging, but reserve production success for a real deployment followed by runtime checks. Cloudflare used separate native-preview configuration in the observed setup (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A configuration can package correctly yet fail under live credentials, routes, or resources. Explicit evidence boundaries prevent a later launch checklist from inheriting a green status that production never earned.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Close deployment verification in the interface operators actually use
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Include the operator-facing deployment view in acceptance checks when it exposes information missing from automated telemetry. Confirm that the intended preview appears there, then compare it with a revision-aware product probe and access-control tests. State which content is expected at the current stage so an intentionally sparse preview is not mistaken for a failed release. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A technically reachable URL can still leave the person maintaining the site unable to find or understand its deployment. Closing the loop across automation and the ordinary interface resolves conflicting evidence and makes the handoff usable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify secret propagation on existing previews instead of assuming inheritance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Existing previews may require explicit secret updates even when newly created previews inherit base configuration. This behavior was observed with Cloudflare Worker Previews (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Inspect the intended preview's secret names without printing values, then apply missing secrets directly using the supported preview secret command. Keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. If bulk import requires a temporary file, restrict access and verify deletion afterward. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Creation and update are separate lifecycle paths. Verify the fix with one controlled submission and database-isolation checks; fail-closed behavior should prevent writes or email when required security configuration is absent.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify preview secrets survive a second deployment through the actual CI pipeline
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test preview-secret persistence across two CI deployments before treating configuration as durable. A reported Workers Previews behavior was that base-configuration secrets were inherited at creation, while a later per-preview secret patch disappeared on the next deployment (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). In your own account, configure secrets in the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. Test a disposable preview first; if recreation is necessary, verify the exact target and any data consequences. Check required secret names and types after both pushes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful manual patch proves only the deployment inspected. The next real pipeline run reveals whether the fix matches the platform's configuration model.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bind rollout checks to both a build marker and the expected deployment revision
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful HTTP response proves deployment readiness only when it identifies the expected build. Choose a probe route containing a marker unique to the new artifact, then check configuration on the deployment associated with the pushed revision. Return a waiting or indeterminate result while the revision differs. If repairing a stale preview requires recreation, test the procedure on a disposable target and guard deletion by exact name. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Old content may continue returning 200 during a rollout gap. Checking a marker and revision together prevents a healthy previous deployment from falsely certifying the new one.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make preview deployment a repeatable runbook with persistence checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A preview runbook should prove isolation, migration targeting, and configuration persistence through the same CI path used for routine pushes. In your own account, create separate preview data bindings, configure required secrets in the platform's secret store, and apply migrations through a configuration that names only the preview database. Keep secrets out of the repo and chat. Deploy twice, checking a build marker and required binding names on each expected revision. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Local deployment success does not establish CI behavior. Two successive deployments expose transient patches, while explicit evidence boundaries prevent preview success or a production dry run from being presented as a completed production launch.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test preview lifecycle behavior before relying on inherited configuration
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Preview setup should test creation-time configuration, repeated deployment, and database targeting as separate behaviors. Workers Previews reportedly inherited base secrets at creation, lost per-preview patches on later deployments, and did not execute cron triggers with Wrangler 4.140.0 (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Configure your own secrets in the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. Use a disposable named preview for two deployments, and isolate migrations to its database. Guard scripted deletion with an exact target check. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Existing previews may behave differently from newly created ones. Testing both lifecycle paths catches stale configuration, while migration isolation prevents experiments from reaching production data.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check preview runtime secrets when deployed functionality fails
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A preview deployment needs runtime configuration checks in addition to a successful build. In your own project, identify the failing feature, inspect sanitized runtime errors and verify that required secret names are configured for the intended preview. Keep secret values in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. If evidence points to stale preview state, test a newly created preview and repeat the failing request. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A preview can serve pages while a secret-dependent feature fails. Recreating it is a diagnostic option, not proof of a universal secret-persistence rule; verify the resulting behavior before declaring the issue fixed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat preview-build settings as potentially affecting existing preview resources
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Changing preview-build settings can affect existing resources, so verify their lifecycle before toggling them. A reported Cloudflare Workers incident associated disabling the preview-branch build option with deletion of an API-created preview (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). In your own account, record the current configuration, identify dependent previews, test the change on a disposable preview and check both resource existence and its URL afterward. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A control that sounds like it governs future builds may also alter existing deployment state. Treat the incident as a reason to verify current behavior, rather than assuming either the dashboard label or one API response fully describes the consequences.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inspect request hosts when local form tests unexpectedly select production validation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a local form handler unexpectedly requires production credentials, inspect its effective request host and environment selection. Check the development server's documented host and forwarding options before changing application logic. Keep secrets in an appropriate secret store. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A host mismatch can select production validation even during local testing. Correct environment routing preserves fail-closed behavior without weakening validation to accommodate a test setup.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Fail production builds when required public configuration is absent or still uses test values
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Production builds should reject missing or dummy public configuration before deploying a broken form. Define required variables, validate them during the build, and configure them separately for each production trigger. Cloudflare Workers Builds trigger configuration must be checked in your own account (as of October 2026; re-check before relying on it). Keep server-side credentials in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A checklist can describe a cutover step without anyone executing it. An executable guard turns an unnoticed configuration omission into a clear build failure; retry only after verifying the corrected environment.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Assess deployment-tool advisories by exposure and validate upgrades in both build environments
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Deployment-tool upgrades need vulnerability triage and checks in both preview and production configurations. Trace each advisory to its dependency and assess execution paths, CI privileges, and credentials; tooling absent from visitor bundles can still expose deployment infrastructure. A 7-day release-aging policy can reduce regression uncertainty, but should not automatically delay an urgent security fix. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Preview success does not prove production behavior when branch-specific variables control headers or indexing. Pin the selected version, update dependencies, run both configurations, deploy a preview, monitor its exact build identity, and verify live routes after promotion. Use a durable reminder for deferred work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check which handler actually serves each route before relying on Worker-added headers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Headers added by a Worker cannot affect requests that bypass that Worker. Cloudflare routing and asset settings can determine whether reserved paths reach application code (as of October 2026; re-check before relying on it). In your own project, request a missing reserved path and inspect its status, headers, and serving path under production configuration. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Removing a preview-wide header can reveal route-specific gaps that local checks missed. Fix the relevant routing or asset behavior, and distinguish a real 404 from an error page accidentally returned with status 200.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make DNS and email hardening explicit launch steps
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Include DNS, certificate and email verification in the launch workflow rather than leaving them as vague post-launch advisories. Identify the authoritative DNS provider and registrar, follow their DNSSEC setup sequence, verify resolution, enable DMARC reporting, and configure CAA against the actual certificate product. Add renewal follow-up and classify agent-discovery checks by applicability. Cloudflare setup paths and certificate behaviour are platform-specific (as of October 2026; re-check before relying on it). Store secrets in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These changes cross provider boundaries and can fail later than deployment. Explicit dependencies and public verification make the checklist useful to someone operating their own accounts.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reproduce production build inputs and verify the deployed pages directly
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A clean local deployment check must supply the same required build inputs and branch conditions as the production build. Start with an empty environment, explicitly load required variables from your own key file or the platform's secret store, and run the build and verification commands. Secrets belong in those stores, never in the repo or chat; a Turnstile public site key is distinct from its secret key. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Missing inputs can make a production simulation misleading. After deployment, inspect live page markers and social metadata directly; build success and a monitoring script's output do not prove every route serves the expected result.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify byte-range responses on the actual video delivery path
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test the deployed video URL with a Range request before relying on seekable playback. An observed Cloudflare Workers static-asset configuration returned HTTP 200 with the full body instead of HTTP 206 for partial requests (as of October 2026; re-check before relying on it). Use curl -H 'Range: bytes=0-99' against your own video and inspect Content-Range and Content-Length. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Desktop playback alone can miss delivery problems that affect Safari or iOS seeking. If a custom Worker handles ranges, route video requests through it and correctly support bounded, open-ended and suffix ranges, HEAD, and unsatisfiable requests. Buffering whole clips per request has resource costs; evaluate a range-capable storage path when files or traffic grow.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check emitted asset URLs against Worker routing when video needs a range handler
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] If routing excludes /_astro/* from Worker execution, a Vite ?url video import emitted there will bypass a custom range handler. Inspect your own routing configuration and the built URL together. Where range handling depends on the Worker, place clips under a route that reaches it, such as public/video/, and use versioned filenames for cache invalidation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A useful caching default can defeat a separate delivery requirement without changing application code. Verify the final deployed URL with a Range request; checking the handler in isolation does not prove that actual video traffic reaches it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Remove inherited cache headers before setting an asset-specific policy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Overlapping header rules can emit duplicate Cache-Control values unless inherited values are explicitly removed. In Cloudflare static-asset header configuration, '! Cache-Control' was observed to detach a broader rule before applying an asset-specific policy (as of October 2026; re-check before relying on it). In your own project, inspect the deployed response after adding the rule rather than assuming local configuration predicts the result. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A general short-lived cache policy can accidentally accompany a long-lived immutable policy. Reserve immutable caching for versioned assets, and verify that HTML and mutable resources retain appropriate refresh behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Monorepo deployments need the correct package root, workspace inputs, and environment declarations
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A monorepo deployment must build the intended application while retaining access to its workspace dependencies. In your own Vercel project, select the application directory, configure a filtered Turborepo build, and verify that required files outside that directory are included. Declare relevant environment inputs for task caching; keep server secrets separate from NEXT_PUBLIC_ values. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Incorrect roots and missing cache inputs can produce stale or incomplete builds. Use the domain target issued for your own project, verify TLS, and retain independent CI checks even when the host performs deployment.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Document environment variables by service and coordinate shared credential rotation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain an environment-variable inventory that distinguishes browser-visible configuration, server-only secrets, and credentials shared between services. When a frontend server authenticates to a separate worker, both deployments must use compatible credentials; coordinate rotation and verify the authenticated request afterward. Store secrets in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Service-by-service documentation makes missing configuration easier to diagnose and prevents privileged keys from being exposed through public build variables.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify each deployment and content CLI independently before running site automation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A workflow spanning your git host, deploy platform and content CMS needs separate installation, authentication, and authorization checks for each service. Install supported CLI versions from official distribution channels, then use each CLI's supported commands to verify identity and project access. Confirm repository access and membership in the intended deployment and content projects. Check current runtime requirements before installation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful browser login does not prove that credentials persisted or that the selected account can reach the required project. A short preflight isolates setup failures before an automation begins modifying content or attempting deployments. Keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check credential persistence after CLI login before diagnosing repeated authentication failures
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] If a CLI reports successful login but immediately requests login again, verify credential persistence before repeating OAuth. A reported Vercel CLI 52.0.0 incident left empty credential files despite a successful browser flow (as of April 2026; re-check before relying on it). Empty staging files are diagnostic evidence, not proof that atomic rename is the root cause. Check the installed version, filesystem permissions, and current upstream reports. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeating the same login wastes time when local persistence is broken. If supported, use a narrowly scoped, expiring API token through the CLI's documented authentication mechanism. Store it in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat, and confirm identity and project access afterward.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check official integration coverage before automating preview-comment collection
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Choose a preview-feedback collection method by checking supported integrations, history coverage, and authentication boundaries. An investigation found Vercel's Slack integration useful for ongoing comment synchronization, authenticated dashboard extraction useful for historical retrieval, and no supported comment-reading surface in the examined REST API or MCP tools (as of April 2026; re-check before relying on it). Confirm whether an integration backfills earlier discussions before selecting it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Deployment access and comment access are different capabilities. Guessed endpoints returning 404 do not prove that no API exists, and a CLI token should not be assumed to authenticate a browser dashboard. Prefer documented interfaces; treat DOM extraction as a brittle fallback with explicit access authorization.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat indexing, deploy triggers, and public access as separate production-cutover checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A production cutover must verify indexing metadata, crawler policy, deployment triggers, and access protection independently. In an Astro project, inspect the layout's noindex default and the deployed robots.txt. Confirm that the intended production branch can trigger builds. Then test the custom domain without an authenticated session while checking that preview protection still matches the intended policy. Vercel deployment and protection configuration fields are version-sensitive (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful build can still produce a private, undiscoverable, or stale production site. Put these checks in the cutover runbook and verify the deployed response, rather than assuming that configuration edits took effect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify production target and domain assignment instead of inferring them from deployment URLs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Diagnose deployment problems by checking the configured production branch, build trigger, deployment target, and domain assignment separately. A branch disabled through Vercel deployment configuration will not behave like an enabled production branch (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it). A generated deployment URL alone does not establish whether a deployment is preview or production. Inspect deployment metadata and test the custom domain. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A local incident should not become a universal claim that `vercel deploy --prod` always creates previews. If Git integration appears delayed, inspect delivery and build status before creating another deployment. Use manual deployment or promotion only after confirming the intended project, target, and revision.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use the hosting provider's exact DNS target and verify HTTPS before configuring webhooks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Connect a custom domain using the DNS values supplied for your own hosting project, then verify HTTPS before wiring dependent integrations. Add the domain to your Vercel project, copy its assigned DNS target, and create the corresponding record in your DNS account. A Cloudflare DNS-only record is a straightforward baseline when Vercel terminates TLS; proxying requires separate compatibility checks rather than being universally invalid. This configuration guidance is perishable (as of March 2026; re-check before relying on it). Confirm domain verification, certificate validity and the intended application response. Then configure webhook endpoints on that verified hostname and test delivery. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Copied DNS targets and layered proxies can obscure which service handles certificates or requests, making otherwise simple integration failures difficult to diagnose.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify preview deployment targets, protection and production aliases before launch
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Preview safety depends on deployment targeting, Git automation and access protection together. From a directory linked to your own Vercel project, `vercel deploy --yes` without `--prod` requests a preview; inspect the reported environment afterward. Git pushes to the configured production branch may still trigger production deployments independently. These CLI and platform behaviors are perishable (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it). Inspect deployments with `vercel ls` and aliases with `vercel alias ls`. Verify protected access from an unauthenticated browser; a status code alone is insufficient. Before using `vercel remove <deployment-url> --yes`, confirm the exact target and impact on active aliases. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An unintended production deployment can bypass a careful preview workflow. Authentication controls access; robots directives and noindex only guide compliant crawlers. Existing previews still deserve retention and exposure review.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Diagnose deployment failures by separating configuration, authentication, CSP, and browser behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Troubleshoot deployment failures by checking the responsible layer before changing application code. For a monorepo, confirm the framework preset, application root, build command, and required environment variables in the correct deployment scope. For Clerk authentication failures, compare the SDK version with enabled features and inspect blocked requests or cookies. For Turborepo, declare build-relevant environment variables so caching tracks their effects (as of March 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A missing publishable key, blocked auth request, or incorrect output directory can resemble a code defect. Keep server-only route configuration in the appropriate server boundary. Use alternate browsers diagnostically, then resolve the original browser failure rather than treating a successful alternate test as closure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Connect deployment tooling through an official endpoint and inspect its available permissions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An official deployment MCP connection can simplify project inspection and log retrieval, but its tools and authorization scope must be checked before use. Vercel documented the remote endpoint https://mcp.vercel.com and OAuth onboarding (as of April 2026; re-check before relying on it). Add the endpoint through your client's supported MCP configuration, authenticate your own account, inspect available tools and begin with a read-only project query. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A connector can reduce manual token handling without guaranteeing every feature, such as comments. Preview bypass links grant access and need deliberate handling. Keep secrets in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Generate deployment redirects from a validated manifest and strip analysis-only metadata
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep redirect reasoning in a source manifest and emit only fields accepted by the deployment platform. Validate source patterns, destinations, conditions and status semantics; do not assume permanent and statusCode can be combined. Vercel documented a 1,024 redirect configuration limit (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it). For larger sets, evaluate the platform's current bulk redirect or runtime routing options and their limits. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Referrer evidence and rationale help maintainers but can invalidate deployment configuration. Separating analysis from generated output preserves both schema compliance and a reviewable migration record.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define bounded analytics events and verify that events reach their destination
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define custom website events with stable names and a small set of flat properties. Prefer bounded strings, numbers, booleans and null values where supported. Check the installed analytics library's current limits, browser and server entry points, and asynchronous delivery requirements. Avoid unnecessary personal data. Verify an invented test event in the receiving system after implementation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Small event contracts are easier to query and maintain. A successful build proves neither event delivery nor correct property handling, so end-to-end verification is necessary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Debug missing analytics events from browser delivery through dashboard filtering
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Diagnose missing analytics events by checking the deployed environment, browser request, and dashboard filters in that order. Fire a known event, inspect the network request and response, and check for script blocking or CSP violations. Confirm which deployment and domain the dashboard represents. Vercel's recorded dashboard route was project → Analytics → Events, with event details grouped by custom properties (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Missing dashboard data can result from collection failure, environment mismatch, filtering, or processing delay. A successful HTTP response narrows the investigation but does not prove that the event has appeared in reports; avoid promising a fixed discovery time.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inspect DNS state before mutation and verify propagation after batch operations
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] DNS automation should read existing records, apply a narrowly scoped change, and verify both authoritative state and public resolution afterward. Confirm the installed CLI's command syntax and authenticate against your own account and zone. Cloudflare batch operations were documented in delete, patch, put, then post order, with non-atomic propagation (as of April 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An accepted API request does not mean every resolver sees a consistent result immediately. Preserve previous values so a mistaken record change can be reversed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Automated subdomain setup must configure both hosting and DNS
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Creating a DNS record is only one part of provisioning a working website subdomain. Create the hosting project in your own account, register the custom hostname with that project, and configure the DNS record using the host's current instructions. Before mutation, check for conflicting records and confirm the intended target. Then verify resolution, certificate issuance, and an application response. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] CLI automation removes dashboard repetition, but it still needs explicit account scope and verification. A resolving hostname can point to a service that has not accepted it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify SVCB parameters and DNSSEC externally before depending on agent-discovery records
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] DNS record-type availability does not prove that a provider supports every SVCB parameter your application needs. Before deployment, confirm support for SVCB or HTTPS records, the required service parameters, and DNSSEC across both the DNS host and registrar. Provider support and editor limitations vary (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it). Publish a test record and inspect its authoritative and recursive answers with `dig`, checking that parameters survive intact. Verify the DNSSEC chain separately. If necessary, consider delegating a dedicated discovery namespace to a compatible provider. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A dropdown can advertise a record type while accepting only a restricted form. External verification tests what consumers receive and avoids inferring capability from the provider's underlying infrastructure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Plan DNS cutover around ownership, cache expiry, certificates and existing mail records
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A domain cutover should preserve ownership and existing services while changing web routing. Keep registration in the site's operator's account where practical, enable renewal safeguards, and record who controls DNS. Lower relevant TTLs to 300 seconds far enough ahead for their previous TTLs to expire; 48 hours is a planning allowance, not a propagation guarantee. After stability, consider restoring TTLs to 3600 seconds or more. Configure apex and www deliberately, choose one canonical hostname, and verify valid HTTPS plus HTTP redirects with `curl`. Coordinate DNSSEC and preserve email-related SPF, DKIM and DMARC records. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Launch failures often come from stale caches, missing account access or unrelated records overwritten during migration. A cutover plan must protect the whole domain, not just the homepage.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate DNSSEC and public readiness at the correct deployment stage
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] DNSSEC setup requires coordination between the authoritative DNS provider and the registrar, followed by external validation. In your own accounts, confirm nameservers, obtain the provider's DS information, submit it through the registrar's supported process, and verify the chain of trust. Check current provider support before changing records. Protect previews with authentication; a noindex directive is not access control. Run public readiness checks after intended production access is enabled. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A private preview can fail external scanners for legitimate reasons, while incorrect DNSSEC configuration can disrupt resolution. Separate private staging checks from public launch checks and define rollback criteria beforehand.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve the complete DNS zone before changing authoritative nameservers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A nameserver migration requires a complete DNS inventory and verification of the new authoritative service. In your own accounts, export existing records, create the destination zone, reconcile web, mail and verification records, and plan DNSSEC handling and rollback. Change delegation at the registrar only when the destination is ready. Verify parent delegation and authoritative answers with DNS queries; a zone appearing in a provider dashboard is insufficient. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Moving DNS can simplify management, but missing mail records or mismatched DNSSEC settings can disrupt unrelated services. Choose a provider for actual requirements rather than assuming a website migration requires changing nameservers.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Gate production cutover on verified DNS readiness and the agreed release authorization
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Production cutover should proceed only when its documented DNS prerequisites and release authorization are satisfied. Prepare and test redirects in preview, confirm destination DNS records, and check authoritative delegation when nameservers are changing. Track readiness with observable checks rather than a provider's zone-list entry alone. If a separate operator controls the registrar, record that handoff and verify the resulting state before continuing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Human confirmation communicates intent but does not prove propagation or correct configuration. Technical readiness and authorization answer different questions; checking both avoids advancing a release while a required external change remains incomplete.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose an HTTP redirect layer deliberately; DNS records alone cannot redirect URLs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Domain redirects are HTTP responses, not a capability of DNS records alone. Registrar forwarding, edge redirect services and application hosting can each supply that response when configured with the required domain routing and TLS. Choose a clear owner for canonical-host redirects and path mappings, then test their combined behavior. Prefer a direct redirect to the final destination when practical. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Calling forwarding a DNS-layer operation obscures the service that actually handles requests. A blanket rule forcing all domain redirects into one provider can create unnecessary chains and split configuration; select the layer based on testability, ownership and deployment requirements.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Compare canonical-host redirect options by testability, ownership and rollback
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Select canonical-host redirect placement by operational requirements rather than assumed speed or universal superiority. Version-controlled application configuration offers review history and deployment-linked rollback; an independent forwarding service can separate domain routing from application releases. Test actual host conditions, HTTPS, paths and query preservation before cutover, because a preview hostname may not exercise production-domain rules. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Both approaches can work, but fixed deployment times, propagation estimates and reliability percentages are not portable guarantees. The best choice is the one the team can inspect, verify and restore reliably across its actual domains and hosting arrangement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit inherited DNS and transport settings before attaching a new deployment
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Inventory existing DNS records and transport settings before assigning a domain to a new application. Export a backup, identify parking or forwarding records, and remove only records confirmed to conflict with the intended routes. Inspect wildcard records separately because they can send unknown subdomains somewhere unexpected. Check HTTPS redirects, the TLS floor and DNSSEC deliberately; TLS 1.2 is a useful minimum baseline where compatibility allows. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Inherited defaults are configuration decisions even when nobody remembers making them. Also verify analytics in delivered HTML and network requests: a dashboard toggle does not prove that a beacon reaches visitors.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate DNS correctness from delayed provider verification
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a provider reports pending verification, first check public DNS independently before changing records. Inspect the expected record names, types and values through trusted resolvers. For DNSSEC, check the parent DS and validating resolver results; an AD flag is meaningful in the context of a trusted validating resolver and transport. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Registry publication, resolver caching and application verification run on different schedules. Correct public records can coexist with a pending dashboard status. Use bounded retries and a recorded follow-up time instead of repeatedly editing healthy DNS, which can introduce errors and restart propagation uncertainty.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate missing discovery records from inapplicable capabilities during launch audits
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Launch audits should distinguish forgotten discovery setup from metadata that would falsely advertise a capability. For experimental DNS agent discovery, verify the current specification and actual service before adding SVCB records in your own DNS zone (as of October 2026; re-check before relying on it). Use credentials in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A scanner failure may identify a small omission, but passing it is not sufficient proof of correct discovery. Check public resolver answers, target names, advertised protocols, and DNSSEC validation where configured; leave unsupported capabilities unadvertised.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify CAA against certificate issuance requirements and later renewal
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate CAA changes against the certificate authorities required by your certificate product, then confirm a subsequent issuance or renewal. In your own DNS account, first export existing CAA records and record the live certificate issuer and expiry. Read the provider's current CA documentation before configuring issue and issuewild records, and query two public resolvers afterward. Cloudflare certificate products and automatic CAA behaviour differ (as of October 2026; re-check before relying on it). Keep API credentials in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Existing HTTPS can remain healthy after an incorrect CAA change because CAA constrains issuance. Today's successful request therefore does not prove that the next certificate renewal will succeed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate public site configuration, runtime bindings, and contact-form secrets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Contact forms need environment-specific configuration plus server-side validation and secret handling. Configure the public site URL, media URL, sender identity, and recipient destination for each deployment. Keep API credentials in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. Validate submitted fields, verify the bot-challenge token server-side, and escape values inserted into email HTML. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Preview deployments should not inherit production destinations accidentally. Explicit configuration also prevents confusing runtime bindings with variables available during a static build.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Combine repository protections with bounded form input and privacy-conscious logging
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Harden contact forms with payload limits, field limits, enum validation, and minimal logging. Example limits are a 10KB payload, 100 characters for names, 254 for email, 200 for organization, and 5000 for comments; define byte and character counting explicitly. Validate topic choices against an allowed set. Combine bot challenges with suitable rate limiting. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Challenges alone do not bound abusive traffic, and organization names can still identify people. Repository two-factor authentication, branch protection, and secret scanning provide separate protection against source and credential exposure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test email delivery with local interception or controlled receiving mailboxes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Never test live email delivery against invented or unverified recipients; use network-free validation, intercepted requests, or receiving mailboxes you control. Validate payloads locally, then inspect outgoing requests with tools such as respx or httpx MockTransport. If a provider offers sandbox behavior, verify that its required header reaches the outgoing request before permitting network access. Keep credentials in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A sandbox flag can appear to work while an SDK silently drops its header. Invalid deliveries can harm sender reputation, but this should not be described as reducing a DKIM or SPF trust score. Authentication checks and reputation are distinct mechanisms.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Confirm whether a marketing endpoint hosts a form or only receives submissions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A hosted marketing form and a form-handler endpoint require different integration designs. In a marketing-automation platform, a hosted form supplies the rendered interface, while a form handler receives submissions from your own form; capabilities and interface locations can change, so re-check before relying on them. Ask the administrator to confirm the artifact type and provide its supported integration instructions. Browser inspection can help, but URL shape alone is not definitive. Use the hosted option when its functionality and presentation fit; choose a handler when a custom interface is justified. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Treating a receiver as an iframe source produces an empty or explanatory page. Custom forms also transfer responsibility for validation, abuse controls, accessibility and success handling to the site implementation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Diagnose form-handler failures across payload, configuration, redirects and CRM records
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Diagnose a form-handler integration by tracing one submission from browser request to the resulting CRM record. Compare HTML field names exactly with configured external mappings, including case and required fields. Inspect request encoding, HTTPS usage, response status and redirect destination. Verify success and error locations independently from any setting that forwards submitted data onward. Review kiosk behavior and repeated-submission throttling with the administrator; do not assume their effects from their labels. Configuration names and behavior in a marketing-automation platform can change, so re-check before relying on them. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A blank response does not prove that storage failed, and a successful HTTP response does not prove that a prospect was created. Separating transport, validation, storage and navigation prevents random code changes and contradictory configuration advice.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test lead capture through the browser, confirmation page, CRM and analytics
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A lead-capture launch test must verify both the visitor experience and downstream receipt. Confirm whether the integration uses a hosted form or custom form handler, then validate the configured field mappings, HTTPS endpoint, request encoding and success/error behavior. Give an iframe an appropriate title and test its height across devices; 500px can be a starting value rather than a universal fit. Allow only the actual integration hosts in the CSP directives they require. Submit synthetic data from preview and confirm the resulting CRM record and intended analytics event. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A thank-you page alone cannot establish delivery, and an analytics event cannot establish acceptance by the CRM. Provider settings are perishable (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it), so record verified configuration rather than copying an untested checklist.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate transactional email authentication, delivery feedback and real inbox rendering
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Transactional email readiness requires authenticated sending and observable delivery outcomes. Configure SPF, DKIM and DMARC with the mail administrator, verify alignment, and tighten DMARC enforcement only after identifying legitimate sending sources. Use a verified sender and a useful reply path. Test templates in representative mail clients, monitor bounce and complaint feedback, and confirm production sending permissions. Provider sandbox behavior and quotas vary (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it); verify your own account's limits instead of embedding a free-tier allowance in the runbook. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful API call does not establish inbox delivery. Authentication, readable rendering and feedback handling make failures diagnosable. Keep promotional unsubscribe handling distinct from essential transactional messages and review the applicable requirements.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate email-domain setup credentials from the production sending key
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use temporary administrative access for email setup and a narrowly scoped credential for production sending. Create the service in your own account, choose a sending subdomain, and publish the exact DNS records supplied for verification. Resend supported domain-restricted sending credentials in the recorded setup (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Store keys in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat; revoke temporary access after verification. Use a verified sender and the submitter's validated address as Reply-To. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This limits the impact of a leaked runtime key. A clearly labeled smoke test to an address you control verifies actual delivery.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure form duration with a monotonic clock and verify rate-limit behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Measure form-fill duration with a monotonic browser clock instead of subtracting client and server timestamps. Validate submitted elapsed time for type and range, and treat it as a spoofable heuristic. Check whether distributed rate limits are strict or approximate before relying on them. Independently verify anti-abuse tokens on the server. Place test timestamps around the intended interaction, excluding artificial pacing delays. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Clock skew, distributed consistency and faulty test timing can distort results. Timing signals and rate limits provide separate layers of protection, each with limits that deployment tests should expose.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify sending-key scope and distinguish email acceptance from delivery
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Email-provider acceptance is a separate milestone from recipient delivery. Use an explicitly authorized smoke test addressed to an inbox you control, mark it clearly, inspect application state and provider delivery evidence, and confirm receipt when inbox arrival is the requirement. Keep production sending credentials narrowly scoped. A credential loader should reject ambiguous duplicate labels or require explicit selection rather than silently choosing a row. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A database field named sent can overstate what actually happened. Duplicate credential labels also make it easy to deploy an administrative key by accident. Store secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat, and remove only identified test records after verification.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give signup forms a clear promise and one optional question that improves audience understanding
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A signup form should state what subscribers will receive and ask only for context that serves a clear purpose. For an invented amateur astronomy club, offer observing-night updates and one optional question about what the visitor hopes to observe. Keep possible future programs conditional, and ensure the form's storage schema supports the new field. Describe the current organizers accurately on About. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A short, useful question can reveal needs that an email-only list cannot, but willingness to answer should not be assumed. Put detailed limitations in a readable section and place any qualification essential to a headline claim near that claim, so visitors can make an informed signup decision.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify email forwarding with an independent sender and confirmed inbox arrival
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test an email-forwarding address from an independent sender and confirm receipt in the destination inbox. In your own account, configure the forwarding destination, verify it, publish the required DNS records and inspect public resolution before sending a smoke test. Keep credentials in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. A successful send response proves submission, not inbox delivery. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Sending from the destination mailbox back through its own forwarding address can produce misleading results because mailbox handling may suppress or group the message. Limited API permissions can also prevent status inspection without indicating delivery failure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make forms easy to understand, complete, and correct
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Design forms with clear action labels, a single-column flow, optional-field labels, and timely validation. Consider first-person wording such as 'Send my message' when it accurately describes the action. Explain privacy practices positively and truthfully. Validate on blur and clear resolved errors as users edit. Use 44px touch targets as a practical design target. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These choices reduce ambiguity and correction effort. Reported improvements of 90% in click-through, 19% in conversion, and 15.4 seconds in completion lack supporting study context here; treat them as unverified examples, not expected results.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Track successful form submissions without counting arbitrary thank-you page visits
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A thank-you page can support conversion tracking when navigation follows a confirmed successful submission. GA4 can derive an event from page_location matching a path such as '/thank-you' (as of February 2026; re-check before relying on it). Configure CSP permissions for the Google analytics resources actually requested, including relevant script, connection, and image origins. Test the event in a browser. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Page visits are only a proxy for submissions: reloads and direct navigation can inflate counts. Prefer a confirmed-success event where possible, and verify that CSP permits tracking without unnecessarily broad permissions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify Turnstile tokens on the server before processing a contact form
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A Turnstile-protected form must verify its browser token on the server before accepting the submission. Register a widget for your own domain, load the challenges.cloudflare.com widget script, capture its callback token, and send it as cf-turnstile-response. Submit the token and server secret to the Siteverify endpoint; remoteip is optional (as of February 2026; re-check before relying on it). Permit required script and frame origins in CSP. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Rendering a widget alone provides no server-side protection. Keep the secret in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat, and handle verification failures explicitly.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Send transactional email with protected credentials and truthful success handling
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A serverless contact handler can call Resend's email endpoint with fetch and Bearer authentication without adding an SDK. Verify your sending domain and store the API key in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. The recorded free allowance was 100 emails/day and 3,000/month (as of February 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Returning success despite delivery failure can lose messages silently. Report success after durable acceptance, such as a persisted submission or queued job, and provide retries and failure monitoring when email delivery runs asynchronously.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Enforce contact-form limits on the server and keep personal data out of logs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate contact-form payload size, field lengths, allowed values, and bot-verification results on the server. Example limits are 10KB total, 100 characters for each name, 254 for email, 200 for organization, and 5,000 for comments. Trim fields and validate categorical choices against an explicit allowlist. Enforce the body limit while reading, since Content-Length alone is insufficient. Escape values inserted into HTML. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Client-side checks are bypassable. Log request identifiers and outcomes rather than submitted names, email addresses, organizations, or free text. Restricted CORS and bot checks provide useful layers but do not replace abuse monitoring or appropriate rate limits.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep resource downloads ungated by default and enable lead forms deliberately
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Prefer direct access to resources, with optional lead forms enabled explicitly for individual items. Maintain a reusable form route and confirmation page if the project needs them, but point ordinary cards directly to their resources. To enable a form, configure its resource metadata, generated route, card destination, and successful-submission redirect, then test the entire journey. Removing navigation links does not restrict direct access to an existing route; actual access control requires enforcement. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Optional forms preserve a reusable implementation without imposing unnecessary friction. A lead form collects information; it does not by itself establish authorization, privacy compliance, or protection for sensitive files.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match calls to action to real availability and publish resource navigation only when content is useful
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Calls to action should describe an action visitors can actually complete today. A ceramic studio preparing a new class could offer an email notification list instead of a booking button before enrollment opens. Collect only necessary information, explain its use and validate submissions server-side. Build a resource section privately, then add navigation and sitemap entries when useful material is available. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An honest notification list measures interest without promising access. Empty resource destinations and premature purchase language create friction because the interface advertises value that the visitor cannot yet receive.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep contact submission short and move optional attribution questions after successful completion
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Collect the essential contact request first, then offer optional attribution questions after a confirmed successful submission. Save the request in a durable store and track email delivery separately so an email failure does not erase the inquiry. Link the optional response through a submission identifier rather than asking visitors to repeat their details. Validate input and anti-abuse tokens server-side; keep mail credentials in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Optional marketing questions should not block the visitor's main task. Separating storage, notification and attribution also makes partial failures easier to detect and recover from.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use accepted submission records as conversion evidence and analytics as supporting context
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Count accepted form submissions from the application record, and use page analytics to explain traffic rather than establish successful submissions. A thank-you page view can be refreshed, bookmarked or missed, so it is an imperfect conversion proxy. Begin with measurement that answers a defined question; add campaign tooling when its benefits justify the operational work. Review the actual tracking behavior and applicable consent requirements before deployment. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] More analytics can introduce complexity without improving the core count. Separating transaction evidence from behavioral observation prevents inflated conversions and avoids assuming that a cookieless tool automatically resolves every privacy obligation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep related form records in a queryable store with explicit uniqueness and retention rules
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Related contact, notification and attribution records benefit from a shared relational store with stable identifiers and explicit constraints. Use separate tables, link attribution to its originating submission, and enforce appropriate uniqueness for notification subscriptions. Track notification delivery status independently. Store only justified fields, define retention and deletion behavior, and test export and restoration before relying on backups. If using Cloudflare D1, create the database in your own account and verify current plan limits and recovery features before deployment. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A common schema turns attribution analysis into a query instead of an integration project. Exact records also require a different storage model from sampled telemetry.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Configure database bindings explicitly and isolate preview bot-check credentials
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify database bindings after resource creation and keep preview bot-check credentials separate from production. A non-interactive CLI may create a database without updating application configuration; inspect the resulting binding before deployment. Cloudflare D1 and Turnstile supported API-driven setup and published testing keys (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Capture secret responses directly into your own key file or the platform's secret store, never the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Resource creation and application wiring are separate operations. Choose testing credentials through trusted environment configuration, then prove that production rejects dummy tokens; a preview hostname convention alone is insufficient evidence of isolation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Create email DNS records from the provider's current response
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use the email provider's current verification response as the source for DNS records instead of copying an old recipe. Record types, names and values can change; a Resend setup requested four records rather than a familiar three-record configuration (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Confirm the intended DNS account, distinguish relative names from fully qualified names and keep mail-related records unproxied where required. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Scripted transfer reduces transcription mistakes and avoids browser integrations silently targeting another account. Introduce DMARC deliberately: p=none monitors rather than enforces, and external reporting destinations require appropriate authorization. Verification should check the resulting public records, not just successful API writes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make form data usable through safe administrative commands
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Provide simple administrative operations for stored form submissions: summarize, list, export and delete. Treat the database as the record and email as a notification. Exclude test records by default, restrict export directories to 0700 and files to 0600, and make deletion a dry run until explicitly confirmed. Use parameterized queries through a supported database interface rather than interpolating addresses into SQL. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Data is not operationally useful merely because it exists in a database. A small interface makes support and privacy work repeatable. Input validation remains useful, but a restrictive email regex should not substitute for parameter binding or accidentally reject legitimate deletion requests.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: An email integration is proven only when its final delivery is observed
