memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify the complete form-to-inbox path before declaring an email integration finished. Submit an authorized test, confirm application validation and database persistence, inspect the email provider's result and confirm arrival in the intended inbox. Record which parts were observed automatically and which required a recipient's confirmation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful API response proves acceptance by one component, not final delivery. The last hop can fail independently through filtering, addressing or delivery problems. Keep test messages clearly marked and distinguish preview bot-check behaviour from production verification so the evidence supports only the path actually exercised.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Roll out optional form fields with compatible migrations and focused validation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Add an optional form field through a nullable schema change before deploying code that writes it, after checking compatibility with existing readers and writers. Derive client and server length limits from shared configuration. Test whitespace handling, missing values, excessive input, administrative views and exports. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Additive changes still affect positional inserts and strict consumers. Focus deployment checks on the changed behavior and use a test notification destination to avoid unnecessary messages.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate form endpoints before testing their delivery side effects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Public form handlers should restrict accepted methods, cap request size, and validate input before triggering delivery or storage. Implement these checks server-side even when the browser also validates fields. Exercise rejection paths in preview, then verify production routing with probes designed not to send messages or create records. Test successful delivery separately with controlled recipients and explicit test data. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A working form has both validation behavior and external side effects. Separating those checks catches routing mistakes without filling real inboxes or databases, and prevents browser-only validation from becoming the sole protection for an exposed endpoint.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit privacy promises against every data copy and every form response
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Privacy copy must match the full data flow, including inbox copies, exports, backups, logs, and visible form states. Inventory those destinations before writing retention or deletion claims. Compare new and repeat sign-ups across response bodies, redirects, tokens, and conditional cards; identical headline text alone does not prevent enumeration. Generate copy briefs from the actual string registry so fields cannot disappear between planning and implementation. Direct automated agents to human consent forms when an endpoint requires personal consent or an interactive bot check. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A fact sheet derived only from database code can omit the copies that make an absolute privacy promise false. Reviewing implementation and rendered behavior catches omissions that polished wording conceals.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make retention, deletion, and logging promises operationally verifiable
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Publish retention and deletion statements only when their scope matches implemented behavior. Define which records expire, what triggers deletion, and whether inbox copies, exports, or backups remain. Implement the cleanup mechanism before claiming automatic deletion. Verify error reports as well as ordinary request logs before asserting that an address or IP is never stored. Inventory browser storage and third-party scripts separately from server logging. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A narrow, accurate description helps people understand actual handling; an absolute promise creates expectations the system may not meet. Honest scope is essential, but it does not replace checking applicable obligations or implementing required deletion processes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Translate a no-tracking promise into explicit browser-storage constraints
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A design that promises no persistent attribution should avoid analytics records in sessionStorage, localStorage, and IndexedDB as well as cookies. If attribution is needed, consider explicitly scoped information submitted with the current form, such as its page path and an optional visitor answer. Review referrers and campaign parameters for sensitive values before collecting them. Document the loss of first-touch attribution as a deliberate tradeoff. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Changing the storage mechanism does not preserve the intent of a no-tracking promise. A concrete implementation rule prevents a useful-looking analytics enhancement from quietly expanding data collection beyond what the interface communicates.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match retention to the service promise and provide an accessible request channel
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define retention by record purpose and provide a request channel that works when the website form cannot. A seed library might expire ordinary enquiries after a documented interval while retaining a requested availability alert until it is sent or the request is withdrawn. Also define what happens when the programme is cancelled, so abandoned lists do not remain indefinitely. Offer a monitored email route if the form depends on JavaScript. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] One convenient retention duration may conflict with a different service promise. Explicit completion and cancellation events make cleanup actionable, while an alternate contact route prevents technical requirements from excluding people who need help with their data.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distinguish transactional sending, inbound webhooks, forwarding, and hosted mailboxes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Choose email infrastructure by the receiving workflow required, not merely by an already verified sending domain. Resend inbound delivery uses webhooks, while Cloudflare Email Routing provides forwarding rather than a hosted inbox (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). For your own domain, inspect existing MX and SPF records, choose a destination, verify it, and grant only the permissions needed to configure routing. Keep credentials in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A simple monitored address should not accidentally become an application that must parse and forward private messages. Existing domain verification does not establish receiving capability or eliminate DNS conflicts.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Include inbox hosts and delivery-provider retention in privacy data-flow reviews
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A privacy inventory should include the inbox host and email delivery provider, not just the website database. Trace contact copies and privacy-request mail to their destinations, then verify retention and processing locations for the applicable plans. Resend was reported to retain sent-email content and logs for 30 days on specified plans (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Prevent diagnostic output from exposing session cookies. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Email introduces additional copies that database-only reviews miss. If a credential reaches logs, assess its validity, privileges, exposure, and available revocation controls explicitly; one narrowly contained incident does not justify a general rule to wait for expiry.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A form smoke test must verify storage, delivery status, isolation, and exact cleanup
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A live form smoke test should trace one authorized submission through storage, email-provider acceptance, and exact-record cleanup. Confirm the row lands only in the intended preview database, inspect expected referrer behavior, and record relevant counts before and after cleanup. Exercise anonymous access separately from authenticated submission. Treat provider acceptance as distinct from arrival in the recipient's inbox, and report untested branches explicitly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful response alone can hide writes to the wrong database or orphaned related rows. Precise evidence establishes what happened without overstating delivery or leaving test data behind.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prevent sign-up enumeration without orphaning repeat-submission data
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Repeat sign-ups should avoid revealing registration status while preserving deletion and retention links. Match first-submission status, response shape, redirects, and visible UI; also inspect timing differences. If issuing a fresh signed identifier, maintain a reliable association to the existing registration before dependent writes can succeed. A background association needs explicit failure and race handling. Require parent existence for answer inserts, using a conditional SQL insert or transaction; a defined contract may return 409 for replay and 403 for a missing parent. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An 'already registered' response exposes membership. Concealing that response without preserving relationships can instead create orphaned answers that deletion and retention cannot reach.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Handle malformed input without logging parser messages that contain request data
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Catch request-decoding failures locally and return a controlled 4xx without logging raw parser messages. Cover JSON parsing, base64 decoding, and token decoding. Use stable error codes such as bad_body or invalid_token. At the outer error boundary, log only an allowlisted error classification and safe operational metadata; arbitrary exception names also need validation. Test with a recognizable synthetic marker and confirm it never appears in logs. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Parser exceptions can quote fragments of their input. Logging a message or stack can therefore disclose submitted content and turn an ordinary malformed request into an unnecessary server error.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Version consent wording and run its verifier as part of the release path
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When consent wording changes, update the versioned consent record and verify that submissions reference the text actually displayed. Preserve earlier versions so historical records remain interpretable. Inspect package scripts: a successful build does not imply that a separate verification command ran. Run both before releasing changes to form or privacy strings. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Otherwise, a stored consent identifier can point to wording a visitor never saw. An existing check offers no protection when the release procedure omits it; connect the check to the actual release path.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test contact forms through delivery and recovery on the current deployed code
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Contact-form verification should follow the current submission through storage, email delivery, confirmation and any follow-up action. Distinguish an email API accepting a request from the message arriving in an inbox. Exercise provider failures, expired tokens, retries and the no-JavaScript path. If using a 2.5-second fill-time heuristic or a 2-hour follow-up token, test their boundary behavior rather than assuming they guarantee protection. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An older delivery observation cannot validate changed code. Silent failures and unusable recovery messages can make an apparently successful form lose real enquiries.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat data-use purpose as one fact rendered across several surfaces
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A change to the stated purpose of collecting an email address requires a sweep of every surface that describes that purpose. Check consent text, the privacy page, confirmation messages and machine-readable instructions together. Run consistency checks before release and inspect the updated deployed text afterward. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Updating one sentence can leave other interfaces promising something narrower or broader. Keeping a shared purpose definition and an inventory of its renderings helps prevent contradictory explanations to visitors and automated clients.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate query-based form defaults and inspect deployed markup structurally
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate query-based form defaults against the form's allowed values. For an invented bakery enquiry form, select only recognized topics and ignore invalid values. Render defaults on the server where supported, or provide client-side enhancement for static pages. Pass page-specific titles explicitly and provide suitable social-preview metadata. Verify selected options through parsed markup or document queries. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Build tools can change attribute order and spacing without changing behavior. Structural checks tested against known-good output prevent brittle string matching from reporting false deployment failures.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Design decorative form progress with restrained accents and clear independent feedback
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A quiet illustration can provide a decorative progress cue by lighting one element as each form field is completed. For a 3:4 panel, begin with mostly dim elements, one brighter node and a single connecting line; keep text zones calm and cap accent sparks at three. One such panel measured 11.4:1 percentile white-text contrast. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Gradual illumination makes completion feel tangible without overwhelming the form. Keep labels, errors and completion status understandable independently of the illustration so the visual metaphor supports the task rather than carrying essential instructions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Diagnose local form configuration independently from unit behavior and incomplete widget checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A local form returning 503 not_configured on success paths needs an environment diagnosis even when its unit tests pass. Check the startup command, effective host, and runtime bindings before changing request-handling code. Listed binding names alone do not prove that required values are available in the active environment. Store secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Unit evidence for token replay handling does not establish a working browser round trip. Likewise, inspecting a verification widget's mount box at 320 px does not establish that the loaded widget fits or works.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Collect DMARC evidence before tightening enforcement
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Enable DMARC aggregate reporting and identify legitimate senders before moving from p=none to quarantine or reject. Inventory sending services, verify SPF or DKIM alignment, preserve the existing policy when adding reporting, and confirm the published TXT record through public DNS. Cloudflare offers managed DMARC reporting without a dedicated report mailbox (as of October 2026; re-check before relying on it). Keep credentials in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A monitoring policy is not caused by the absence of a paid mailbox. Reports provide the evidence needed for enforcement; roughly two weeks may be an initial observation window, but it must cover infrequent legitimate senders too.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Configure repository transport and hosting API authentication separately
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Successful authentication for repository pushes does not authenticate hosting-service API operations. Load the intended passphrase-protected key into a managed authentication agent and verify the repository destination before pushing. Configure API credentials separately for repository settings and other management operations. Keep private keys in protected storage, outside repositories and messages. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separate authentication paths explain why code transfers can work while management operations fail. Identifying the failing path avoids unnecessary credential changes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate reusable templates from site instances and configure each deployment explicitly
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep reusable website templates separate from site repositories containing private content or configuration. Set access permissions, connect the hosting integration and designate the production branch for each instance. Verify a test deployment before relying on automatic publishing. Check current collaboration limits and integration support when selecting hosting. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separate repositories allow template improvements to travel without exposing site-specific material. Explicit deployment settings reduce accidental publishing and make ownership clear.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Explicitly isolate nested repositories to prevent accidental parent tracking
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An independent repository nested inside another repository needs an explicit ownership boundary. Exclude its directory from the parent repository when it is intentionally managed separately, and check git status from both roots before committing. If the parent already tracks those files, an ignore rule alone will not remove them from its index. Remove obsolete implementations after confirming their replacements. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Clear boundaries prevent accidental snapshots of another repository and confusion about which remote receives application changes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Diagnose Git failures by separating host trust, identity, repository access, and history
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Git troubleshooting is easier when each error is mapped to its authentication or history layer. For host-key failures, verify the server fingerprint through a trusted source before updating known_hosts; ssh-keyscan alone does not establish trust. For public-key failures, inspect the agent and loaded identities. For missing projects, inspect git remote -v and repository permissions. For rejected pushes, fetch and inspect remote changes before merging or rebasing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Layered diagnosis avoids insecure trust shortcuts and destructive attempts to bypass ordinary history conflicts.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Activate secret-scanning hooks after cloning and avoid broad scan exclusions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Commit secret-scanning configuration with the repository and run pre-commit install after each clone. Pin a reviewed gitleaks version, retain default detection rules, and add narrowly justified exceptions for public identifiers. Do not broadly allowlist environment files, which are precisely where accidental secrets may appear. Keep secrets in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Verify detection using a documented synthetic fixture that matches an enabled rule. CI scanning supplies coverage when local hooks are missing or bypassed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep shared skill repositories separate from private project instructions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Clone a shared skill library into its own repository and register it through the agent tool's supported discovery mechanism. Keep private project instructions outside that repository's working tree. Where supported, symlinks can provide global discovery without copying shared files into every project; verify the tool's current discovery and precedence rules before relying on this arrangement. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separate repository boundaries reduce accidental inclusion of private material in ordinary commits and make shared updates easier to manage. They do not make leakage structurally impossible: scripts or manual copies can still cross boundaries. Inspect staged changes, keep generated outputs scoped, and test which instruction version wins when global and project-local names overlap.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make a repository reproducible and understandable to its next maintainer
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Repository hygiene should let a new maintainer install, run and understand the project without private context. Put the project purpose, stack, 3–5 setup commands and deployment overview in the README. Declare the supported Node version and commit one lockfile matching the documented package manager. Ignore generated output and local secrets, while deliberately retaining safe example configuration. State licensing terms, remove obsolete code and launch-only placeholders, and run the configured lint and type checks. Justify TypeScript escape hatches and document ownership when multiple contributors are involved. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Small ambiguities compound: stray lockfiles change dependencies, stale instructions waste onboarding time, and unexplained exceptions spread. Keep useful operational logging rather than applying a blanket ban on every console call.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve repository-host ambiguity before wiring deployment integrations
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Confirm the repository host, owning account, visibility, and deployment target before connecting a site to automated builds. If a brief names conflicting hosts, resolve that specific conflict first. Create the repository in the reader's own account, verify the remote and authentication identity, then connect the deployment service and test a preview branch. Keep credentials in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Familiarity with a previous project's setup can silently choose the wrong integration. Explicit account mapping prevents avoidable rewiring and ownership confusion.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat repository relocation as a migration when worktrees and services depend on paths
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Moving a repository with linked worktrees and path-dependent tooling requires a migration plan. Inventory worktrees, uncommitted changes, service definitions, scheduled jobs, scripts, and editor settings before relocation. Check Git's supported worktree move or repair operations, prepare rollback, and verify repository status and dependent commands afterward. Schedule the move apart from an unrelated active build when possible. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A directory move can leave Git metadata or background services pointing at the old location. Recording the desired destination preserves intent, but dependency checks are what make the eventual move safe and complete.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify private repository visibility and remote contents with separate checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify repository privacy with authenticated metadata and anonymous access checks, then verify the pushed revision separately. In your own GitHub account, create the repository with gh repo create <your-project> --private. Before pushing, exclude secrets, editor locks and separately managed repositories, configure repository-local identity, and run a secret scan. Confirm authenticated visibility is private and compare git ls-remote with local HEAD. Keep credentials in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An anonymous 404 alone cannot distinguish a private repository from a missing one. Remote revision checks answer a different question: whether the intended files actually reached the backup location.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use an isolated worktree for production fixes beside ongoing development
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Create a separate Git worktree when a production fix must proceed alongside another checkout's active development. Fetch current refs, then use git worktree add ../release-fix -b release-fix origin/main. Build and inspect the branch preview, complete the repository's review process and integrate through its protected branch workflow. Before a direct fast-forward update where permitted, fetch again and verify ancestry. Keep access credentials in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Switching a shared checkout can disrupt another task's files and assumptions. A worktree isolates working state while preserving a clear integration path.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bring production fixes into an active refactor before relying on its regression evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a production hotfix lands during a refactor, incorporate it into the working branch and repeat the relevant baseline comparisons. Keep the refactor isolated, label placeholder media clearly and record which component, media and workflow checks are complete. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A branch can pass against an outdated baseline while silently omitting the newest production correction. Updating the branch preserves that fix and makes subsequent comparisons meaningful. Fast-forward when the history permits it; otherwise use the repository's normal merge or rebase policy and inspect conflicts. The useful milestone is reproducible behavior on the updated branch, not merely a list of completed tasks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reuse a managed authentication agent across shell sessions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When shell sessions need a passphrase-protected repository key, use a trusted agent manager to reconnect them to the intended authentication agent. Initialize the documented identity and unlock it interactively when required. Keep private keys in protected storage outside repositories and messages, and configure an appropriate credential lifetime. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Agent reuse reduces repeated prompts and avoids disconnected agents in every shell. It manages access to unlocked credentials without removing the need to protect or unlock the key.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Initialize the configured authentication agent before repository operations
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before authenticated repository operations, connect to the documented authentication agent and select the intended identity. If authentication fails, inspect that identity and the configured agent connection instead of searching temporary directories for arbitrary sockets. Allow interactive unlocking when required. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Guessing which agent to use creates inconsistent behavior and can select an unintended identity. A documented initialization path makes troubleshooting repeatable and keeps credential selection deliberate.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Record existing changes and stage only the files or hunks belonging to the task
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Inspect git status --short before editing an active repository and stage only the task's own changes. Record pre-existing modifications, enumerate files touched during the task, and inspect the staged diff before committing. Avoid git add -A when unrelated work exists; use selective hunks when changes share a file. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Preserving existing work is only half the requirement. Without selective staging and disclosure, a small maintenance change can accidentally publish someone else's unfinished work or obscure which changes were reviewed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prepare collaboration with protected branches, private previews and scoped data access
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Separate repository access, preview access and production-data access when preparing a website for collaborators. Protect the production branch, review feature branches through change requests and provide private previews. Decide whether administrative access is needed before granting it, especially when the account also stores form submissions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A contributor updating an invented bakery's opening hours may need code and a preview without needing visitor messages or deployment secrets. Explicit access boundaries support useful collaboration while limiting unnecessary exposure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Onboard collaborators with scoped repository access and verified previews
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Protect the production branch, grant contributors access to the intended repository and verify their preview sign-in. Check the hosting and repository services' current role and access-control options. Store secrets in protected credential storage. Document setup, local development, invented test fixtures and the branch-to-preview workflow. Add secret scanning to shared build checks and tune routine preview notifications. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Contributors can work effectively without shared account credentials or visitor data. Verified onboarding and centrally enforced checks reduce reliance on individual setup habits.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check lint and staged hunks before committing changes that share files
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Run relevant lint checks and stage individual hunks when separate tasks modify the same file. Inspect the staged diff to confirm that it contains only the intended change. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Task boundaries do not automatically become commit boundaries. Focused commits make review and rollback easier; if unrelated work enters a shared commit, document and correct it transparently.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Split parallel visual work by shared code boundaries and preserve rollback
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Divide parallel visual changes by renderer or component ownership, using separate Git worktrees and an explicit integration plan for shared configuration. Select artwork variants at build time, emit only the chosen assets, and verify that switching back reproduces the baseline. Update visual tests when the interaction metaphor changes, while preserving no-script access and descriptive content. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Splitting by page alone can leave contributors editing the same engine. Clear ownership limits conflicts, and a verified variant switch makes aesthetic experimentation reversible without shipping every alternative.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Assert the intended merged artifact before accepting a successful build
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful build does not prove that the intended merge happened. Stop the release sequence if a merge fails, inspect repository state, and assert an expected artifact before deployment. For a multiline merge message, write it to a temporary file and pass that filename to git merge -F rather than assuming stdin behavior. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A failed merge followed by a successful build can validate the old tree. Checking an expected share-image reference or another concrete output catches this mismatch before release; repeat the relevant artifact check after deployment.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Read the full article and choose the visual's job before writing an image prompt
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Editorial image direction starts with the complete article and the specific explanation the visual must provide. Identify its central idea, audience, emotional register and figure callouts before choosing a format. Use illustration for atmosphere or metaphor, and a diagram or chart when labels, relationships or data carry the meaning. Read the relevant design procedure before composing a prompt. A useful eight-part prompt covers style, subject, action or state, setting, composition, lighting, mood and exclusions. Generate 2–3 candidates when variation will help, then judge them against the article. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An isolated image brief tends to produce decoration. Context makes it possible to reject attractive images that merely repeat nearby text or imply something the article does not support.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Change geometric prompt instructions when an image becomes too literal
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Image prompts containing 'evenly spaced,' 'rows' or 'tier on tier' strongly invite regular geometry. If an illustration should feel organically ordered, replace those structural instructions with a clearer spatial metaphor and specify irregular spacing, depth and soft transitions. For a tide-pool field guide, describe clusters following natural rock contours instead of arranging subjects in uniform bands. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Adding softer adjectives rarely cancels an explicit grid instruction. Diagnose which words produced the unwanted structure, change those words and compare the next render against the intended composition.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review image families for composition, readable text zones and continuity between adjacent sections
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate a website's image family both as individual assets and as adjacent sections in the rendered page. For an invented ceramic studio, prepare wide and portrait compositions that preserve the same subject while moving visual emphasis around the intended copy. Check full-bleed coverage, palette consistency and text-free artwork. A calm region measuring at least 8:1 at p95 can guide placement, but does not establish contrast beneath every word. Inspect adjoining images for stacked bright edges and abrupt transitions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Contact sheets expose inconsistency across assets; page integration exposes collisions with text and neighboring sections. Separating measurable constraints from aesthetic choices makes review clearer without pretending that a contrast statistic decides composition.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Repair image blemishes against their local surroundings and preserve the original grain
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Local image repairs should match neighboring luminance, color and texture. A useful starting recipe for a soft residual halo is a 40 px fill radius feathered to 52 px, using a 101 px median-filtered background, Gaussian smoothing with sigma 12 and restrained fine grain recovered from the image. Define acceptance before editing: for example, spot maximum divided by surrounding-ring mean no greater than 1.15, plus red-channel deviation no greater than 4 on an 8-bit scale. Inspect before-and-after crops for seams. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Whole-image statistics miss small blemishes. Luminance alone misses warm smudges on cool backgrounds, and a smooth repair can remain visible as a textureless hole.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Correct unwanted image shapes with explicit topology and edge descriptions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When an image model turns a portrait cloud composition into a closed capsule, describe the desired open structure explicitly. Specify irregular lobes, torn veils, ragged dry-brush edges and no enclosing outline; evaluate the portrait independently from a successful landscape version. Keep the style stable while changing the problematic composition instructions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A broad phrase such as one vast cloud leaves substantial freedom for the model to choose smooth, rounded geometry. Positive descriptions of topology and texture give a more useful correction than repeatedly requesting the same subject.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reuse a successful style prompt while changing only the target composition
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When adapting approved artwork to a new aspect ratio, keep the successful style description and change the composition instructions first. For a tide-pool field guide, a 9:16 image can reposition pools and rock shelves for a narrow viewport without introducing a new texture or palette. Inspect the resulting crop and placement before integrating it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Changing style and composition simultaneously makes failures harder to diagnose. A controlled prompt variation preserves visual continuity while leaving room to solve the genuinely different spatial needs of a phone layout.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give isolated asset sheets their own style prompt
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use a dedicated isolation prompt for asset sheets instead of appending exclusions to a scenic prompt. Specify the material, lighting, object scale and a flat featureless backdrop; remove style language that asks for surrounding stars, clouds or scenery. For ceramic-studio assets, request separate vessels against a uniform ground suitable for extraction. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reusable style paragraph may also contain strong scene instructions. Those instructions compete with later exclusions, so clean cutouts require separating surface treatment from environmental composition before rendering.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe visual arrangements explicitly to avoid lettering and accidental faces
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe objects and their arrangement directly when generated illustrations must avoid text or face-like forms. A ceramic-studio prompt can specify three unevenly spaced vessels on stepped shelves, with no lettering, instead of supplying a title that may appear inside the image. If paired round objects resemble eyes, change their orientation or spacing rather than relying solely on a negative prompt. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Composition creates recognizable patterns even when they were not requested. Concrete geometry provides a stronger correction than an abstract subject name or repeated rejection.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe established forms precisely when combining illustrations
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Preserve visual continuity in a composite illustration by describing each recurring object's physical form rather than relying on its name. For a bicycle-repair co-op, specify the repair stand's silhouette, tool board arrangement and cargo bicycle proportions when combining them into a homepage scene. Review duplicates, orientation and accidental emblem-like shapes before acceptance. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An image model may interpret a familiar label differently in a new composition. Concrete descriptions carry the visual vocabulary across scenes and make deviations easier to identify and correct.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use concrete visual language and explicitly limit what a style reference should contribute
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Image prompts should distinguish material style, composition and subject instead of relying on ambiguous nouns. For a neighborhood bakery's flour-to-loaf illustration, specify suspended flour particles or folded dough surfaces rather than a metaphor that could become unrelated foliage. When providing a reference, state whether it supplies paper texture, palette or brushwork, and exclude its subject if necessary. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A model can satisfy the requested medium while missing the intended visual meaning. Reserve the text area explicitly and measure its luminance alongside edge continuity. Inspect the generated image for alternate readings before animation begins; a beautiful still with the wrong semantic shape is an expensive foundation for a sequence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Switch from repeated rerolls to targeted edits when composition remains stuck
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After repeated composition misses, edit the best existing image instead of repeatedly generating the scene from scratch. State the single spatial change and the elements that must remain fixed. When a margin is truly uniform paper, a deterministic shift and matching pad can also preserve the artwork while creating reading space. Keep original files and inspect the repaired boundaries. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Some scene descriptions repeatedly pull a model toward the same layout despite rewritten placement instructions. Targeted edits constrain that tendency. Evaluate reading-space measurements with the image itself: a p1 luminance floor of 230 can over-flag tiny dark specks even when the overall area is quiet. Means, crops and text contrast provide complementary evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Generate figures from an explicit source inventory rather than improvising extra illustrations
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Read the approved content source and enumerate its figure callouts before producing images. Generate exactly the requested inline figures, plus a featured image when the publishing contract requires one. Under that contract, zero inline callouts means one image total, while three callouts mean four. Verify both count and correspondence: every image must serve the specified location and purpose. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Unrequested illustrations increase production cost and introduce creative drift into an already edited piece. A source inventory gives review a concrete acceptance check while leaving room for explicitly approved changes when the content itself needs a revised figure plan.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use generated imagery for atmosphere and keep factual labels in accessible HTML or SVG
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Generated artwork should supply the visual background while editable HTML or accessible SVG carries factual labels, numbers and controls. Reserve quiet negative space in the image for overlays, then test actual text contrast across responsive crops. Use a calibration batch of 3–5 images before committing to a larger production set. Keep essential information available independently of the artwork. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Baked-in labels are difficult to correct, translate, search and audit. Separating art from information lets a visual direction evolve without regenerating facts or sacrificing accessibility whenever copy changes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe the visible picture, not the webpage layout, in image prompts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Image prompts can accidentally turn layout instructions into painted borders, boxes, and overlay regions. Describe the desired pixels instead: full-bleed artwork reaching every edge, naturally smooth dark space, and a concrete limit such as at most three tiny accent sparks. If HTML or SVG will supply diagrams, request a background without diagram lines or nodes. Inspect file signatures too: a returned JPEG can carry a misleading .webp extension. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A model may render the nouns in an instruction literally. Describing what viewers should see reduces cleanup and preserves separation between generated artwork and functional interface elements.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Calibrate a shared image prompt on several roles before generating a full set
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test a revised shared prompt across several image roles before committing to a production batch. Use the same subjects in both rounds and compare a contact sheet for borders, empty space, accent density, and unwanted diagram elements. For an astronomy club, test a masthead, footer, observation-card background, and event banner. Treat numerical ornament limits as instructions to inspect, not guarantees. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A prompt that succeeds on one composition can fail on another. Side-by-side calibration reveals whether a wording change fixes the underlying problem across the set, making a small pilot more useful than repeated isolated renders.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve an approved visual direction as both written rules and example images
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Record a successful imagery direction with a reusable prompt, approved exemplars, and explicit composition constraints. For a ceramic studio, the guide might specify clay textures, diffuse daylight, restrained glaze accents, and uncluttered space for HTML captions. Separate web requirements such as full-bleed composition from print requirements. Keep the guide easy to find and distinguish stable style rules from subject-specific instructions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Text alone leaves room for interpretation, while examples alone hide the decisions that produced them. Keeping both prevents later sessions from repeating calibration work or gradually drifting into a different visual language.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Lead hero-image prompts with composition and verify the rendered text zone
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Put focal placement and reserved text space early in a hero-image prompt, then inspect the result rather than trusting positional wording. For a neighbourhood bakery, request the bread display in the right third and a quiet left area before describing flour, light and texture. Check the intended crop and text region at actual layout sizes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A generator may follow the subject closely while pulling its focal point toward the centre. Mean or percentile contrast can summarize a region, but neither replaces checking the backgrounds behind the actual letters.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Align generated artwork with the visual vocabulary of nearby diagrams
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe visible materials and forms in image prompts, and align their detail scale with adjacent interface graphics. For a ceramic studio, a painted clay surface and a process diagram can share muted colours and similarly weighted contours without copying each other's subject. Scan prompts for ambiguous layout terms that might generate unintended objects. Reserve a quiet text zone and check its contrast after rendering. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Artwork and diagrams feel coherent when their edges, density and contrast agree. A prompt that sounds evocative can still introduce visual structure that conflicts with the page.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit metaphors for unwanted objects and match image intensity to the page's role
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review prompt metaphors for objects or settings they may accidentally introduce. If a tide-pool field guide needs an abstract background, “quiet as a workshop” can invite furniture and architecture; describe sparse shapes, low contrast and stillness directly instead. Use calmer artwork on explanatory pages when it supports their reading task, and reuse an existing suitable asset when it already meets the brief. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Generators can literalize associations intended only as mood. Clear visual properties reduce accidental scenery and avoid spending another render on a problem that wording or asset selection could solve.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use count and shape to create visual order without making an image mechanical
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Specify count, shape, scale and placement when an image needs visible order without rigid machinery. For an amateur astronomy club illustration, request three or four broad curved rows of softly glowing observations, with the lowest row widest, instead of relying on an architectural metaphor. Compare variants for both structure and surface character. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Geometric vocabulary can overproduce hard engineering forms, while poetic language can dissolve the organization entirely. A small count plus a clear shape gives the generator a concrete arrangement while leaving room for a soft painted treatment.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Align background direction with process flow while preserving space for labels
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Directional background artwork can reinforce a process diagram when its movement agrees with the diagram's reading order. For a seed library's sorting guide, keep textured seed forms along the lower third and reserve the upper two thirds for stage labels and controls. Check the composition after responsive cropping. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A consistent direction helps the picture and interface support the same explanation. The background must remain secondary, however; increasing brightness or density toward an endpoint should not obscure labels or imply a status the underlying process does not have.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep decorative clusters small and peripheral around a dense information diagram
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Place decorative clusters near the edges and preserve a quiet central field when the foreground contains a dense information diagram. For a tide-pool field guide, faint peripheral shell forms can establish context while the centre carries the species relationships. Inspect desktop and mobile crops for overlap and competing focal points. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Background detail should orient the reader without appearing to add another data layer. Small edge motifs can supply atmosphere, but their brightness and grouping still need to remain subordinate to the meaningful nodes and labels.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Let background geometry support a diagram without carrying essential meaning
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Background geometry can echo a diagram's structure when it remains decorative and leaves the information area clear. For a ceramic studio's circular glazing workflow, a soft peripheral wash can frame the stages while a calm centre holds instructions. Verify that labels, ordering and relationships remain understandable with the background removed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Matching shapes can make an illustration and interface feel coherent, but decoration must not become the only explanation of distance, sequence or readiness. The diagram should retain its meaning across crops, reduced visual detail and fallback presentations.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use directional imagery to reinforce a banner while keeping copy space quiet
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give a banner one directional visual movement and reserve an opposing quiet area for its text. For an invented bicycle-repair co-op, scattered paths might converge on a repair stand at the right while the left remains uncluttered. A measured asymmetric composition achieved 14.9:1 white-text contrast at the 95th percentile, though actual glyph locations still require inspection. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A supporting banner can advance the page's idea instead of repeating its hero. Directional composition connects the illustration to the message without requiring additional explanatory copy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reuse images by semantic fit and preserve aspect ratios in review sheets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reuse an established image when its subject and composition serve the new slot, and preserve its aspect ratio in contact sheets. Before requesting another render, compare existing assets against the slot's purpose, crop and text zones. Letterbox a 3:4 portrait inside a 16:9 review tile instead of stretching it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reuse reduces unnecessary generation and helps a visual set remain coherent. Distorted contact sheets undermine that decision by making good compositions look wrong and hiding the proportions that will determine whether they work on the page.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use a middle-third subject when portrait content needs quiet space above and below
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A small subject in the middle third can leave both the top and bottom of a portrait image available for interface content. Specify those quiet regions explicitly rather than relying on the generator to infer them. A roughly 3:4 composition at 896x1200 measured 12.1:1 percentile white-text contrast in the intended lower text zone. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Not every portrait requires its subject at the top. Let the actual content placement determine the composition, then inspect the served crop so the reserved spaces survive responsive rendering.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Confine decorative movement to the lowest fifth of a diagram background
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Constrain decorative movement to the lowest fifth when a portrait diagram needs an open upper and central field. For an invented tide-pool field guide, a subdued waterline could provide context beneath the labels without running behind them. A roughly 3:4, 896x1200 background measured 13.5:1 percentile white-text contrast in its content zone. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Spatial constraints are more actionable than asking for a background to feel calm. They define where detail is welcome and where it would interfere with reading or interaction.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use small corner details to frame a diagram without creating false focal points
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep decorative clusters small and near the corners when the centre of a portrait image will carry a diagram. Side-edge texture can provide depth while the central field remains quiet. A roughly 3:4 portrait at 896x1200 measured 13.0:1 percentile white-text contrast in that central area. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Large decorative objects near labels can be mistaken for meaningful diagram elements. Corner placement helps separate atmosphere from information, but the final crop must be checked because responsive cover rendering can move or remove that framing.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Control image encoding explicitly when making a local retouch
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep a lossless working master and set export encoding parameters explicitly when retouching an image. Investigate unexpected file-size changes by checking compression settings, subsampling and image quality beyond the edited region. Revalidate any asset replaced after testing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A local pixel edit can trigger lossy re-encoding across the entire image. High JPEG quality settings do not make the format lossless, and a shared export mistake can affect multiple assets.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Apply approved local edits to the master before producing delivery files
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Composite approved local edits onto the original master, using masks suited to each boundary. Compare edited and untouched regions separately, then produce delivery files with deliberate encoding settings. Verify that deployed files match the approved exports. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Editing an already compressed derivative can compound damage outside the intended correction. Starting from the master protects surrounding detail, although a lossy export may still change pixels throughout the image.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give related scenes distinct silhouettes and reserve visual space for meaning supplied by animation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Distinguish related illustrated scenes through silhouette and action, not merely different props or colors. For a seed library, an empty tray that gradually fills can communicate sorting more clearly than a finished pile painted into the background. Preserve a consistent style description while changing subject instructions deliberately, and remove negative prompt constraints that conflict with required objects. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Similar central shapes can make unrelated scenes feel interchangeable. Leaving the active region unfinished allows motion to carry meaning. Targeted prompt revisions and local inpainting provide clearer control than repeatedly generating variants without identifying the defect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Request a clean background variant before extracting glowing overlays from structured artwork
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Removing luminous overlays from detailed artwork can leave visible tracks even after inpainting. In one extraction trial, colour filling introduced grain, morphological opening left dark edges, and biharmonic inpainting within a ±6 px band produced the cleanest result but retained soft traces. Inspect the background with replacement elements moved away from their original positions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A convincing composite can conceal damaged background pixels until animation exposes them. Requesting an artwork variant without the overlay often avoids a difficult reconstruction problem.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose segmentation methods according to the artwork's edge and transparency characteristics
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Segmentation techniques that work on opaque forms may leak across translucent watercolor edges. In a two-image comparison, seeded random-walker segmentation isolated solid bodies on dark ground, while a generous silhouette polygon paired with un-matting worked better for soft washes. Treat that result as artwork-specific evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An algorithm cannot reliably recover boundaries the painting does not sharply define. Compare candidate masks after compositing over the intended replacement background; visual reconstruction matters more than the apparent precision of the mask alone.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe abstract forms through light and value instead of object nouns
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Prompt abstract imagery using material, value, edge softness and spatial relationships rather than object names that imply solid construction. Lock a shared style, palette, lighting and camera block; vary the subject and composition separately. For a tide-pool field guide, describe translucent washes and soft reflected bands instead of sculpted underwater monuments. Generate wide 16:9 and phone 3:4 compositions with deliberate text-safe regions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Object vocabulary can pull a model toward crisp props even when the prompt also says abstract. Targeted exclusions can address recurring failures, but positive descriptions should establish the desired visual language first.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Control generated focal points with explicit size and brightness relationships
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Specify a focal form's size and brightness relative to its surroundings when generated artwork becomes too dominant. A useful instruction might limit it to about one fifth of the canvas width and make it no brighter than nearby translucent washes. Evaluate contact sheets for text space, interaction competition and accidental resemblance to brand marks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Evocative nouns often trigger strong visual clichés. Relative constraints give the model more actionable direction than simply asking for a calmer image, while selection against the intended page catches failures that prompt compliance alone misses.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inspect generated focal details at 2x even when the prompt explicitly forbids a shape
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Inspect generated artwork at 2x before cropping or integrating it, because forbidden shapes can survive in small focal details despite explicit negative prompts. Check bright cores, ornaments, crowns and repeated geometric accents against the visual brief. Reject or repair unwanted forms before producing responsive crops. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A tiny geometric accent can become conspicuous once isolated or placed beside text. Prompt compliance is an intention; close visual inspection establishes whether the delivered image actually meets it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test texture restoration after blurring unwanted structure out of painted artwork
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A provisional repair for an over-smoothed painted region is to restore brush-scale high-frequency detail inside the edited mask. First suppress the unwanted large structure, then test whether selected texture detail can be reintroduced without restoring that structure or exposing the mask boundary. Compare the repaired patch with the surrounding brushwork at display size and close range. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Blur can remove an unwanted form while leaving an airbrushed patch that looks out of focus beside textured paint. Texture restoration addresses that mismatch, but the proposed fix remains unverified until the composite is inspected.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Extend painted backgrounds with broad cross-fades and limited low-frequency light carry
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Extending a painted background can require both a broad seam cross-fade and a limit on carried edge brightness. Mirroring alone may leave vertical seams, while unrestricted low-frequency light carry can stretch bright features into horizontal streaks. One successful calibration used a 14-level carry cap, 170 px decay and 160 px seam blend. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Those values are starting examples tied to a particular image scale and tonal representation. Inspect the extension for both boundary discontinuities and smeared features before accepting it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A dedicated social image with one focal point can outperform a crowded hero recomposition
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A purpose-made share image with one centred focal point can remain legible at a 120 px square where a hero recomposition fails. For a bicycle-repair co-op, use one recognizable wheel or repair stand, with an existing illustration as a palette and texture reference. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shrinking several meaningful objects does not preserve their meaning. Evaluate candidates at actual thumbnail size before choosing the full-resolution favourite, and treat visual consistency as a constraint alongside immediate recognition.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Size protection masks to the actual glow to avoid dark collars
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep a bright-point protection mask close to the extent of the glow it must preserve. An oversized mask can retain dark surrounding pixels while nearby filtering brightens the rest of the image. In one image, reducing the protection disc from 30 px to 18 px removed the resulting collar. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Protecting more area is not automatically safer. The retained background can become an artificial ring after the surrounding texture changes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure bright-area coverage on the finished image after resizing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] If an image requirement depends on the area above a brightness threshold, measure the final resized composite. Adjust cropping and drawing scale separately rather than inferring thresholded coverage from geometric scale alone. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Resampling changes pixel values and can move bright details below the cutoff. Composition and measured brightness coverage therefore need separate checks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Extend painted backgrounds using subject-free texture samples
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Do not extend an image using an edge strip that contains part of the subject. Mirroring or repeating that strip can create ghost objects, duplicate rings or recognizable silhouettes in the continuation. Select a subject-free painted region elsewhere in the image and inspect the join at the final display size. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Texture continuity alone is insufficient: a mathematically smooth extension can still introduce a second subject that changes the composition.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe material and irregularity when abstract prompts produce unwanted grids
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Words such as thread, weave and knot can steer an image model toward rigid grids; material descriptions can encourage softer abstraction. Try brushed silk, slow currents, feathered light and uneven spacing, and describe crossings as faint glows rather than dots. Compare wide and portrait outputs independently. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] In a seed library's seasonal visual story, flowing textures may communicate growth better than a diagram-like mesh. Preserve quiet space for copy and compare background luminance across adjacent scenes before writing video prompts. A few carefully limited warm accents can remain meaningful, while uncontrolled flecks or brightness shifts weaken continuity.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify image provenance and compression before blaming the video model
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check source-image hashes, crop geometry and compression before using generated stills as video ingredients. In one diagnostic comparison, a 675x1200 crop re-encoded near JPEG quality 75 showed an 8x8 blocking ratio of 2.18 versus 1.03 in the source. Rebuilding the crop with quality=100 and subsampling=0 avoided another lossy preparation step without upscaling. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Existing compression damage can be mistaken for a rendering defect. Record intentional transformations when hashes differ, and keep failures observed in another video model as hypotheses until a probe reproduces them in the current model.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Present a complex capability inventory as a workflow readers can understand
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Group a large capability inventory by the work people perform rather than by internal module names. For a seed library's volunteer portal, show stages such as learn, plan, prepare, review, distribute, and measure, with a concrete outcome under each. Keep implementation names out of public labels unless they help someone make a meaningful choice. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Internal inventories describe how a system was assembled, while readers need to understand what they can accomplish. Workflow groupings reduce scanning effort and can communicate breadth without exposing private operational details or implying that every internal component is independently available.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose card image exports from rendered dimensions and verify crop direction
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define card image ratios by layout and export enough pixels for the largest intended rendering. A 16:10 featured card can use a 1200×750 source, providing about 2.6× pixel coverage for a 456×285 CSS-pixel frame. A list card might use 16:11 on desktop and 16:9 below 680px, with a 1200×675 source. Use explicit frame sizing and `object-fit: cover`. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A 16:9 image filling a 16:11 frame loses roughly 18% of its width, not its top and bottom; inspect focal points accordingly. WebP quality 80 and a 40–80 KB budget are starting targets, not guarantees. Compare actual encodes and provide responsive sources instead of sending the largest image everywhere.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Evaluate navigation copy at real widths before shortening approved wording
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test navigation descriptions in the rendered desktop and mobile menus before deciding they are too long. Compare wrapping, crowding and hierarchy alongside adjacent items using the actual fonts and spacing. Record suspected fit issues as design checks; if shortening changes approved meaning, make the wording change explicit and review it under the project's established process. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Character count alone cannot predict visual fit. Silent trimming during layout work can alter an agreed message, while premature rewriting wastes effort on a problem the actual design may already solve.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve ambiguous layout feedback with visible, incremental previews
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Translate layout feedback into distinct properties before applying it: block width, block position, text alignment and font size are separate decisions. Show incremental changes in a current preview and record the final values after revisions. Sequential percentage changes multiply: a title set to 75% of a heading and then reduced by 25% becomes 56.25% of that heading. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Requests such as centering can refer to a container or its text. Concrete previews expose the intended meaning quickly, while recording the final state prevents superseded directions from resurfacing during later maintenance.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Place decision-critical status where readers need it and judge reversible layouts in context
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Put availability or status information near the point where visitors decide whether to continue. An amateur astronomy club might place a weather-dependent event notice directly below its homepage hero while keeping detailed attendance information beside the booking form elsewhere. Test the rendered layout and treat easily moved elements as reversible experiments. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A placement rule that works on a detailed page may fail on an entry page. Fresh readers reveal when essential context arrives too late, and seeing the content in place often settles questions that prose-only review cannot.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Switch image composition at the content's layout breakpoint
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An art-directed image should switch composition at the breakpoint of the content it supports. Share the breakpoint between the content layout and the picture source instead of independently choosing device categories. With object-fit: cover, visible image-width share is min(1, (box width / box height) / (image width / image height)). A 1376x768 image inside a 768x2040 box exposes about 21.0% of its width; an 896x1200 image exposes about 50.4%. Sweep the intermediate range when content changes at 64rem but imagery changes at 48rem. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Both components can look correct independently while their mismatched breakpoints create a severe crop between them. Arithmetic makes that integration defect explicit.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Sweep interactive states as well as widths when testing image coverage
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Responsive image coverage must be tested in every content state that changes the image container's dimensions. Couple composition changes to content breakpoints, then measure open disclosures, expanded accordions and script-disabled fallbacks. Calculate visible width share as min(1, (W/H)/(w/h)) using the actual image box. A portrait source may improve coverage without meeting a chosen 50% floor; a viewport-height sticky image can bound the crop where appropriate. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Opening a panel changes height even when viewport width is unchanged. A comprehensive width sweep with every panel closed can therefore miss the crop visitors trigger with a single click.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure copy before commissioning artwork so mobile compositions reserve enough reading space
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use measured text geometry to constrain artwork composition before generating final images. For a seed library's instructional journey, render the longest stop with its final font and proposed column width, such as min(32rem, 40cqw), then measure desktop and phone layouts. If phone copy occupies the lower portion of the stage, place the focal form above it and reserve quiet paper beneath. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Moving text after painting can force awkward crops or obscure the subject. Measurements turn vague requests for negative space into usable composition boundaries. Test a smaller viewport such as 320x568 as well; when the text cannot fit, show the painting followed by its words in normal document flow.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Place full-width banners outside constrained content wrappers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A full-width banner should be a sibling of the constrained content container, with its own inner wrapper for readable text. Keep the banner inside the semantic section, then place the card grid in a separate max-width container beneath it. A grid might use a 1280px maximum while banner copy uses 540px or clamp(280px, 32vw, 420px), adjusted for small screens. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Different layout purposes need different width constraints. Separating the wrappers avoids fragile viewport-width breakout tricks and lets the background span the available width without stretching the text measure or disrupting card alignment.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: When visual access is missing, make one mechanism-based CSS change and state verification limits
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Debug unseen layout problems with one evidence-based CSS change at a time, and distinguish implementation checks from visual confirmation. Inspect markup, computed layout assumptions, and the box model before editing. Verify that the deployed response contains the change, then obtain rendered evidence. Avoid speculative overflow clipping or fixed sizing that could hide content. Position: relative alone does not generally create a stacking context. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Several defensive guesses can conceal the symptom while creating a new defect. If two attempted fixes leave the report unchanged, revisit the model and request precise visual evidence rather than assuming cache problems. Syntax checks and fetched HTML cannot prove that a page looks correct.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Autosize editors after font loading and width changes, with matching CSS and JavaScript bounds
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Textarea autosizing should reset height to auto before measuring scrollHeight, then clamp the measured height to explicit bounds. A practical calculation is scrollHeight + 2 pixels to absorb rounding, followed by matching minimum and maximum limits. Refit after document.fonts.ready and on resize with a 120 ms debounce, because font metrics, wrapping and breakpoint padding can change content height. Assert that CSS and JavaScript bounds agree. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A plausible round-number ceiling can still clip the initial template. Measure the actual content and viewport behavior, including whether the editor pushes its primary action out of reach; autosizing serves readability and task completion together.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use accessible layered diagrams to explain dependencies and boundaries
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A layered architecture diagram should show what each component depends on and expose the same information as readable text. For an astronomy club's observation portal, separate shared catalog services, optional observing tools, and member records. Use SVG or HTML labels, hover and keyboard-focus previews, click-to-pin details, and a reserved-height readout to avoid layout movement. Provide a plain-list equivalent and a static reduced-motion state. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A boundary line can explain modularity more clearly than a feature list. The diagram must not promise safe upgrades or preserved data unless the underlying behavior has actually been verified.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.
