memories.summary: Show availability where visitors first decide whether an offer is usable
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Place availability information near the page’s first meaningful invitation to act. On a ceramic studio homepage, present-tense descriptions of workshops can imply that booking is open even if a footer says registration has not started. Review the first viewport separately from the complete page and resolve conflicts between wording and placement before approval. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers form beliefs before reaching the bottom. Repeated copy edits cannot reliably solve a layout rule that hides the qualification until after the decision point.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test first-screen beliefs separately from the understanding formed after reading the whole page
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Ask readers what they believe after the first viewport and again after the full page. A seed library’s present-tense descriptions can imply that reservations are open even when a later status band says otherwise. Put the key limitation and the reason to care close to the opening offer. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A correct final answer can conceal an earlier misleading impression. Layout and copy operate together, and a qualification that arrives after the visitor has decided what to do may arrive too late.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Place availability information near the hero when visitors decide on the first screen
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Put availability information directly below the hero when introductory copy otherwise makes an unavailable offering seem usable now. On an amateur astronomy club site, a planned telescope-booking service should disclose its status before visitors start looking for a reservation action. Preserve this placement deliberately during component refactors. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Present-tense descriptions can accurately describe work that exists without establishing public access. Page-level consistency is less important than putting a decision-changing qualification where visitors form their first belief.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Solve figure layouts at build time and reject target collisions at the narrowest supported width
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A deterministic figure solver should enforce target spacing at the narrowest CSS width served by each layout. One reusable configuration uses a 1200×600 wide viewBox at a minimum 1024 CSS pixels and a 390-unit compact layout serving widths down to 320 pixels. For 48-pixel targets, compute the viewBox half-width as 24/scale, where scale = minimum CSS width/viewBox width. Test candidate positions against every existing target. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Phone layouts need different arrangements, not proportional shrinking. Seeded placement makes output repeatable; label collision checks and build failures turn overcrowding into an explicit design decision. Font-width estimates remain approximations and should be checked against rendered text.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Calculate label fit before committing to an always-visible figure design
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Always-visible labels must fit the available geometry, not merely look plausible in a sketch. In one 1200-unit panel served at 1024 CSS pixels, a roughly 28-character label occupied about 253 viewBox units while its cluster column allowed about 220. When labels cannot fit, retain cluster names at rest and reveal item labels through hover, focus and selection in a reserved readout area. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Arithmetic can reject an impossible layout before visual polishing begins. Every target still needs an accessible name, and a complete HTML list preserves access to all items.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Adding position to a wrapper can silently change absolute menu geometry
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Adding position:relative to a content-width wrapper can make it the containing block for absolute panels that previously spanned the viewport. Read positioning comments before changing layered navigation. Where appropriate, place decoration at z-index:-1 inside an existing stacking context instead of positioning another wrapper. Verify panels while open at 1440 px and 390 px, checking both full-width geometry and text-column alignment. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A stacking fix can become a layout regression without altering the closed header's appearance. Closed-state screenshots miss the defect. Decorative animations inside panels should also run only while those panels are open.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate label clearance against the full curve beneath each label
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Labels placed above or below a curved channel need clearance checks across their full width, not just at their centre. The channel's rise over a label's half-width must remain below the available gap after accounting for stroke and label bounds. In one layout, a 16 px gap required reducing the curve to an amplitude of 9 coordinate units and a 3% bow; those values depend on scale and geometry. Run the same collision validator on manually arranged and automatically solved layouts, across responsive sizes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A composition can look balanced at its control points while crossing words between them. Shared geometry checks remove the false distinction between a trusted hand layout and a layout that needs validation because a solver produced it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reserve the browser's text box when solving label collisions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Collision detection for wrapped labels must reserve the browser's layout box rather than only the visible text width. In one layout, labels occupied 150 px boxes while the solver reserved their widest lines, measured at 102–139 px. This produced 11 label-target overlaps at a 1024 px viewport and 9 at 320 px. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Ink bounds and element bounds answer different questions. A solver based on narrower text estimates can approve a layout whose real boxes overlap. Match the reservation to actual wrapping rules and validate it at each responsive layout.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give decorative art clear space when text masking fragments its shape
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Move decorative art into a text-free region when masks around dense copy make the artwork unreadable. For an invented ceramic studio page, a layered illustration could sit above three text columns instead of behind them. Preserve the text's background and contrast while allowing the illustration's silhouette to remain whole. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Increasing opacity cannot repair a composition whose important shapes are repeatedly cut away. Clear placement solves the spatial conflict and lets both the words and the illustration remain legible without competing for the same area.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Derive aligned coordinates from shared anchors and assert the relationship
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When two figure elements must align, derive the dependent coordinate from the source coordinate rather than typing both independently. For an invented bicycle-repair diagram, a connector endpoint and its destination marker should share a calculated anchor. Assert that their difference stays within an explicit tolerance in every responsive layout. If the design needs asymmetry, express it as an intentional offset from that anchor. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Independent constants stay still when scale, phase, wrapping or solver parameters change. The drawing can remain plausible while its connection becomes wrong. Shared derivation prevents drift, while a geometric assertion catches incorrect source selection or an overly permissive tolerance. Apply the same principle to label reservations by using the dimensions the browser actually lays out.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Refresh image-dependent geometry after loading and assess text against the brightest artwork state
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Recalculate image-dependent overlay geometry after lazy images load, and check text contrast against the brightest relevant artwork state. Anchors measured before image dimensions settle can miss their intended targets. For a ceramic studio's illustrated introduction, reserve a calm region behind the heading and correct distracting composition defects in the source asset when practical. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Layout measurements describe a moment, not a permanent truth. Fixing stable composition problems in the artwork can also avoid accumulating runtime overlays whose only purpose is to conceal an unsuitable background.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep geometry-dependent label offsets inside the shared component specification
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Label offsets that satisfy a layout solver belong in the component's geometry configuration rather than page-specific CSS. Supply those offsets alongside the figure specification so production pages, previews, and review fixtures render the same arrangement. Test the component without surrounding page overrides. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A page can look correct while its standalone review version places labels over nodes. Keeping geometry in one shared contract prevents hidden dependencies and ensures the tested layout is the one other callers receive.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Decide which radial labels remain visible before solving node positions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Persistent labels are geometric constraints across an entire radial layout. Include their measured dimensions before selecting orbit radii and angles. In one constrained arrangement, fourteen labels of 14–39 characters across three orbits had no collision-free solution within the available space. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeatedly nudging angles cannot fix an overconstrained design. Reduce persistent labels, enlarge the stage, or provide labels through focus and selection with an accessible alternative. Choose the information policy first so the solver works on a feasible problem.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Sweep intermediate widths when multiple flexible gaps compete for space
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Responsive spacing can reach its worst value between familiar device widths. In one row, label gaps measured 10.7 px at widths of 390 and 430 px but fell to 7.0 px at 407 px because another growing gap competed for the available width. Sweep the relevant interval and record minimum separation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A few standard screenshots can miss non-monotonic layout behavior. Test the constraint across widths and simplify competing growth rules when the resulting spacing becomes difficult to predict.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use measured spacing to keep interactive groups visually distinct
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test a grouping heuristic of minimum inter-group distance at least 1.5 times the maximum within-group nearest-neighbour distance. Compute it separately for each responsive composition and inspect whether the result matches perceived grouping. Placing controls along outward-facing arcs can separate adjacent groups where full rings bring their inner edges too close. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Controls attached to distinct illustrations can still read as one column or cluster. A spacing rule makes that ambiguity visible and provides a concrete adjustment target without prescribing one universal layout.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reserve text clearance at the viewport where lettering occupies the most artwork
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Size a text clear zone at the viewport where the lettering occupies the largest proportion of its background artwork. For one responsive composition, the critical widths were 320 pixels for the phone image and 1024 pixels for the wide image. Check every label box against bright image peaks at 1440, 1024, 390 and 320 pixels. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A layout that clears a bright focal point at most widths can still collide at its narrowest breakpoint. Testing the largest relative text footprint catches failures that a desktop-first review misses.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test label proximity and stage-edge clearance together across responsive sizes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate both a label's proximity to its associated group and its clearance from the stage edge at every supported size. One composition used a maximum box-edge-to-group distance of 140 artwork pixels and a minimum edge clearance of 56 artwork pixels across viewport widths from 320 to 1920 pixels. Define measurements in a consistent artwork coordinate system before applying responsive scaling. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Moving text away from bright objects can accidentally detach it from its group or crowd the bottom boundary. Simultaneous constraints prevent a local collision fix from creating a new composition problem.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make interactive artwork discoverable and place it beside the content it explains
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Interactive artwork needs visible interaction cues and a layout that connects it to the relevant text. For a ceramic studio, place an explorable kiln diagram beside its explanatory heading, add a concise hover-or-tap hint, and use a soft highlight to indicate activity without unnecessary zoom. Check narrow and wide layouts separately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Decorative polish does not ensure that visitors recognize an interactive figure. Clear cues, nearby context and restrained feedback help the image function as useful content rather than an unexplained ornament.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Balance perceived visual weight across illustrated cards rather than matching dimensions alone
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A row of related illustrations needs balanced perceived weight even when each image faithfully follows its own source artwork. On an astronomy club page, a delicate star chart may feel weak beside a bold telescope silhouette despite occupying the same card dimensions. Adjust scale, contrast, surrounding space or crop while preserving each subject's identity. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Consistency within individual assets does not guarantee balance across a group. Review the whole row at desktop and phone sizes before approving its components separately.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Pair unchanged-layout checks with a viewport where change is expected
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An unchanged-layout comparison needs a control case where the layout should differ. For changes above 56rem or 64rem breakpoints, compare preserved smaller layouts and also capture a wider viewport with an intentional difference. One probe measured mean difference 0 below the breakpoints and detected changes in all 3 controls at 1440 px. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated zero differences are weak evidence if the probe could be blind. A positive control demonstrates that it can detect relevant changes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Design the absent-state layout for conditionally displayed cards
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A conditionally displayed card needs an explicit layout and artwork state for visits where the card is absent. A selector such as :has(.card[data-token=none]) can restore the fallback layout, while script or rendering logic selects the matching scene. A picture element's viewport media query cannot inspect that token state. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Direct visits can otherwise inherit space and artwork intended for a missing card. Test both states; client-side layout state is not an authorization mechanism.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep harmless wrappers from breaking element-based layout comparisons
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An added layout-neutral wrapper can shift element lists and break positional comparisons even when rendered geometry is unchanged. Match stable elements where possible, or explicitly exclude a verified neutral wrapper while retaining pixel comparison. One corrected probe returned zero difference in 12 of 12 preserved cases and still detected the intended change at 1440 px. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Structural bookkeeping should not masquerade as visual regression. The failing control confirms that the exclusion did not blind the test.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check existing interaction copy before writing new hints and place it near the control
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Interaction hints may already exist in a copy registry and need visible placement rather than rewriting. Render a shared hint component beside the relevant figure or caption. CSS using (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine) can select pointer-oriented wording, with touch-oriented wording as the default, without JavaScript. Avoid making either input method the only way to operate the feature. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Hidden instructions do not help users discover an interaction. When the design requirement changes, update tests that enforce the old behaviour and remove orphaned copy for elements that no longer exist.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give visual stories one clear ending and place supporting information outside the main arc
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A visual narrative should reach one clear conclusion, with supporting status information positioned where it does not interrupt the main sequence. For example, a ceramic studio could place kiln-service notices after its making process rather than between the introduction and first demonstration. Combine repeated closing messages and position image labels relative to their depicted objects. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Interruptions and duplicated endings weaken continuity even when each section looks good alone. Review the complete page at phone and desktop sizes, and keep a still-image fallback when mobile video is enabled so playback quality can be evaluated without rebuilding the narrative.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe placement relative to visible objects rather than previous coordinates
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Spatial feedback should name the visible reference object and the intended final relationship. For a bicycle-repair co-op's illustrated service cards, 'place the label below the bicycle frame' is clearer than 'move it halfway from its old position toward the header.' Confirm the relationship independently in portrait and landscape layouts. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Relative edits can reverse the intended direction when a prior layout or reference point is misunderstood. A short restatement of the target relationship, followed by a screenshot check, prevents an apparently precise implementation from producing the opposite visual result.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Identify shared knowledge stores explicitly and read their operating guide before editing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Shared knowledge tooling should identify its target store explicitly and load that store's operating guide before reading or editing content. Document the distinction between personal and team stores, the configured connection, and the supported commands. Keep machine-specific locations in local configuration rather than reusable instructions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Similar store names and parallel local services make accidental writes plausible. A clear target and entry guide reduce misplaced notes, inconsistent organization, and assumptions that a personal convention also applies to a shared knowledge base.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Put supersession warnings on obsolete memories themselves
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Mark an obsolete memory as superseded within that memory, not only in a newer replacement. Explain which claims are historical and identify the current source of truth through a stable reference. Reduce the obsolete entry's retrieval priority where supported, then test realistic queries to confirm that the current guidance is found. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An outdated design specification can remain the highest-ranked result after a replacement is published. A warning that travels with the old content prevents history from silently becoming implementation guidance.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate saved lessons through retrieval and keep release status separate from review completion
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After a substantial review cycle, save reusable lessons and test whether realistic queries retrieve them. Reconcile overlapping notes, update the durable workflow guide, and distinguish verified changes from deployment status. Record any fallback execution method and the checks it received without retaining a session chronicle as general guidance. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Successfully writing notes does not prove they will help the next task. Retrieval checks expose missing coverage and stale instructions, while explicit release status prevents reviewed work from being mistaken for deployed work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Require semantic indexing readiness before writes that depend on searchable sidecars
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check semantic indexing readiness before writes whose successful retrieval depends on generated embeddings or sidecars. Poll a documented health endpoint, verify encoder readiness rather than HTTP status alone, and impose a bounded startup deadline such as 3 minutes with 3-second polling. If indexing is unavailable, stop the operation or explicitly queue recoverable indexing work. Verify indexing completion after writing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A document can exist on disk yet remain invisible to semantic recall. This is a discoverability failure rather than loss of the source file. Headless jobs also need noninteractive authentication; keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat, and avoid unattended password prompts.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Replace active templates atomically and clearly separate superseded guidance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Update a reusable template by capturing its existing version, constructing the complete replacement, validating it, and performing an atomic write. Preserve original creation metadata, update modification metadata, and identify the active version prominently. Archive superseded material with a clear boundary and a brief replacement rationale. Verify both the rendered document and any retrieval index after the update. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Partially rewritten templates can mix incompatible instructions and mislead later generation. Archives preserve reasoning, but retrieval should favor active guidance and exclude superseded directives from ordinary execution context. Avoid repeatedly nesting whole historical archives, which duplicates content. If interrupted, recover the last known good version before retrying the complete operation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Harvest validated build lessons into memory with provenance and incremental tracking
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Extract reusable lessons from implementation notes, review findings, and test results into a searchable memory system. Track source paths, content hashes, processing status, and validation evidence so only new or changed artifacts need reconsideration. Distinguish measured results, design decisions, unverified proposals, and generated hypotheses before promotion. Use cross-workspace comparisons to identify repeated failures or missing documentation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Construction artifacts contain valuable reasoning that otherwise disappears after release. Automatic harvesting can also amplify mistakes, leak private context, or contaminate evaluation sets. Generated query-answer pairs are not automatically ground truth. Deduplicate lessons, filter sensitive material, preserve source links, and require independent evidence before converting a plausible synthesis into durable operational guidance.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Promote related memory-system changes with coordinated backups, migration checks and invocation tests
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Batch promotion of related memory-system components needs a recoverable snapshot and checks across their shared interfaces. Back up both application code and the database before applying schema migrations. Record migration order, verify compatibility between components, and inventory scheduled jobs so retired and replacement tasks do not run together accidentally. Run component tests, then exercise the installed commands and scheduled entry points against representative data. Verify rollback against the resulting schema rather than assuming restoring code alone is sufficient. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Individually passing modules can still fail when combined with migrations and background jobs. A coordinated promotion boundary makes failures easier to isolate and gives recovery a concrete starting point.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review memory exports through a manifest and an incremental diff
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Pair each public memory export with a manifest of included entries and a private quarantine report explaining exclusions. Review the full manifest for the first release, then review additions and changes against the previous approved export. Include deletions and policy changes when they affect the release. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Requiring someone to reread an unchanged corpus encourages rubber-stamping. Incremental review concentrates attention on new exposure while preserving accountability. Keep quarantine material private because rejected entries may contain precisely the information the public pack must exclude.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Create one topic index that makes a large memory cluster navigable
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A topic index gives a large collection of atomic memories a stable entry point and a suggested learning order. In Voidloom, inspect the actual stored cluster before writing its map; list subtopics, durable retrieval tags, scope, and when each section is useful. Include a foundation-first reading path and a query that retrieves the index. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fragment retrieval does not necessarily reveal how a topic fits together. Tags generally survive imports better than local identifiers. Keep one maintained index per topic, and update it as the collection changes instead of creating competing maps.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Add a topic index when retrieval produces fragments without a useful entry point
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Create a topic index when related memories become difficult to navigate, using roughly 10–15 entries as a practical prompt rather than a strict threshold. Large source ingests, research batches, frequently revisited topics, and scattered search results are useful triggers. Search for an existing index first and update it where possible. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A small map can save repeated reconstruction work. Its benefits depend on accurate links and maintenance; do not assume that marking an index important automatically improves graph clustering, trust ranking, or every retrieval mechanism.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve useful problem-solving methods as explicit artifacts and test their transfer
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Capture useful problem-solving methods as procedures, worked examples, decision records, and retrieval indexes rather than assuming they will transfer automatically between models. Define the target task, document the method, and evaluate a new session on independent examples with and without the artifacts. Keep model identity and configuration in the evaluation record. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A compelling explanation of a method is not evidence that another system can apply it reliably. Explicit artifacts make knowledge reviewable, while comparative checks reveal which parts improve outcomes and which are merely stylistic.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate experimental output capture from durable memory writes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Have experimental agents produce reviewable Markdown artifacts before allowing their findings into durable memory. Capture proposed memories, supporting evidence, assumptions, and storage rationale in the artifact. A separate review step should decide what belongs in the reader's installed Voidloom memory tool. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Direct writes can contaminate future runs with unverified conclusions and make the experiment alter its own context. Staging the proposed memories preserves the agent's reasoning while keeping persistence deliberate, inspectable, and reversible.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Turn observed planning improvements into conditional, contrastive lessons
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Encode a reusable planning improvement as a triggering condition, decision rule, worked contrast, and limitation. Show two plausible approaches, explain why one works better in the stated context, and specify when escalation or a different choice is needed. A compact set of 8–12 atomic lessons can be linked from a short retrieval index. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Abstract maxims are easy to repeat without changing behavior. Contrastive examples make the actual decision visible, but their value should be tested on new tasks rather than assumed from persuasive wording.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Store atomic memories by knowledge type, retrieval trigger, and failure cost
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] In the installed Voidloom memory tool, classify memories by what they assert and state when they should be recalled. Use technical_decision for choices, error_pattern for failure-and-fix lessons, workflow_pattern for repeatable procedures, insight for implications, and skill_lesson for learning reflections. Keep one central idea per entry and use generic retrieval tags. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Storage quality determines whether future recall changes a decision. Estimate importance from likely reuse and the cost of silently missing the lesson, while preserving uncertainty instead of promoting every reflection into a fact.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Mark reusable knowledge assets with explicit distribution scope
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Declare whether each skill or memory collection is local-only or intended for distribution. Put that status in its metadata and review dependencies, private context, examples, and installation assumptions before packaging it. Maintain a release inventory so inclusion is deliberate rather than inferred from file location. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Useful local guidance can contain account details or rely on tools a stranger does not have. Explicit scope prevents accidental publication and makes shared knowledge easier to install, maintain, and audit.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Capture the plan and its reasons before execution changes the context
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Record the proposed method, assumptions, decision gates, and reasons before starting a complex workflow. Preserve enough context for later review without relying solely on mutable file links. Label the record as a plan and subsequently distinguish completed actions, deviations, and observed results. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Pre-execution capture makes it possible to compare intent with outcome instead of reconstructing a convenient history. Stored memories can also become stale, so explicit status and later corrections matter as much as early capture.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Create retrieval indexes that explain when to read each knowledge cluster
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Organize a large memory collection with a short index mapping themes to retrieval terms and situations where they are useful. Include a starting path, required prerequisites, optional deep dives, and unresolved decision gates. In the installed Voidloom memory tool, use descriptive topics to connect methodology, evidence, procedures, and validation lessons. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A flat collection forces readers to rediscover its structure. An index should guide retrieval without reproducing private chronology or presenting an old project status as a permanent rule; review its links and status periodically.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Capture a plan and its proposed reusable lessons in one structured response
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A structured response can contain both a task plan and a separate batch of proposed memories. Evaluate the plan for its decisions and verification strategy, then evaluate the memory proposals for relevance, specificity, category, tags, and retention rationale. Keep both linked to the same source response. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This supports two analyses without collecting another response. The memory proposals remain model suggestions, however; their presence does not establish that the plan is correct or worth retaining.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define separate output contracts for plans and memory proposals
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Request clearly delimited planning and memory sections when both artifacts are needed. The plan should cover framing, dependencies, alternatives, risks, verification, and decision rationale. The memory section can contain 6–10 JSON objects with content, category, tags, importance, and retention rationale; include the allowed category values in the prompt. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Explicit boundaries make extraction dependable and keep explanatory prose from breaking JSON parsing. Separate review criteria prevent an attractive plan from automatically legitimizing every proposed memory.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review task quality and memory quality as separate dimensions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A response containing a plan and proposed memories supports two linked but distinct evaluations. Assess whether the plan solves the task, then assess whether the memories capture durable, accurate lessons without unnecessary private context. Link accepted memories to their supporting evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reusing one response reduces collection work, but the two sections are correlated outputs rather than independent confirmations. Good memory prose cannot rescue a flawed plan, and a useful plan may contain little worth storing permanently.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep guidance self-contained and startup indexes small
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Package reusable guidance with its evidence links, installation instructions, and evaluation procedure. A startup index should briefly identify when to consult the full guidance rather than injecting the entire corpus. Optional retrieval should fail gracefully, with failures observable for maintenance. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Self-contained instructions survive changes to surrounding plans, while a compact index limits unnecessary context. Test through actual retrieval and loading paths: a manually supplied document does not establish that ordinary sessions will discover or apply it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give memory index notes an explicit retrieval path
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A newly created index note can rank below the detailed memories it organizes. Link the index directly from an always-read guide and give it stable topic and index tags as a secondary lookup route. Verify that both routes work after creation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Semantic similarity rewards matching detail, so an overview is not guaranteed to win its intended query. Explicit links make entry points dependable without assuming that future access counts or graph ranking will eventually correct the ordering.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use tested retrieval queries instead of database-local IDs in portable memory maps
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Portable memory maps should lead with tested retrieval queries rather than machine-local database IDs. For each map entry, record a distinctive hybrid search query and verify that it retrieves the intended lesson in the target corpus. A local ID may remain a convenience, but must not carry the portable contract. Re-test after importing a subset or changing retrieval configuration, and check the returned content before using it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Autoincrement IDs can point to unrelated entries in another database. Search terms improve portability, but invented queries are not guarantees: ambiguous or untested retrieval can create the same silent context gap.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build memory indexes around decisions and retrieval needs rather than chronology
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A useful memory index maps each theme to its scope, retrieval method, and the situation in which it should be read. Begin with architectural decisions that would force a rebuild, then operating practices, then specialist details. Give readers a short learning path and tested ways to reach individual lessons. Keep the index distinct from the full design document and validate its references after packaging. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A chronological archive makes newcomers reconstruct dependencies themselves. A decision-oriented index reduces that burden while preserving access to the reasoning behind each choice.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Capture decisions and their reasons at explicit workflow checkpoints
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build knowledge capture into phase exits instead of relying on a final retrospective. Record consequential discoveries while the evidence is available, then check each phase for missing outcomes, rationale, unresolved questions, and follow-up ownership. Keep review notes isolated until blind comparisons are complete. Track whether captured workflow improvements were actually incorporated. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Momentum makes explanatory notes easy to defer, and later reconstruction often loses the reason a decision mattered. Checkpoints preserve useful context, but quality and coverage should govern capture; arbitrary entry quotas can create repetition instead of reusable knowledge.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Public-content writers need curated context, including control over automatic memory injection
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Restrict public-content writing runs to a reviewed digest and verify that startup hooks do not inject additional private memories. Inspect the effective prompt where supported, use an isolated configuration when necessary, and test retrieval with a harmless canary whose answer appears only in the intended source. Have workers return proposed memories for validation by one designated store writer. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A carefully filtered handoff is ineffective if automatic recall adds confidential context afterward. Output scanning helps, but paraphrases can escape string matching; controlling what enters the writing context reduces that exposure earlier.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Capture small lessons immediately after each meaningful step
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Store one to three concise memories after each meaningful executed step, before starting the next step. Record the result and the reasoning while both are fresh. If capture was delayed until a checkpoint, label it retrospective rather than claiming it happened during execution. Batch closely related observations when storage has a fixed initialization cost. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Execution momentum makes the next action feel more urgent than recording the last one. Immediate capture preserves surprises and discarded assumptions; honest timing labels distinguish firsthand context from later reconstruction.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make project learning capture a regular completion step
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Attach a short learning note to the completion of each meaningful web-development action. Record what changed, what was unexpected and why the outcome affected the next step. Separate factual observations from interpretation and exclude credentials or personal details. If several actions have passed, label the notes as retrospective and return to recording them promptly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reliable capture depends on workflow rather than reminders alone. The expectation contradicted by a result often explains a decision better than its final status, and that context is easy to forget.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inspect per-item batch receipts before declaring success or retrying writes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful process exit does not prove that every item in a batch operation succeeded. Parse the receipt's per-item status and aggregate counts before reporting completion. If database contention produces explicit failures with zero successful items, retry according to the tool's guarantees; if success is partial or ambiguous, reconcile existing records or use idempotency keys first. Preserve sanitized receipts. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Concurrent writers can cause application-level failures inside an otherwise successful command invocation. Blind retries can duplicate successful items, while trusting the exit code alone can silently lose the entire batch.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use targeted recall to identify stale assumptions in large workflow guides
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Audit a large workflow guide through its heading index, targeted sections and relevant memory recall before applying it to a new stack. Compare recalled lessons against the actual deployment platform, analytics choices and approval boundaries. Add only reviewed, transferable material to shared guidance, and keep private context out of reusable documents. Record why an inherited step is applicable, replaced or unnecessary. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A comprehensive guide can quietly encode an old stack's assumptions. Targeted reading reduces overload, while explicit applicability checks prevent obsolete hosting, tracking or authentication patterns from steering a new build.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give delegated memory writers a metadata contract and collision-safe identifiers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Every delegated memory writer needs either an explicit prohibition on writes or a shared metadata and identifier contract. Specify required categories, retrieval tags, visibility rules, and a collision-safe identifier allocation strategy before delegation. Verify persisted records afterward, including whether tag updates actually took effect. If a metadata-only update is rejected, inspect the tool's supported update behavior rather than assuming success from the attempted command. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Concurrent writers can create duplicate identifiers and records that maintenance queries never retrieve. A lesson missing required metadata is operationally absent even when its text exists; write contracts protect both uniqueness and discoverability.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate immutable starter knowledge from writable user work
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A reusable knowledge-pack design separates an immutable base, independently versioned packs, and a writable user instance. Pin distributed layers by checksum, direct user writes only to the instance, and define identifier namespaces and read precedence explicitly. Declare each pack's compatible base versions and resource requirements. Test pack upgrade and rollback without changing user work or unrelated layers. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Bundled knowledge and personal additions have different ownership and lifecycles. Keeping them separate makes replacement and rollback understandable, while explicit merge semantics prevent duplicate records or hidden precedence rules from turning a simple layered design into unpredictable retrieval.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Trace silent automation failures across selection, persistence, ranking and presentation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Diagnose a silent synthesis failure by tracing an item from selection through storage, ranking and user-visible output. Confirm that the active path actually calls persistence, inspect profile-level ranking multipliers and test whether relationship creation requires conditions the selector cannot produce. Verify that uncertainty labels exist in rendered results. Share reproducible queries and distinguish observed results from hypotheses. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Each component can look plausible while their composition produces nothing or promotes speculation above evidence. End-to-end tracing exposes contradictory assumptions, and executable evidence lets another maintainer extend the diagnosis instead of reconstructing it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give generated reflections explicit provenance and evidence-based reinforcement
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Generated reflections should carry explicit provenance, uncertainty and source links throughout storage and retrieval. One candidate policy starts confidence at 0.40, applies a 30-night half-life with a 0.10 floor, and permits evidence-based increments of 0.10 capped at 0.65; these are design parameters to validate, not universal constants. Exclude derived items from recursive synthesis, label them as unverified and require a persisted record before marking an output meaningful. Plan backfills with a preview, ledger and reversible archival path. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Hidden ranking boosts and repeated retrieval can otherwise turn speculation into apparent fact. A single explicit confidence policy reduces conflicting adjustments, while provenance and row invariants make failures inspectable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use bounded retrieval channels for different evidence types
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define retrieval channels through explicit provenance filters, quotas, labels, ranking recipes and relevance floors. Enforce a total auxiliary-result cap across channels, and require each channel to pass a predefined relevance test before enabling it. Reuse existing embeddings or lexical search where suitable, while measuring actual resource use rather than assuming it is free. Keep authored evidence distinguishable from generated reflections. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A configurable registry makes new evidence sources easier to add without scattering special cases through retrieval code. Per-channel limits alone are insufficient: several individually small channels can collectively overwhelm the primary results.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Tag lessons for every workflow that can encounter the failure
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Memory tags should describe where a lesson is useful, including maintenance workflows beyond its capture context. Audit records with an exact inventory, then read relevant entries rather than relying solely on semantic recall. For additive tag repairs, back up the original values, preserve importance, apply the union of old and new tags and reread each record to verify the result. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Capture-time attention favors the workflow currently running. That bias hides reusable accessibility, testing and tooling lessons from later maintenance work. Asking which other workflows could encounter the same failure improves retrieval without duplicating the memory.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check exact identifiers before adding retrospective memories
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before adding a retrospective memory with a chosen stable key, query the store for that exact key. Semantic recall is useful for finding related ideas but does not prove that a record is absent. Include duplicate-key counts in routine checkpoints and investigate nonzero results before adding more records. When a newer version corrects an older one, establish an explicit supersession relationship. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Retrospective capture often happens after context has faded, precisely when personal recollection is least reliable. An exact inventory prevents parallel versions from competing silently, while supersession preserves useful history without leaving conflicting guidance equally authoritative.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Organize large craft libraries by decision point while preserving the underlying research
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Split a large craft library into focused guides organized around when a reader needs them, with a small routing index. For browser graphics, useful divisions include renderer choice, hardening, interaction, lighting, graph figures, art direction and handoff. Keep concise instructions separate from detailed research, preserve source status and link each claim to its evidence. Validate reference targets and guide names, including deliberately broken examples that the validator must reject. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A single enormous document burdens retrieval, while disconnected summaries discard context. A router and focused guides preserve depth without loading everything at once. Promote reusable code only after it has been exercised and measured.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Maintain technical guidance with traceable measurements and verified shared files
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep technical guidance current by recording measurement conditions and separating estimates from observed results. For browser graphics, identify the rendering environment without assuming that background-compute settings control browser rendering. Add tested helpers and checks to the relevant guide, verify referenced paths and confirm that intended files are included in version control. Inspect broad ignore rules that may exclude useful files. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Guidance becomes unreliable when evidence and implementation changes never reach it. A helper available only in one working directory is absent from the shared knowledge package.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build a durable topic index that connects practical guidance to evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A useful topic index connects decision areas, learning order, evidence status and source locations through durable semantic keys. For a browser-graphics collection, lead from renderer choice and budgets to production safety, then interaction, appearance and handoff. Separate verified findings, contradicted claims, unsettled questions and estimates. Use exact inventories to maintain membership; treat database row numbers as installation-local references rather than portable identifiers. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Search can retrieve isolated facts without revealing missing prerequisites or disputed evidence. A maintained index gives readers a route through the subject and a path back to original sources, while avoiding dependence on someone else's filesystem or memory numbering.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Retire or relocate lessons that no longer fit a workflow
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain a useful lesson collection by retiring obsolete rules, narrowing overbroad claims and relocating guidance to the workflow where it applies. Preserve retired text for auditability while removing it from active retrieval. Review usefulness and scope before adding more entries, and check overall collection size rather than hiding growth under a different topic. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A collection that only grows becomes harder to use. Maintenance advice can be valuable yet distracting during an initial build; curation should improve relevance as deliberately as it preserves knowledge.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate memory bodies before batch storage, not just counts and tags
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Normalize heterogeneous lesson records and validate their bodies before storing a batch. Accept supported forms explicitly, such as strings and objects containing text, and reject missing or empty content. A minimum length check such as more than 200 characters can catch header-only records, but also require substantive objective and reasoning sections. Recover damaged entries from their source reports, verify replacement counts, and archive superseded shells. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Counts and tags can look complete while every useful sentence is missing. Reading and validating the bodies prevents silent data loss from propagating into later summaries; derived summaries may also need regeneration.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make large memory integrations auditable with complete source coverage
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Large memory integrations need a machine-checkable source assignment and verification against current operational state. Inventory active entries, repair empty bodies, split the material into manageable batches, and assign every source entry to exactly one synthesis cluster. Verify coverage and duplicates before writers update documentation. Check live configuration when guides and memories disagree, and exclude archived records from active citations. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A fluent summary cannot prove that it consumed everything. Explicit coverage makes omissions visible, while live checks prevent outdated documentation from becoming authoritative merely because several historical accounts repeat it. Public exports also need a separate privacy review.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Pair readable documentation with a small set of atomic retrieval memories
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Shared documentation and retrieval memory serve complementary purposes and should share an explicit source of truth. After documenting a reusable workflow, extract 2–5 atomic facts into Voidloom and link them to the maintained document. Keep private preferences and sensitive debugging context out of public documentation. When a shared rule changes, update its retrieval records or mark them superseded. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A readable guide supplies context, while small memories help an assistant find the relevant rule quickly. Unmanaged dual writes create contradictory copies, so provenance and update ownership matter more than copying everything into both systems.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Batch broad memory searches, then retrieve full evidence for promising results
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use a batch of distinct queries for broad discovery and targeted retrieval for decisions requiring full context. An initial batch of 8–15 queries can explore terminology, failure modes and implementation options. Display compact summaries of about 220 characters, deduplicate results, then open the strongest matches. A shell for-loop is sequential; actual parallel execution requires bounded concurrent workers. Record failures rather than silently dropping malformed output. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Compact batches reduce interaction overhead, but truncated summaries can hide exceptions. Neither a batching wrapper nor unchanged search parameters proves identical retrieval quality or a particular speedup; those claims require measurement on the actual workload.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check indexing completion separately from successful document writes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A successful file write does not prove that semantic indexing or retrieval metadata was created. In a document pipeline, track storage and indexing outcomes separately, inspect structured results and warnings, and verify retrieval coverage after batch writes. A preflight health check can detect an unavailable indexer but cannot guarantee a later write succeeds. Queue or record failed indexing work for idempotent backfill. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Commands sometimes exit successfully after persisting a document while reporting an indexing failure only on stderr. This creates content that exists on disk but remains undiscoverable, so end-to-end verification must include the retrieval path.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate reusable resource-page knowledge from project-specific template examples
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain one canonical document for general resource-page behavior and separate project templates for local presentation choices. The general layer should describe content patterns, structured data, embeds, accuracy checks, slug handling, and idempotency. The project layer should capture tested markup, scoped CSS, design tokens, voice, and link conventions. Review both after a build and update whichever changed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] General guidance explains how a page works; concrete templates preserve how a particular site implements it. Keeping their responsibilities distinct prevents branding details from becoming universal rules and avoids losing implementation knowledge behind an overly abstract checklist.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Put current template instructions first and clearly isolate superseded material
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Rewrite a template's primary body to express the complete current rules instead of appending revisions beneath obsolete instructions. Identify the current version at the top. If historical material must remain in the file, place it below a clearly marked superseded archive boundary and label each archived iteration as reference-only. Keep version-control history and exclude the archive from generation inputs where possible. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers and agents often consume only the beginning of a document, so append-only revisions can leave stale instructions operational. An archive preserves rationale and rollback context, but labels alone cannot guarantee that retrieval systems will avoid obsolete text; retrieval boundaries matter too.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Pair reusable technical modules with symptom-based retrieval triggers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A reusable technical lesson needs both a detailed module and a retrieval trigger keyed to the problem it solves. Put implementation rules, failure evidence, alternatives and a release checklist in the module. Link it from workflow guidance using recognizable symptoms such as an inert widget after a build or a request for an interactive file validator. Prefer a canonical module with references over unmanaged copies. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] People often recognize a symptom before they know the relevant technology. A well-written document provides little operational value if the workflow never directs anyone to it when that symptom appears.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Organize dense technical knowledge into decision paths for proposing, building and verifying a feature
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A technical knowledge index should route readers by decision and symptom rather than merely listing documents. For browser compute, separate architectural fit, fallback design, runtime mechanics, accessibility, framework integration and verification. Provide a short proposal path that checks disqualifiers before discussing benefits, and a build path that reaches failure tests before release. Connect the index explicitly to relevant runbooks instead of relying only on semantic search. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Dense implementation notes can outrank their overview during retrieval. A durable entry point helps readers discover constraints early and prevents a compelling demonstration from being mistaken for a complete production design.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep speculative connections separate from established knowledge
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A generated connection should remain a labeled hypothesis until evidence supports it. In a research notebook, distinguish associations between distant topics from contradictions between factual claims, and preserve uncertainty rather than turning either into an authoritative conclusion. Check proposed syntheses against retrievable sources; record an evidence gap when the check fails. Describe the user-visible result without exposing private implementation details. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Unexpected connections can aid discovery, but novelty is not truth. Keeping hypotheses, contradictions, and verified observations distinct lets exploratory work remain useful without allowing a plausible invention to become the next session's assumed fact.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify memory loading with controlled evidence rather than agent assurance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test a memory-loading integration with a controlled marker and a comparison run instead of asking the agent whether it remembers. Define what should load automatically, what requires explicit retrieval, and what a task-specific digest contains. Use a harmless marker unavailable through other inputs, inspect execution evidence, and repeat the check for each supported environment. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An agent can sound informed by reconstructing context from the prompt. A controlled test distinguishes actual memory access from plausible inference and makes failures easier to locate when hooks or environment behavior differ.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give complex repairs a clear handoff with scope, risks and acceptance checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Create a handoff entry describing the observable failure, intended behavior, scope boundaries, compatibility risks and acceptance criteria. Link supporting notes through a stable topic label and distinguish verified facts from proposed fixes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A receiving developer should be able to act without reconstructing an investigation from scattered records. Explicit acceptance checks prevent a plausible partial repair from being mistaken for a complete solution.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Backfill retrieval paths when a useful tag is introduced midway through an investigation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When an investigation gains a tracking tag midway through, include earlier relevant records through backfilling or a concise index. Distinguish confirmed findings, superseded hypotheses, unresolved questions, and final procedures. Make the retrieval path sufficient to reconstruct the lesson without searching private session history. In Voidloom, use generic topic tags that describe the technique and failure mode. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A later tag query can appear complete while omitting the observations that discovered the problem. Explicit links across the gap preserve causal context and prevent maintenance work from promoting an early, disproven recipe simply because it was easier to retrieve.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A reusable skill library needs outcome evidence, unique identifiers, and canonical sources
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain a skill library with unique identifiers, a canonical source, derived counts, and recorded outcomes for each rule. Track helpful, neutral, and harmful applications with context so consolidation and retirement can use evidence. Detect duplicate identifiers and divergent live copies before merging; preserve historical snapshots separately. Keep review briefs free of budget or final-round pressure. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A library that records only additions tends to grow without a defensible way to shrink. Typed totals and duplicated sources conceal that growth, while outcome records help distinguish useful guidance from stale, redundant, or platform-specific rules.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep backups outside live source folders and verify versions before synchronizing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Synchronize canonical source files only after verifying target versions, and store backups outside directories consumed as live input. Record the expected prior version, check each destination before replacement and verify the resulting copies. If an authorized update requires temporarily changing file permissions, preserve and restore the exact original mode. Keep obsolete facts clearly separated from current evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A backup beside a live document may be harmless to a human but become conflicting evidence for a reader instructed to ingest the entire folder. Version checks prevent silent overwrites of independent edits. Read-only protection is useful precisely because it forces an update to be deliberate and narrowly scoped.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build handoff indexes around decisions, evidence, dependencies and unresolved work
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A useful handoff index gives the next reader a retrieval path to decisions, verified behavior, dependencies, tests and remaining work. Group related notes under generic topic tags in Voidloom, and provide search phrases that retrieve the complete package. Separate released behavior from branch work and proposed changes. Record superseding corrections and known deviations beside the claims they qualify. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reminder to revisit a feature leaves the next person to rediscover its difficult parts. A structured index preserves the reasoning and makes omissions visible. It is especially valuable when a low-level resolver returns a value but a higher-level policy must still reject that value under ambiguous conditions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Document deferred work with evidence, decisions, scope, acceptance checks and a return path
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A deferred-work handoff needs evidence, the decision taken, repair scope, acceptance checks and a clear return path. Store these as related notes with searchable topic tags and a short index. Include current status, distinguish proposals from verified behavior and identify dependent materials that will need updating. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Future contributors should be able to continue work without reconstructing a conversation. Durable records preserve why a task was deferred and what evidence would establish completion.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Trace repeated claims to their original evidence and verify that the scope still matches
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Repeated memories do not independently corroborate a claim when they share the same source. Follow citations to the original evidence and check the product, component, platform and test conditions it actually covers. Separate newer positioning decisions from newer implementation evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A portability requirement for one component can become an unsupported platform claim for an entire application after repeated summarisation. Source tracing catches this drift and prevents confident retrieval from turning an inherited misunderstanding into apparent proof.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep source evidence alongside distilled technical guidance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain a research index that links each distilled recommendation to its original evidence and verification status. Preserve prompts, raw reports, source URLs, screenshots, measurements, contradictions and unresolved questions alongside the synthesis. Distinguish confirmed, contradicted and unsettled claims rather than collapsing them into one confidence label for an entire document. Record missing research coverage explicitly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A concise memory is useful for retrieval, but it cannot replace the evidence needed to correct it. Keeping the raw record accessible lets future maintainers revisit a mistaken summary, update a perishable claim and understand why a decision was made.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Organize graphics guidance around a small router and a traceable evidence record
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Organize a graphics knowledge base with a short entry point that routes readers to focused guidance and a shared evidence record. The entry point should state the core rules: the fallback is a complete design, HTML owns interaction state, essential meaning remains accessible, and rendering has explicit resource budgets. Keep original sources, licence notes, unresolved conflicts and superseded proposals available behind those rules. Mark recommendations as tested, provisional or historical rather than presenting every note with equal authority. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A collection becomes easier to use when readers can find the relevant discipline without loading the whole archive. Centralized provenance also prevents several specialized guides from quietly maintaining contradictory versions of the same claim.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Store corrections alongside experimental memories so rejected hypotheses do not become rules
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Record explicit corrections when artifact review contradicts a captured implementation claim. Keep proposed lighting values, color multipliers and diagnostic explanations labelled as hypotheses until independently checked. In this example, a claimed gold alpha multiplier was contradicted by the artifact, and a tail-sector explanation failed review; even the replacement diagnosis needed reproducibility checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Rapid capture can preserve a confident explanation before the evidence catches up. A memory tool such as Voidloom needs the demotion and replacement guidance as well as the original experiment, otherwise retrieval can repeatedly recommend an attractive but unsupported rule.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep explicit correction records when a reusable technique fails its own test
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Retire a remembered technique explicitly when evidence shows that it recreates the defect it was intended to remove. Recombining a high-pass layer after a structure-removing blur can bring back spiral bands because texture and structure overlap in frequency. Keep the failure mode attached to the retired advice. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Simply adding newer guidance leaves old instructions available for retrieval. A correction record helps a memory tool return the qualification with the original rule instead of confidently repeating a disproven shortcut.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test concise retrieval queries instead of assuming more context improves recall
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Short, distinctive retrieval queries can outperform longer descriptions when extra terms dilute the intended topic. In one comparison, the desired result moved from eighth to first when the query was shortened to its essential concepts; an exact unique identifier also retrieved it directly. Treat this as a local observation rather than a universal ranking rule. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] In Voidloom, a saved recall query is part of the workflow's tooling. Verify the wording that future sessions will actually use, retain successful queries, and re-check them as the collection changes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test recall phrases exactly as readers will type them
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Short, distinctive phrases drawn from a memory's own vocabulary can retrieve lessons more reliably than opaque identifiers or lengthy descriptions. In Voidloom, test the intended recall phrase verbatim and check whether the relevant entry appears in the top 3 results. Try concrete combinations such as 'scroll passage render gate' rather than an internal handle. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A memorable label is useful only if retrieval actually finds it. Testing the literal phrase exposes query dilution and vocabulary mismatches before someone depends on recall during real work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify semantic compatibility before comparing generated vectors
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before comparing generated vectors, verify that their producers use a compatible representation space and preprocessing contract. Record compatible versions, normalization requirements and distance metrics in configuration, and reject unsupported combinations. Validate relevance thresholds with representative examples. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Matching dimensions establish structural compatibility only. A numerical comparison can succeed while its apparent similarity has no useful meaning, so compatibility and calibration require explicit evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check pinned-stage text against real mobile browser toolbars
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Text anchored near the bottom of a full-screen sticky stage needs real-device checks for browser-toolbar interference. An example portrait allowance is clamp(2.5rem, 10svh - 1rem, 5.5rem), added to the text's bottom offset and tuned against actual content. Check at 360x640, 375x667, 390x664 and 430x932, then inspect a physical phone while its bars expand and collapse. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A pale strip reported during scrolling may belong to the browser rather than the page. Chromium viewport emulation does not reproduce that browser chrome. The allowance is a layout-specific remedy, not a universal safe-area value; excessive padding can create a different overlap higher in the stage. Confirm that an entire stop remains readable at once.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use a multi-size and real-device battery for pinned mobile sections
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test pinned mobile sections at several widths and heights, then verify them on a physical device. Include 360x640, 375x667, 390x664, 390x844 and 430x932 as useful samples. At every hold, compare text, labels and link rectangles; confirm that the complete reading block fits without internal scrolling. Account for visible browser controls near the stage foot. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] One emulated phone size can hide both short-screen overflow and toolbar interference. An svh-sized stage can provide more stable geometry than dvh during toolbar changes, while dvh can resize container-relative artwork mid-scroll. Neither unit replaces observation on the target browser. Keep a stacked fallback for content that cannot fit comfortably.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Repeat text-fit measurements after web fonts load
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Any layout decision based on text dimensions should be re-evaluated after document.fonts.ready resolves. A parse-time fit check may measure a fallback font whose shorter text block fits, then leave the final web font overflowing a pinned screen. Refit when the controller activates and after fonts settle, updating scroll-band geometry if the layout switches to stacked content. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The initial measurement can describe a transient page that the reader barely sees. Test long copy at small viewports such as 320x568 and account for fixed headers as well as stage boundaries. A readable stacked fallback is preferable to preserving a pinned layout that clips the final typography.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make measured layout checks and physical-phone review a routine mobile acceptance step
