memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Mobile acceptance should combine per-element geometry checks with observation on a physical phone. Measure every reading hold at 360x640, 375x667, 390x664, 390x844 and 430x932, check label clearance, and tune browser-control allowances where bottom-anchored text needs them. Temporary browser-local CSS can help evaluate a candidate before editing source. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These checks address different failure modes: measurements reveal overlap, while the device exposes dynamic toolbars and interaction behavior absent from viewport emulation. Apply the method to ordinary mobile pages as well as elaborate scroll sections. Record the actual browser and conditions tested rather than treating one successful screenshot as general proof.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat mobile browser chrome as part of the layout test environment
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A pinned section that fits an emulated viewport can still place text beneath controls on a physical phone. Include short and tall viewport checks, inspect text clearance at every hold, and test with the actual browser's controls visible during scrolling. Investigate reported bars or overlays before assuming they originate in page CSS. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Emulation and device review provide different evidence. The former makes geometry repeatable, while the latter reveals browser behavior that a screenshot of the page cannot reproduce. Preserve the failure mechanism and its verification method in reusable notes, rather than recording only that a particular release was accepted.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Evaluate background composition as part of responsive layout
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check which image features remain visible when a responsive container uses cover cropping. For an invented lighthouse museum, verify that the building remains in frame on narrow screens; provide a portrait asset or adjust the focal point when needed. Update dependent overlays when the source changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A container can fit the viewport while its crop removes the subject. Responsive review must include image composition as well as overflow and control sizing.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use dedicated mobile artwork when a landscape crop loses the subject
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Create a portrait composition when cropping a landscape hero removes meaningful content. For an invented garden centre, place a greenhouse above a quiet region reserved for the mobile headline. Verify text contrast in the rendered layout. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A crop can preserve empty background while discarding the subject. Dedicated mobile art direction lets the image and copy share the available space deliberately.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Place broad decorative features above mobile hero copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Recompose broad decorative features for portrait heroes rather than relying on a landscape crop. For an invented garden centre, an overhead canopy can occupy the upper area while a quieter lower region supports the headline and action. Check contrast after cropping. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Keeping decoration clear of copy preserves visual structure on narrow screens. Consistency can come from the subject and style without requiring identical framing.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use asymmetric mobile compositions when they create clearer text space
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Try placing a portrait hero's subject toward an upper corner when this creates usable space for copy. For an invented swim school, pool equipment could sit above and beside a quiet headline area. Check the actual crop and text contrast. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Asymmetric composition can balance the subject with the mobile interface. A desktop crop may otherwise leave the copy over busy detail or remove the subject entirely.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep a mobile hero's focal subject clear of its copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Position a portrait hero's focal subject outside the intended copy area and inspect the rendered crop. For an invented lighthouse museum, the tower could appear above a subdued region reserved for the opening message. Verify readability across supported screen sizes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Keeping the subject visible is insufficient if text overlaps its defining details. Mobile composition should protect both the subject and the message.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep portrait background detail clear of central diagrams
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Place decorative background detail near the sides when a mobile panel contains a central diagram. For an invented garden centre, border foliage could frame a planting guide while leaving its labels and controls unobstructed. Check that responsive cropping preserves useful framing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A narrow crop can remove edge decoration or push it behind labels. Dedicated composition supports both the visual setting and diagram readability.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recompose decorative borders around mobile information panels
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a mobile information panel needs decoration above and below its content, design the portrait background around the content's full height. Keep the middle quiet and test with longer text and enlarged type. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Cropping a landscape asset may remove its borders or leave too little readable space. The information should determine the usable area rather than being squeezed into a convenient crop.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reserve clear space for closing copy and inspect the footer transition
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Place decorative detail below a closing message when the upper area needs to remain readable. For an invented swim school, a poolside illustration could sit beneath the closing invitation. Check text contrast, responsive cropping and the transition into the footer. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A section can work in isolation yet create a distracting seam beside its neighbor. Review the closing composition and footer together.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Budget hero content and sticky navigation for short mobile viewports
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test narrow, short viewports as well as tall phones. Size the hero against the usable viewport after accounting for navigation, and check the headline's actual position. Keep sticky headers compact and coordinate anchor offsets with their rendered height. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A layout that works on a tall screen can hide essential content on a shorter one. Sticky navigation consumes space throughout the page, particularly when text enlargement causes extra wrapping.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use the large viewport for a sticky decorative background that must cover retracting browser chrome
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A viewport-sized sticky decorative background can use height: 100lvh to remain stable and cover the screen when mobile browser toolbars retract. A 100svh background may leave a strip exposed in the larger visible viewport; 100dvh can resize during the transition. With lvh, some decoration may sit beneath the toolbar while it is shown, so keep essential content independent of that region. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Choose viewport units according to the element's job. A background that must never expose its lower edge benefits from covering the larger viewport. Recompute crop coverage using that height, and report toolbar behaviour as untested unless checked in an environment that actually reproduces it. Desktop emulation alone cannot certify the transition.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check first-screen headlines against visible viewport heights and sweep intermediate sizes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate mobile headline placement against the visible browser viewport and sweep heights as well as widths. Treat 375x553 and 360x560 as illustrative reduced-height test cases, not fixed dimensions guaranteed by a device name. Sweep heights from 540 to 720 in 20 px steps across widths from 320 to 430, then measure the headline's bounding box. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Device presets do not reproduce every browser toolbar state. Bottom-aligned content in a frame sized with calc(100svh + 1rem) can retain a constant below-fold error across many heights, even after passing two selected examples. Use emulation for geometric coverage and real-device checks for browser chrome behaviour; mark unperformed device checks as conditional or not run.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give hover animations an explicit touch path and prevent duplicate static and animated layers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Gate hover-specific behavior with @media (hover: hover) and define an explicit touch interaction for animated artwork. On mobile, use an appropriate tap or scroll-entry trigger and ensure that the animated representation replaces its still rather than appearing alongside it. Retain the still for no-JavaScript, reduced-motion, and rendering-failure states. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Touch can leave hover states latched, exposing both layers at once. Record which viewport a review comment concerns before applying changes everywhere; an improvement needed on desktop may already work well in the mobile composition.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Solve portrait hero composition with scale, visible starting positions, and suitable artwork
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Matching desktop hero impact on a phone requires more than retaining every scene element. In one 390x844 composition, an artwork scale near 0.51 made the animation too small; a 0.85 scale floor and first-screen starting positions improved visibility. Those values were specific to that artwork. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A portrait frame may not accommodate readable copy and an entire detailed scene simultaneously. Request artwork with additional quiet space above the subject, or accept a deliberate fold, instead of forcing text across important details.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test text over artwork at narrow widths and short viewport heights
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Text placed in a quiet region of artwork must remain inside that region after mobile wrapping. Test both narrow width and short viewport height, including a 320 px-wide layout where appropriate, using the final copy and fonts. Inspect every wrapped line against the rendered background. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Extra heading lines can extend into detailed artwork even when the overall text block technically fits. A decorative flourish can consume the remaining safe space, so grade actual pixels rather than relying on the desktop composition or container bounds.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Align portrait media crops and use text protection that covers the entire mobile copy block
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Portrait stills and video should share crop alignment so the transition does not shift the subject. For upper-weighted compositions, object-position: 50% 0 preserves the subject while cropping unused space below. A full-width linear light band with a 3.5rem feather can protect long copy more consistently than a radial veil. Intersect vertical and horizontal masks when painted edges look like a rectangular card. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Desktop previews hide portrait cropping and text-density problems. Example mask boundaries of 12/88% vertically and 16/84% horizontally need visual tuning. Measure the first stop after the sticky stage actually pins, not during its approach.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Size mobile heroes against the actual header and keep animated overlays aligned with image crops
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A one-screen mobile hero must account for the full header visible at page entry, including navigation rows. If that header is 136px, subtracting a later 60px pinned-bar height creates 76px of overflow. Use small viewport units where appropriate, then test minimum heights and copy fit on short screens. Share the image crop parameter with any canvas or WebGL overlay. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A visually correct still can become misregistered when its animation uses an old cover offset. Removing redundant mobile copy may improve fit, but a minimum height can still exceed the available screen and must be checked explicitly.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Extract embedded media before publishing and enforce explicit page budgets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Extract base64 media from editorial HTML into durable assets before committing the content to the CMS. A practical local budget can flag HTML above 200 KB, with documented exceptions for intentionally complex pages; ordinary article HTML might target 30–80 KB. Specify whether budgets measure compressed or uncompressed bytes. Give images explicit dimensions and serve appropriately sized responsive variants. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Inline media inflates HTML and prevents independent asset caching. Treat Lighthouse performance ≥85, LCP ≤2.5 seconds, and CLS ≤0.1 as chosen acceptance targets under documented test conditions, not guaranteed outcomes. Do not retain FID as the sole responsiveness measure or invent missing CDN parameters. Verify current metrics and image-service options, then inspect representative pages after deployment.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inspect pixel count and transparent overdraw when a WebGL hero feels sluggish
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Device-pixel ratio, antialiasing and transparent overdraw are useful first suspects in a sluggish particle hero. Reducing a DPR cap from 2 to 1.5 reduces drawing-buffer pixel count by 43.75% at the same CSS size; this arithmetic is not a measured frame-rate improvement. Compare antialiasing on and off, then inspect particle density and sprite area. Example tuning candidates include 900 to 560 particles and point size 0.9 to 0.82, subject to visual checks on target devices. Default untextured Three.js points appear square; use a shared alpha sprite when a soft star shape is intended. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Attractive additive particles can accumulate substantial overdraw. Measure frame behavior before claiming a speedup, and retain fallback, reduced-motion, pause, resize and context-loss handling during optimization.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Browser computation can preserve static hosting while shifting costs to the visitor
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Computation that needs no server-side secrets or private backend data can run in the browser on a statically hosted site. For example, a ceramic studio's batch calculator could process inputs locally without a computation endpoint. Lazy-load a large dependency, such as a roughly 13 MB runtime, after explicit user action and keep it off the initial rendering path. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This can remove server execution costs and operational work for that feature, but delivery bandwidth, dependency maintenance, device limits, battery use, and accessibility still matter. Every visitor contributes compute capacity; that does not make distribution or execution unlimited or free.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Publish comparative performance claims only after a reproducible evaluation of the released version
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Comparative website claims require a reproducible evaluation of the specific product version being described. Select relevant benchmarks, record their protocols, preregister the comparison, and separate third-party results from self-reported scores. Include ablations when claiming that a particular subsystem contributes to the outcome. Record configuration, correctness checks, and evaluation limitations before converting results into copy. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A favorable score can reflect protocol differences, selective reporting, or a configuration unavailable to users. Functional claims can remain useful before benchmarking; measured superiority should wait until the evidence supports that narrower and more demanding statement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure scroll-triggered initialization separately from steady animation frames
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A decorative layer can have inexpensive frames while its scroll-triggered initialization blocks the main thread. Measure context creation, shader setup, buffers and geometry preparation separately from steady rendering. Aim to keep individual boot tasks within 50 ms under a declared test condition such as 4x CPU throttling. Yield through macrotasks, defer nonessential preparation and reject geometry candidates with bounding boxes before detailed sampling. Feature-detect scheduler.yield if used. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Navigation audits can miss below-the-fold initialization, while frame traces omit setup. Observe long tasks during an actual scroll-to-section scenario and compare repeated runs with a control; smooth animation after a long freeze does not make the interaction responsive.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test disclosure deep links on initial navigation and initialize their state before visible layout shifts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Fragment-targeted disclosures must be tested through direct page navigation, not only clicks. Open the target early enough to avoid changing already visible layout; a small inline script immediately after the disclosure markup is one candidate, using is:inline in Astro. Keep hashchange handling for later navigation, and update any hash-based script CSP to authorize the new script. Verify the result with a buffered layout-shift observer on desktop and phone sizes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Click-induced shifts within 500 ms of input can be excluded from CLS, masking a defect seen by visitors following shared links. Early parsing is a proposed remedy, not a guarantee for streamed documents; test the actual delivery path.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define performance budgets with their test conditions and handle conflicting constraints explicitly
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Specify performance budgets with the viewport, CPU conditions and measurement scope attached. Example project targets are at most 50 ms per main-thread boot task under 4x CPU throttling and 2 ms per animation frame at 1920x1080. Split work with scheduled continuations; feature-detect scheduler.yield and provide a fallback. If a 1.5 DPR cap makes a required raster resolution impossible at 320x568, record the constraint conflict explicitly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Unqualified numbers invite inconsistent enforcement. Written decisions prevent repeated debate while keeping genuinely incompatible requirements visible.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reduce duplicated responsive markup before pursuing small score changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Inspect duplicated responsive stages and repeated inline decoration when a visually rich page has a large HTML document. Ship one stage plus compact layout data where feasible, then measure document size and loading behavior under consistent conditions. If remaining costs belong to shared headers or components, address them across the site and retest affected routes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Structural duplication can outweigh small code optimizations. A page-specific score does not mean the underlying cost is page-specific, and moving that cost requires a broader regression boundary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check all importing routes before adding behavior to a shared module
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Identify every route importing a shared module before adding page-specific behavior. Prefer a dedicated module where appropriate, then compare emitted per-route payloads with both their baselines and budgets. Verify whether conditional code is actually removed by the build. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A route can remain within its budget while acquiring an unintended cost. Inspecting all importers makes the impact on otherwise unchanged pages visible.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify code splitting through emitted chunks and per-route totals
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After extracting page-specific behavior, compare the emitted chunks and total required payload for each affected route. Confirm that unrelated routes no longer receive the feature and that shared dependencies have not been duplicated unexpectedly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Moving source code does not prove that delivery costs moved as intended. Build-output comparisons reveal whether the extraction isolated the feature or merely rearranged its cost.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use repeated Lighthouse runs to distinguish noisy measurements from consistent problems
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A single Lighthouse performance score is insufficient evidence for a release decision when local measurements fluctuate. For routine triage, run the same built page five times under consistent settings and report the median together with the spread. Keep device emulation, browser version, cache conditions, and background workload controlled. Examine the underlying metrics and traces rather than relying only on the composite score. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Local preview measurements can vary with CPU contention and other conditions unrelated to a code change. A median-of-five check reduces sensitivity to one unusual run, but it is a practical diagnostic summary rather than strong proof of a small performance improvement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use separate advisory and hard timeouts for slow optional runtime downloads
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Distinguish a slow runtime download from an abandoned one with two timeout stages. An example uses ADVISORY_MS = 12000 to reveal an immediately usable fallback while loading continues, then HARD_MS = 40000 to commit to fallback mode and ignore late completion. For a roughly 13 MB payload, 12 seconds implies about 9 Mbps before overhead. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A single short cutoff discards downloads that would succeed on slower connections, while a long silent wait wastes attention. Honest intermediate messaging gives users a working alternative without prematurely cancelling progress.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Correct mislabeled image extensions without recompressing the source master
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When an image's extension disagrees with its encoded format, identify the actual bytes and correct the filename without unnecessary re-encoding. Preserve that original as the source master, then generate genuine WebP or AVIF derivatives at the sizes needed by the site. Configure responsive delivery from those derivatives and verify their actual formats. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Renaming a JPEG to WebP does not convert it, but converting a lossy master prematurely adds another generation of compression damage. Honest naming fixes tool confusion while leaving the build pipeline free to choose appropriate dimensions and quality from the best available source.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match Lighthouse test conditions to deployment before diagnosing the design
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An uncompressed local static server is not equivalent to a production deployment when interpreting Lighthouse results. Record browser and Lighthouse versions, emulation, throttling, compression and serving environment. A text LCP of 4.2 seconds on a 343 KB uncompressed document is reason to investigate transport before blaming visual effects, but it does not prove the cause alone. Retest under comparable deployed conditions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Sparse-page scores provide a baseline, not evidence that the completed design will retain them. For authenticated preview checks, keep credentials in your own key file with restrictive permissions such as 0600 or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use fixed resolution caps and render-on-demand before adding adaptive complexity
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] For a mostly idle graphics panel, evaluate a fixed DPR cap and render-on-demand before introducing continuous dynamic resolution. Candidate scene ceilings such as 300 stars, 500 threads or 20,000 particles are starting hypotheses that require representative-device testing. Analytic GPU motion may avoid repeated CPU particle updates, but compare the actual workload before adding a Worker or a larger engine. Check maintenance dates against the repository rather than an aggregator's listing date. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Adaptive systems have their own coordination costs and can produce visible resolution changes. A simpler bounded renderer is easier to reason about when the scene spends much of its time paused.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Diagnose translucent graphics through pixel coverage and overdraw
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test rendering resolution when a translucent scene is slow, because overlapping pixel coverage can dominate object count. A supplied software-renderer observation improved from 5.3 fps at 2545x946 to 11.8 fps at 1280x800: about 2.2 times the frame rate with 2.35 times fewer pixels. This is consistent with a pixel-related bottleneck, but it is not a controlled hardware-GPU benchmark. Reduce DPR, layer coverage or overlap, then measure again on representative devices. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Counting cloud planes or particles misses how often the same screen pixels are shaded and blended. Resolution experiments help identify the limiting work without mistaking software-renderer results for user-device performance.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test reduced-resolution buffers for soft particles and glow
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Render soft particle effects into a reduced-resolution buffer when their appearance tolerates upsampling. A supplied reference observation rose from 6.2 fps to 14.6 fps at render scale 0.5, but its environment and limited protocol do not justify a universal speedup claim. Scales around 0.5–0.7 are candidates to evaluate, keeping text and sharp interface elements at normal resolution. Compare edge quality, compositing artifacts and frame time on the intended devices. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Halving both dimensions quarters the buffer's pixel count, though total execution cost need not fall proportionally. Soft effects often offer room to trade unnecessary detail for a smaller rendering workload.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Budget graphics in pixels, bytes and frame time, with estimates clearly labeled
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Set graphics budgets around frame time, pixel coverage and shipped bytes, then validate scene limits on representative hardware. A 60 Hz frame lasts about 16.7 ms; at 120 Hz it lasts 8.3 ms. Capping DPR from 3 to 1.5 removes 75% of backing pixels. A 1200x560 panel at DPR 1.5 covers 1.512 million pixels, or about 90.7 million pixel visits per second for each full-panel layer at 60 fps, before overdraw. Candidate limits include 300 stars, 500 threads, 20,000 particles and 30 KB gzipped graphics code. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Object counts alone hide fill cost. Treat startup thresholds, such as five frames averaging over 33 ms, as heuristics; probe float-target support, avoid half-float drifting positions where precision is inadequate, and keep the static image available during startup.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Cap route candidates before slicing their construction into smaller tasks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reduce combinatorial candidate counts before spreading graphics initialization across smaller tasks. A route pool combining 36 group pairs, every member pair and 6 shapes produced an observed 1.9-3.8 s main-thread task under 4x CPU throttling. Limiting each group pair to its nearest 8 member pairs bounds the candidate count before scheduling construction in slices capped at 30 ms. Verify that the retained candidates still provide valid, varied routes, and cache results when the layout signature is unchanged. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Slicing alone changes when work occurs without reducing how much work exists. Candidate caps address the multiplication of group pairs, member pairs and shape variants, while short slices protect responsiveness during the remaining computation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give texture decoding and upload their own bounded startup tasks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Adding a texture to an existing initialization function can create a long task unless decoding and upload receive separate scheduling. In one measured implementation, texture upload took 39–52 ms and total initialization took approximately 90–100 ms. Off-thread decoding followed by uploads in bands from premultiplied ImageBitmaps reduced individual slices to 1–11 ms. Treat these as workload-specific observations. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A task budget applies to everything executed within that task. An asset added to a previously acceptable startup path can make the entire path block interaction, even when steady rendering remains smooth.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Report which assets and parser paths contribute to a page budget
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A page's asset budget should count its reachable assets and disclose any conservative fallback used to identify them. One shared-loader analysis counted 35.7 KB of layers, including a layer the page never loaded. A revised parser missed Vite's preload wrapper and silently fell back to counting everything, reporting 34.3 KB. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A total without its contributing files hides classification errors. Print the included layers and whether dependency parsing succeeded so a parser miss cannot look like a real payload regression. Reconcile the result with actual page requests where possible.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use canonical explanatory text while preserving accessible static content
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Where repeated explanations serve the same purpose, keep a canonical DOM source and populate enhanced readouts from it. Preserve accessible reading order and useful content without scripting. Measure markup changes separately from loading behavior. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated text can inflate documents and drift during editing. Consolidation can reduce duplication, but a smaller document alone does not establish an improvement in an aggregate performance score.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use controlled page variants to investigate loading costs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Investigate loading problems with controlled variants that alter one relevant factor at a time, such as a section, stylesheet or image. Compare repeated runs with an unchanged control under consistent conditions, and record individual loading metrics alongside aggregate scores. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Request size, scheduling and rendering interact. A result from one page does not establish a universal conversion between bytes removed and loading improvement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Avoid geometry reads that defeat deferred rendering
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Audit initialization code for geometry reads on subtrees deferred by content-visibility. Delay work until relevant content approaches visibility and use observer-provided size information where suitable instead of demanding fresh layout. Verify the resulting behavior in a browser trace. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Requesting geometry can force the browser to render content it would otherwise skip. Deferred rendering helps only when application code respects that boundary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test disclosure deep links on initial navigation to catch layout shifts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Open a fragment-targeted disclosure early enough that initial navigation does not paint its closed layout first. For a details group, a small inline script immediately after its markup can read location.hash and set the target's open state during parsing; retain a hashchange listener for later navigation. In Astro, is:inline preserves this placement. If the Content Security Policy authorizes scripts by hash, authorize the exact generated script. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A deferred opener can expand the page after fragment scrolling and cause layout shift. A click-only test misses this because shifts within 500 ms of recent input are excluded from CLS. Use a buffered layout-shift observer on direct fragment loads at desktop and phone sizes, summing entries without recent input. Confirm that a deliberately deferred opener fails. Streaming or unusually long markup can still paint early, so verify the actual load behavior rather than assuming parser placement guarantees zero shift.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Compare Lighthouse changes against a control before attributing gains to byte cuts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Bisect a Lighthouse regression against a control build measured under the same conditions before attributing the result to payload size. One investigation observed two LCP modes near 3.30 and 3.53 s; a 139 KB document variant scored worse than a 142 KB variant. The observation does not establish that larger documents are faster. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Request timing, document delivery and measurement variation can outweigh a small byte difference. Repeat interleaved control and candidate runs, inspect the timing distribution, and change one factor at a time so a favorable sample does not become a false optimization claim.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Avoid geometry reads that force layout inside deferred sections
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reading descendant geometry inside a section with content-visibility: auto can force layout of deferred content. Where the design permits, derive overlay bounds from the section's own box and a separate viewport-sized probe. Verify the approach with a complete interaction trace under representative mobile conditions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Deferred rendering helps only while measurement code respects its boundary. Narrow initialization timers can miss expensive layout work triggered elsewhere, so inspect the full interaction before attributing a delay.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep bulky derived geometry out of executable JavaScript when it can load as data
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Fetch bulky derived geometry as a separate asset when importing JSON would inline it into a JavaScript chunk. One recorded bundle grew from 22 to 41.9 KB gzipped after geometry was embedded; separating the data left 28.4 KB of JavaScript. Measure the data transfer separately and define loading and failure behavior. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Geometry is content rather than executable logic. Separating it can preserve a code budget and allow independent loading, but the smaller JavaScript figure must not be presented as the total cost of the experience.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Evaluate compressed module boundaries by what each page loads, not source reuse alone
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Extracting shared code can increase independently compressed JavaScript payloads, so measure the actual chunks each page loads. In one recorded experiment, sharing a small effect saved 1 B on one route but added 241 B on another. Splitting visual layers so a route loaded only its declared features saved 2,955 B. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Source deduplication and transfer-size reduction are different outcomes. Compression context, module overhead, and unused feature loading can outweigh a small reuse benefit. Choose boundaries from measured loading behavior while retaining maintainable code.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Attribute long rendering tasks with controlled variants before blaming the last WebGL call
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An opacity-hidden canvas can continue drawing and distort software-renderer timing experiments. In one investigation, a 5.5 s task appeared at a later synchronous GL call; controlled variants recorded 0 ms with display:none, GL disabled, or no WebGL, and 191 ms with canvases visible. Long Animation Frames helped attribute the work. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The call that pays for queued work is not necessarily the source of that work. Compare multiple controls before theorizing, then validate the replacement probe with a deliberate delay; a 90 ms injected delay was detected in this case.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure texture uploads as part of initialization and yield between bounded upload batches
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Texture upload work can create a long initialization task even when surrounding JavaScript is split into small steps. In one 4x CPU-throttled test, 1376x768 uploads took 25–34 ms and contributed to a 62 ms task. Consider uploading bounded bands across separate macrotasks and measure the resulting behavior. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These timings describe one test environment, not a device guarantee. Splitting decoding or setup alone does not split the upload. Preserve the fallback until all required texture data is ready for a complete frame.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Load scene-specific data separately from shared renderer code
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Fetch scene-specific data when its scene is needed if importing it causes every page to ship every scene's configuration. Store the data alongside the relevant assets, validate its shape and provide a failure fallback. A measured bundle example removed 6.2 KB of gzipped scene data from shared code, reducing a renderer payload from 17.4 KB to 11.2 KB. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared rendering logic does not imply shared scene payloads. Separating them can reduce unnecessary downloads, although the extra request and loading behaviour must also be evaluated.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Count shader-string comments in client bundle budgets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Comments inside GLSL strings embedded in JavaScript can remain part of the downloaded client payload. Move explanatory prose outside shader strings or use a shader-aware processing step, then inspect the production bundle. One measured case removed 13 embedded comments, saving about 670 B gzipped and resolving a 570 B overrun against a 30 KB WebGL budget. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] JavaScript minification does not necessarily strip text inside strings. A shared renderer change can also push an otherwise untouched page over its budget, so validate every consuming page.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Control host contention before interpreting throttled browser measurements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat throttled browser measurements as inconclusive when substantial concurrent work is competing for the host CPU. Under 4× CPU throttling, compare the baseline and candidate in equivalent conditions, preferably after other jobs finish, and repeat the measurements. A system load of 7–13 requires interpretation relative to the host's capacity. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Environmental contention can make both versions fail the same control. Even candidate slices of 23/22 ms versus baseline slices of 28/32 ms would not establish an improvement without a controlled comparison and an estimate of variation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check shared dependencies when an unrelated route's bundle grows
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A change to a shared chunk can increase a route's payload even when none of that route's files change. One shared-import edit added 99 B gzipped to a route with an unchanged-payload requirement. Place scene-specific behavior in a separately loaded module when it does not belong in the shared renderer. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Source-file boundaries do not guarantee delivery boundaries. Compare emitted route assets to verify that an isolated change is also isolated in the build.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check every consuming route after changing a shared bundle
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A shared-chunk edit can increase the payload of routes that were not the intended target of the change. One observed edit added 99 B gzipped to another route. Record route-level compressed sizes before and after shared code changes, and compare them with the project's explicit budgets. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Source ownership and delivery ownership differ: a small component change may travel through a common bundle to many pages. Route-level checks reveal this coupling and help determine whether code belongs in a shared module or a feature-specific entry point.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use simulated audience reviews to generate hypotheses for real usability checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate a website through distinct audience scenarios that vary goals, familiarity, constraints, and accessibility needs. Ask each simulated reviewer to record the task attempted, observed page evidence, points of confusion, and suggested fixes. Synthesize findings by severity and corroboration rather than averaging subjective scores alone. Keep the reusable evaluation framework separate from any private research library. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Multiple simulated perspectives can reveal overlooked questions, but a fleet of roughly 50 agents is not equivalent to 50 independent users. Shared model biases can produce repeated assumptions and fictional reactions. Treat the reports as hypotheses, validate claims against the interface, and use real user research for conclusions about actual audience behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep an automation's review role stable across long runs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Specify an automation's role, evaluation lens, and communication conventions at startup, then preserve those responsibilities through clarification, execution, and handoff. Put the role contract near the top of the operating guide and carry its relevant constraints into delegated tasks. Define an explicit completion boundary so later work does not accidentally inherit an obsolete role. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Long runs can drift from a careful reviewer into an uncritical implementer, weakening the original checks. Stable roles help maintain continuity, but theatrical character persistence should never override factual accuracy, clear communication, or instructions. The transferable value is consistent responsibility and judgment, not preserving a fictional personality at all costs.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate reusable competency from optional personal configuration in distributable packages
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A reusable starter package should keep shared competency separate from optional personal configuration. Build an agnostic mode that includes generic procedures and examples while allowing the recipient to define their own working style. If a private migration mode is needed, make inclusion of personal configuration explicit and keep it outside the public seed. Test both packaging paths, including generated files, examples and installer defaults, for accidental cross-contamination. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A package can teach useful methods without importing someone else's identity or assumptions. Separating these layers also makes updates easier: shared fixes can reach every installation without overwriting the recipient's choices.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Ship portable reasoning lenses with reversible installation and opt-in background execution
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A public reasoning toolkit should separate reusable perspectives from personal lore and autonomous execution. Offer generic lenses for precedent, skepticism, architecture, alternatives and synthesis. Keep interactive use the default, and make any global installation additive and reversible: inspect existing files, back up conflicts and provide an uninstall path. Background model calls and recurring jobs should require explicit configuration with clear usage implications. Store secrets in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Useful reasoning patterns do not require importing another person's identity. Interactive use also avoids hidden scheduled work; local execution still consumes resources, and neither local nor in-session reasoning should be described as universally free.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make persona configuration a testable interaction contract
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A reusable persona configuration should define its role, version, scope, behavioral defaults, quality checks, and response to uncertainty or failure. Optional creative fields can describe voice, habits, and sources of curiosity, but keep them subordinate to truthful task execution. A calm, low-arousal baseline can be stated explicitly without pretending the system has human emotions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Rich character details are useful only when they improve behavior. Numerical trait weights and long catchphrase lists are design conventions, not validated measurements; assess the resulting outputs against practical acceptance criteria.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Differentiate agent roles by decisions and evidence standards
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define agent roles through distinct responsibilities, evidence standards, and failure checks. For example, one role may design controlled comparisons, another verify provenance, and another preserve anomalous runs for audit. Explain how their responsibilities interact and where authority ends. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Different names and personalities do not guarantee different reasoning contributions. Operational distinctions make coordination easier to assess and reduce duplicated review, while role effectiveness still requires observation rather than a decorative uniqueness score.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Connect reflection outputs to an explicit, bounded behavior-update path
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A reflection system needs an explicit path from stored observations to material loaded in later sessions. Configure the relevant tags, candidate destination and session-loading behavior rather than hard-coding a particular persona. Separate unconfirmed observations from governing instructions, and require review before changing foundational behavior. Verify the entire path with a real candidate and a later session. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Producing reflections does not demonstrate learning if nothing consumes them. A bounded update path makes changes visible and traceable while preventing speculative generated text from silently becoming authoritative instructions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define a configurable persona lifecycle during setup
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Record persona configuration at creation time so later reflection and review can operate without identity-specific code. A manifest can identify observation tags, foundational files, candidate records and the material loaded at session start. Keep user-authored foundations separate from generated suggestions, and document which transitions require confirmation. Validate the configuration before enabling scheduled processing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reusable lifecycle depends on explicit interfaces rather than assumptions about one installation. Capturing those interfaces during setup prevents generated material from being written somewhere no session reads, or from modifying files intended to remain under user control.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate frequent observation from reviewed changes to persistent instructions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Separate behavioral adaptation into observation, synthesis and ratification. Collect observations frequently, periodically propose a concise change supported by independent evidence, and update persistent instructions only after review. A candidate should name the triggering situation, intended behavior and relevant foundational section. Treat thresholds such as three confirmed examples as configurable proposal criteria, not automatic permission to edit. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Frequent sensing captures useful context, but frequent self-rewriting can amplify one bad inference. Separating the stages allows responsiveness without granting generated observations authority over the instructions that govern future work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep generated candidates separate from live instructions until ratification
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Store generated behavior-change candidates outside live instruction files until a user ratifies them. Make candidate generation idempotent on its cited evidence, filter machine telemetry from human-authored observations and surface candidates where they will actually be seen. Append confirmed decisions with provenance; report stale candidates without promoting them. Before any permitted file write, resolve symlinks and verify the destination stays within the authorized directory. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated nightly processing can manufacture apparent consensus from the same evidence. Separating candidates from instructions prevents repetition from becoming authority, while path confinement protects against accidental writes through aliases.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Design agent personas around observable behavior and explicit boundaries
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Structure an agent persona around its role, tasks, behavior, and constraints, then evaluate whether those instructions improve actual outputs. Describe traits such as directness, rigor, warmth, verbosity, and epistemic humility as concrete actions under specific conditions. Optional weights from 0 to 1 can document emphasis, but they do not measure a model's personality. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A coherent behavioral specification can improve consistency without invented personal history or staged mistakes. Do not treat a reported correlation of ρ ≥ 0.90 as established without its study context. Filler phrases, artificial errors, and higher perplexity are not reliable evidence of authenticity or quality.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use versioned persona schemas with explicit behavior and testable constraints
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Store agent persona settings in a versioned schema with an identifier, description, behavioral traits, knowledge scope, and constraints. An optional three-part trait allocation can use weights of 0.40, 0.35, and 0.25, validated to sum to 1.0. Include examples of acknowledging limits and correcting errors when warranted. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Structured settings are easier to inspect and compare than sprawling character biographies. Trait weights are configuration conventions, not scientifically calibrated controls. Avoid fabricated expertise, simulated delays, and intentional mix-ups. Any fictional flavor should remain clearly fictional and subordinate to truthful communication and reliable task execution.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Share behavioral standards across orchestration and bounded agent tasks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Load a workflow's operating guide and behavioral specification before orchestration, and pass the relevant standards to delegated tasks. Translate personality language into explicit rules: check coverage before declaring completeness, reassess scope when work exceeds capacity, and report failures without concealing them. Keep communication style consistent while identifying separate agents accurately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared standards reduce inconsistent decisions across a workflow. A persona can organize instructions, but it does not establish causal quality gains or replace tests. Behavioral rules should remain inspectable and effective even when all fictional characterization is removed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build dependent capabilities in stages with recovery points and explicit design rationale
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Sequence a system roadmap by dependency, capturing design rationale and a tested recovery point before each major stage. Apply the same acceptance discipline to foundational and user-facing components. Schedule environment upgrades at natural boundaries before dependent work begins, and periodically review system health, proposed improvements, and candidates for removal. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Later features cannot compensate for missing foundations, and a snapshot is useful only if restoration works. Preserve decisions, constraints, and evidence in focused memories rather than maximizing entry count or word count. A recurring review should produce prioritized proposals tied to observed problems; it should not automatically expand the system merely because a calendar interval has elapsed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Consult specialist procedures at consequential decisions and repeated stalls
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use specialist review when a decision exceeds current expertise, affects many downstream artifacts or remains unresolved after 3 or more iterations. Map workflow stages to relevant disciplines: intake to requirements, images to art direction, factual claims to evidence review, and architecture to interface and failure analysis. For a bounded question, read the relevant procedure and references, extract its decision rules, and apply them to the current evidence. Execute the full workflow when its deliverables are actually needed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Targeted consultation can expose assumptions before they spread through a build. Repeatedly simulating different voices is not independent verification; useful consultation contributes specific checks, counterexamples or evidence. Mechanical edits usually need execution rather than another review layer.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bound polish iterations after the release floor is met
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A release process can pursue polish without endless iteration by separating mandatory acceptance from optional refinement. One explicit policy is to reach a 9.8/10 review floor, then allow at most 2 additional iterations toward 10/10. Start that counter only after every required gate passes. Ship the best verified candidate when the polish budget ends, provided it still satisfies the floor. Privacy leaks, broken behavior and other release blockers remain blockers regardless of the score. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A stopping rule prevents diminishing cosmetic improvements from consuming unlimited effort. Preserve a passing candidate and recheck changed behavior so a final refinement does not replace a sound release with a regression.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate evidence gathering from positioning and messaging decisions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build an evidence package before turning research into positioning and website messaging. Gather product facts, buyer language, alternatives, competitive claims, and available proof; attach source URLs to factual claims and label unresolved gaps. Then construct the positioning, audience-specific messages, use cases, and risks under a separate review step. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separating research from synthesis makes unsupported claims easier to spot. One coherent position can support different audience emphases without averaging incompatible needs into vague copy. Explicit citation requirements and uncertainty labels should work together, rather than treating either as a substitute for evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Route strategy work by the decision needed and the evidence already available
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Choose a strategy workflow according to the question being answered rather than invoking every available framework. Diagnose unclear performance before rebuilding positioning; gather research when evidence is missing; synthesize messaging when research already exists. For a campaign, sequence strategy, existing-content assessment, planning, review, and production. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A ceramic studio asking why bookings fell may need a focused diagnosis rather than a complete brand overhaul. Routing by the decision and required output reduces duplicated work and prevents production from starting before audience, proof, and purpose are clear.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review consequential technology adoption before encoding it into standard practice
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Apply an explicit decision review when an unfamiliar technology could replace or materially change established architecture or workflows. Examine evidence, alternatives, compatibility, operational cost, failure modes, and rollback before recording adoption as settled policy or updating reusable automation. Use distinct review perspectives where they expose different risks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An attractive experiment can become permanent infrastructure through documentation alone. Keep the gate limited to consequential adoption decisions so routine maintenance, ordinary observations, and harmless research remain easy to perform.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify model capabilities and restrictions before building a dependent workflow
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Design model-dependent web workflows around verified capabilities and documented restrictions. Confirm supported tasks, restriction handling and whether fallback behavior changes the required output. Use a suitable supported model when necessary, and test with invented examples representative of the intended website feature. Record unresolved uncertainty explicitly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Speculation about hidden routing or trigger words is an unreliable engineering basis. Capability checks and observable behavior provide stronger foundations than unsupported promises about what a service will produce.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Record execution metadata before attributing an unexpected result to model routing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Investigate model fallback using explicit service notifications or response metadata. Record the requested model, reported execution model, task type, and documented fallback reason. Preserve uncertainty when execution details are unavailable. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Differences in writing can arise from sampling, context, configuration, or routing. Observable evidence prevents unsupported explanations from distorting web-development evaluations.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify repository-specific fixes against the actual code and relevant checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use general reasoning to develop hypotheses, then inspect the repository through an authorized coding workflow before validating a proposed fix. Read relevant files, make the necessary changes, and run appropriate checks. Separate verified conclusions from hypotheses. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Advice without code access cannot establish that a repository-specific repair works. Verification requires evidence from the implementation and its behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Account for task mix before comparing local fallback rates with aggregate claims
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define whether fallback rates count requests or sessions, record task categories and configurations, and sample a representative web-development workload. Compare equivalent tasks before proposing explanations for differences from aggregate rates. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A small set of demanding tasks cannot establish typical behavior. Prompt changes also alter the experiment, so assess output quality alongside routing outcomes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Assess planning through independent generation and critique of a shared baseline
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Compare planning approaches by asking each model to generate a website plan from the same brief and separately critique a shared baseline. Use equivalent context and resource limits. Keep independent generation isolated from the baseline and require reasons for proposed revisions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Generation reveals what a model notices unaided; critique reveals what it recognizes in an existing plan. Record baseline authorship because it can influence the comparison.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Compare generated plans, shared-baseline critiques, and consistency within each approach
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] In a two-model comparison, collect independent website plans and critiques of the same baseline. Compare plans across models, compare critiques, and check whether each model includes the safeguards it requests from others. Translate supported findings into concrete plan revisions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These views reveal different strengths and inconsistencies. They remain related observations and must not be counted as independent replications.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use identical self-contained briefs when testing reasoning from fixed context
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Include requirements, constraints, relevant evidence, and explicit unknowns directly in each evaluation brief. Disable external tools when testing reasoning from a fixed information set, and give every model identical context. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Controlled context reduces differences caused by search access and repository familiarity. Findings apply to that limited condition; live debugging requires a separate evaluation with tools.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep evaluation prompts relevant and track wording changes as experimental changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Write prompts around the web-development task, remove unrelated narrative, and disclose relevant constraints. Version prompt revisions and preserve the intended task meaning. Record declined or rerouted requests and use supported workflows. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Unrelated framing introduces confounds. A wording change alone does not reveal hidden routing rules, so comparisons require consistent meaning and transparent reporting.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Cover distinct reasoning demands when evaluating web-development assistance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build a task matrix covering architecture, ambiguous requirements, debugging, estimation, prioritization, data modeling, teaching, visual planning, and failure analysis. Label each task's primary reasoning demand and include multiple tasks where capability claims matter. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A polished implementation plan does not establish competence with uncertainty or competing constraints. Broad coverage reveals differences, while repetition supports stronger conclusions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Vary domain, scope, and difficulty independently of reasoning mode
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test each reasoning mode across multiple invented website contexts, such as a ceramic studio catalog and a bakery ordering page. Vary scope and pilot difficulty to avoid uniformly trivial or impossible tasks. Treat any target score range as a design heuristic. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A debugging task tied to only one domain can confuse domain familiarity with debugging ability. Balanced task selection makes capability comparisons easier to interpret.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use uncertain problems to test reasoning beyond polished plans
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Include ambiguous requirements, consequence analysis, analogy transfer, and attempts to disprove an initial diagnosis. Ask which observations would overturn a conclusion and which assumptions need clarification before implementation. Pilot tasks before claiming they distinguish approaches. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Formatting and decomposition can conceal weak reasoning. Tasks requiring belief revision may expose meaningful differences, but that possibility needs evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define statistical claims in advance and separate significance from adoption criteria
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Choose the primary paired-task metric, statistical test, and directional alternative before viewing results. Mark unplanned dimension-level findings as exploratory. Define whether an adoption threshold refers to relative improvement or percentage points, and report effect sizes, uncertainty, ties, and task coverage. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Practical value and statistical certainty answer different questions. Complex analysis cannot compensate for a sparse or unrepresentative task sample.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Budget evaluation work around a pilot, repeated core tasks, and exploratory breadth
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Run a pilot before committing the full evaluation budget. Separate repeated core tasks from exploratory tasks, calculate expected output counts explicitly, and budget retries with a fixed limit. Use observed pilot acceptance rates to refine cost estimates. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Explicit counts expose the cost of repetition and breadth. Exploratory findings warrant weaker claims than results supported by repeated core tasks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check whether familiar tasks or existing answers contaminate a comparison
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before reusing a website task, identify whether participants can access previous solutions or accumulated project context. Isolate answer artifacts and use fresh invented briefs when independent reasoning is the target. Document unavoidable prior exposure. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Convenient baselines can undermine measurement. An apparent planning advantage may reflect familiarity with an existing solution rather than stronger reasoning.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check whether the planned sample can support the intended statistical claim
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Determine the smallest attainable significance level for the chosen test and sample size before spending the evaluation budget. Distinguish independent tasks from repeated runs of the same task, and allocate task breadth and within-task repetition deliberately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A small study may be unable to support its intended claim even if every result points in the same direction. Repetition measures variability without automatically adding independent task evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match task difficulty and interaction format to the capability under evaluation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Pilot tasks to avoid floor and ceiling effects. Evaluate adaptive debugging through staged observations or an interactive website environment, and clearly identify static approximations. Use planning-only tasks for claims about planning from fixed evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Describing an investigation differs from updating it after an unexpected result. Removing feedback can exclude the very capability the evaluation intends to measure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat early qualitative observations as hypotheses to test on fresh tasks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Turn initial response differences into provisional evaluation dimensions, such as consequence awareness, outcome validation, resistance to metric gaming, and actionable repairs. Define observable examples and counterexamples, then test recurrence on fresh invented website tasks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Memorable responses help identify useful questions but do not establish stable traits. Separate discovering a hypothesis from confirming it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Evaluate software design reasoning separately from codebase implementation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use self-contained briefs for design reasoning and repository-enabled tasks for implementation ability. Fixed-context tasks can ask for decision logic, interpretation of an invented error log, or a data model. Record execution conditions without inferring undocumented routing rules. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reasoning about a design does not establish an ability to inspect and repair a codebase. Separate conditions produce clearer capability claims.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Evaluate planning across varied tasks and preserve complete responses with context
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Include architecture, ambiguous requirements, debugging, prioritization, data modeling, risk analysis, and teaching in planning evaluations. Save each complete response with its task identifier, prompt version, and execution conditions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeating one narrow task can overstate usefulness. Varied tasks reveal where an approach transfers, while complete records make conclusions inspectable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Sequence evaluation collection, critique, judging, and synthesis by their dependencies
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Create baseline plans before requesting critiques and collect matched outputs before ranking differences. Preserve prompts, document execution conditions, anonymize responses, and apply a shared rubric. Derive reusable guidance only from inspected supporting examples. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Each evaluation stage depends on evidence produced by the previous stage. Correct sequencing prevents unsupported critiques, rankings, and recommendations.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Align evaluation constraints with the capability being measured
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use single-response, tool-free tasks to test reasoning over fixed information. Include every necessary fact and require a distinction between evidence and assumptions. Evaluate repository inspection, browsing, and iterative repair separately when those capabilities matter. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Restricting external information improves experimental control while narrowing the conclusions. Claims should stay within the conditions actually tested.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat changes to an analogy as changes to the evaluation input
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Preserve original and revised prompts when changing an analogy. Use repeated comparisons and record execution differences without assuming their cause. Choose familiar invented examples that clarify the website problem, and state where the analogy stops applying. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful replacement supports a conclusion about that attempt, not a universal routing rule. Untracked reframing can change the task being evaluated.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate software design exercises from repository repair evaluations
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A software design exercise can be evaluated from an inline specification without granting repository access. Ask for logic, data structures, assumptions, edge cases, and verification steps; require invented details to be labeled. Evaluate repository repair separately using the actual code and relevant checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Designing from a summary and diagnosing an implementation require different evidence. A strong conceptual answer does not demonstrate that a model can locate a defect, integrate a fix, or preserve existing behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Apply reasoning guidance in proportion to the task
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use reasoning guidance as a lightweight aid to framing, alternatives, downstream effects, uncertainty, and root-cause analysis. Select only the moves relevant to the task, and verify that guidance is discoverable through the intended loading or retrieval mechanism. Keep a manual invocation path for diagnosis. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A cross-cutting checklist can improve consistency, but applying every technique to every task creates unnecessary work. Preserve a sound existing plan unless evidence identifies a concrete weakness that the additional reasoning can resolve.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give planning agents self-contained design tasks and bound concurrent requests
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A closed-book planning task should include its context, constraints, and output contract without requiring repository access or execution. Ask for alternatives, decomposition, assumptions, and failure scenarios; require invented details to be labeled. Describe the task honestly and keep execution or lookup work separate. For service calls, use bounded concurrency and backoff after rate-limit responses; batches of 4–5 are an experimental starting point, not a universal limit. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Clear task boundaries make plans easier to assess and prevent unsupported implementation claims. Bounded fan-out also keeps a temporary service limit from turning an entire planning batch into retries.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Pair a concise decision brief with a dependency-ordered website implementation plan
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Begin a website plan with its objective, scope, exclusions, tradeoffs, and assumptions. Sequence account setup, content, design, integrations, verification, and release by their dependencies. Maintain a versioned approved baseline and record reasons for material changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Detailed plans can obscure decisions. A concise brief and explicit prerequisites help builders continue after interruptions while distinguishing exploratory ideas from approved commitments.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use a governing design principle to connect visual choices with verifiable content
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] State a website's governing principle in terms that resolve concrete design and content decisions. For a seed library, a principle might be: make selection inviting while keeping growing conditions easy to verify. That can guide illustrated category cards, readable planting tables, sourced advice, and useful pages without JavaScript. Record evidence for consequential claims and keep private records outside the publishing inputs. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A good principle reduces repeated debates because each choice can be tested against the same purpose. Visual character and factual discipline become coordinated parts of the experience.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep future commerce options open without building an unneeded stack
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A content site can preserve future commerce options by keeping records exportable and documenting the triggers for adding authentication, billing, and authorization.
