For a neighbourhood bakery, an enquiry form does not yet require a subscription platform; online ordering would introduce distinct payment, access, and fulfillment requirements. Record those future requirements without treating a familiar stack as an approved choice. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Premature infrastructure adds maintenance before its value is established. Portable data and explicit decision triggers preserve flexibility, while pricing, dependency licenses, and operational readiness can be reviewed when commercial scope becomes concrete.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Sequence repository setup after safe authentication and distinguish references from implementation inputs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Schedule account-dependent setup only after its authentication boundary is available and verified. Organize assets, motion, documentation and prompts with a folder map, and explicitly label reference documents that must not become implementation requirements. Keep temporary editor lock files out of the canonical source set. If repository creation depends on isolated credentials, make that dependency visible in the plan. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A phase label does not make a prerequisite exist. Deferring a dependent action is sound sequencing, while clearly marked reference material prevents an unrelated example from quietly dictating the new site's architecture or copy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make research output structure follow the hard questions and prohibit invented measurements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Research prompts should assign each important question an explicit output section and require measured claims to carry evidence. Give overlapping topics a single owner, include a confirm-or-refute table for existing assumptions, and label arithmetic estimates as estimates. Ask for the date of the most recent source rather than implying that a requested date has evidence. Generate related prompts from one shared specification. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Research systems organize answers around the requested output structure; sharp questions buried in unnumbered context can disappear behind generic headings. For browser graphics research, explicit budgets such as 1200x560 CSS pixels at DPR 1.5, or approximately 1800x840 device pixels, make analysis concrete. Limits such as 300 stars, 500 threads and 20,000 particles are design inputs, not measured performance guarantees. Require discussion of first-frame handover, interaction startup and motion accessibility alongside rendering choices.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat external research prompts as disclosures and structure them around falsifiable questions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An external research prompt is an outbound document and should contain only information cleared for that audience. Describe the public problem without exposing private implementation details, internal measurements, personal data, or unpublished mechanisms. Give each research question a numbered section, request a mechanism comparison, and require supporting and contradicting evidence with references. Review the prompt for accuracy, disclosure, and leading assumptions before submission. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A question can reveal a design as effectively as a specification. Structured counter-evidence requests also reduce the chance that research merely confirms the claims the eventual website hopes to make.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distinguish unavailable evidence from refutation when commissioning research
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Research instructions must distinguish 'could not retrieve' from 'the evidence refutes this claim'. Require full-text inspection and section or table references for numerical claims, define each prompt's scope, and attach citations per table row when per-cell citations make the output unwieldy. Ask reviewers to separate a feature's behavior from adjacent platform features and explicitly seek counter-evidence. Run a final disclosure check after edits. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Search indexes can lag publications, and abstracts can omit decisive conditions. An independent critique can catch both inaccurate premises and questions that accidentally describe confidential mechanisms too precisely.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use reference implementations as evidence without expanding the change scope
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use an existing implementation to understand a mechanism, then verify its assumptions against the target application. Label reference-only material clearly and test the changed path independently. For an invented document-review tool, confirm that a reference approval flow matches the target roles and revision rules before adapting it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A working precedent can clarify an approach without proving that it works elsewhere. Explicit boundaries prevent scope creep and unsupported completion claims.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve conflicting requirements before building shared site components
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reconcile conflicting requirements before implementing shared layouts, navigation, forms and metadata. Inventory required components, existing code, missing assets and unresolved decisions in one canonical specification. Define accessible color roles, keyboard behavior, preview indexing, structured-data types and form success paths explicitly. Test no-JavaScript submission and return errors to the originating page. Keep unresolved infrastructure questions separate from settled design decisions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared components multiply contradictions across every page. Settling them early lets review rounds evaluate the implementation instead of repeatedly debating incompatible inputs, while a visible open-items list prevents assumptions from becoming accidental requirements.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use concrete editorial defaults to elicit useful corrections
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Present editorial decisions as a concrete proposed structure with explicit defaults and reasons. For an invented ceramic studio, propose a short process story, a sourcing statement and a workshop invitation, then identify the few choices that materially affect meaning. Remove duplicated proofs already maintained on other pages. Record which defaults were accepted and which feedback changed the framing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reviewers can respond more precisely to an actual draft than to an abstract request for direction. Their corrections reveal priorities, while a bounded brief keeps the conversation focused on decisions that change the result.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate safe editorial defaults from business decisions that need explicit answers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A review brief should distinguish proposed editorial defaults from unresolved business choices. Present the finished draft, explain what accepting it would approve and isolate any decision that changes the offer or scope. Give that decision enough context to assess its consequences, and preserve its unresolved status if a general approval does not clearly answer it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This reduces review effort without converting silence into authorization. Reviewers can accept routine wording together while spending attention on the choice that genuinely changes what the site promises.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate bounded polish from a major interaction redesign
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Put small layout corrections and a major visualization redesign into separate iterations with distinct acceptance criteria. A polish pass can verify headers at 320, 360, 390, 430 and 768 px, preserve touch targets and check text over artwork. Freeze the component scheduled for replacement until its dedicated pass begins. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Combining every request into one loop makes scope and verification grow together. Separating work produces reviewable previews and prevents an ambitious interaction from delaying straightforward fixes elsewhere.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give each page a purposeful interaction without delaying its core task
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Plan distinctive page interactions around the page's job while reusing established components and verification rules. A bakery homepage might animate an illustrated oven on pointer movement, while a contact page lights a small indicator after valid input. Navigation and form submission must proceed independently of decorative completion. Provide static and reduced-motion behavior from the outset. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] One purposeful new technique can distinguish a page without multiplying unrelated systems. Treating animation as enhancement protects the visitor's task and keeps performance, accessibility and testing within a manageable scope.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use citation overlap as a reproducibility signal, never as proof that a source is real
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Repeating a research query can reveal citation instability, but repeated URLs do not prove authenticity or claim support. Run a critical prompt twice with comparable settings, normalize the URL sets and compute Jaccard overlap. An overlap below 0.5 can trigger additional review as a chosen heuristic, not a validated fabrication threshold. Fetch important sources and verify their content directly; a successful HEAD request only establishes limited reachability. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Real sources may vary between runs, and fabricated citations may repeat consistently. Recording both URL lists, overlap and claim checks makes reproducibility useful without mistaking consistency for truth.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make fidelity expectations explicit before translating reference material into a website
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Establish whether reference material is binding before deciding how much creative freedom a build allows. A complete extraction bundle and page index can indicate reconstruction work, but the task's stated acceptance criteria determine authority. In strict-fidelity mode, preserve content, ordering, and approved structure; record necessary implementation deviations. In creative mode, use the brief to guide layout, copy, and interaction choices. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Filesystem presence alone is an unreliable decision rule because reference folders can be stale or merely inspirational. An explicit source hierarchy gives builders and reviewers the same definition of correctness and prevents unexpected changes from being defended as improvements.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Do not confuse a model's predicted measurement with the human state you want to understand
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A model that predicts a physiological measurement does not automatically measure emotion, intent, or behavior. Before using research-model output to guide interface decisions, identify its training target, input conditions, temporal resolution, validation population, and documented limitations. Distinguish predicted signals from direct observations and from downstream interpretations. Require separate evidence for any proposed relationship to usability or user experience. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Technically sophisticated outputs can invite claims beyond what a model was trained to establish. Keeping the measured construct separate from the desired business or design conclusion prevents scientific terminology from becoming unsupported evidence for product decisions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose execution architecture against explicit constraints and revisit it when those constraints change
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Compare browser runtimes, server execution, hosted embeds and JavaScript implementations against the actual delivery constraints. Server execution adds operational and abuse-control responsibilities; hosted embeds require checking data handling, styling and availability; JavaScript is appropriate when the logic is small enough to maintain safely. Browser runtimes can preserve existing code and local processing, but offline use requires cached or bundled dependencies. Prefer Workers for expensive hosted computation and assess isolation whenever executed code is untrusted. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An architecture wins under particular assumptions. Local-file delivery, offline requirements and data sensitivity can change the winner, so record the reasons instead of turning one project's choice into a universal rule.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve positioning before page messaging and batch related decisions to reduce approval fatigue
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Establish audience, offering and positioning before asking someone to approve page-level messaging. Present related decisions together when they depend on the same assumptions. Give figure labels and constrained components character budgets before copy is finalized, then batch necessary build-stage copy changes into a clear diff. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated approvals lose value when later decisions invalidate earlier ones. Ordering dependencies first reduces rework, while fewer coherent review packets preserve attention for meaningful judgment. Character budgets also prevent a layout problem from triggering scattered, unreviewed changes to previously accepted claims.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Split graphics research into decision-focused questions with explicit output requirements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Structure graphics research around implementation decisions, operating constraints and evidence requirements. Separate renderer selection, production hardening, interaction physics, art direction and graph legibility so each report answers a clear question. For an amateur astronomy club, specify complete HTML content without JavaScript, readable labels, reduced-motion handling and a mobile Lighthouse target of at least 90. Request sources, assumptions and implementation tradeoffs. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Broad inspiration searches rarely resolve engineering choices. Share the visual and functional requirements rather than private project internals. Drafting prompts while independent work proceeds is useful, but research spending and dependent implementation still need their own authorized scope and readiness checks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Parallelize research and implementation only across independent dependencies
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Run research alongside implementation only when the implementation does not depend on unfinished findings. Write down which components consume each research output, then begin independent work such as content structure, basic forms or design tokens. Hold renderer selection and research-dependent interactions until their inputs are reviewed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Parallel work saves waiting only when dependencies remain explicit. Otherwise, early guesses harden into code and create rework. A dependency map makes productive waiting possible while preserving clear stopping points; an unanswered suggestion to add a tool or service should remain unapproved rather than becoming an implicit installation decision.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Map research outputs to components and use complete fallbacks while waiting
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give each research-dependent component a named input, readiness criterion and usable fallback. An astronomy club's hero can render a complete still image while its interactive star field waits for renderer and accessibility findings. Constellation labels and linking rules should wait for legibility research rather than borrowing untested assumptions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A written dependency map distinguishes work that is safe to start from work that only appears independent. Review periods are useful slots for checking report completeness, following primary sources and building small demonstrations. Log unresolved dependencies so a temporary fallback remains intentional and an unfinished input cannot quietly become an accepted design decision.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Compare alternatives through the buyer's task and setup burden
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Competitive research should include the alternatives a buyer would actually choose, not just technically similar products. Compare the task solved, setup effort, required expertise, operational limits, and evidence for each capability. Distinguish a complete feature from partial coverage. Treat an apparently empty market position as a finding within the sources checked, not proof that no alternative exists. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Technical categories can conceal the simplest competitor: an easier way to finish the same job. A comparison matrix helps separate common vocabulary from meaningful differences and shows which proposed advantages need live-page verification before entering public copy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Turn research findings into scoped claims and concrete acceptance tests
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use literature reviews to narrow claims and derive tests, rather than treating abstracts as proof of product performance. Read the relevant methods and results before publishing a number. Separate common mechanisms, useful capabilities, and potentially distinctive combinations. If research identifies a failure such as outdated information surviving retrieval, turn that scenario into an acceptance test before promising the opposite. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A paper's result depends on its models, tasks, and experimental setup. Compatibility does not imply equal capability across configurations. Retaining raw sources and rechecking behavior after component changes makes both technical repairs and public explanations more defensible.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat generated research as provisional until its claims are checked
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A complete research report is still provisional until its consequential claims and quotations have been verified at their sources. Check structural completeness separately from factual correctness. For competitor comparisons, record which products, documents, and mechanisms were inspected. Translate 'none found' into a bounded search result rather than a universal absence claim. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Detailed tables, numerous links, and confident synthesis can make unverified conclusions feel settled. Preserving an explicit provisional status prevents those conclusions from slipping into headlines while leaving the report useful as a map for targeted follow-up research.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verification should narrow differentiation claims and preserve corrections
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Classify checked research claims as confirmed, contradicted, or unsettled, then revise public messaging accordingly. Follow actual source URLs rather than trusting generated citation numbering. When a supposed differentiator is already documented elsewhere, remove its exclusivity claim while retaining any supported user benefit. State absence findings only within the inspected source set. Preserve a correction trail so earlier summaries do not reintroduce rejected claims. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Verification is valuable precisely because it changes the story. A narrower, supportable difference is stronger than a memorable 'only' claim built on missing evidence, and explicit corrections keep later writing from reviving attractive mistakes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify complete user workflows before claiming feature availability
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test supporting infrastructure and the complete user-facing workflow separately. Describe availability in terms of what the intended audience can actually access and complete, including relevant prerequisites or limitations. Update public wording when validated behavior changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An implemented component does not establish a usable feature. Clear availability labels keep claims aligned with observable behavior and give unfinished work concrete acceptance criteria.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test a platform boundary with two materially different packages
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate a proposed shared platform by building or specifying two packages with different workflows and dependencies. For example, compare a bicycle-repair co-op's service-booking tools with its volunteer rota. Identify what belongs in the shared layer and what each package should own, then test whether either requires inappropriate changes to the other. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] One successful extension may simply reflect assumptions tailored to that extension. A second, different use case exposes hidden coupling and gives stronger evidence that the platform boundary is useful rather than merely named.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify cited sources before turning research summaries into design rules
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Open the sources behind consequential research claims and confirm that they support the proposed design decision. Check the relevant passage, example, or screenshot rather than trusting a synthesis alone. Prioritize the references carrying the most weight and record unavailable or contradictory sources explicitly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A polished research summary can hide a dead link, a mismatched API version, or a source that says something narrower. Source verification turns a reading list into usable evidence and prevents unsupported conclusions from hardening into reusable craft guidance.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Draft against a planned fix only when publication is gated on verified delivery
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Copy may be prepared against an intended repair only if publication is blocked until the promised behavior is verified. Write a detailed repair handoff with reproducible evidence, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and a concrete release gate. For scheduled behavior, require evidence from a real scheduled run in addition to focused tests. Coordinate related work without weakening the proof required. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Approval to draft does not make an unfinished feature true. A release gate allows design and engineering to proceed together while preventing a confident promise from reaching readers before the repair actually delivers.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Scope related defects by dependency and evidence without conflating their status
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A repair handoff should include related findings with separate evidence, impact, and disposition. Check producer-consumer schema mismatches, nondefault configuration assumptions, misleading health checks, and fallback behavior that changes advertised results. Identify which defects block the current promise, which fit the same repair, and which remain separate limitations. Verify model or dependency licensing independently before making distribution claims. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A shared truth map can reduce repeated investigation, but bundling everything into one repair obscures completion. Explicit boundaries let a team fix connected causes while keeping unrelated limitations visible and accurately described.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate numerical behavior and installation when porting computation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When moving computation between backends, check installation, supported operations, precision assumptions and fallback behavior. Compare representative outputs and recalibrate decision thresholds where needed before claiming equivalent results. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A backend change can alter numerical behavior or invalidate surrounding assumptions even when execution succeeds. Document supported combinations based on complete workflow checks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Land shared correctness fixes, align their dependencies, then connect setup flows
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A shared-policy migration should land the core fix, align its dependencies and only then connect setup flows to it. If unrelated feature work delays an important correction, consider a separately reviewed change. Prefer one shared implementation; where vendoring is necessary, record its source version and verify parity. Reuse existing valid declarations, provide explicit setup choices when missing and audit every caller for bypasses. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Adding an installer question before runtime reads the answer correctly produces reassuring interaction without reliable behavior. Updating an isolated branch can also leave the released application unchanged. A sequenced migration keeps each visible improvement backed by the code that actually runs.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate environment discovery from resource-selection policy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Put environment discovery behind an interface that reports available resources and supported operations. Keep selection rules separate from discovery and execution, and test each implementation against the same interface contract. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This separation makes platform changes easier to assess without rewriting application policy. A shared interface does not establish compatibility; each implementation still needs functional validation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate factual accuracy, cross-claim consistency and audience relevance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A page can pass factual checks while remaining contradictory across sections or unpersuasive to its intended audience. Review individual claims against sources, compare related claims with each other, and ask unfamiliar readers what would make the offering useful to them. Record unresolved positioning decisions separately from wording defects. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Another copy revision cannot supply a missing reason to care. Repeated accurate comprehension without interest suggests a question about the offer or audience, while conflicting source facts require correction upstream.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recognize when missing product evidence limits what copy can accomplish
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Once readers understand the category and development status, further persuasion may depend on demonstrable capability rather than better wording. Ask what readers can inspect, try or verify, and separate those gaps from remaining clarity defects. Do not present planned functionality as available to make a page more compelling. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Naming the category solves recognition; it does not prove usefulness. Continuing to polish language around an untested offer can consume effort while the decisive next step is a working demonstration or a clearer available service.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Clearer copy can reveal that no useful offer is currently available
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Improved comprehension can reduce interest when it reveals that the advertised options are not yet available. For a tide-pool field guide, distinguish a usable guide, a planned app and a request for future updates. Ask readers what they could do today, then resolve gaps in the offer itself. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Honest clarity may expose a business decision that vague copy concealed. A positive response followed by a negative response from different individual readers is not evidence of a trend; their explanations identify questions worth investigating.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inspect approved copy, factual status and rendered structure before writing a page brief
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build a page brief from three complementary inspections: approved wording, current factual status and the actual page structure. Identify stale claims, content that must remain stable, reusable components, heading constraints and metadata fields. Independent read-only inspections can proceed alongside unrelated final edits. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A brief written from assumptions can encode obsolete facts or impossible layout requirements. Frontloading these checks exposes conflicts before drafting and gives the writer a coherent set of constraints to satisfy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Surface conflicts between mandatory wording and repetition rules before forcing a paraphrase
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check whether mandatory wording, repetition limits, and standalone clarity can all be satisfied together. If an approved phrase is effectively unusable elsewhere, test a concise category description that preserves the fact and identify which rule needs an exception or revision. Keep any interim choice explicit. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeatedly inventing near-synonyms can introduce semantic drift without resolving the underlying contradiction. A documented conflict is more useful than a superficially compliant sentence that quietly changes what the site claims.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reconcile conflicting design instructions before implementing their next revision
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When the original brief, later decisions, approved implementation and automated checks disagree, document the conflict and establish which instruction governs the next change. For example, a bakery menu might specify a left-to-right highlight completed in 0.5 seconds while a later implementation uses a static highlight. Trace both requirements and their approval history. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated summaries can gradually replace a specific visual requirement without anyone explicitly deciding to change it. Neither the oldest request nor the latest implementation automatically resolves contradictory evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve conflicting graphics advice with scoped decisions and reopening criteria
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Turn conflicting implementation advice into decision records that state the context, evidence and conditions for reconsideration. For a lightweight decorative figure, candidate defaults might include raw WebGL2 with a helper, sprite halos, static dither, a DPR cap of 1.5, 48 px targets and a 200 ms reveal. Treat these as choices to validate, not universal winners. Reduced motion can skip GPU initialization while preserving SVG hover and focus highlights. A one-time quality reduction may be simpler than continuous resolution changes when the workload is stable. Record unresolved questions separately from decisions supported by tests. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A list of conclusions loses the circumstances that made them sensible. Preserving alternatives and evidence avoids repeatedly debating settled details while allowing a new device target, visual requirement or measured failure to justify a different choice.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat research summaries as leads until their consequential claims are checked
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify consequential research claims against primary evidence before turning them into implementation rules. Classify each claim as confirmed, contradicted or unresolved, and retain the supporting passage or measurement. Check that a cited page actually contains the quoted statement, that package-size figures use the intended version and compression, and that release dates are not merely aggregator timestamps. Recompute percentages: a fraction of 0.004 is 0.40%, not 0.004%. Inspect licences directly and verify browser support on the target environment. A successful link fetch proves availability, not relevance or truth. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Plausible citations can conceal category errors, stale facts and invented quotations. A claim-level audit prevents uncertain research from becoming a confident rule that later builders repeat without seeing its weaknesses.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure the variable that governs the outcome rather than an attractive proxy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Completion counts and nominal durations can misrepresent quality when they omit the variable that actually governs the outcome. A completed extraction job may still miss important facts; an 8 s scroll-scrubbed clip may be crossed in under a second. Define success using independently checkable content coverage or experienced interaction behavior. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Convenient dashboard numbers can create confidence without explaining usefulness. Test across conditions that change the governing variable, such as difficult documents or fast and slow scrolling, and avoid treating a single favorable run as evidence of consistent quality.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Combine browser coverage with real-device tests and user preference checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Cross-browser testing should include representative browser engines and real mobile devices, not only resized desktop windows. Check Chromium, Firefox and Safari, with real iPhone and Android coverage where they matter to the audience. Choose an older supported browser from audience evidence rather than freezing an arbitrary version into the checklist. Exercise navigation, forms, scrolling and viewport changes. Inspect JavaScript errors, CSP violations and mixed-content warnings. Test reduced-motion preferences and any supported dark theme. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Device emulation is useful for layout coverage but does not reproduce every mobile browser behavior, input method or viewport transition. A small, deliberate test matrix catches meaningful compatibility failures without treating every browser combination as equally valuable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify the renderer and capture-tool limits before interpreting browser automation results
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Inspect the browser's renderer information before treating a headless graphics capture as evidence of hardware acceleration. Record software rendering when present. Check both the capture timeout and the surrounding tool deadline, and save artifacts in authorized locations. Use supported source-retrieval methods when a page request fails. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Measurement constraints can resemble application defects. Successful capture establishes what was rendered, while renderer evidence determines which performance conclusions are justified.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review sticky and fixed layers through viewport captures at explicit scroll positions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Capture sticky and fixed layers at the top, middle, and bottom of their containers for each relevant viewport size. Use these viewport captures for contrast and other pixel checks. Keep full-page images as overviews and document their limitations for pinned content. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A full-page image may depict a sticky element only at its initial position. Reviewing actual scroll states prevents capture artifacts from driving unnecessary design changes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use visitor-visible captures and state the limits of desktop mobile emulation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Pixel-based audits of pinned imagery should use viewport captures taken at the container's top, middle and bottom. Compare them with a full-page capture to establish whether the overview misrepresents the sticky layer. Keep capture positions and interaction states explicit so contrast and image-coverage checks inspect the same visible scene. Test browser-toolbar expansion and collapse on a suitable real-device setup when those transitions matter. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A screenshot can be internally consistent yet depict a background no visitor sees while scrolling. Desktop mobile emulation also does not reproduce a mobile browser's toolbar lifecycle; report that missing coverage rather than converting it into a pass.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Probe computed styles with scripts disabled after changing generated CSS
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test computed SVG styles with JavaScript disabled when CSS is assembled through template strings. A missing declaration block can leave a valid-looking selector while stars fall back to black fill, even though builds and unrelated checks pass. Assert the intended computed fill and prove the check rejects an injected fill:initial rule. If script-dependent style injection stalls, alter the served response through Playwright routing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Syntax checks may not understand embedded CSS. Testing the static presentation catches defects that disappear once the live renderer takes over.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Scale visual probe search radii to the feature being measured
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A brightest-pixel search must stay inside the intended feature rather than use a fixed desktop-sized radius. At a 390 px viewport, a 12 px search disc can reach a bright rim whose radius is only 10.5 px and misidentify it as the core. Use a bound such as min(12 px, 0.5 times the rim radius), then compare the same saved frames. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This failure can look like unstable artwork when the measurement has moved onto another feature. Geometry-aware sampling reduces that ambiguity; separately verify that the smaller search still detects legitimately displaced cores.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Isolate visual subjects with references captured from the same paused frame
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A live-minus-reference visual probe should compare the same paused frame with only the measured subject hidden. Disabling every animated layer contaminates the difference with unrelated glow and motion. For shape checks, pair p90/p10 with max/median: thin spikes occupying under 10% of samples can evade percentiles. A four-point defect produced percentile ratios of 1.28–1.46, passing a 1.6 threshold, while max/median reached 4.64–5.71 and failed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Controlled subtraction distinguishes an actual shape defect from a changing background. Record the subject position and excluded sectors, and keep a thin-feature mutation to demonstrate that the probe remains sensitive.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test both stability and displacement sensitivity when shrinking probe searches
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Bound brightest-pixel recentering by feature geometry, then test whether the bound preserves legitimate displacement detection. A practical candidate is min(12 px, 0.5 times rim radius); an uncapped 12 px search can reach the rim of a 10.5 px feature at a 390 px viewport. Repeat unchanged frames at least three times and plant a core offset of 0.3 times the feature radius. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Stable passes alone do not establish causality when artwork changed alongside the probe. Compare capped and uncapped searches on identical assets, and retain provisional confidence until the displacement test or an isolated reproduction resolves the remaining uncertainty.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reuse subject-hidden capture hooks to isolate different animated effects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A same-frame subject-hidden capture hook can isolate light, shape or motion without removing unrelated scene layers. Pause the scene, capture it, hide only the target draw or layer, and capture again with all other state fixed. Verify that an intended unchanged initial frame produces mean difference 0 and p99 difference 0. For shape measurements, supplement percentile spread with a statistic sensitive to thin protrusions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reference that disables the whole animation answers a different question from an element-level probe. Reusing controlled capture hooks makes new checks less vulnerable to background contamination while preserving meaningful negative controls.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define visual metrics around the required shape and disclose blind regions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A visual gate is evidence only for defects its measurement can distinguish within the region it examines. If the requirement is round points, count compact round shapes rather than arbitrary bright blobs that may be dashes or reflections. Apply the same definition to reference and candidate. Name regions too small to provide useful discrimination, such as a 120 px strip expected to contain only about two points. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A plausible count can pass visibly wrong artwork. Inspect crops in weakly covered regions and retain rejected examples to test whether the metric measures the intended property rather than a convenient proxy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose metrics that detect the full defect rather than a convenient local proxy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A local step-size limit cannot establish that an entire fade has a smooth, monotonic luminance profile. A transition can pass a maximum four-pixel step threshold of 15 with a reading of 13.4 while accumulating an approximately 40-level dip that looks like a border. Sample the full fade trajectory when monotonicity is the requirement. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The same mismatch occurs when counting bright fragments as stars or accepting tiny regions with too few expected features to discriminate. Define the visible failure first, demonstrate that the metric detects it, and disclose regions or behaviors that remain dependent on inspection.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use computed-style checks when pixel metrics cannot distinguish acceptable and defective visual forms
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a pixel metric cannot separate accepted and rejected examples, test the element's computed form and bound its critical dimensions. For a feathered text veil, inspect backgrounds, shadows, mask geometry and feather width. In one calibration, rejected boxes scored 23.8–39.9 while accepted halos scored 22.6–41.8, making an edge-step threshold of 25 unsuitable. Keep those pixel measurements as diagnostic evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Background artwork can dominate an edge measurement. A structural check isolates the implementation responsible for the shape, but checking only that a mask is radial is insufficient: a tightly feathered ellipse can still look like a card. Treat this approach as provisional until visual review and deliberately defective variants confirm its coverage.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A visual test pass supports only the properties and regions the test can actually observe
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define visual metrics around the required shape and explicitly identify regions where the test cannot detect a defect. A star counter should distinguish compact round points from bright thread fragments. A narrow region expecting about two stars may provide weak evidence even when its count passes. Apply the same measurement to reference and candidate images. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Convenient proxies can produce convincing green logs for visibly wrong results. Median-row grading misses defects confined to fewer than half the rows; consider a calibrated high percentile or masked worst-row check. When a fix moves the beginning of a fade, move the inspected span too. A small maximum pixel step cannot establish that an entire luminance ramp is monotonic. Complement each blind spot with a different measurement or direct visual inspection.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bound visual geometry at its weakest point rather than its easiest measurement point
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A computed-form visual gate should measure its critical parameter where the geometry provides the least protection. For an elliptical veil, calculate the distance from each text-box corner toward the transparent rim instead of relying solely on CSS side insets. Require the corners to remain within the intended opaque region and test a deliberately tightened variant. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A radial mask can pass a type check while remaining visibly cramped. Side measurements of several rem do not prove equivalent corner clearance, and a rough diagonal factor is no substitute for evaluating the actual ellipse. Use structural gates when calibrated pixel metrics cannot separate good and bad examples, retain pixel figures as diagnostics, and keep visual review because computed form remains a proxy for appearance.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prototype mobile CSS in a browser session and measure each stop before committing the change
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use a temporary style element in a Playwright-controlled page to test candidate layout rules without repeated deploys. Replace its textContent for each trial, visit every reading hold and compare text and label rectangles using getBoundingClientRect. Useful viewport samples include 360x640, 375x667, 390x664, 390x844 and 430x932. Copy successful rules into source, then run the normal checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Browser-local CSS injection makes the proposal measurable without modifying server files or other visitors' pages. Record overlap amounts, not just screenshots. Also inspect hover and pointer media-query results: a narrow desktop context can show pointer instructions instead of touch instructions, so its measurements may describe a different layout than the intended phone experience.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inspect rendered pages across viewports before requesting human review
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use Playwright to inspect a local or preview build before presenting frontend work for review. Capture pages at widths of 1440, 768, and 375px, inspect the accessibility tree, and exercise navigation and important interactions. Check loaded images, content completeness, cards, overflow, and unresolved placeholders. Fix observed defects and rerun affected checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Browser inspection catches problems that source review cannot establish. If a browser context closes, recreate the session. HTML fetching can help diagnose missing markup, but it cannot verify layout, interaction, or visual accessibility; report that limitation if browser testing remains unavailable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Freeze animation state before comparing canvas screenshots
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Canvas screenshot comparisons are meaningful only when animation state is controlled or timing variance is explicitly accommodated. Prefer seeded randomness, time fixed at t=0 and initial displacement d(0)=0, with a test hook that pauses rendering at the reference frame. Compare canvas size, position, aspect ratio, background and device-pixel scaling. If freezing is impossible, calibrate a regional tolerance such as 5% against known good and defective captures. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Different particle positions can create false regressions, but broad tolerances can hide real defects. Deterministic captures make poster parity and layout errors visible while preserving stricter checks for static text and controls.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Locate consent dialogs by accessible role instead of assuming a generated element ID
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Consent-modal tests should locate the actual accessible dialog rather than assume a library-generated ID. An observed vanilla-cookieconsent v3 preferences modal used the .pm class rather than an element ID of pm; verify the installed version's markup. Prefer a scoped Playwright dialog locator with an accessible name, then assert visibility and exercise its controls. Use a class selector only when necessary. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A nonexistent ID can produce a false failure even while the modal is visible and functional. Role-based assertions better reflect user interaction and are less coupled to incidental markup, though multiple dialogs still require precise scoping.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Respect configured screenshot output roots and verify files were created
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Save browser screenshots within the tool's configured output roots and verify the resulting artifact exists before relying on it. A Playwright MCP setup may restrict writes to a directory such as .playwright-mcp/; that is an environment constraint, not a universal Playwright requirement. Export or copy the artifact afterward only where permissions allow. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A screenshot command can fail because of the destination rather than the page or browser. Checking the allowed path first avoids repeated capture attempts and keeps a missing artifact from being mistaken for successful visual verification.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify the rendering backend before interpreting browser graphics measurements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Browser automation can use a software renderer, so a WebGL2 context alone does not prove hardware GPU execution. Record the renderer and verify the intended device before interpreting frame rates. Save screenshots inside the tool's allowed output root. If a heavy scene exceeds a wrapper's 5-second screenshot limit, use an authorized Playwright path with page.screenshot({timeout:45000}). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A longer timeout can capture a software-rendered scene but cannot make its timing representative of hardware. Headed mode is useful to investigate, yet the backend still needs verification.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Turn observed interface regressions into measurable browser checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build a browser regression battery around concrete geometry, interaction and fallback requirements. Check horizontal overflow at 320, 375 and 390 px; use 44×44 px as an explicit project target for controls, with documented inline-link exceptions. Verify reduced motion produces zero running animations and no-JavaScript mode retains usable content while hiding inactive controls. Exercise hover, focus, Enter and Escape, and measure layout shift during interaction against a chosen threshold such as 0.01. Open menus to verify viewport width and sticky-header offsets. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Screenshots and accessibility scans miss some size and state defects. Record measured values and preserve the command's real exit status. Mark environment gaps explicitly: a form requiring a Worker must also be tested on an environment that runs it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit measurement methods and viewport assumptions after each visual review
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify that visual checks observe the intended rendered state after each iteration. Align artwork and content breakpoints, sample backgrounds beneath text when assessing image-backed contrast, and inspect sticky layers at explicit scroll positions. Define image-coverage requirements for named viewport dimensions and cropping rules. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Automated checks and broad luminance summaries can miss local contrast failures. Coverage depends on geometry, so a universal percentage may reject an appropriate composition or certify the wrong state.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test graphics failure states and document measurement conditions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test browser graphics with scripts disabled, startup failures, unavailable rendering contexts, context loss and reduced motion. Verify keyboard controls, off-screen suspension, hidden tabs, touch scrolling, resizing and page restoration. Check the static fallback, accessible labels, contrast and layout stability. Record the browser, rendering mode and test conditions when reporting performance. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful page load does not establish reliable graphics behavior. Results from one rendering mode or test environment cannot establish performance in another.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use a hidden-canvas control to investigate software-rendering startup costs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Compare visible and hidden canvas runs before attributing a software-rendered browser's first-frame long task to application initialization. One observed headless Chromium case produced a 90-105 ms task at 4x CPU when the canvas first became visible; hiding it removed the task while leaving initialization slices unchanged. Treat that as a diagnostic observation, not a universal browser cost or proof of a particular compositor mechanism. Repeat the comparison with matched conditions and, where possible, an identified hardware-rendered run. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A rendering environment can add costs outside the code under review. A control helps isolate that contribution without excusing the visible delay or claiming that a hardware result has been demonstrated when only software rendering was tested.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Load and decode lazy images before taking a full-page design screenshot
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A full-page screenshot does not guarantee that below-the-fold lazy images have loaded. Before a complete design capture, scroll through the page in controlled steps, wait for intended image requests, and await decoding for the images being reviewed. Return to the desired starting position and stabilize animations or record their chosen state before capture. Check for broken images separately so waiting does not hide failed requests. Keep a distinct cold-load capture when initial loading behaviour is the subject of the test. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Otherwise, reviewers may judge blank backgrounds that disappear during normal browsing. Deliberate screenshot preparation makes visual evidence representative while preserving separate tests for the loading experience itself.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Wait for images needed by the active layout, with a timeout
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Screenshot readiness checks should wait only for images required by the rendered layout and must have a timeout. One capture waited 26 minutes because it awaited every document image, including a lazy image inside a stage hidden at that viewport width. That image had no reason to load. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Responsive pages routinely contain assets for inactive layouts. Waiting for all of them confuses resource existence with visual readiness. Identify the visible capture region, wait for its required assets, and report unresolved images explicitly when the deadline expires.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate automated touch gestures against a plain-content control
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An automated touch test needs a control gesture that proves the input mechanism works. In one browser setup, CDP Input.synthesizeScrollGesture and Input.synthesizePinchGesture moved nothing, even over plain text. Input.dispatchTouchEvent produced a 329 px scroll and a 3.33x pinch zoom. These results describe that setup, not a universal API guarantee. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A failed gesture over an interactive figure could mean the figure intercepted input or the tool never delivered usable input. A control swipe over ordinary page text separates those explanations before diagnosing the component.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Restore viewport position after control clicks before comparing animation frames
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After clicking a motion control, verify the scroll position and capture bounds before taking comparison frames. In an invented bakery page test, clicking a pause button in an off-screen header could scroll the document and change the captured content. Restore the intended viewport and let layout settle first. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Automation can scroll controls into view before interacting. Matching capture bounds prevents page movement from being mistaken for animation that failed to pause.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Isolate compositor clipping before applying a capture-only opacity workaround
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] If a headless capture appears to clip canvas content beneath a sticky header, compare opaque sticky, static, and slightly translucent header variants. Treat opacity 0.999 as a diagnostic candidate, not a universal fix. Scope any confirmed workaround to the affected capture and retain an unmodified rendering for other checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Missing canvas rows can corrupt seam and contrast measurements. Isolating the workaround helps distinguish a capture defect from a page defect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Isolate headless View Transition failures and report which transition phases remain unverified
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A headless failure to render a cross-document View Transition does not establish that the transition fails in a normal browser. Reproduce the behavior with a minimal two-page example using @view-transition navigation: auto, then record separately what the leaving and arriving pages actually demonstrate. An observed 66 ms click-to-navigation-start interval did not verify the arrival animation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A minimal reproduction helps separate application defects from test-environment limitations. If the destination frame remains unavailable, report arrival as unverified and check it in a real browser, including the reduced-motion path.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure motion in the intended animated region and make preview probes reproducible
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Motion probes must sample the region intended to animate rather than an arbitrary first-screen crop. In one recorded mobile capture, an animated lower region changed by 4.9% while the deliberately calm upper region changed by only 0.5%. Verify that the deployed build is available before measuring it. Keep reusable probes with the project and resolve dependencies from its installed packages. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A calm crop can falsely suggest a frozen scene. Temporary scripts and accidental dependence on globally installed modules also make later investigations difficult to reproduce.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify that each test observes the intended page state, timing window, and injected failure
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Run accessibility checks on the unmodified page. Preserve measurements across navigation in the external test controller. Require fault-injection helpers to confirm that the served code changed, and place deliberate delays inside the initialization path being measured. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Navigation can erase page-local measurements, text replacement can modify nothing, and initialization can finish before observation begins. Verifying both stimulus and observation prevents misleading passes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep visual probes inside the viewport and verify that request interception reaches the tested fetch
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Visual assertions must exclude off-screen sample points, and network fault injection must target the request mechanism actually used. One seam check reported a 5.9 px discrepancy at x=1024.9 on a 1024 px viewport. Separately, browser-context routing did not intercept a request made through Playwright's page.request; moving the fetch into the page allowed the intended injection. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Invalid coordinates and unreachable interception rules can masquerade as rendering defects or produce meaningless passes. Confirm both the sampling domain and the applied mutation before interpreting the result.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Confirm blank bands in full-page screenshots with scrolled viewport captures
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Full-page screenshots can misrepresent sticky and pinned artwork, so verify suspicious blank bands with viewport captures taken inside the affected section. Scroll to the relevant position, allow the scene to settle, and capture the visible composition at the same width. Compare the result with the full-page image before declaring a regression. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A stitched or extended capture does not necessarily reproduce every sticky element's position across the scroll track. A viewport capture tests the composition a reader actually encounters and helps separate capture artifacts from missing content.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recheck suspected regressions on the prior build using identical inputs and measurements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Compare current and previous builds using the same measurement method, viewport, and interaction sequence. Use an isolated checkout and server when practical, then remove temporary resources. Confirm that visibility triggers fire and that pointer actions generate new events. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An initially still scene may be waiting to enter the viewport, and moving a pointer to its existing position may trigger nothing. Controlled comparisons distinguish regressions from test setup errors.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Isolate competing visual signals before interpreting a failed rendering check
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A visual test must isolate the intended effect from other layers, input motion, and test-runner delays. Background movement can contaminate canvas comparisons, nearby artwork can distort shape probes, pointer parallax can move targets, and Playwright actionability waits can inflate click timings. Disable unrelated contributions selectively rather than hiding the entire canvas. Confirm that injected faults actually modify served code. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A precise-looking metric can measure the wrong phenomenon. Controlled isolation and a detected known failure provide stronger evidence than repeatedly adjusting a threshold until a noisy check passes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inject test CSS through the document response when JavaScript-disabled pages stall style insertion
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] If page.addStyleTag stalls in a Playwright context with javaScriptEnabled:false, inject the required CSS by modifying the document response through routing. Keep the modification confined to the test and confirm that the resulting document contains the intended style. Add bounded timeouts and progress reporting around background checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A recorded test remained silent for two hours because a stalled operation looked like slow execution. A no-JavaScript test should avoid depending on page-side execution for setup, and silence should not be accepted as evidence that useful work continues.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure composited color and unsaturated shape at the effect's observed position
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Classify an effect's color from the final composited pixels, and assess its shape outside the saturated core. Added white light over a violet background can produce channel relationships that differ from the light source's nominal color. Re-center probes on the observed effect when reported canvas state updates less frequently than rendered frames. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Source colors and stale coordinates do not describe the image the reader sees. Saturation can hide shape differences, so validate the probe with a deliberately wrong color or shape and verify that the check detects it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Capture animation frames using the layer's own clock and pause mechanism
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Deterministic animation screenshots can use a requestAnimationFrame predicate that pauses the layer when its own clock reaches a target. Expose elapsed animation time under a test configuration, use a fixed seed, and capture after the application's pause takes effect. One software-rendered trial landed within one frame; fake-clock control produced roughly fourfold timing disagreement in that setup. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A test clock is useful only if it controls the actual animation clock. Verify pause continuity and timing alignment before trusting frame comparisons.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use identically prepared reference frames for live-minus-still image probes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Image-difference probes require matching background preparation in both the live capture and its reference still. Blanking artwork in only one image can make a painted highlight appear to belong to the animated object, corrupting shape measurements. Capture the reference under the same blanking, crop, scale, and timing conditions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An intermittent roundness failure can be contamination rather than a rendering regression. Correct the comparison setup before loosening thresholds, especially when the allegedly failing animation code has not changed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Initialize paused-frame tests through the application's real preference path
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A frame-zero pause test should initialize the same persisted preference that the application reads during startup. If motion settings use sessionStorage, seed the documented key before navigation rather than setting a DOM attribute that startup code will overwrite. Verify the animation clock or frame counter before capturing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A screenshot can look plausible while representing a later frame; one faulty setup captured frame 26 as frame zero. Testing the real initialization path prevents false assumptions about pause state.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prove test mutations were installed before interpreting a passing result
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A mutation test is inconclusive unless the intended defect was actually applied. Match intercepted network requests by their transmitted URL, which excludes the fragment, and register DOM observers only after their target exists. An initialization script may run before documentElement is available; use an appropriate readiness check. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A green test can mean the detector missed a defect or that no defect was planted. Require each mutation to emit evidence of the changed resource or DOM state before judging the detector's response.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Revalidate screenshot regions after component size or positioning changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A figure's bounding box can include pixels visually covered by fixed or sticky interface elements. After widening or repositioning a component, inspect screenshot regions and account for overlapping headers before grading figure pixels. Ensure the intended test region is visible and use consistent scroll positioning. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A visual probe can blame the figure for header colours or motion captured above it. Layout changes therefore require checking the measurement boundary as well as the component itself, especially when tests derive clips automatically.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Avoid stalled style injection in JavaScript-disabled browser tests
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] If Playwright's addStyleTag stalls in a JavaScript-disabled context, insert a style element through page.evaluate and verify the computed result. Create the element, assign its textContent and append it to the document head. Give the operation a bounded timeout and check the behaviour in the browser version under test. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A style-injection helper can wait on an event that does not arrive in this test configuration. That can hang both the baseline and deliberately broken cases without revealing anything about the page's no-script support.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose visible test targets using current viewport bounds
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A test that selects an on-screen target must compare its current bounding rectangle with the viewport, not merely its containing illustration. Recompute visibility after focus, scrolling or layout changes. In a 900 px-high viewport, a target at y=901 is outside the view even if it remains inside an 804 px-high illustration. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Container membership does not establish visibility. A test can otherwise report a missing label or broken interaction when its own target selection is the actual failure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure hue outside clipped highlights and refresh moving-subject coordinates every frame
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Sample color outside a clipped white center and update the measured subject's coordinates for every captured frame. Use a deterministic animation seed and synchronize coordinate reporting with rendering. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Clipped highlights reveal little about underlying hue, while stale coordinates sample the wrong pixels. Correct placement and timing prevent valid artwork from being changed to satisfy a faulty color check.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit a failing shape probe without promoting its first explanation to fact
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Audit both reference construction and probe geometry when a shape test keeps failing after unrelated animation layers are isolated. Compare the assumed tail direction with the actual trajectory, but keep that explanation provisional until a controlled test distinguishes it from background contamination. In one investigation, a tail-sector explanation was later falsified. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A persistent outer-ring failure does not by itself identify the faulty component. Recording candidate explanations as hypotheses preserves useful diagnostic work without turning an attractive but incorrect story into a permanent rendering rule.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep surrounding glow identical when subtracting a reference to measure a star
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Construct a shape-test reference from the same paused scene with only the measured subject hidden. A surrounding glow that remains in the live capture but disappears from the reference contaminates the difference image. Preserve every unrelated layer, animation state and camera setting while toggling the subject. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Background light can create a directional gradient that makes a round object appear malformed to the probe. An earlier geometry explanation may sound convincing, but controlled subtraction is needed to isolate whether the measured shape itself is actually responsible.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Isolate the measured subject in difference images and verify sensitivity to real defects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Create a reference from the same paused frame with only the measured subject hidden. Preserve other layers so shape measurements exclude unrelated changes. Validate any background-subtraction fallback using a deliberately deformed subject and repeated runs. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A useful measurement isolates the intended variable. A correction that makes a valid shape pass must still reject a defective shape, or it may conceal the problem it is meant to detect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Add a peak-sensitive statistic when percentile ratios miss thin shape defects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Pair a ring's p90/p10 ratio with maximum-to-median intensity when testing for narrow protrusions. Use a same-frame, subject-hidden reference first so unrelated live layers do not contaminate the measurement. One provisional experiment reported a four-point defect scoring 1.23, 1.21 and 1.11 under p90/p10, but 4.64–5.71 under maximum-to-median. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Thin arms can occupy too few samples to move percentile statistics substantially. A peak-sensitive companion measurement catches localized defects that a robust distribution summary may intentionally suppress.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Capture animation frames before grading them to reduce sampling interference
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Separate frame capture from image grading when analysis work disrupts the capture cadence. Calling Python for every captured frame can reduce sampling density on a slow renderer. A provisional report at 1440 pixels recorded an increase from 1–2 to 4–5 captured streak frames per cycle after grading moved outside the capture loop. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The test harness can alter which moments it observes. Capturing first and analyzing afterward reduces one source of intermittent failures and makes it easier to distinguish a visual defect from insufficient temporal coverage.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate visual checks with controlled references and deliberately defective examples
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When measuring a rendered shape, capture a reference under identical conditions with only the target shape hidden. Test the check against acceptable examples and deliberate defects, including narrow protrusions that broad summary statistics may miss. Select complementary measurements and calibrate thresholds on representative cases. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Changes in unrelated background content can distort comparisons. A measurement that accepts clean examples must also demonstrate that it rejects the defects it is intended to detect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Cross-check mobile full-page captures against viewport screenshots and media-query state
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A mobile screenshot that contradicts the page's reported input capabilities needs a viewport-sized capture and explicit media-query checks before it is trusted. One observed 390 px full-page capture showed pointer-oriented styling despite the context reporting no hover capability. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Screenshot behaviour can depend on browser version, capture mode and layout, so this observation does not establish that Playwright universally drops touch emulation. Record viewport, touch settings and matchMedia results, then compare viewport and full-page captures to isolate the discrepancy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bound browser concurrency and close contexts during heavy visual testing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] On a memory-constrained test machine, serialize heavy browser probes, close contexts after each probe and keep persistent servers outside job locks. A conservative starting point is one Chromium process at a time, with flock -o used for finite locked commands where appropriate. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Concurrent browser workloads can exhaust memory, while inherited locks can stall the queue. Persist edits before long runs and increase concurrency only after checking available resources and observed memory use.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distinguish painted detail from transition defects when measuring image fades
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define the transition region before sampling brightness. Compare representative rows and outliers, and use median filtering cautiously to reduce isolated decorative highlights. Calibrate against accepted reference images while retaining local visual inspection. Document the reason for each aggregation choice.
