[SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Brightness profiles include both the fade and the artwork beneath it. Worst-row rules can reject intended detail, while median-only rules can hide local defects.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify test-only styles reach their intended elements before measuring pixels
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A visual test that hides text must verify that its injected selector matches the page's actual text elements. A stale selector or template variable can leave words visible, causing a background-brightness check to classify letters as dark artwork. Share selector definitions where practical and inspect computed styles before measuring. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Test setup can fail silently while pixel analysis continues normally. Confirming that masking took effect prevents design changes prompted by a defect in the measuring instrument.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Extend visual checks whenever an effect starts outside the original test span
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A fade test must cover the earliest visible effect, including a tint ramp that begins before the image-opacity fade. Moving the tint earlier without extending the measured span leaves the new transition untested. Revisit both the sampling region and the row aggregation whenever the compositing design changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A carefully calibrated threshold can still miss the defect if its coverage is wrong. The most vulnerable area is often the newly added region, so test boundaries should follow the rendered effect rather than remain attached to the original implementation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build resource hubs around shared resource types and reusable taxonomy references
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A resource hub can use one resource type with taxonomy references, plus separate collection and series types. For a tide-pool field guide, habitat, organism group, and observation format can become reusable taxonomy documents. Create your own CMS project, define and deploy its schema through the supported workflow, then import normalized inventory data. An initial importer might cap uploads at 10 concurrent requests, spacing creates by 100ms and uploads by 200ms; adjust to actual responses. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared taxonomies prevent duplicated content models. Retries, stable identifiers, and import validation matter more than fixed delays alone. Keep CMS credentials in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define an explicit editorial-to-CMS field contract before building ingestion
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Map editorial fields to CMS fields explicitly, including types, publication rules, taxonomy relationships, and asset handling. For a seed library, a resource might contain title, stable slug, publication date, abstract, external URL, downloadable file, image, authors, and featured status. Separate single-choice resource type from multi-choice facets such as growing conditions or season. A slug policy can normalize case and diacritics with an 80-character limit, but must also resolve collisions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A mapping contract prevents ingestion code, filters, and templates from interpreting the same column differently. Keep review content out of public builds unless deliberately enabled, and treat taxonomy choices as domain-specific rather than imposing one industry's categories on every resource hub.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Generate filter controls and card metadata from one taxonomy definition
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use one taxonomy definition to generate editorial mappings, filter controls, option counts, and card metadata. For a ceramic studio library, useful facets might be resource type, material, technique, and firing method. Compute initial counts during server rendering, then expose stable category and slug identifiers to the client-side filter code. Maintain a normalized search haystack separately from taxonomy tokens. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Independently maintained category lists drift, leaving filters that cannot match any cards. Shared configuration makes renames and additions predictable. Define whether counts represent all resources or the current filtered result, and implement accordion and filter controls with keyboard access and clear selected states.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve resource destinations with an explicit, tested precedence rule
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Centralize resource-link selection in a helper with a documented precedence rule. For a download-oriented library, a reasonable order is an editorial external URL, an uploaded file URL, and then a valid internal detail route. If none exists, render an unavailable state instead of a misleading clickable `#` fallback. Validate allowed URL schemes and distinguish internal navigation from external destinations. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Without a shared rule, homepage and library cards can send readers to different places for the same resource. Direct file links remove unnecessary steps when the asset is the intended destination. If an editorial landing page becomes the primary experience, revise the precedence deliberately and test that route before linking it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use the underlying content API when a connector omits attachment metadata
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check whether a connector exposes downloadable attachment URLs before designing a file-ingestion workflow around it. Some Notion connector surfaces omitted property-file URLs while the REST API exposed temporary signed URLs (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it). Create an integration in your own workspace, grant only required capabilities, share the relevant source with it, and use endpoints appropriate to the selected API version. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Search access through one connector does not imply file access through another. Download temporary attachments promptly and upload them to durable storage. Keep tokens in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat; use a proper environment-file parser rather than ad hoc quote removal.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check credentials, source permissions, and connector capabilities before ingestion
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before content ingestion, verify credential availability, access to the specific source, and every connector capability the workflow actually needs. Make a read-only request against the configured source and record access results without logging tokens. A 403 or 404 should trigger diagnosis of permissions, identifiers, and API version, rather than an immediate content mutation. Notion integration access and discovery interfaces are version-sensitive (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A valid token does not prove access to a particular collection, and an active connector does not prove attachment support. Require both API and MCP checks only when both are dependencies; an API-only workflow should not fail because an unused connector is absent.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Design editorial auto-sync as separate trigger, transform, asset, and deployment stages
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Split an editorial auto-sync pipeline into change detection, transformation, asset transfer, CMS mutation, and deployment. Add explicit policies for idempotency, publication status, retries, observability, and secrets. For a bicycle-repair co-op, publishing a repair guide could trigger validation, durable attachment upload, a CMS update, and then a static-site rebuild. Temporary source URLs must not become permanent published links. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Replacing a manual script with a webhook does not solve duplicate delivery, partial uploads, or build storms. Establish stable source identifiers and completion checkpoints before choosing the execution host. Measure end-to-end publication delay instead of promising that every update becomes visible immediately after the editor saves.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Share media ingestion while preserving format-specific processing and provenance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use a shared media-ingestion library to extract embedded assets, validate them, upload durable copies, and replace inline payloads with stable references. Deduplicate by content hash and retain source-to-asset relationships. Handle images, audio, video, and documents through format-specific adapters rather than assuming identical optimization. Complete required asset work before publishing the content that references it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A common implementation prevents repositories from accumulating incompatible copies of the same extraction logic. Reference tracking supports safe deletion and broken-asset diagnosis; it does not by itself measure asset popularity, which requires delivery telemetry. Version the library, test upgrades, and retain enough provenance to repair an interrupted ingest without duplicating uploads.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve featured images with a deterministic editorial-first fallback chain
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define featured-image selection as an ordered chain: explicit editorial image, documented resource override, relevant collection image, type-specific default, then a designed text or color placeholder. For an amateur astronomy club, an observing guide might inherit its collection's sky-map artwork when no individual cover exists. Persist the selected source and its provenance so synchronization remains explainable. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Optional image fields should not create broken cards or unpredictable choices between runs. Overrides should live in portable configuration rather than depend on one workstation's files. Copy temporary source attachments into durable storage, preserve focal-point and alternative-text metadata, and ensure generic imagery does not imply that it depicts the resource's actual subject.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review resource pages individually and as a connected library before publication
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build resource landing pages through inventory, bounded generation rounds, page-level review, and a final cross-library review. Map content types to page patterns and priorities first. Batches of 5–7 pages can be a starting capacity choice, but size them to available review resources. Verify slug uniqueness, filters, search, related resources, card destinations, structured data, accessibility, and representative performance before publishing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Individually polished pages can still break navigation or create visual inconsistency as a collection. Prefer internal landing-page links only when those pages exist and provide useful content. Keep publication and source-slug write-back behind validated results, with a preview observation period appropriate to the release risk rather than relying only on a numerical review score.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Place specialist checks at the content-maintenance steps where they can prevent errors
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Resource-hub maintenance benefits from explicit review checkpoints at ingestion, visual production, factual verification and publication. At startup, confirm that the relevant procedures are current. Resolve ambiguous editorial statuses before selecting content for publication. Read each complete source before creating figures; prepare a specification before rendering a complex infographic. Verify technical claims against authoritative product material and domain claims against appropriate references. Compare rendered layouts with the intended design. Route feedback by whether it is cosmetic, substantive or foundational. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Checks placed near their decisions catch problems before expensive integration. End each run by recording verified lessons and estimate-versus-actual timing, then update the shared procedure so first builds and later maintenance benefit from the same corrections.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Publication is incomplete until the editorial source of truth reflects what shipped
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat editorial writeback as a verified publication step whenever a separate tracker is the source of truth. After publishing through a CMS, reconcile every shipped slug with its tracking record. Verify publication status, required metadata, live URL and featured-image reference by reading the record back. Use the platform's supported field and asset representations rather than copying internal serialized URLs. Record partial failures and make retries safe against duplicate rows. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful deployment can leave editors working from stale records. Explicit reconciliation prevents duplicate publishing, missing assets and misleading dashboards, while making interrupted workflows recoverable without guessing which operations completed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify content-addressed asset URLs before using them to decouple build and upload
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Sanity file URLs can be derived from a file-content hash when the current asset convention has been verified (as of August 2026; re-check before relying on it). The observed form was https://cdn.sanity.io/files/<your-project>/<dataset>/<sha1>.<ext>. Hash representative uploaded files, compare their returned identifiers, then confirm the actual upload matches the derived URL. Treat a pre-upload 404 as ambiguous until upload state is checked. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Derivation can let page preparation proceed before ingestion, but publication still needs an availability check. Image assets and negotiated image formats have different behavior; inspect returned metadata and bytes instead of applying the file convention indiscriminately.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: FAQ provenance checks must catch fabricated prose without relying on numbers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Number traceability does not establish the factual provenance of an FAQ answer. Bind every answer's substantive claims to supporting source passages or verified records, and test the process with a plausible fabrication containing no numbers. Calibrate against faithful paraphrases so wording changes do not cause automatic rejection. Until the check works, require explicit human source review. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A numerical gate may catch fabricated quantities while accepting invented relationships, methods, or explanations. Correct current content and an effective regression safeguard are separate achievements; reporting that gap is more useful than claiming blanket coverage.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Convert approved documents through repeatable transformations and verify textual fidelity
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Convert approved documents through a repeatable transformation and compare the resulting text with the original document. Remove only explicitly approved print elements, merge continued sections, create one main heading and appropriate section headings, and add links without changing approved wording. Compare token counts in both directions after accounting for permitted removals, then inspect reading order and semantics separately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fidelity checks catch accidental omissions and additions, including mistakes in the removal list. Token counts alone cannot establish order or meaning, so structural review remains necessary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Design content automation around schema limits, read freshness and controlled rebuilds
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep automated content schemas stable, batch mutations and combine redundant rebuild triggers. Verify current limits for attribute paths, concurrent writes, request sizes and monthly usage before sizing a system. Use cached reads when suitable and uncached reads when freshness requires them. Generate types from schemas and separate quota or billing boundaries where operational requirements justify it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Arbitrary generated fields can exhaust schema capacity, while bulk imports can trigger unnecessary builds. Choose rebuild delays according to publishing needs. Separate large-media delivery can simplify content operations.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Model related resource formats with shared documents and reusable taxonomies
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A resource hub can use four document types: resource, taxonomy, collection and series. For an invented ceramic studio, resources might include care guides, downloadable templates and workshop references, using shared fields plus format-specific optional fields. Taxonomies describe format, topic or difficulty. Collections query matching resources; series use a reference and an explicit order field. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared structure reduces duplicated schemas and keeps classification flexible. Validate required fields by format and measure actual attribute usage. Dynamic collections avoid maintaining duplicate membership lists.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve media placeholders and reconcile document structure before publishing imported HTML
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat imported article HTML as an intermediate artifact until media placeholders and page structure are resolved. Upload images and audio, maintain an explicit asset-to-article mapping, and replace placeholders with verified URLs and appropriate alternative text. When the site supplies the main heading, remove the imported duplicate while preserving useful elements such as audio controls. Sanitize imported HTML before rendering. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Successful ingestion does not guarantee publishable content. Check for leftover instructions and placeholder tokens, confirm media loads, and validate heading structure before publication.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Seed related content documents in a bounded transaction with deterministic identifiers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Seed related content documents together using deterministic identifiers and a transaction. Build a bounded mutation list, validate references and submit it within current request limits. Replace existing documents only when the seeding process owns them; replacement can overwrite editorial changes. Mark disposable placeholders explicitly. Keep credentials in protected secret storage, outside repositories and chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Stable identifiers prevent duplicates on retries, while a transaction keeps related documents consistent. Repeatability does not make replacement harmless, so ownership boundaries remain essential.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Ingest related resources and taxonomies atomically while protecting editorial changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Commit a bounded batch of related resources and taxonomies in one transaction with stable document identifiers. Validate documents and references before committing. Use deterministic identifiers and stable array keys where possible. Reserve whole-document replacement for documents owned by ingestion; use targeted patches for owned fields when other fields contain editorial work. Split oversized batches according to current request limits and document the resulting consistency boundaries. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Atomic writes prevent partially connected collections, while stable identifiers make retries predictable. Neither property prevents valid edits from being overwritten, so ownership is part of ingestion correctness.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate preview and production publication filters and reconcile previously imported content
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Production ingestion should include only published content, while an isolated preview may also include items ready for review. Exclude drafts and archived items unless the workflow explicitly serves those states. At promotion, recompute the eligible set and reconcile previously imported records through unpublishing, deletion or query filtering as appropriate. A narrower import filter alone does not remove documents already present. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Preview content helps reviewers assess launch readiness, but shared datasets can expose unpublished material. Explicit reconciliation and environment separation enforce the publication boundary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define deterministic selection and safe empty states for featured-resource grids
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A featured-resource grid needs explicit rules for selection, ordering, missing data and empty states. For an invented bakery's three-card display, select eligible featured guides, sort by publication date with a stable tie-breaker and take at most three. Map each item to a title, description, format-specific action and valid destination. Use a meaningful collection link or intentional empty state when none qualify; omit dead links. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Editorial flags alone do not guarantee a complete interface. Deterministic selection, appropriate image alternatives and usable destinations preserve quality when content is incomplete.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Normalize slugs deterministically and handle collisions independently of document identity
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A slug generator needs deterministic normalization, collision handling and an empty-result fallback. For an ASCII policy, apply NFKD normalization, remove combining marks, lowercase, replace ampersands with and, remove unsupported characters, collapse spaces and hyphens, trim, truncate to 80 characters and trim again. Treat 80 as a chosen URL budget rather than a universal CMS requirement. Preserve stable document identity separately from editable titles. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Transliteration and truncation can make different titles identical or erase non-Latin titles entirely. A stable suffix or explicit editorial slug resolves collisions, while stored slugs and redirects prevent a routine title edit from breaking existing URLs.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use one idempotent ingestion pipeline to move approved Notion resources into Sanity
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A Notion-to-Sanity ingestion pipeline should enumerate all source records, read complete properties, filter publication status, and reconcile documents using deterministic IDs. Discover the database and schema first, paginate through every result, then fetch individual pages where full property values are needed. Create taxonomy references and resource documents together where transactional support permits. Verify document counts, build Astro, and inspect a configured preview deployment before release. Keep credentials in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A repeatable pipeline prevents missing pages, duplicate resources, and accidental publication of drafts. Explicit preview verification catches rendering failures that successful database writes cannot reveal.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Upload attachments to durable storage and patch resource references explicitly
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Move imported attachments into durable asset storage and update resource documents with the returned asset references. Upload documents as files and visual assets as images, then patch the corresponding file or image fields using stable set operations. Resolve asset URLs through the content query layer and define card-link precedence explicitly. Verify that every intended download and thumbnail resolves after ingestion. Treat replaced assets as cleanup candidates only after checking remaining references. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Temporary source URLs and incomplete patches can leave otherwise valid cards broken. Separating upload, reference updates, and verification makes retries understandable without assuming that every upload creates a unique asset or that an old asset is safe to delete.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Selective patches are safe only when create operations still populate the complete schema
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Any synchronization script that can create documents must populate every required mapped field, even when its immediate purpose is a small field update. A narrow patch preserves untouched fields on existing records; the same payload used for creation produces incomplete records. Read the complete canonical source schema and branch explicitly between full creation and selective updates. Use stable source identifiers rather than mutable titles or slugs for identity. Include attachment transfer and taxonomy resolution in the creation path. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Missing images, dead links, fallback labels, and unusable filters can all originate from an apparently successful minimal sync. Extending one canonical ingestion pipeline prevents field coverage from diverging across competing scripts.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Load the resource-page contract before generating any page
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Resource-page generation should begin by reading the current page-building contract and selecting the appropriate content pattern. Define patterns for essays, articles, downloadable documents, publications, videos, podcasts, case studies, procedures, and topic pages. Include access defaults, contextual calls to action, transcript requirements, and structured-data expectations. Make the first review check verify adherence to that contract. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A shared contract prevents each generator from independently inventing navigation, gating, or metadata behavior. Loading it before drafting is more reliable than repairing omissions afterward, especially when a batch contains several media types with different accessibility and presentation requirements.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give PDF resources an accessible HTML summary and a direct download
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A PDF resource page should explain the document in HTML and provide a direct download alongside any embedded viewer. Place a two-paragraph summary, author and publication metadata, and 5–7 useful contents bullets above the viewer. Below it, include the measured file size, page count, and 2–4 relevant resources. Give the iframe an accessible title and responsive dimensions. If using PDF.js, test cross-origin loading and configure hosting or asset access appropriately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers should not need a working iframe to understand or obtain a document. HTML summaries also expose useful page content independently of how search systems process the embedded PDF; self-hosting a viewer alone does not eliminate asset-origin restrictions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Pair responsive video embeds with transcripts, takeaways, and deliberate privacy controls
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Video resource pages should combine a responsive 16:9 player with a short abstract, 4–6 takeaways, and a verified transcript. Use aspect-ratio: 16 / 9 or the equivalent 56.25% padding technique, provide an iframe title, and avoid autoplay. Privacy-enhanced YouTube embeds and Vimeo's dnt option are available controls (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it); inspect actual requests and consent requirements rather than assuming zero tracking. Add chapters when source timestamps exist. A transcript longer than 800 words can use an accessible details element. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Captions, readable transcripts, and restrained loading make video useful beyond playback. Review automatic transcription and speaker attribution; if unavailable, report the gap rather than inventing text.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make podcast pages useful through episode links, verified notes, and speaker-attributed transcripts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A podcast page should identify the episode, provide playable audio, and expose useful information in ordinary HTML. Include episode-specific listening links, 2–3 paragraphs of notes, and a verified speaker-attributed transcript. Add 3–5 timestamped quotes only when checked against the recording. Use a provider embed or native audio with controls and preload='none', and test the layout on narrow screens. Structured data should reflect verified episode and series metadata. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers may prefer scanning, searching, or reading over listening. Source transcripts should be checked before commissioning new transcription, and summaries must remain labeled as summaries rather than being presented as a substitute for the full spoken record.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Write derived slugs back to the authoritative source without overwriting editorial choices
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Persist a derived canonical slug in the source system so later imports reuse the same URL. Skip matching values, populate empty fields, and treat a conflicting nonempty value as an explicit reconciliation case. Validate uniqueness before publication and preserve redirects when an established URL changes. Use bounded requests, honor rate-limit responses, and retry transient failures with backoff. Keep credentials in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Without write-back, separate runs can derive different URLs from the same title. An explicit conflict rule prevents automation from silently overriding editorial decisions, while a failure report makes incomplete synchronization visible.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Place the primary document action near the top of a resource page
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Put the main document link between the resource header and introductory summary so visitors can act without scrolling through commentary. Use a shared button component with precise labels such as 'Read the full paper' or 'Download the brochure'. Distinguish external navigation from downloading with text and appropriate icons. Verify keyboard focus, contrast, destination, and actual browser download behavior; the download attribute alone does not guarantee cross-origin downloads. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A prominent, consistent action serves returning readers and people already familiar with the resource. Shared components prevent slight styling and behavior differences from accumulating across publication, report, and brochure templates.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Embed actual generated content in CMS mutations and reject unresolved placeholders before publishing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] CMS mutation files must contain the actual body, styles, and schema values expected by the destination schema. Read generated files and construct the payload with a JSON serializer such as Python json.dumps(), rather than inserting literal content placeholders for an unspecified later step. Allow only explicitly supported temporary asset placeholders, resolve them before publication, and reject any remaining template tokens. Validate whether structured data belongs in a string, object, or array of strings. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A payload can be valid JSON while publishing placeholder text as the page body. Explicit serialization contracts and a final unresolved-token check catch this failure before a successful API response makes it appear complete.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve internal links from canonical slug records instead of workspace names
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build cross-resource links from the target document's authoritative slug field, not from its title or directory name. Read the generated CMS payload or a shared slug manifest and construct the route from that value. For targets that do not exist yet, record an unresolved reference and resolve it before publishing. Verify every internal destination against the final route inventory. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Workspace labels and public URLs evolve independently, and a small word-order difference can produce a plausible but broken link. A shared source of truth removes guessing and lets a final link check catch forward references without exposing knowingly broken anchors to visitors.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use browser Python when it preserves substantial existing logic and keeps visitor processing local
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A browser language runtime is most useful when it reuses substantial existing calculation or validation logic without sending visitor inputs to a backend. An amateur astronomy club could reuse a tested Python observation-file validator in an interactive resource page. Check package compatibility and download requirements against the chosen runtime release, then load expensive dependencies only after an explicit action. Verify that analytics and other scripts do not transmit submitted data before claiming local processing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Maintaining separate Python and JavaScript implementations creates opportunities for divergence. Reusing the implementation can preserve consistency, provided browser execution is tested against known reference cases.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distinguish unavailable evidence from a completed search that found no answer
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A searchable resource pipeline should distinguish successful retrieval, insufficient evidence and inability to inspect the source. Preserve source provenance through parsing, indexing and summarization, and surface degraded processing instead of presenting it as a normal empty result. Validate the finished resource with representative questions, missing-source cases and deliberately unanswerable queries; a successful process exit is insufficient acceptance evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Visitors interpret no result differently from service unavailable. Combining those states hides operational failures and encourages unsupported answers. Clear result states and source-grounded acceptance checks make a resource hub useful even when part of its processing fails.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build scroll-driven painted sections as a shared readable component
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Implement a recurring painted scroll section as one component with a persistent background and sequential text panels. Keep each claim available in the document, support phones and provide a stacked still-image mode when pinning would impair reading. Measure translucent panel contrast over frozen animation phases rather than selecting opacity by eye. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared behavior prevents accessibility and layout fixes from diverging across pages. A single background can connect several ideas visually, but the reading order and text contrast must remain dependable throughout the sequence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose scroll presentation before paint and measure each orientation separately
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Decide a scroll section's presentation mode before its first paint and test landscape and portrait treatments independently. Short phone viewports may need stacked panels over a still rather than a pinned sequence. Measure each orientation's veil: example passing values were 0.76 at 4.70:1 and 0.84 at 4.64:1. Verify pause after all animation styles are applied. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Late mode changes cause visible jumps, and one opacity need not work over different crops. A more specific animation rule can also reset play-state and silently defeat a shared pause control.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build scroll-video seams from the real boundary frames of normalized clips
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Generate connecting clips from the actual extracted end and start frames of neighboring normalized clips. A scroll stage can stack videos, map segment progress to currentTime and apply smoothing, such as lerp 0.2 per animation frame. Hide copy during travel and hold a stable image for reading. One encoding recipe is 1280x720 cover-crop, 24 fps CFR, libx264 slow, CRF 20, yuv420p, -g 8 -keyint_min 8 -sc_threshold 0, -an and +faststart. Extract boundary PNGs after trimming and normalization. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Near-matching boundary frames make a short crossfade convincing; a short GOP limits the decoding distance required by seeking. These settings are starting points to test on target devices. Whole-file Blob preloading needs an eviction policy, otherwise a long journey retains every downloaded clip.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Paint readable stops, use video for passages and prove scrubbing before producing the full story
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build scroll journeys around standalone stills, with video used only to travel between them. For a tide-pool field guide, each stop can pair an identifiable habitat with ordinary HTML text and links; the still also serves as its poster and fallback. Start with a placeholder scrub test comparing GOP-8 H.264, all-intra H.264 and a frame-based alternative before commissioning the full artwork. Probe one generated passage before batching the rest. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This sequence exposes seeking and endpoint problems before they multiply across expensive renders. Preserve readable document order, keyboard access and a skip link. Use a static or stacked presentation for reduced motion and no JavaScript, and avoid fetching video for those modes. Test missing clips, pause, chapter jumps, resize and rotation. Package ingredients, raw renders, working evidence and final web encodes separately so each result remains traceable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit hidden selector dependencies when replacing a shared visual section
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Replacing a page section requires checking scripts that depend on its attributes and structure, even when they do not throw errors. Search for selectors attached to the old component, retarget each dependent behavior and exercise it on the replacement. For a white-ground journey, test paper-colour continuity and text fit alongside the component refactor. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A decorative layer may silently stop when its query selector no longer finds a target. A clean console and successful build do not reveal that omission. Preserve a baseline page during the shared-component change, compare its geometry before and after, then verify each newly integrated page with placeholder media before investing in finished artwork.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give each page one coherent visual world and make abstract symbols distinguishable at a glance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Storyboard a page as a continuous visual world whose stops use simple, distinguishable forms to support its claims. A bicycle-repair co-op could connect inspection, adjustment and a completed ride through one illustrated workshop environment, changing emphasis without changing the visual vocabulary. Mark focal points, reading regions and travel direction for every stop and passage. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Abstract imagery becomes useful when a stranger can identify its relevant difference without decoding a private metaphor. An empty position, a separated element or a visible connection can communicate structure more clearly than elaborate symbolism. Alternating text sides also changes the required camera movement, so composition and passage direction should be designed together.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use a monotonic per-element clock for one-shot scroll animations
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A one-shot scroll animation can use a per-element clock that advances normally while visible, accelerates after the reader passes it, and never runs backward. Setting the accelerated rate to duration/0.3 targets completion within 300 ms of animation time. A recorded implementation took 307–356 ms of wall time across five widths, so the target was not a strict measured guarantee. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separating whether an element has been reached from how much it has played simplifies skip-ahead and scroll-back behavior. Monotonic progress prevents previously completed content from visibly dismantling itself.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Enable sticky panel sequences only when their measured content fits the available viewport
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A sticky sequence should fall back to ordinary stacked content when its tallest panel cannot fit below the pinned header. Measure rendered panels after layout and font readiness, and reassess when dimensions change. One example measured 916 px at 320 px viewport width and 502 px at 1440 px. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fixed viewport-height cutoffs ignore copy length and wrapping. Content-based fit checks avoid clipped phone panels while preserving the sticky experience on screens that genuinely have enough room.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Translate a motion metaphor into observable behaviour before reusing an engine
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Specify the intended motion metaphor as observable behaviours before adapting an existing animation engine. For a seed library, diffuse colour could gather from painted planting beds into one seed-shaped light that settles into a collection. Define source masks, gradual convergence, a 3–5 s gathering phase, one result per cycle and a clear resting state. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reusing an engine can preserve mechanics that contradict the new idea. Behavioural requirements help retain the intended feeling while allowing the underlying paths, timing and rendering technique to change.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build scroll stories around calm reading holds and short continuous camera passages
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A readable scroll story can alternate long, calm compositions with short camera passages that connect them spatially. A useful reference pattern held scenes for roughly 6–9 seconds of scroll progression and used transitions of about 1.5–2.5 seconds. Outgoing copy disappeared within about 0.25 seconds of a transition starting; incoming copy appeared as the destination settled. These are pacing references, not fixed reading-time guarantees. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] For a tide-pool field guide, drifting water or sea mist can conceal joins while HTML text occupies quiet areas of each still. Contact sheets sampled at 1 fps, with 4 fps around transitions, help distinguish genuine camera travel from a crossfade and reveal when text competes with motion.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Probe delivery, accessibility and loading constraints before building a video scroll section
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A scroll-video prototype should prove byte-range delivery, poster loading and motion controls before production artwork is commissioned. Inventory the current section, content-security policy, asset routing, page budgets and semantic headings. Keep the poster as the initial visual, defer heavy work until visibility after load and idle, and provide complete still-based content for no JavaScript, reduced motion and data-saving modes. Wire pause controls to video as well as other animation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An astronomy club could replace an existing observatory tour section with a journey that ends at observing resources, preserving the page's visual balance. Delivery and loading constraints can invalidate the whole approach; discovering them with a small prototype is cheaper than rebuilding a finished sequence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose story stills for copy space and continuity before generating connecting clips
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Select scroll-story stills as a sequence, prioritizing quiet copy areas, consistent backgrounds and viable portrait compositions. For a neighbourhood bakery, alternate views of ingredients, preparation and the oven while keeping each text region uncluttered. Inspect wide and phone variants side by side; a centre crop from 896×1200 to 675×1200 yields 9:16 but still needs composition review. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A detailed image can be a poor reading surface. Storyboard holds of roughly 1.2–1.4 screens and passages of 1.6–1.8 screens are useful starting experiments, not fixed rules. Assess brightness changes between stops before deciding whether the transition medium can absorb them or the stills need adjustment.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Scroll distance controls passage pacing independently of video duration
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] In scroll-scrubbed video, clip duration is not viewing time because scroll position controls currentTime. An 8 s clip contains 192 frames at 24 fps, yet a fast flick can traverse it in under a second. Tune scroll span separately from media duration; roughly 1 to 1.6 viewport heights per passage can serve as experimental starting points. Trim redundant settled footage only after checking endpoint continuity. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shortening the source clip does not directly fix a passage that feels slow. Explain the mapping in handoffs, then test slow drags, fast flicks and backward scrolling to judge the actual experience.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate scroll-controller startup, media fetching and responsive position restoration
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Initializing a lazy scroll controller must not automatically trigger video downloads. A 150% viewport observation margin can activate it during initial page load, so gate media fetching separately on page completion and actual approach to the sequence. Put size containment on the sticky stage when child stacking contexts would prevent video from sitting between stills and text. Preserve the last drawn progress before an aspect-ratio change. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Measuring progress after resize uses geometry that has already changed, potentially jumping to another stop. Component replacements should also preserve navigation lifecycle handlers that may have lived in the removed script.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build a scroll journey with semantic content, bounded loading and still-image fallbacks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A robust scroll journey keeps text and links in HTML while treating video as an optional visual layer. Stack readable stops without JavaScript, provide chapter navigation and a skip link, and reveal video only after a decoded frame has been presented, using requestVideoFrameCallback where available. Fetch the current and next passages, release passed media, and support still-image modes for reduced motion, pause and data-saving preferences. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Media readiness, keyboard navigation and visual pacing are separate concerns. Verify byte-range responses, resize continuity and focus behavior, then inspect touch devices and accessibility directly; passing desktop automation does not settle mobile playback quality.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reuse the journey method while redesigning each page around its own copy and visual ground
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reusing a scroll-story technique requires a new copy-first storyboard when page meaning or background treatment changes. A seed library might illustrate collecting, sorting and sharing with distinct abstract scenes, each derived from the text at that stop. A dark immersive sequence does not prove that white-ground watercolor passages will preserve clean edges, readable words or seamless transitions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Consistent mechanics can coexist with different page rhythms. Probe the new visual ground and its hardest transition before producing every still, so uncertainty about white margins, wash behavior and contrast can still influence the composition.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Cross-dissolve adjacent paintings and reassess media-loading thresholds after overlap changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Adjacent painted sections blend more naturally when the images overlap and one fades to transparency over the other. An 11rem overlap is a concrete starting example, not a universal setting. A flat intermediate background color can leave a visible dark band even when partially transparent. After introducing overlap, revisit the media-loading trigger; waiting until the next section's top passes 50% of the viewport can avoid premature fetching. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A visual fix changes layout geometry and can silently defeat lazy loading. Inspect the seam and network activity together, including the initial viewport on short screens.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Font stylesheets and font files may require different CSP source allowances
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] External typography can fail when Content Security Policy permits the stylesheet host but blocks the font-file host. Inspect browser console errors and network requests to identify the actual origins, then add only the required sources to style-src and font-src. Keep development response headers and packaged application policies consistent. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A fallback font can disguise a blocked request as an unexplained layout change. Copying a broad domain list or adding unsafe-inline without investigation weakens policy while obscuring the real dependency.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Overlapping hosting header rules can produce duplicated response values
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Overlapping Cloudflare Pages header rules can combine values rather than behave like CSS specificity overrides (as of April 2026; re-check before relying on it). A specific Markdown route and a broad Markdown catchall can therefore duplicate Content-Type. Avoid assigning the same singleton header through overlapping patterns, and inspect deployed responses with curl -I. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Configuration can look locally reasonable while producing malformed headers on the wire. Check Cache-Control combinations too, and verify function-generated responses separately from static assets.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate permission to run an analytics tool from its permission to read analytics data
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Authenticate the person invoking an analytics CLI separately from the credential used to read analytics data. Give the data credential only the required read permissions, audit queries, and keep secrets in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. A local identity check does not prevent direct use of a copied shared key. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These layers answer different questions: who may invoke the tool, and what data it can access. Long-lived credentials also need rotation and revocation plans; convenience alone does not justify a shared secret with broad access.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify local processing before promising that user data stays in the browser
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Claim that input stays in the browser only after verifying the complete data flow, including analytics, error reporting, third-party scripts, and persistence. Inspect network activity across representative interactions and review code paths that could transmit data; repeat these checks after changes. A local file-analysis tool should explain its actual behavior in plain language. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Local processing can reduce exposure and make privacy easier to inspect, but static hosting alone proves nothing about outbound requests. A quiet network trace covers the tested scenario, not every possible path, and architectural choices do not automatically settle compliance obligations.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify headers separately on preview and production hosts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate response headers on each deployment environment instead of assuming preview and production return identical values. Cloudflare preview hosting was observed replacing a configured X-Robots-Tag value with noindex (as of October 2026; re-check before relying on it). Reproduce behavior on your own hosts, inspect duplicate headers and retain exact production assertions where required. Use a narrow environment-specific expectation only for a verified platform difference. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Weakening every assertion to accommodate preview behavior can hide a production regression. Separate checks preserve the intended production policy while accurately modeling what the hosting layer controls.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test asset loading and animation under the production content security policy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Apply the production Content Security Policy when testing fetched scene data and live rendering. Small imported JSON assets can become data URLs during bundling; fetching them can fail under a restrictive connect-src policy even when larger emitted files load successfully. Decode supported data URLs locally or emit real asset files, then check motion, initial appearance and policy violations. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A plain local server may test a weaker runtime than deployment. A silent fallback can conceal the failure, so matching production headers is essential to verifying the actual experience.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Combine narrow browser policies with server-side authorization and upload controls
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Secure private applications with server-side authorization, validated inputs, constrained browser policies, and scoped file access. Build CSP from actual resource requirements; avoid copying another application's allowlist or adding unsafe-eval without evidence. Consider HSTS max-age=31536000 only after confirming HTTPS readiness, especially before includeSubDomains or preload. Example upload limits are 25MB/file and 100MB/batch; validate content as well as declared MIME type. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] robots directives and dynamic rendering are not access controls. Verify tenant membership on every protected operation, sanitize errors, rate-limit sensitive endpoints, verify webhook signatures, deduplicate events, and issue short-lived downloads with traversal protection. A one-hour URL lifetime is a policy choice, not a universal requirement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Ship analytics and its required CSP changes together instead of pre-allowlisting unused services
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Add analytics origins to Content-Security-Policy when the corresponding integration is implemented and tested. A bundled consent banner does not itself justify permissions for future trackers. Determine the required script-src, connect-src, img-src and frame-src entries from the actual integration, document them in project configuration notes, and verify behavior before consent, after consent and after withdrawal. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An allowlist entry does not load a script, but it expands what the policy permits and is therefore not zero-risk. Shipping code, consent controls and minimal CSP changes together prevents forgotten configuration without accumulating speculative third-party permissions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat analytics, consent settings, privacy disclosures, and CSP as one maintenance surface
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Adding an analytics or marketing integration requires coordinated review of its network access, consent behavior, and privacy disclosures. Inventory the site's existing integration before making changes. Update Content Security Policy directives only for verified script, connection, or frame origins, and test both consent acceptance and rejection. Update cookie descriptions and policy revision information when behavior changes. Keep content-management write credentials in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A working tracking script can still break consent controls or conflict with browser security policy. Maintaining these pieces together prevents handoffs from silently undoing earlier privacy and security work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify response headers independently for static assets and dynamic routes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Configure and test headers at the layer that actually produces each response. For Cloudflare Pages static assets, the documented _headers convention uses a URL-pattern line followed by indented Header-Name: value lines; place the file where the build copies it to the output root. Treat that platform behavior as perishable (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it). Dynamic function responses require their own header handling. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A correct static configuration does not establish coverage for server-generated pages. Request representative routes and inspect actual headers before claiming a site-wide security policy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Browser compute cannot protect secrets or supply server-trusted results
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Browser execution cannot keep a shipped secret confidential or make client-generated results trustworthy to a server. Keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat, and perform privileged operations server-side. Treat returned results as untrusted input. Prefer ordinary JavaScript for simple arithmetic, defer optional runtime downloads until interaction, and move expensive computation into a Worker where supported. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A substantial runtime is justified by meaningful reuse or capability, not convenience for a trivial expression. Stating these architectural limits early prevents insecure designs and avoids blocking the interface with long-running work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Secret sweeps must cover ignored files, history, transcripts and database storage
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A secret-leak sweep must inspect every relevant storage surface, including ignored files and historical output. Scan working files, Git history, tool transcripts, memory databases, SQLite write-ahead logs and search-index storage. Exact secret values and selected fragments can serve as search needles, but never print those needles or matching secret-bearing lines. Distinguish clean, hit and unreadable outcomes, such as exit codes 0, 1 and 2. Re-run after credential rotation because the needles have changed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Searching one database column or respecting .gitignore can miss the most likely leak locations. Zero matches means only that the tested needles were absent from the readable surfaces; transformed or encoded secrets may require additional detection.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Allowlist public tokens by exact value and reject normalized vendor test values
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Secret-scanning exceptions should match exact public values rather than exempting entire paths. Keep actual secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. Normalize production configuration before comparing it against the vendor's full test-value list. Turnstile checks in the source audit covered five test site keys (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Add and test scanner coverage for sensitive formats such as a JWK private d field. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A directory exception can conceal a real private key beside a legitimate public token. A partial test-key pattern or untrimmed comparison can silently admit development credentials into production.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Classify browser storage by purpose and verify consent requirements before deployment
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Inventory browser storage by purpose, trigger and lifetime rather than treating cookies as the only mechanism needing privacy review. Include localStorage, sessionStorage and IndexedDB. Separate visitor-requested display preferences from attribution, analytics and experiments. For a motion preference, consider session scope, writing only after the visitor acts, and a concise disclosure. Verify applicable consent rules and exemptions against current authoritative guidance before deployment. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A blanket storage ban can obstruct accessibility, while blanket permission can permit undisclosed tracking. A banner's existence does not establish that every storage purpose is covered; the implementation and consent configuration need to agree.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Run initial-frame and motion checks under the production CSP
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Browser checks for initial rendering and motion must run with the same Content Security Policy as production. Serve the generated policy headers locally or apply them to document responses in the test harness, then inspect violations. In the reported build, assets below 4 KB became data: URLs through Vite's configured inlining behavior, and fetching one violated connect-src. Verify the project's actual inlining configuration instead of assuming a universal threshold. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A local server without production headers can make every animation test pass while deployment blocks a required resource. Test the built output and resolve the asset delivery or policy mismatch deliberately.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose video loading behaviour before changing the content-security policy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Blob-URL video loading can fail under a production content-security policy that omits media-src and falls back to default-src 'self'. Decide whether the player uses direct video URLs or Blob URLs before changing the policy. Direct same-origin delivery can avoid needing blob: permission; a Blob-based design needs an appropriate media-src directive and explicit URL revocation and cache eviction. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A development server without production headers can conceal this failure. Test the player under the actual policy and grant only the source types the chosen implementation needs.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review crawler permissions deliberately when replacing preview robots rules
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] At production launch, replace preview crawler restrictions with a deliberate policy and a canonical sitemap reference. A public site might allow ordinary crawling while excluding selected paths, but training, search, and inference permissions should reflect the publisher's actual choices. Content-Signal directives and named AI crawler policies were used in emerging agent-readiness configurations (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it). Verify current crawler identifiers and supported directives before copying a template. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Leaving `Disallow: /` in production can suppress discovery, while blindly allowing every bot grants permissions without considering intent. robots.txt communicates crawler preferences; it does not protect private APIs or replace authentication, and it is not a reliable substitute for noindex controls.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Store incompatible JSON-LD payloads as validated strings and render them safely
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a CMS rejects JSON-LD keys such as `@context` or `@type`, store validated serialized JSON rather than renaming those keys. This incompatibility was reported for Sanity document attributes (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it). An array of JSON strings can preserve multiple schema blocks; validate each block during ingestion and again at the rendering boundary. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Renaming semantic keys changes the external format and creates fragile reverse transformations. However, serialized JSON must not be injected blindly into an HTML script element: use safe serialization that escapes characters capable of closing the script context. Preserve JSON-LD meaning while preventing content-controlled markup from becoming executable code.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Publish accurate discovery metadata and validate indexability without inventing capabilities
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Search and agent metadata should describe the content and capabilities the site actually provides. Generate a sitemap of intended canonical, indexable URLs and verify successful responses. Use absolute HTTPS canonical and social-image URLs, with suitable image descriptions. Add structured-data types only where the page supports their meaning; FAQ or speakable markup is not mandatory everywhere. Keep noindex pages out of the sitemap, and remember that blocking crawling can prevent a crawler from seeing noindex. Offer Markdown alternatives or service metadata only when implemented and maintained. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Checklists become harmful when optional features turn into empty declarations. Search and agent conventions are perishable (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it); validate semantics and actual responses alongside syntax.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify search ownership, submit canonical sitemaps and inspect actual indexing outcomes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Search discovery setup should verify site ownership and inspect how intended pages are crawled and indexed. In your own webmaster accounts, verify the relevant property, submit the canonical sitemap and inspect the homepage plus important landing pages. Confirm that sitemap URLs resolve correctly and that robots rules, canonicals and noindex directives match the publication plan. Add other search engines according to the site's audience. Console interfaces and report availability are perishable (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Sitemap submission is a discovery hint rather than a promise of indexing. Inspecting real URLs exposes accidental exclusions and conflicting signals without relying on retired report names or assuming immediate search visibility.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Apply the same factual standards to structured data and visible article copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Moving an unsupported claim into articleBody does not make it acceptable to publish. Treat structured data as part of the page's editorial output: preserve attribution and qualifications, align it with visible content, and apply the same source checks to both. Recompute derived metadata when the text changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Hidden machine-readable text can escape ordinary visual review while remaining available to crawlers and downstream systems. Whether answer engines preferentially use articleBody requires a retrieval experiment; that unmeasured mechanism is unnecessary to justify consistent factual standards across representations.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make unlisted pages crawlable for noindex and keep access control separate
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An unlisted public page should expose its noindex directive to crawlers without being advertised in navigation or discovery indexes. If relying on noindex, do not block the same URL in robots.txt, because compliant crawlers need to fetch it to see the directive. Exclude alternate text representations and downloadable variants from discovery as appropriate, and apply Referrer-Policy: no-referrer if outgoing requests should omit referrer information. Verify actual routes and response headers. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Unlisted means difficult to discover, not private. Indexing directives and referrer policy reduce particular disclosures but cannot prevent forwarding, noncompliant crawlers or direct access; restricted material needs authentication.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Apply hero art requirements to share cards and thumbnails
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Social cards, thumbnails and poster frames should inherit the visual requirements of the page artwork they represent. Begin with the processed asset that actually ships, or apply the same processing and review to a fresh render. For an invented ceramic studio, a thumbnail should preserve the hero's intended clay texture rather than recover distracting patterns removed during editing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Derived images are often produced late from raw sources, allowing old defects to return. Check full size, square crops and small previews. A hero's numeric gate may require recalibration for the new framing; its transfer is a hypothesis until tested.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Revalidate visual checks when adapting artwork for social sharing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test an artwork check on both a deliberately defective social image and a corrected version before relying on it. Recalibrate measurements for the new crop and scale, and compare automated outcomes with visual review. Inspect full-size, thumbnail and square presentations. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Resizing and cropping change the features a measurement observes. Reusing a threshold without validation can accept visible defects or reject suitable artwork.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Apply structured-data rules consistently while checking their relevance to each page
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Audit structured-data coverage across page templates, including the homepage, instead of assuming a component appears everywhere. If speakable markup is appropriate to the supported publishing use case, ensure its selectors resolve to meaningful visible text such as a heading and concise explanatory passage. Validate the emitted markup and inspect representative routes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared intent does not guarantee shared implementation: a schema component can be present on an article template and absent from a landing page. Consistency is useful, but a heading alone does not establish that every page needs speakable markup. Separate internal coverage rules from current search-platform eligibility, and verify the latter before promising discovery or voice-search benefits.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Generate structured data from visible page content rather than a fixed schema quota
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Add structured data that accurately describes each page instead of requiring a fixed number of schema blocks. An Astro layout can supply shared organization data, while pages supply appropriate breadcrumbs, FAQs, or other types. Include FAQ markup only when the corresponding questions and answers are visible. Treat indexing controls and schema selection as separate decisions. Add a validation script and run it during builds. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A universal four-schema rule encourages irrelevant markup. Accurate, maintained structured data is easier to validate and avoids implying that markup quantity guarantees search visibility.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match reference-guide metadata to its actual content and navigation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Choose structured data for an interactive reference guide according to the guide's visible content and purpose. A tide-pool field guide might use WebPage, BreadcrumbList, an ItemList for its index, and appropriate article markup; add HowTo or FAQPage only for genuine instructions or visible FAQs. Supply a canonical URL, descriptive metadata, sharing cards, and accurate publication or modification dates. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A fixed six-block recipe can overstate what a page contains. Keep an editorial metadata brief with the direct answer, intended questions, section inventory, and source coverage so search-oriented work remains grounded in useful content.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Expand migration discovery in tiers and measure coverage against a defined inventory
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Start migration discovery with sitemaps, search-console exports and public crawl archives, then expand sources when meaningful gaps remain. Distinguish URL inventory from backlink discovery: a sitemap identifies pages but does not establish inbound links. Additional sources may include webmaster tools, code search and relevant scholarly indexes. Deduplicate results and record each source's contribution. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Broad searches have diminishing returns, and source usefulness depends on the site's audience. Claims such as 85% coverage in an hour or a 95% ceiling are not portable without a known denominator. Report observed coverage and unresolved gaps instead of promising universal percentages.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify deduplicated referrer pages before treating discovered backlinks as current
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Confirm a discovered backlink by fetching its referrer page and inspecting whether a link still targets the legacy domain. Deduplicate candidate referrer URLs before crawling. Record the referrer URL, resolved target URL, anchor text, response status and verification outcome, including blocked or inconclusive fetches. Resolve relative links against the page URL and account for redirects. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Search-console and crawl datasets can contain stale evidence. Restricting verification to the deduplicated candidate set limits unnecessary requests, while explicit outcomes prevent inaccessible pages from being misclassified as absent links or archived links from being presented as current.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Include historical redirects in migration discovery and map old URLs directly to final destinations
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A current sitemap omits many historical URLs that still need redirects after migration. Inspect existing server rules, including WordPress .htaccess exports, alongside logs and archive evidence. Build the old redirect chains, identify the appropriate new equivalent, and map each retained legacy URL directly to that destination where possible. Test for loops, missing endpoints and unintended query-string changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Rebuilding only today's pages can strand links to earlier versions of the site. Flattening chains reduces extra requests and failure points; avoid asserting that every redirect hop necessarily loses ranking value.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match structured data to visible content and omit facts that cannot be verified
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Choose JSON-LD types that describe the actual page content, and include only verified properties. ScholarlyArticle, VideoObject, PodcastEpisode, and Article serve different purposes; their properties are not interchangeable or universally required. Use measured ISO 8601 durations such as PT12M34S, verified identifiers, canonical URLs, and accurate publisher information. Add transcripts or FAQ content only when genuinely present. If a Sanity schema defines htmlSchemas as an array of strings, serialize each schema object separately and parse every entry during validation. Escape embedded script content safely. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fabricated metadata and mismatched storage types create misleading or broken output. Structured data supports machine interpretation, but choosing a type does not guarantee rankings, citations, or rich results.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build answer-friendly pages from clear prose, accurate metadata, and deliberate crawler policy
