memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Make pages understandable through direct answers, semantic HTML, accurate structured data, and discoverable canonical URLs. A 40–60-word opening answer is a useful editorial target when the topic permits it. Add Organization, WebPage, BreadcrumbList, or FAQPage data only where appropriate and supported by the page. Validate generated JSON-LD and sitemap URLs. Define crawler access deliberately, distinguishing search discovery from other uses. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Machine-readable metadata cannot rescue unclear or unsupported claims. Passing a schema validator demonstrates structural correctness, not guaranteed citations or visibility, and allowing every bot is a policy choice rather than a universal optimization requirement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit public claims and structured data against the same evidence and disclosure rules
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Public copy, metadata and structured data must describe the same verified availability, price, licensing and supported capabilities. Maintain a claim ledger and a disclosure checklist covering private identifiers, confidential implementation details and unsupported promises. Review JSON-LD, downloadable assets and generated summaries alongside visible prose. Omit properties that cannot be supported rather than filling them with optimistic defaults. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A restrained page can still publish a false offer or license through machine-readable markup. Disclosure control should protect private information without concealing limitations that visitors need to make an informed decision.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Scope noindex checks to the environment and every response type
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Apply a nonindexing policy consistently to every response in an environment intended to stay out of search. On a Worker-based site, inspect X-Robots-Tag on static pages, generated alternatives, errors, and API responses as applicable. Check deployed responses as well as build configuration, and keep robots.txt crawlable where crawlers need to observe noindex. Test public production indexing separately from preview policy. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Copying a hosting-specific checklist can omit dynamically generated responses or accidentally suppress the public site. Headers, robots directives, and authentication serve different purposes; noindex is not access control.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Rebuild indexing controls when changing hosting platforms
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reevaluate indexing and access controls during a hosting migration instead of copying a platform-specific checklist unchanged. For a private preview, configure authentication and verify a suitable noindex policy across static and generated responses. Where noindex must be discovered by crawlers, avoid blocking the same routes in robots.txt. Inspect any content-export generator before adding global robots meta tags; its filtering may remove those pages from exports. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A control that works in one stack can conflict with another stack's generators or middleware. Verify the actual response paths and export behavior rather than assuming identical feature names or provider defaults.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat every added definition as a new factual claim
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check each definition added during revision for factual accuracy, a clear subject and appropriate qualifications. Review it both alone and within the sentence. For an invented swim school, defining a course that has no dates yet must not imply that enrollment has opened. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Wording borrowed from a source can lose the context that made it accurate. An edit that improves clarity can still introduce an unsupported claim.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve essential meaning before navigation under a word limit
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] In short FAQ answers, prioritize definitions, eligibility and availability over optional navigation instructions. List the meaning the answer must preserve, trim repetition, then review the answer without surrounding headings. Recheck previously corrected issues after shortening it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Extracted answers lose context supplied elsewhere on a page. Removing a seemingly redundant qualification can make a concise answer incomplete or misleading.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distinguish bookable services from proposed services within each answer
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] State the availability of each service directly in standalone answers. For an invented garden centre, distinguish workshops accepting bookings from courses proposed for a later season. Avoid making readers infer status from conditional verbs or a banner elsewhere. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Describing what a visitor could do can sound like an invitation to book. Explicit availability keeps possibilities from becoming accidental promises.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep availability beside each option in extractable answers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Include each option's availability in the FAQ answer that describes it. Use direct labels such as booking open, sold out or date to be announced when supported by current information. If a word limit removes an essential distinction, revise the format or allow a documented exception. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Extracted answers may omit surrounding explanations. Brevity should not leave readers guessing whether they can take the action described.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Design editorial rules for every place content is reused
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Account for independent reuse when setting copy rules. If visible FAQ answers also populate structured data, ensure each answer retains its definitions and availability conditions. Permit scoped exceptions to style rules when necessary for accuracy, and inspect the resulting standalone text. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A rule that works for a complete page may remove essential context from an excerpt. Repeated editing conflicts can reveal a gap in the editorial policy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review reusable text in the form readers will encounter it
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review independently reused answers without the surrounding page. Include necessary definitions and attach each eligibility or availability condition to the option it qualifies. State those conditions before inviting the reader to act. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Page position does not determine what accompanies an excerpt. An answer beneath an explanatory banner may appear elsewhere without that explanation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Attach an explicit availability condition to every offer
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give each offer its own availability condition in answers that may be quoted alone. For an invented swim school, distinguish lessons open for enrollment from a holiday course with no dates yet within the sentences describing them. Name the relevant service without relying on surrounding text. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers may attach a nearby status statement to the wrong offer. Explicit sentence-level qualifications survive excerpts more reliably.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: End standalone-answer reviews with an open question about what remains unclear
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Ask an open-ended clarity question after targeted checks of an extracted answer. A bakery FAQ might explain how to commission a cake yet never establish whether the named service is the bakery itself or a separate booking platform. Read the answer without its heading, navigation, or footer and ask what remains confusing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A checklist can validate every stated fact while overlooking an essential missing fact. Unscripted questions help reveal what a stranger needs to know before the answer makes sense.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify preview indexing controls on the deployed response
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify preview indexing controls on the actual deployed host. Inspect the HTML robots directive, HTTP X-Robots-Tag and robots.txt separately. Check whether crawlers can retrieve indexing directives, since crawl restrictions can prevent them from being seen. Do not assume identical behavior across hosting environments. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Deployment settings can override repository configuration. Checking effective responses provides evidence of indexing controls, while authentication remains necessary when preview content must have restricted access.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat navigation visibility, indexing, content freshness, and visual acceptance as separate decisions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A page can be absent from the main navigation while remaining publicly linked and indexable. For a ceramic studio's workshop handouts, record separate choices for navigation, search indexing, structured data, and direct-link access; compare published content with the current source before rebuilding. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Broad requests such as making a document a complete landing page do not settle every discovery or privacy choice. Document assumptions and resolve consequential ambiguity. Likewise, acceptance of an animation on real devices can settle visual preference without proving that an intermittent automated test is technically sound.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Apply privacy rules to every published representation and customize the surroundings of brand marks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Privacy checks must cover HTML, structured data, downloadable files, and machine-readable text together. Removing contact details from JSON-LD or marking an HTML region with data-nosnippet does not remove those details from other published representations. Define allowed fields and enforce them during validation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Alternate formats can quietly undo a careful presentation choice. Keep navigation and indexing decisions explicit, and make metadata describe the page accurately. For branded social links, consult current brand guidance and place decorative effects around the approved mark; retain an accessible name, keyboard focus, and reduced-motion behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Compose social images for both wide presentation and a central square crop
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Social images should keep their essential subject legible in both the intended wide format and a central square crop. For a 1200×630 composition, inspect the central 630×630 region as a design check rather than assuming every platform crops identically. A seed library might use a centred seed pod instead of cropping a text-heavy page hero. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Website compositions often distribute meaning across a wide scene. A dedicated share image preserves recognition when previews discard peripheral artwork or reduce the image to a thumbnail.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review social images against the same visual constraints as the website
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A social share image should preserve the site's intended visual meaning rather than reintroducing a rejected motif. If a tide-pool field guide deliberately avoids aquarium-like imagery, its thumbnail should not imply a glass tank merely because that composition looks attractive in isolation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The share card may be a visitor's first encounter with the site. Review it beside the page artwork and the design constraints, including prohibited interpretations, so derivative assets do not quietly reverse an earlier art-direction decision.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check analytics access per dataset and distinguish edge counts from browser measurements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Analytics availability depends on the dataset, dimensions, permissions and account entitlement. Test a minimal query with the intended account before designing a dashboard around particular fields. Verify access separately for coarse aggregates and detailed dimensions. Browser measurements also require functioning event collection. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A rejected dimension can indicate an access restriction rather than a syntax error. Missing browser events do not prove that traffic is absent, and a paid subscription does not necessarily unlock every dataset.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Sparse browser analytics can indicate missing collection rather than low traffic
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When browser analytics covers only a few routes, inspect shared layouts and beacon requests before interpreting traffic trends. Compare route coverage with server or edge observations, recognizing that bots, blockers and measurement definitions prevent direct count equivalence. If collection is intended sitewide, configure it through a shared layout or verified hosting feature and check representative pages. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Partial collection can make popular content appear unused. Confirm that events arrive successfully, rather than checking only for a script tag, before using analytics to guide site changes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose monitoring sources according to the question each can answer
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Edge analytics, browser measurements, deployment records and service metrics answer different operational questions. Use edge data for request volume and caching, browser measurements for page experience, deployment records for publishing reliability, and service metrics for execution errors or storage usage. Confirm available fields and permissions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Referrer hosts do not provide complete traffic attribution, and URL query parameters may be omitted during collection. A useful monitoring plan documents coverage and blind spots for each source.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Analytics installation requires collection checks, CSP alignment, and correct site configuration
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Installing browser analytics requires more than adding a beacon to a shared layout. Use the public site identifier issued for your own deployment, allow the required script and collection origins in CSP, and check for duplicate injection. Test separate builds independently and verify that events appear under the intended site. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Blocked requests and copied identifiers can quietly corrupt coverage. Treat public analytics identifiers separately from secrets, use narrow scanner exceptions, and do not infer blanket consent exemptions merely from a vendor's cookieless description.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build privacy documentation from the site's actual data flows
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Include privacy documentation in the initial site scope and populate it from an inventory of actual collection, storage, sharing, and tracking behavior. Cover the operator's identity, purposes, providers, retention practices, contact method, and relevant rights information after appropriate review. Link the page from the footer and use the site's normal accessible layout. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Copying a template without auditing its claims can list absent advertising tools, invent retention periods, or promise unsupported processes. A section checklist helps discover missing questions but does not establish legal compliance. Revisit the page when forms, analytics, vendors, or data-handling practices change so the public description stays aligned with implementation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Define analytics events by user outcomes and keep payloads free of personal data
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain a shared event dictionary with stable snake_case names, precise triggers, and documented properties. Examples include `form_fill`, `gated_download`, `resource_view`, `cta_click`, and `video_play`. Fire completion events after confirmed success, and prevent refreshes or retries from duplicating conversions. Prefer resource identifiers and controlled categories over arbitrary text. A 240-character truncation rule can be a local payload budget; verify the chosen provider's actual limits. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Consistent names make comparisons possible only when event meanings are also consistent. Titles, referrers, URLs, and anchor text can contain personal information, so truncation alone is insufficient. Use allowlisted properties and document extensions alongside the common schema.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep analytics consent behavior consistent with the published policy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Do not infer that analytics needs no consent solely because it is described as cookieless. Vercel Analytics was described as cookieless in the source material (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it); actual obligations depend on jurisdiction, configuration, and processing. If analytics is assigned to a consent category, apply that choice consistently to page views and custom events. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Calling analytics consent-controlled while firing it unconditionally undermines the interface's promise. Submitting a form does not automatically authorize unrelated analytics or marketing. Inventory the data sent, review the applicable requirements, and test both acceptance and rejection paths instead of relying on a provider label.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify consent persistence, preference changes and accurate privacy copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A consent interface must persist valid choices and propagate later changes to the services it controls. Separate necessary functionality from optional analytics and advertising where applicable. Match banner copy to the services actually deployed and provide a persistent settings link. Test first consent, returning visits, withdrawal and cross-subdomain behavior. Omit an optional cookie-domain field when unused rather than serializing the text `undefined`; verify the resulting cookie in the browser. Choose retention according to applicable requirements rather than treating 182 days as a universal rule. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A polished banner can conceal broken persistence or inactive callbacks. Platform APIs are perishable (as of June 2026; re-check before relying on it). Keep CSP permissions aligned with deployed integrations rather than preauthorizing unused services.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use an evidence-based launch checklist that spans implementation, operation and recovery
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A launch checklist should cover the site's full operating lifecycle and assign evidence and responsibility to each applicable gate. Include repository hygiene, builds, hosting, DNS, CMS behavior, forms, analytics, consent, discovery, visual quality, browser coverage, accessibility, content, performance and security. Add monitoring, backup recovery, documentation, email and localization when relevant. Separate prelaunch review, production cutover, post-deploy verification and subsequent monitoring. Mark exclusions with a reason rather than forcing irrelevant features into every site. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A long checklist is useful only when it supports decisions. Named responsibilities and observable acceptance criteria prevent deployment success from obscuring unfinished editorial handoff, broken lead capture or an untested recovery path.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Monitoring needs actionable alerts, readable errors and a response owner
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Production monitoring should connect detectable failures to someone who can act on them. Configure error tracking with matching source maps, an external uptime check and tested alert delivery. A 1–5 minute uptime interval can suit a small site, depending on its response requirements. Include important application paths rather than relying solely on a homepage status check. Document responsibility and short runbooks for broken forms, stale CMS content, certificate issues and deployment failures. Retain logs according to operational and privacy needs. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Installing a dashboard does not establish an incident process. Useful monitoring answers what broke, who responds and what they should try first; test alerts so the first real incident is not also the notification-system test.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prove recovery with restored content and a rehearsed deployment rollback
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A backup strategy is incomplete until the site can be restored from it. Keep code in a remote repository and back up CMS content, required assets and editorial tracking data separately. Restore a recent export into an isolated environment and rehearse a rollback using a preview deployment. Define recovery time objective as acceptable downtime and recovery point objective as acceptable data loss; use those requirements to choose backup frequency and retention. Keep secrets in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat, with controlled recovery access. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful export proves that a file exists, not that the system can recover. Restoration exercises reveal missing assets, incompatible schemas and inaccessible credentials before an outage makes them urgent.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Document real operating tasks and the reasons behind non-obvious architecture choices
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A website handoff should explain how to operate the site and why its important choices were made. Provide a concise architecture map, an editor walkthrough, form-to-CRM data flow, analytics locations and deployment and rollback instructions. Include a troubleshooting guide for the five most likely issues and document administrative roles without embedding credentials. Record architecture decisions such as static versus server rendering or hosted versus custom forms, including their tradeoffs. Define unfamiliar domain terminology. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Documentation written while the build is fresh preserves reasoning that source code alone cannot show. Have an unfamiliar operator follow the guide: their missing steps are stronger evidence than the author's confidence that the instructions are obvious.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose redesign automation by its actual infrastructure behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use an in-place maintenance workflow when redesigning an existing site whose repository, domain, and deployment must be preserved. Before selecting automation, inspect whether it edits the current project or scaffolds new infrastructure, which hosting platforms it supports, and what metadata its template would retain. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A visually complete redesign may feel like a first build while requiring maintenance mechanics. For a seed library, starting from a less complete template could silently discard working forms, redirects, or discovery files. Mechanical fit matters more than the workflow's label.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Include dependency currency and migration assessment in website maintenance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Website maintenance should check framework, runtime, and integration versions alongside content and styling. When a meaningful gap appears, consult official migration guidance, record breaking changes, map them to the repository, and perform a scoped upgrade with build and deployment verification. Evaluate compatibility and support requirements before choosing a target release. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Dependency drift can accumulate operational and maintenance costs that are invisible in screenshots. Separating documentation research from repository inspection prevents generic upgrade advice from overlooking the exact code and configuration that need attention.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use a lightweight version check to trigger focused migration research
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Split dependency maintenance into a routine version inventory and a deeper migration review triggered by relevant differences. Maintain a project-specific package list, use npm view <package> version to inspect the registry's latest tag, and use the lockfile or npm ls to inspect resolved installations. package.json records requested ranges, not necessarily installed versions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This keeps ordinary checks small without ignoring drift. A mismatch is a review signal, not an automatic upgrade command: inspect release channels, runtime requirements, breaking changes, and hosting compatibility before changing dependencies.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Record out-of-scope defects with evidence and route them to the responsible workstream
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When exploration uncovers an unrelated defect, record its evidence, likely impact, responsible workstream, and next verification step before changing shared artifacts. Examples include inconsistent dependency licensing notes, mismatched default configurations, or incorrect repository identity settings. Resolve urgent blockers within existing authority; route independent changes through the relevant maintainer or active workstream. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Adjacent discoveries are valuable, but uncoordinated fixes can collide with concurrent work or mix unrelated changes into a release. A concrete issue record preserves the finding without pretending that recording it has repaired the underlying problem.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify asset migrations with checksum manifests and preserve paths until dependencies are checked
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Copy shared assets before retiring their old location, and verify the copy with relative-path SHA-256 manifests. Inventory scripts, templates and documents that reference the existing location. Compare source and destination manifests, record intentional changes separately, and leave a relocation notice at the old location. Remove the old copy only after dependent consumers have migrated. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Matching file counts do not prove matching contents. Moving a folder can silently break hardcoded paths in unrelated tools; a verified copy preserves a recovery route while making the migration's claims independently checkable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inspect relative references before reorganizing a shared asset bundle
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Preserve a bundle's directory structure when reorganizing it would break relative links. Before copying, use rg to inspect references in Markdown, HTML, CSS and scripts. If the existing layout is internally connected, add a role-based README index instead of moving files into new conceptual groups. A byte-identical copy and a reorganized destination require different acceptance checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A tidy directory tree can conceal broken dependencies. An index improves navigation without changing the paths that make the bundle work, and the reference audit reveals whether a proposed cleanup is actually a migration.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate setup guides with a cold read and a real execution
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An assume-nothing setup guide needs both a cold-reader review and a real execution test. Ask someone without project context to identify unexplained terms, missing prerequisites, and ambiguous steps. Then follow the instructions in a representative environment, recording where actual behavior differs from the guide. Revise the instructions from those observations and repeat the affected steps. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An author can unconsciously fill gaps using knowledge that a newcomer lacks. Cold reading reveals comprehension problems, while execution exposes environmental assumptions and commands that look plausible but do not work as described.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Base availability claims on the scope of the released service
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Compare website claims with the documented scope of the service visitors can currently access. Separate confirmed features from proposals. If source documents disagree, flag the conflict and withhold the disputed claim until it is resolved. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Plans and demonstrations do not establish what a customer receives. Release-specific evidence helps writers describe availability honestly without turning intentions into commitments.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Ship new functions with working adapters, setup instructions, and discoverable examples
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A new capability is incomplete until its public entry points and documentation expose it correctly. Check compatibility shims and wrappers for the new function names, update setup instructions for added dependencies, and revise user-facing query examples and automation guides. Verify that the documented path invokes the intended implementation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A working function can remain practically unavailable if users and agents only see older examples. Updating the entire discovery path prevents a feature from existing in code while support instructions continue to steer every caller toward the previous behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate a reusable workflow description from permission to distribute its underlying materials
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Publishing the shape of a workflow does not establish permission to distribute its underlying knowledge, assets, or code. Before packaging reusable materials, document their provenance, remove confidential content, and resolve ownership and redistribution questions through the appropriate review. Keep public availability claims separate from architectural examples until those questions are settled. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An anonymized diagram may be suitable for explanation even when the source material cannot be released. Treating those as separate decisions prevents a compelling concept page from becoming an unintended offer to distribute material whose rights or release conditions remain unresolved.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use website claim audits to detect product drift and route findings with evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A website accuracy audit should compare public claims with default installation behavior, configuration and current documentation. Check for hard-coded nondefault resources, incompatible dependency licensing, stale setup instructions and features that execute without producing useful output. Label code-reading inferences separately from reproduced failures. Route each finding to the responsible maintenance queue with evidence and a verification step. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Public copy often receives a fresh reading long after implementation assumptions have changed. Capturing discrepancies makes that review useful beyond the page, while keeping product repairs scoped prevents an editorial task from becoming an uncontrolled software change.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit capability claims against implementation, tests and publication scope
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before writing a capability page, classify each claim as planned, implemented, tested or observed in operation. Compare requirements, repository evidence and existing public copy, especially for supported platforms and security boundaries. Keep sensitive implementation details out of public prose without concealing material limitations. For an invented seed library, distinguish a planned reservation system from a working catalog and a verified pickup workflow. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Ambitious plans and candid engineering notes serve different purposes from public explanations. A claim inventory helps writers choose accurate tense and prevents stale platform assumptions or broad security language from becoming promises.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Read release rules before implementation and identify conflicts with supplied content early
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review a site's deployment rules and content checks before implementing a new page. Establish the preview process, production authorization, indexing policy, heading structure, fidelity requirements and rollback procedure. If supplied text conflicts with automated punctuation or name checks, resolve the conflict explicitly instead of editing approved content silently. For non-HTML downloads, indexing controls may need response headers. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Existing automation often contains constraints that a visually correct page can still violate. Discovering them early prevents premature release and exposes missing operational guidance while it is still cheap to fix.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Centralize changing facts and trace public claims back to their supporting evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain changing public facts in one registry and connect each substantive claim to supporting evidence. At a content milestone, audit missing sources, outstanding review findings and facts that may have changed during drafting. Re-render dependent pages after a registry update and inspect the resulting language in context. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Copy can become inaccurate because the underlying service changes even after careful review. Centralization reduces scattered fixes, while explicit dependencies help ensure a single update reaches every relevant page without leaving contradictory descriptions behind.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review shared copy in every consuming page and distinguish configuration states precisely
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before changing a shared heading or sentence, inspect all pages that consume it and verify that its meaning remains accurate in each context. Describe enabled, disabled and unavailable configurations separately, using verbs that match actual behavior: receiving data does not necessarily mean storing it. Update canonical strings and scan rendered output for stale claims. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A locally sensible edit can alter several pages at once. Precise state language and dependency checks prevent ambiguous promises, especially when a service's capabilities change faster than its marketing copy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep immutable media configuration separate from runtime diagnostic attributes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use separate DOM attributes for media-source configuration and runtime state. For example, data-video-template can hold a URL pattern while data-loaded-clips reports available passages. Do not overwrite the template with diagnostics after initialization, even if the controller has already cached its value. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reusing an attribute creates a time-dependent interface: a test may see a URL before interaction and clip identifiers afterward, while a stacked fallback never changes it at all. Rename the attributes together with their readers and tests. Until that migration is complete, document the transition explicitly so debugging tools do not mistake configuration for current state.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep deferred release checks explicit and verify deployed behavior independently of the push
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A release with deferred checks needs a visible follow-up ledger that distinguishes completed validation from outstanding work. After deploying, verify expected page content, successful route responses and video range requests, rather than treating a successful push as proof of delivery. Compare production layout with the preview and retain unresolved contrast, accessibility, media and real-device checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A visually acceptable preview does not establish that all quality requirements passed or that the deployment is serving the intended build. Explicit deferrals prevent later readers from mistaking release status for complete validation. Record concrete remaining defects and their closure evidence so polish and missing checks do not disappear into a vague promise to revisit them.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Maintain a recurring security checklist with verified credential rotation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Make dependency checks, access reviews, header reviews, and credential maintenance recurring operational tasks. An example cadence is npm audit before deployment, quarterly pre-commit autoupdate and CSP review, monthly repository membership review, and annual credential review. Rotate exposed credentials immediately regardless of schedule. Store replacement secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Security settings drift as dependencies and teams change. During rotation, update every consuming environment, verify operation, and revoke the old credential. Public widget site keys and server secrets have different exposure requirements and should not be treated interchangeably.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make maintenance platform-aware and treat production promotion as a verified transition
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintenance workflows need an authoritative record of hosting platform, deployment environment, domain ownership and indexing status. Read that record before choosing platform commands. Before promoting a preview, verify the intended production target, approved release scope, environment variables, domain configuration and rollback path. Run browser, accessibility, performance and header checks; deliberately reconcile preview authentication, noindex directives and robots rules. Verify the public deployment and update the record afterward. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Cloudflare and Vercel operations are not interchangeable, and a successful preview does not establish production readiness. A documented transition prevents accidental public exposure, stale access controls and production pages remaining excluded from indexing.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Assign migration discovery and production cutover separate responsibilities with a shared handoff
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Site migration workflows should identify who discovers legacy URLs, authors redirects, places assets and performs production cutover. Keep one authoritative redirect manifest and pass its location and validation status to maintenance and content workflows. Downstream workflows should consume that evidence rather than independently repeating discovery unless the inventory is incomplete or stale. Record who owns corrections and final verification. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated discovery wastes effort and can produce conflicting mappings. A shared handoff preserves continuity while allowing the cutover operator to verify readiness independently of the person or automation that prepared the migration.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Archive migration evidence outside disposable build directories
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep migration discovery, verification results, final mappings and cutover handoffs in a durable archive separate from build output. Organize artifacts by purpose and include a short mapping summary, source provenance and instructions for regenerating deployment configuration. Identify the authoritative redirect manifest and retain enough evidence to explain uncertain mappings. Apply appropriate access controls to private exports. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Build directories are routinely cleaned, but redirect decisions may need investigation months later. A durable archive lets maintainers repair broken legacy links and audit changes without repeating the original discovery process.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use a deployment inventory to coordinate shared changes while verifying each site independently
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Apply fleet-wide website changes from an explicit deployment inventory that records each site's repository, platform, environment, and current implementation. Design the shared change once, adapt it per site, and retain acceptance evidence for every deployment. Check preview and production targets before release, stage rollout where appropriate, verify live behavior, and update the inventory afterward. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A common implementation reduces drift, but a shared review score can hide a missed site or environment mismatch. Per-site checks preserve accountability while allowing reusable changes such as security headers, analytics updates, and structured-data improvements to propagate consistently.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit shipped behavior before turning a product vision into website claims
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify marketing claims against the delivered build and observable behavior, not just plans or source-code presence. Distinguish shipped and exercised features from dormant modules, test-only safeguards, optional integrations, and future work. For a tide-pool field guide, an offline download promise requires testing the delivered guide without a connection; an unused caching module is insufficient evidence. Record limits beside the strongest defensible claim. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Ambitious descriptions often combine several maturity levels into one confident sentence. A behavior audit preserves the direction of the project while preventing readers from mistaking an architectural intention for something they can use today.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Translate unsupported website promises into actionable product checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Convert each unsupported public claim into a specific implementation question or acceptance test. Record the proposed sentence, missing evidence, responsible workstream, and condition that would justify publishing it. Check runtime dependency choices against license obligations, confirm that advertised safeguards ship in the product, and verify that dormant features actually execute. Keep repairs within the authorized scope of the relevant project. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Some copy problems cannot be solved honestly by polishing language. A short list of evidence gaps gives engineering work a clear purpose and prevents the website from silently resolving product decisions that remain open.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve release-scope conflicts before stating availability
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Conflicting statements about baseline scope and release timing require an explicit product decision before they become availability copy. Record both interpretations: a feature might belong in the base offering yet arrive after the initial release. Assign the timing question to the responsible workstream and use planned-status wording until the release scope is settled. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] 'Included' can mean included in pricing, architecture, or the next shipment. Website wording must not silently choose among those meanings. A concise handoff preserves the conflict and gives the decision-maker enough context to resolve it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep optional integrations distinct from default product capabilities
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe an exploratory or optional integration according to its actual availability, activation requirements, and data flow. Distinguish 'may support,' 'planned,' and 'available by default.' If enabling an integration requires an external account or sends data to a hosted service, explain that choice where users decide whether to enable it. Confirm the current scope before expanding navigation or feature lists. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A tentative idea can become an apparent commitment through repeated copy alone. Explicit status and opt-in boundaries prevent readers from assuming that an experimental connection is shipped, mandatory, or entirely local.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make disclosure placement and rule precedence explicit before another writing pass
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define where each disclosure is required, its canonical wording, and which rule wins when editorial constraints conflict. A practical default is one concise status sentence per independently reusable block, with any necessary qualification adjacent to its claim. Keep distinct operations distinct in source facts, then rerun content checks after shared strings change. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Another writing round cannot reliably resolve contradictory instructions. Explicit scope and precedence reduce redundant caveats while preserving honesty when a block appears outside its original page. Fixing the governing constraints also prevents the same fault from returning in later drafts.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Update feature claims after acceptance checks confirm the visitor experience
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Tie website claim updates to acceptance evidence for the released feature. Map each feature to affected descriptions, limitations and page checks. For an invented garden centre, advertise online workshop booking only after visitors can complete a representative booking successfully. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Merged code does not establish that a feature works in its intended setting. A recorded update trigger prevents premature promises and outdated descriptions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Introduce tracking through a consent-first deployment sequence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Add consent controls and script blocking before enabling analytics or advertising tags that require consent. Define categories, establish denied defaults, and connect preference changes to tag activation and withdrawal. Inspect the chosen vendor's current consent semantics rather than assuming a denied flag prevents every network request. Update CSP directives for the endpoints actually used, then update processor and cookie disclosures. On preview, inspect network traffic before consent, after consent, and after withdrawal; verify cookie cleanup, preference persistence, console errors, accessibility, and performance. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Sequencing prevents an intermediate deployment from collecting data before controls exist. Testing actual traffic also catches silent CSP failures and consent libraries that appear correct while scripts still run.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Update platform decision trees as well as adding new deployment instructions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When adopting a new hosting platform, update workflow routing, commands, checkpoints, and reference maps together. Distinguish Cloudflare Workers, Cloudflare Pages, and Vercel rather than assuming one generic hosting branch covers them. Parameterize branch names and document which deployment view counts as evidence. Check that promised appendices exist and every referenced command has been verified. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A correct new section can remain unreachable if the surrounding decision tree still routes work to an older platform. A gap list is useful evidence: it reveals contradictions between fresh lessons and standing instructions before a later maintenance task follows the wrong path.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Mark known-bad runbook advice immediately while the replacement is still being validated
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Place a clear superseded warning beside known-harmful instructions as soon as contrary evidence appears. Identify the affected steps, state the observed failure, and point to the currently supported evidence without presenting an unfinished replacement as proven. Track what still needs validation before rewriting the complete procedure. Update dependent checklists and indexes when that validation finishes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Waiting for a polished replacement leaves dangerous instructions available to the next reader. A focused interim correction prevents repeated mistakes while preserving an honest distinction between established findings, provisional guidance, and work still outstanding.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit privacy promises sentence by sentence against implementation evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check every statement about data practices against implementation evidence before publishing it. Build one row per privacy sentence, consent line, and machine-facing restatement. Mark each TRUE with code or measured behavior, FALSE with contradictory evidence, or UNVERIFIABLE with the missing proof. Block publication of contradicted claims and resolve or clearly qualify unsupported ones. Repeat the audit after relevant fixes and against the intended deployment. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Privacy copy often reflects design intent while code and infrastructure evolve. Build, accessibility, and performance checks do not establish whether retention, logging, deletion, or email promises describe the deployed behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit the installed system and distinguish absent mechanisms from untested ones
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify public capability claims against the installed system, including the path from stored state to user-visible behavior. Use read-only queries and inspect diagnostic commands before assuming they are read-only. Check whether producers and consumers use compatible relationships, whether installed code matches the reviewed checkout, and whether health checks sample eligible activity. Describe a missing mechanism as not implemented, rather than merely untested. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful scheduled job or plausible database row does not prove downstream behavior. Even approved limitations can understate a defect when they imply a mechanism exists that the live application never connects.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify public claims against the released build and the actual demonstration data
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Public capability claims must match the released build and the dataset visitors actually see. Check the release branch, feature availability, acceptance evidence and demonstration schema before writing copy. Distinguish unavailable inspection from an empty result, incomplete execution from success, and installation downloads from offline operation. Derive displayed counts from explicit queries instead of typing them into prose. Keep experimental features visibly separate from demonstrations that cannot exercise them. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A feature diagram beside a demonstration can imply a capability that neither explicitly promises. Repository code, successful exits and populated tables are weaker evidence than a verified visitor experience. Precise scope prevents attractive presentation from quietly overstating readiness.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify feature claims through visitor-visible behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test claimed capabilities through visible interactions and returned results. For an invented lighthouse museum, verify that exhibit filters return appropriate items and that result links open the promised details. Check empty results, unsuitable queries and whether counts accurately name what they count. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Stored data and internal structures do not prove that visitors can use a feature. Representative journeys expose gaps that polished descriptions can conceal.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reconcile code findings with release evidence and documented deviations before changing public claims
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reconcile repository findings with documented deviations and release evidence before turning them into implementation tasks or public copy. A pinned dependency difference may be known debt with a bounded impact, while an apparent missing fix may already be included in a pending release. Verify the release actually lands, then exercise the capability through the reader-facing path before changing its status. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Code inspection establishes what is present, but it may not explain why a divergence exists or how it is scheduled to resolve. Combining those perspectives makes a handoff more precise. New edge cases should extend the validation matrix even when the existing deviation is intentional.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check live outcomes before publishing promises about automated behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Claims about automated behavior must be checked against live outcomes, not just documentation and intended code paths. For a seed library's reservation site, inspect whether reminders were actually produced and delivered, rather than merely confirming that a scheduled task exists. If copy is drafted around an upcoming repair, mark that dependency explicitly and block publication until a real execution proves it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A central behavior can stop silently while its interface and documentation remain convincing. A reviewer who inspects operational evidence can discover failures that a copy-only reviewer cannot. Keep regression checks for wording too, but do not let mechanical polish substitute for proof that the promised experience happens.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Lock approved copy with narrow merges, retained history and deployed-content checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Approved copy should be versioned, merged through a constrained interface and verified at its deployed destination. Preserve the reviewed text and its evidence mapping. Reject unknown content keys and require explicit authorization for replacing protected wording. Keep superseded versions available outside live input folders, run relevant validation and secret scanning, then confirm the intended text is actually served. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Approval is easy to lose when copy moves through scripts, shared strings and deployment pipelines. Narrow merges reduce accidental changes, while arrival checks distinguish a successful push from a successful publication. Any remaining product dependency must stay an explicit launch condition rather than disappearing inside the copy approval record.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Support capability claims with released behavior and explicit limits
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Expand a capability claim only after checking the released feature through a representative visitor journey. Read acceptance results alongside their exclusions. For an invented swim school, verify that a course finder supports the ages and locations named in its description, and state any coverage limits beside the claim. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Successful checks support only the behavior they cover. Keeping limits with the canonical description helps later revisions preserve the same evidence boundary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Correct public claims immediately when an implementation fix is deferred
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a verified implementation gap contradicts published copy, correct the copy while tracking the deferred fix separately. Record the evidence, current limitation, proposed repair and acceptance criteria. Mark the repair as deferred so later contributors cannot mistake it for completed or rejected work. Keep present-tense claims tied to current behaviour. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A backlog decision does not make an inaccurate statement safe to publish. Separating truthful copy from future engineering work preserves trust and gives the next contributor an actionable handoff.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give engineering fixes an explicit return path to the public claims they affect
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A deferred engineering fix should identify both the evidence required for closure and the public copy that evidence will permit changing. Track affected headlines, FAQs, metadata and limitations alongside the issue. Restore stronger wording only after the required acceptance proof exists, then remove obsolete caveats consistently. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A handoff that ends at the implementation can leave a website permanently understating its capabilities. A defined return path keeps claims accurate in both directions without treating an intended fix as a completed one.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Trace a corrected claim to related promises that share its assumptions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a claim fails review, identify other statements that depend on the same assumption. For an invented garden centre, a change to delivery coverage may affect checkout guidance, service-area pages and promotional copy. Update the supporting facts and affected claims together. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fixing one sentence can leave contradictory promises elsewhere. Following the underlying cause reveals dependencies that an exact phrase search may miss.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Remove retired claims from every active input, including authoritative examples
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A fact amendment must propagate through every active brief, digest, example and source summary that restates the old claim. Search for retired wording and inspect paraphrases before handing the packet to another writer. Review coordinator-supplied suggestions with the same standard applied to generated copy. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A careful writer can reproduce a false claim because an authoritative input still instructs it to do so. Correcting the canonical fact alone does not resolve contradictory guidance, and an example carries practical authority even when labelled optional.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit the highest-authority instructions for stale decisions before drafting
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Preflight a writing packet by checking its highest-authority instructions against current facts and decisions. Resolve retired metaphors, outdated availability language and conflicting terminology before drafting begins. Keep historical approvals distinguishable from active guidance, and define which source wins when documents disagree. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An obsolete instruction becomes especially dangerous when it lives in the file declared authoritative. A diligent writer will follow it precisely, so reliability depends on maintaining the instruction hierarchy as carefully as the copy it governs.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Approved wording must be reopened when its factual basis changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A wording lock preserves an editorial decision, not the continuing truth of the sentence. Recheck approved copy when evidence or implementation changes, including technical nouns such as files, database and upgrade. Verify that public terminology matches the scope actually implemented and tested. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Older approvals can shelter the most consequential overclaims because reviewers assume they were already settled. Technical readers interpret familiar terms concretely, so language inherited from a plan may remain misleading even after it has become standard internal vocabulary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: After a factual repair, review the joins between changed and unchanged copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A repair pass should check both the requested corrections and new inconsistencies at their boundaries. Compare revised paragraphs with unchanged labels, captions, FAQs and limitations, especially when terms such as default, designed and planned carry different meanings. Record affected source dependencies so the review extends beyond edited slots. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A locally accurate replacement can leave the page telling two incompatible stories. Keeping the edit small is useful, but closure requires checking how the new wording interacts with everything readers still encounter.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make amendment sweeps auditable by listing changed and retained dependent claims
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A completed fact-amendment sweep should list every dependent slot, whether changed or retained, with its revised justification. Include labels, readouts, body copy and limitations. Review retained text for new ambiguity created by the amendment, then check the rendered page for consistent terminology. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A visible inventory proves that closure considered more than the named defects. It also reveals missed surfaces and distinguishes a deliberately retained sentence from one that escaped review, making future changes easier to trace.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Find affected copy through source references, then reread it in its rendered context
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After amending a fact, locate dependent copy through the claim ledger's source references rather than relying only on a finding's slot list. Reread each hit with its heading, tier label, legend and standalone text alternative. Retain a sentence only after rederiving its full meaning from the new evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Wording can remain individually defensible while still conveying the old account in context. A generic plural or nearby status label may expand the claim, so dependency tracing must be followed by semantic review of what readers actually receive.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check whether replaced copy was the sole carrier of a required fact
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before replacing a line, identify every required fact that appears nowhere else on the page. Update the claim-to-source mapping after the edit, then check both factual coverage and repeated wording. Phrase-overlap measurements can document exact shared runs, but necessary status language may deserve an explicit exception. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A stronger headline can silently remove a mandatory limitation or explanation. Tracking facts independently of sentences prevents a successful stylistic revision from becoming an incomplete or misleading page.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify deployment arrival using content unique to the intended release
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Confirm a content deployment by checking a newly changed string on the deployed page, not merely by observing a successful build. Keep a snapshot of the reviewed text, inspect the merge or dry-run report, run required checks, then probe the intended environment for that release's distinctive content. Check access behavior separately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reachable page may still serve an older build. A release-specific probe ties the observation to the change being shipped and distinguishes content arrival from build completion or access-control behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recheck approved copy when the facts and neighboring pages change
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Previously approved copy must be reassessed when source facts change or another page becomes the primary home for its evidence. Give each page a clear purpose, identify duplicated proof, and check whether older wording now contradicts updated descriptions. A ceramic studio's About page can explain its working practice while course pages carry detailed class evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Approval records a decision at a point in time, not permanent correctness. A claim register makes overlap and drift visible without reducing every editorial decision to personal taste.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Apply page-wide requirements to shared chrome as well as body copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Requirements about what appears on a page apply to its header, footer, shared blocks and other rendered content, not only its primary source file. If a topic must be absent, inspect the assembled output and any visitor-visible variants. Include shared content in review snapshots. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Removing a sentence from the body achieves little when the footer repeats it. Reviewing the actual page ensures that decisions concern what visitors encounter rather than an incomplete representation of the interface.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reconcile shared source documents without silently changing frozen review inputs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Shared content sources should be checked against current approved facts before they feed another page. Record changed availability, narrowed claims and obsolete approval labels. Preserve frozen inputs for completed reviews, attach explicit corrections to new briefs, and refresh the shared source through a versioned update. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Facts often change page by page while shared summaries remain untouched. Silent edits obscure what an earlier review actually assessed; documented corrections preserve reproducibility while preventing later pages from inheriting stale claims.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check absolute availability claims against all relevant booking conditions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify statements such as all classes are available against schedules, capacity, eligibility and location restrictions. For an invented swim school, distinguish courses listed on the website from sessions currently accepting enrollment. Use wording that names the actual condition. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A single exception can invalidate an absolute claim. Precise availability labels help visitors choose a workable next step.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Handwritten status text creates another copy of a fact that must stay synchronized
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat every manually written status statement as a dependency of the underlying status record. If a bicycle-repair co-op renders booking availability from structured data but repeats it in an FAQ, changing the data will not necessarily update the prose. Generate both from a shared source where practical; otherwise record the manual dependency and check it during status changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Standalone answers need explicit facts, but duplicating those facts creates maintenance work. A polished page can quietly become inaccurate after its first approval.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Carry confirmed defect classes into the first review of each new page
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Turn confirmed cross-page defects into reusable review prompts for subsequent pages. If an ambiguous possessive previously implied ownership or authorship that the evidence did not support, check new drafts for the same construction. Prefer a clear noun or omit an unnecessary possessive when the meaning remains intact. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A correction on one page does not automatically teach the next writer. Recording the general failure class, rather than only the repaired sentence, helps reviewers catch recurrence without forcing every page into identical wording.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve specific factual corrections before reusing older wording
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Writing briefs must include applicable corrections before writers reuse verbs from older fact records. Distinguish operations such as retrieving passages and composing answers, and resolve conflicting descriptions against verified current behaviour. Update restricted citation lists when they exclude the correction needed to describe that behaviour accurately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A repair can restore an obsolete claim when a familiar verb remains in the brief. Recency helps locate corrections, but verified specificity—not merely the newest timestamp—should determine the wording.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Refresh public claims when verified implementation changes make them stale
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Feature completion should trigger an audit of every public statement that describes the feature as unavailable or planned. Maintain shared facts in a central registry, update those facts from verified behaviour, and separately search FAQs, cards and prose for hard-coded versions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Previously approved copy can become false without anyone editing it. A shared registry reduces repeated changes, but it cannot refresh independent wording automatically. Connecting implementation milestones to a content audit keeps capability and limitation claims aligned with the release.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe privacy by selected execution path and disclose skipped capabilities
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Privacy copy for configurable software should state how data flow changes between hosted and local execution paths. Verify where content goes under each supported configuration, which account receives it, and which capabilities require network access. If a capability is unavailable in a supported mode, expose the skip rather than presenting invented results. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Adding local execution changes more than a feature list: it can invalidate an older blanket statement about external transfers. Rewrite from verified configuration-specific facts, and distinguish intended behaviour from capabilities actually exercised.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Register approved copy through an atomic import that rejects unauthorized changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Approved copy needs an import path that preserves its protection against later automatic overwrites. Restrict keys to the intended page namespace, add unknown keys, leave identical values unchanged and reject conflicting values unless an explicit revision record authorizes them. Validate the entire input before writing anything. Store source provenance and a content hash, and retain superseded wording when a revision is accepted. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A general merge utility may treat generated text as refreshable. Reusing that path for approved copy silently weakens the approval contract. Negative controls for foreign keys, malformed references and changed approved values make the boundary testable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Derive published counts from explicit queries and verify what each count includes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Generate changing website statistics from their declared source and record the query, derivation time and result together. Use read-only database access for extraction. Before publishing a count, inspect whether the counted entities match the wording, whether groups are empty and whether mixed record types belong in the total. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A tide-pool field guide might count observations, species and illustrated entries differently. A discrepancy can reflect a changed denominator rather than bad arithmetic. Reproducible queries make claims refreshable; composition checks make their labels honest.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Read shared copy in every host context and replace ambiguous pronouns
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Shared text must remain clear in every page that includes it, especially when it explains privacy or network behavior. If a passage mentions both a local model and online research, “because it needs the web” may attach to either. Name the intended activity explicitly and review each rendered occurrence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Saving a few words can introduce a false technical claim across multiple pages at once. When a passage uses only 31 of an allowed 40 words, clarity is a better use of the remaining space than unnecessary compression.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Refresh dependent claims and conflicting instructions whenever a source fact changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A fact update must include the rows, pages and instructions that depend on the changed claim. Search for references to the updated fact identifier, revise stale summaries, record the change and inspect whether the new requirement conflicts with older wording restrictions. Explicitly retire incompatible clauses. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Updating the named source alone leaves indirect references ready to revive the old claim. A dependency sweep protects future writing as well as the current page, preventing a later contributor from following obsolete guidance that still appears authoritative.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Adding an option requires checking every exclusive claim and fallback
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Whenever a choice list expands, review every “only,” “never,” “every” and fallback statement affected by the new option. On a bicycle-repair booking form, adding “inspection only” changes claims that previously assumed every booking included a repair. Explain the new option's consequences alongside the choice. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A small interface change can invalidate distant copy without changing that copy directly. Checking quantified claims in the same maintenance pass prevents an apparently complete option list from leaving users with a false account of what happens next.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Update shared two-way descriptions when a third option is introduced
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a third option is introduced, find every shared sentence that still presents the original two choices as exhaustive. A ceramic studio adding self-guided sessions must revisit descriptions that say all visits are either classes or demonstrations. Check the replacement wording against neighbouring status messages on every destination page. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fixing an omission can create a new ambiguity when a short word has another meaning nearby. A useful review finding includes both the missing option and any contextual constraint the replacement must satisfy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate content migrations in generated output, including metadata and agent files
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify a content migration in built artifacts rather than relying on replacement counts in source files. A structured rename can miss list-valued entries, breadcrumb JSON-LD or generated text files that derive names from navigation labels. Traverse arrays as well as scalar strings under intended display keys. Give canonical names their own registry entries, then update consumers such as breadcrumbs, page introductions and agent-facing documents to use them. Scan the output for remaining variants and classify each as intentional or missed. Keep the reviewed build stable while a review is in progress. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An edit can be internally consistent yet incomplete because downstream generators use different sources. Output inspection exposes those hidden dependencies and helps distinguish a display label from the actual name of an entity.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat image-tool security updates as visual changes and make launch configuration explicit
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Security updates to image-processing dependencies need visual validation because they can regenerate site assets. Isolate the update, rebuild affected images, and compare outputs before combining it with launch configuration changes.
