For your own deployment, explicitly verify intended indexing headers, robots.txt, the production build command, deployment target, and form verification configuration. Store secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A dependency change can alter the page even when described as maintenance. Separating asset validation from cutover configuration makes failures easier to diagnose and prevents a launch checklist from substituting for evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Release generated pages through the normal preview and deployment workflow
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Edit canonical content, regenerate derived pages and downloads, and check for missing or stale output. Build in a clean environment and inspect the preview before promoting the tested revision through the normal release process. Verify live routes and downloaded file types afterward. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separate deployment shortcuts create undocumented maintenance paths. Source fingerprints and deployment-specific checks help establish that the reviewed output is what visitors receive.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Turn audit leftovers into a verified maintenance register
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep unresolved audit findings in one maintenance register with evidence, a next action and a completion check for each item. Separate confirmed defects from missing evidence and optional improvements. Measure usefulness before pruning accumulated guidance, compare counts only when their units match, and distribute only scrubbed generic lessons. If credentials appear in retained text, replace exposed credentials and remove their plaintext copies. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Findings scattered across long reports are easily forgotten. A register preserves accountability without presenting every advisory as a defect or silently treating an unverified claim as completed work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve overlapping page edits by preserving both layout changes and metadata
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When branches change the same page wrapper, resolve the conflict by preserving each branch's intended behaviour, including layout and social metadata. Inspect the merged page, build with production settings, check expected output, and verify the deployed result. For a bicycle-repair co-op, a redesigned booking page should retain the sharing image added by a separate metadata change. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A syntactically clean conflict resolution can silently discard one branch's contribution. Keep remaining defects in an explicit follow-up list, and serialize memory-heavy build or review work when concurrent jobs exceed the machine's available memory.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Carry deferred work forward with an explicit post-release handoff
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A post-release handoff should record unresolved defects, missing validation and cleanup tasks with clear next actions. Separate copy and metadata checks from rendering defects, real-device checks, form smoke tests and obsolete worktree removal. Describe animation defects by viewport and cycle so they can be reproduced. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A successful deployment does not resolve every known issue. A compact, actionable handoff prevents deferred work from disappearing behind a release announcement and helps the next maintainer distinguish a confirmed defect from a check that has simply not been performed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve workspace roots centrally so folder renames do not break tooling
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Resolve a workspace root through one documented configuration mechanism instead of hardcoding its absolute path across scripts. Keep reusable templates distinct from instantiated projects, and document which directory contains application code, tools, and supporting material. After a rename, check scripts and documentation for stale references. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A directory rename can otherwise become a scattered configuration migration. Central resolution makes templates portable and reduces failures caused by assumptions about another developer's machine.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: An automation shell may lack the SSH agent socket available in an interactive terminal
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] SSH authentication can fail in an automation shell because it did not inherit SSH_AUTH_SOCK from the interactive session. Check the variable and run ssh-add -l before assuming the key is missing. Prefer a known agent socket; if discovery is necessary, restrict it to sockets owned by your user and verify the loaded identities. Unlock passphrase-protected keys through an interactive terminal. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Agent availability depends on process environment, not simply whether a private key exists on disk.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distribute team CLIs from a canonical repository with reproducible installation instructions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give shared command-line tools a canonical source repository and document installation for each package. Python editable installs and npm link can support local development, while released artifacts should have explicit versions and reproducible build steps. Keep third-party tool documentation distinguishable from code maintained by your team. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Informal copying creates uncertainty about which version colleagues are running. Testing the documented installation from a clean checkout catches missing dependencies and assumptions inherited from the original development machine.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Ship CLI updates from a canonical source and verify the distributed artifact
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A CLI update is complete only when the distributed source, documentation, defaults, and installable artifact agree. Prefer one canonical repository; if separate development and distribution trees are unavoidable, synchronize reviewed changes and inspect the resulting diff. Keep user configuration separate from package defaults. Exclude caches, repository metadata, and generated archives from release bundles. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Editable installs can hide packaging mistakes because they run directly from a working tree. A clean installation of the release artifact verifies what another developer will actually receive.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Unlock credential stores through trusted local interfaces, never through chat
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Never request or paste a vault master password into a chat conversation. Have the operator unlock the vault through its trusted interactive prompt, or use a supported noninteractive credential mechanism scoped to the operation. Keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. Avoid command-line arguments that expose secret values through shell history or process listings, and suppress secret-bearing diagnostic output. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A convenient workaround can turn a credential protecting many accounts into a retained conversation artifact. Environment variables may help automation, but they still require careful scoping and are not a substitute for secure storage.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bound unattended CLI runs and detect hidden interactive credential prompts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When an unattended CLI appears hung, check whether a credential backend is waiting for interactive input. Diagnostic output may include a getpass warning or an encrypted-keyring password prompt even when another credential source is configured. Reproduce in the foreground, use a hard ceiling such as `timeout 180`, and close stdin with `< /dev/null` when the tool supports noninteractive failure. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A running process with no output can look like slow network work while actually waiting forever for a terminal. Closing stdin may cause failure rather than successful authentication, so inspect the exit status and configure the supported credential path. Keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Design analytics CLIs around compact output, scoped access and reproducible queries
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An analytics CLI should default to compact summaries and write large result sets to files to avoid overwhelming its consumer. Define the supported reporting scope, pagination, filtering and export formats before adding broad API coverage. Discover accessible properties through supported administrative APIs where appropriate, with explicit overrides for ambiguous mappings. Grant only the necessary reporting access in your own account and prefer short-lived authentication where available. Keep secrets in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Large raw responses can exhaust an agent's context while hiding the useful answer. A bounded interface improves inspectability, and durable credentials should not be chosen merely because they avoid refresh-token setup work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reuse proven CLI infrastructure while keeping service-specific assumptions explicit
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A new API CLI can reuse a proven command architecture without copying its predecessor's domain assumptions. Identify reusable responsibilities such as configuration, authentication, redaction, retries, audit logging, output formatting and error codes. Keep the service adapter separate from command parsing and user-facing output. Review which retry rules are safe for each operation, which permissions are necessary and how pagination differs. Document installation and authentication using generic examples. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A mature sibling tool is valuable because it exposes operational concerns a greenfield implementation might miss. Copying it wholesale can also import stale hosts, excessive privileges and inappropriate cache behavior, so reuse should begin with boundaries and contracts rather than an inventory of private packages.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distinguish OAuth client approval failures from unavailable API functionality
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An OAuth consent failure can block an otherwise supported API operation. If a generic CLI OAuth client cannot request an analytics-management scope, inspect the scope, consent configuration, organizational policy, and client eligibility before concluding that the API lacks the operation. A dedicated OAuth client may require additional configuration or approval. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Manual administration can be a reasonable temporary fallback for infrequent grants. Keep that limitation explicit, and store downloaded credentials in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve each agent's transcript from its returned identifier before checking provenance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Capture the identifier returned when an agent starts and use it to locate that agent's execution transcript. Prefer a documented transcript reference or runtime lookup over assuming a fixed directory layout. If an output reference is a symlink, resolve its target and confirm that the transcript belongs to the intended run before parsing metadata. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Checking the wrong transcript can produce a convincing but invalid verdict. Explicit run-to-transcript mapping makes provenance checks repeatable across machines and runtime versions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Capture the producer's exit status before truncating command output
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A shell pipeline normally reports the last command's exit status, so successful output truncation does not prove the underlying task succeeded. Piping a Python command through head can report 0 even when argument parsing exits 2. Redirect output to a file, capture the producer's status immediately, then inspect the file. In Bash, pipefail or an immediately captured PIPESTATUS can also expose upstream failures. Check CLI help before guessing flag spelling. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Familiarity with this trap does not prevent repetition. Encode status handling in scripts so a display command cannot turn a failed operation into apparent success.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit an agent's effective configuration before relying on cross-tool behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before introducing another coding tool into a workflow, inventory its effective instructions, hooks, skills, environment inheritance, and workspace permissions. Use a harmless canary to verify which startup behaviors actually execute in unattended mode. Check symlink targets and document-discovery rules rather than assuming installed files are active. Record only nonsecret configuration findings. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Interactive and unattended runs can differ, and a familiar workstation may supply hidden dependencies. A read-only inventory separates missing capability from misconfiguration and makes later handoffs reproducible without exposing account details or copying a private machine's setup.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give unattended coding runs explicit inputs, bounded access, and auditable outputs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An unattended coding run needs an explicit workspace, constrained environment, clear input delivery, and a validated output contract. Verify supported flags for the installed CLI before constructing its invocation. Close unused stdin, capture structured events and stderr separately, and retain the process exit status. After completion, validate the result schema and compare declared changes with the actual workspace diff. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Unbounded environment inheritance can expose secrets, implicit instructions can change the role, and open stdin can leave a job waiting indefinitely. Logs and file audits provide evidence of what happened, but kernel-enforced access controls remain the boundary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bound filesystem searches and preserve the exit status of the command being tested
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Scope filesystem searches to known directories and capture the tested command's exit status before filtering its output. Prefer filename discovery when file contents are unnecessary, and apply a timeout to potentially broad searches. Account for mounted volumes that can expand the search unexpectedly. A pipeline may report only its final command's status; use supported pipeline failure detection or capture individual statuses immediately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A small lookup can become an uncontrolled crawl, and a successful output filter can conceal an earlier failure. Preserving the relevant status keeps routine checks trustworthy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate projects through credentials and explicit targets rather than remembered flags
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use project-scoped tooling when a shared CLI carries unrelated identity or implicit mutation targets. Inspect how the tool selects its project, dataset and credentials before reusing it. Require an explicit target for writes, remove unrelated ambient credentials, and keep secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. Reuse transferable schema and query patterns independently of the original tool. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separation that depends on remembering a flag is fragile. A distinct credential boundary and validated target reduce accidental cross-project writes without requiring every implementation pattern to be reinvented.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use quoted heredocs for literal SQL or search text containing shell metacharacters
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Double-quoted shell strings still execute backtick and dollar-parenthesis substitutions, so literal SQL or search text needs a safer transport. Use a script with a quoted heredoc delimiter, such as python3 <<'PY', and parameterize database queries inside it. Avoid interpolating search needles into shell command strings. Validate query results after correcting a quoting mistake. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A command name intended as data can execute before the database sees the query. Even a harmless help command corrupts the measurement; a mutating command could cause damage. This is an execution boundary, not merely a formatting concern.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Stop the dev-server process tree, then verify that the session left no orphan processes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Killing a dev server's listening child can leave its parent process and shell wrapper running. Prefer the original task handle or inspect the process tree, identify the session-owned parent, stop it, and confirm termination with `ps -o pid -p <pid>`. Before pausing work, inspect development and research processes started by the session. Use portable option forms such as `tail -n 3`, and check command resolution when shell wrappers behave unexpectedly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A freed port proves only that the listener stopped. Explicit lifecycle checks prevent orphan processes from consuming resources or confusing later sessions; ownership checks avoid terminating unrelated work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Diff shared rules before copying and verify review inputs with hashes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Inspect and diff a shared rules file before overwriting it with another copy. Prefer one canonical source; when copies are necessary, verify their bytes at each handoff. Do not treat a truncated directory listing as evidence that a target is absent, and do not hide diagnostic errors during synchronization. Record input hashes when a review begins and invalidate affected findings if those inputs change. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Recently edited does not mean authoritative. Independent copies accumulate unique decisions, and a successful copy command can silently erase them. Hash checks expose mid-review changes that otherwise make a review appear reproducible when it is not.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check output progress before trusting a background task's running status
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After machine sleep or a long interruption, verify a background task's progress through output timestamps, file growth and new artifacts. Compare writes against a recorded start marker and confirm frozen input hashes before resuming work. If the task is stalled, stop it, inspect partial outputs and shared state, then restart from a known checkpoint with a new run marker. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A running status may describe a process handle rather than useful execution. Artifact-based liveness checks help distinguish slow work from abandoned work and reduce the risk of restarting a second writer over incomplete results.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bound optional dependency checks and expose failures clearly
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give optional dependency checks a bounded wait and a visible failure state. Allow unrelated work to continue, and use a fallback only when it preserves the required behavior. Distinguish stopping the caller's wait from terminating the underlying operation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Silent waiting makes a limited dependency failure look like an application-wide freeze. Clear status and validated fallback behavior support diagnosis without masking incorrect results.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve the real Node installation when rebuilding PATH for a clean environment
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A clean-environment build can lose npm when PATH is reconstructed from a Node symlink's directory. On Linux, derive the installation directory with NODE_BIN=$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$(command -v node)")") and check that it actually contains the expected executables before using it. If a shim manager is involved, configure its environment explicitly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An allowlisted environment improves reproducibility only when its tool paths are correct. Read the build's actual exit status and log; filtering for warnings can miss a command-not-found failure entirely.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Capture the test command's exit status before filtering its output
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A shell pipeline can report success from tail or head even when the test command failed. Redirect the test output to a log, save its exit status immediately and inspect the log afterward. In Bash, pipefail can detect pipeline failures, while PIPESTATUS can identify individual command statuses if captured before another command overwrites it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A tidy final screen is not evidence that a gate passed. This small runner mistake can turn a serious accessibility finding into an apparent success and undermine every downstream release decision.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match measurement regions to the layout and launch long jobs with observable completion
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Image measurements must sample the region where content actually appears, and long jobs need an observable lifecycle. A landscape text region at x 6–48%, y 18–82% is unsuitable for every 3:4 portrait. Define regions per composition, such as y 55–92% for lower hero copy or y 30–70% for central labels. Use the execution tool's supported background mechanism and retain a job handle and completion status. When inspecting processes, avoid search patterns that match the inspection command itself. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Incorrect sampling produces convincing numbers for unused pixels. Untracked background work creates equally misleading silence: a healthy job can look stalled when its completion notification was never configured.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Set Linux temporary directories explicitly when running browser tooling under WSL
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Browser tooling under WSL can create malformed working-directory folders when inherited TEMP or TMP values contain Windows paths. Before launching Lighthouse or chrome-launcher, set TMPDIR, TEMP and TMP to an existing writable Linux temporary directory. If malformed folders already exist, inspect them first and remove only verified matches within the intended directory, checking resolved paths before deletion. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A Windows-style path may be interpreted as a relative Linux filename rather than a temporary-directory location. Repeated audits then accumulate browser profiles in the project tree. Pinning the environment prevents the fault instead of repeatedly cleaning up its symptoms.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Invalidate timing measurements that span host sleep and verify resumed work before restarting it
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Host sleep can suspend long-running work without terminating its processes, invalidating timing measurements that span the pause. Investigate using file modification times, system logs, process states and service responses. Gaps in logs and clock corrections after wake can support a suspension diagnosis, but no single signal proves every subsystem is healthy. Verify active work and rerun affected timing, timeout and page-performance checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A process marked running may have made no progress during sleep. Separating execution continuity from measurement validity avoids unnecessary restarts and acceptance of distorted timings.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Isolate Lighthouse temporary profiles when running through WSL
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give Lighthouse a Linux scratch directory and run it outside the repository when mixed Windows and WSL temporary paths produce stray browser profiles. Set TMPDIR, TEMP and TMP explicitly in the launch wrapper. Inspect unexpected directories before deleting them, and use lstat when a dangling lock symlink defeats ordinary file-size inspection. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A Windows-style temporary path can be interpreted as a relative directory name in a Linux process. Putting the correction in the actual command prevents recurrence more reliably than leaving it in a report.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prevent background children from inheriting build locks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A background process can keep a flock lock held after its parent script exits if it inherits the locking file descriptor. For a finite command, use flock -o LOCK cmd so the supervising flock process retains the descriptor while the command does not. Start long-lived servers outside the locked command, or explicitly close the relevant descriptor, such as 9>&-. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A harmless-looking preview server can stall unrelated work long after the build ends. Test cleanup with a nonblocking lock attempt after the finite job exits, and keep work that truly requires serialization inside the supervised command lifetime.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Record the server PID rather than a background shell wrapper
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Backgrounding an entire cd-and-command list can make $! identify a shell wrapper rather than the server that needs cleanup. Prefer (cd "$serve_dir" && exec server) & followed by server_pid=$!, adapting server to the actual executable. Verify the recorded process identity before signaling it, and arrange cleanup with a trap. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Killing a wrapper can leave its child serving a port or holding inherited descriptors. Shell optimization can affect the process tree, so verify behavior in the shell you use. Explicit exec makes the intended replacement clear while retaining failure handling if the directory change fails.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep preview-server lifetimes separate from finite locked jobs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Start persistent preview servers outside a finite build lock and use flock -o for the serialized command. Confirm that child processes do not retain the lock descriptor after the job finishes. A simple diagnostic is to attempt flock -n LOCK true while the server remains alive; success shows the finite job's lock has been released. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Lock ownership follows inherited descriptors, not the conceptual boundary of a build step. Separating server lifetime from serialized work avoids hidden lock retention and makes cleanup easier to reason about when several test jobs share a resource.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Download expiring attachment URLs promptly and verify the resulting file
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Download binary attachments using the complete authorized URL, then verify the saved file's type and size. Notion attachment links can be presigned and expire, commonly after about one hour (as of April 2026; re-check before relying on it). Obtain a fresh link and use curl -fL -o filename.ext with the URL safely quoted. Inspect the result with file and ls -lh. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Missing query parameters or expired authorization can save an error page instead of the intended image or document. Treat signed URLs as temporary credentials and avoid exposing them in logs, shared commands, or documentation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify command-line tool provenance and preview stability before adoption
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before adopting a new infrastructure command-line tool, verify its package origin, installed version, supported commands and relationship to the existing deployment process. Check whether advertised features are available or merely planned, and treat preview releases as provisional. Test read-only operations first and retain a working deployment path. Store authentication material in protected secret storage. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A familiar-looking package name does not establish authenticity or feature compatibility. Verifying concrete behavior before migration reduces disruption and makes rollback practical.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use direct HTML retrieval as a fallback for document verification
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a document connector fails, retrieve the public page directly and check the response before extracting text. Use an HTML parser to remove scripts and styles while preserving headings and paragraph boundaries. Find relevant terms, read the surrounding explanation and record the source URL with supporting passages. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A connector failure need not force reliance on a generated summary. Direct retrieval offers another review path, but access restrictions still apply and a keyword match alone does not support a claim.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep configuration values out of shell command strings and secrets out of process arguments
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Interpolating writable configuration into a shell command can turn a deployment operation into arbitrary command execution. Use execFileSync with a trusted executable and an explicit argument array instead of shell-evaluated template strings. Parse environment files with dotenv.parse and pass values through the child environment, not argv. Validate project identifiers and resolve filesystem paths before checking containment within an allowed root. Store secrets in your own key file / the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shell quoting, environment-file syntax and path traversal are separate failure modes. Removing the shell eliminates one boundary hazard; identifier validation, path checks and secret handling address the others.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify the active project before every CLI mutation and after context switches
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A CLI with persistent project context requires explicit target verification before mutations. At session start, select your project and run the tool's identity or configuration inspection command. Check the project identifier, environment and a plausible resource count. Repeat after switching contexts, and restore or clear the active target using a supported operation before ending the session. Prefer explicit project arguments in automation when available. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Persistent defaults can outlive both the terminal session and the operator's attention. A successful command against the wrong project may be harder to detect than a failed command, making target verification part of correctness.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify skill discovery through the running tool instead of inferring it from directory existence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Confirm an extension or skill installation by checking the tool's discovered inventory after loading it. Claude Code used ~/.claude/skills/<name>/ for personal skills and ~/.claude/commands/<name>.md for custom commands (as of May 2026; re-check before relying on it). A missing directory does not prove the location is unsupported; consult the current discovery rules and create the expected structure when appropriate. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Files can exist without being discovered because of naming, structure, scope, or session-loading behavior. Observing the running tool's inventory tests the outcome that matters and avoids turning a filesystem assumption into a misleading installation success claim.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Pin the browser runtime version and verify its bootstrap API against the release actually shipped
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Bootstrap a browser Python runtime with an explicit asset base URL, checked loader availability and captured output streams. Load the pinned loader script, verify that loadPyodide is callable, then supply indexURL and supported stdout and stderr callbacks. Verify execution-option names against that release rather than passing speculative keys. A Pyodide 0.26.4 recipe used filename and globals with runPythonAsync (as of July 2026; re-check before relying on it). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Runtime assets, API options and origin restrictions are foundational dependencies. Test file-origin behavior, CDN CORS and Worker support in the target browser; serve through localhost when local-file restrictions interfere. A successful local-file fetch does not establish offline availability.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify credentials through minimal authenticated checks without exposing their values
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Credential validation should report whether authentication and required scope work without displaying the secret. Load credentials through an authorized mechanism from your own key file or the platform's secret store, never from the repo or chat. Use a minimal read-only request against the intended service and redact request headers, logs and error output. If a tool boundary denies secret access, stop that approach rather than rerouting around it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Comparing secret strings answers a narrower question than testing their intended capability. A no-echo validation path can establish usability while reducing unnecessary exposure; the authenticated process still handles secret material and must be protected accordingly.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: After moving a project, verify that its tools resolve assets from the new canonical location
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A project migration is incomplete until build scripts and asset references stop depending on the old location. Search configuration and tooling for absolute paths, replace them with project-relative resolution or explicit configuration where practical, and run the migrated tooling independently. Record intentional changes so a copied archive remains distinguishable from an actively maintained project. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Files can appear successfully relocated while builds still read stale assets from the previous directory. Verifying dependency resolution prevents later deletion or modification of the old tree from unexpectedly changing the new project's output.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Migrate credentials by document structure without displaying secret values
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Parse credential notes by section heading and field name rather than line number. Validate that required sections and fields exist before writing anything. Store secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. Use umask 077, directory permissions 0700 and file permissions 0600; report field names and success states only. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Structural parsing survives ordinary document edits. Restrictive permissions and silent handling reduce accidental exposure during migration, while explicit validation prevents a missing field from silently producing an unusable configuration.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Share environment isolation and project guards across deployment wrappers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Put environment allowlists, project-directory checks and credential loading in one shared wrapper core. Start child commands with env -i, restore only required variables, then load credentials for the intended account. Prefer the project's installed CLI and explicitly pin any fallback version. Refuse execution outside the configured project root unless a deliberate override is supplied. Store secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Thin wrappers reduce duplicated security logic and prevent one tool from drifting into a different account or inheriting unrelated credentials.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make credential synchronization atomic, repeatable and silent
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Implement credential migration as a repeatable one-way synchronization command with atomic writes. Parse named sections and fields, validate completeness, create a temporary file with mode 0600 and replace the destination atomically; keep its directory at 0700. Report only states such as present, changed or unchanged. Store secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Rotation is a recurring operation, so an improvised parser invites inconsistent handling. A named command preserves the same protections each time and avoids partially written credentials if the process fails.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make parsers tolerant of reasonable headings and compare normalized credential values
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Normalize parsed values before comparing credential files produced by different writers. Quoting or whitespace differences can trigger a changed flag even when the credential itself is unchanged. For human-authored notes, prefer exact heading matches, then allow a unique case-insensitive prefix match; reject ambiguous matches. Store secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A tool should accommodate reasonable document edits without silently selecting the wrong section. Unexpected change reports deserve a safe identity check, not dismissal; successful authentication supports usability but does not by itself prove that two credential values are identical.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prevent unattended CLI jobs from hanging on interactive credential prompts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Make unattended CLI jobs explicitly non-interactive and verify which mechanism actually prevents prompting. Redirect stdin from /dev/null where appropriate, set a bounded timeout and inspect logs for successful authentication and useful output. A keyring backend environment variable may not affect a CLI running in an isolated environment; test the effective process rather than assuming inheritance. Store secrets in your own key file or the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A warning followed by successful execution differs from a stalled password prompt. EOF may cause a tool to fall back or fail, so confirm its behaviour and treat missing output as failure regardless of reassuring startup messages.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make offline operation an explicit and verifiable configuration
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define offline behavior before initializing dependencies. Require needed assets to be available locally, disable automatic downloads through supported settings and report missing assets clearly. Verify the workflow with network access unavailable. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Hidden downloads can contradict an offline promise. Explicit configuration and a disconnected test provide stronger evidence than assumptions about cached files.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve runtime symlinks before constructing a minimal CI environment
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Resolving the Node executable's symlink can prevent a minimal build environment from finding Node but missing npm. On systems supporting readlink -f, derive the real executable directory rather than using only the directory returned by command -v node. Clone the intended branch into a fresh scratch directory, construct a minimal PATH, supply required CI variables, and run npm clean-install followed by the build. Use an explicit path for your own key file when needed; secrets belong there or in the platform's secret store, never in the repo or chat. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shell shims and inherited environment variables can hide dependencies. Capture a command after it actually succeeds rather than reconstructing it later from memory.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inspect protected HTTP responses without exposing cookies or credentials
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Protected-host probes should emit only allowlisted response metadata and never expose authentication cookies. Keep service-token headers in your own key file with mode 0600 outside the repository, never in command arguments or chat. If raw headers must be captured, use a protected temporary file and guarantee deletion with a trap or finally block. A curl probe can use -s -o /dev/null -D with that file; filter named headers before displaying anything and redact redirect queries. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Header dumps commonly contain session cookies. Combining HEAD requests with output files can also place sensitive headers where a script expects harmless body content.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make generated review reports readable and subject their own prose to validation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Generated review reports should group evidence by recognizable page sections and validate their own explanatory text. Aggregate rows under labels such as hero, FAQ, status and metadata while preserving traceability to individual entries. Pass the real site root into checks that require whole-site coverage, and report the actual scope inspected. If a project requires generated numerical claims, ensure report notes do not accidentally introduce manually maintained numbers. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A technically accurate ledger can still waste reviewer attention when every internal key becomes a separate line. Grouping by reader concepts makes omissions easier to notice. Validating the report itself prevents the reporting layer from understating or violating the rules it claims to enforce.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reuse configuration validation together with its integration behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Share validated configuration logic across related tools rather than copying only its central algorithm. Carry over input validation, persistence rules, error handling and relevant tests. Handle absent, single and multiple valid options explicitly without assuming a fixed environment. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reuse preserves earlier fixes only when the surrounding behavior travels with the implementation. Consistent interpretation prevents related applications from treating the same setting differently.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Record explicit configuration choices instead of inferring intent from temporary runtime conditions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Setup should record explicit choices, validate them and provide equivalent options for unattended installation. Reject ambiguous required settings with a clear error, and ensure setup and runtime read the same configuration contract. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Temporary runtime conditions do not reliably express user intent. A shared configuration contract prevents installation and execution from applying different assumptions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Complete a shared-policy migration across every executable entry point
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When centralizing configuration policy, audit commands, setup scripts, utilities and background tasks for competing overrides. Route each entry point through the shared implementation. Define when fallback is allowed and make its use visible. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A validated shared module cannot enforce policy in callers that bypass it. Migration is complete only when all executable paths follow the intended contract.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep configuration parsing consistent with the system that consumes it
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When multiple components consume a configuration file, verify that they interpret supported syntax consistently. Test quoting, comments, encoding errors and malformed input against the authoritative parser. Include required dependencies when copying a parser, and detect incompatible versions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Identical file contents can produce different settings when readers disagree about syntax. Parser compatibility is part of the configuration contract and must survive packaging and updates.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Turn configuration failures into explicit invariants and regression checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Distinguish missing, empty, invalid and explicitly supplied settings. Validate values before starting dependent work, define precedence between configuration sources and make unsupported fallback behavior fail visibly. Convert each discovered failure into a regression check for the underlying rule. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Configuration mistakes can produce plausible output under unintended settings. Testing invariants catches more variants than checking only the syntax involved in an earlier failure.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test initialization with real dependencies to verify that application settings reach the full stack
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify restricted execution modes with the actual dependency stack. Imported libraries may perform initialization outside application guards. Trace unexpected behavior to its source and prefer supported configuration or a dependency fix over a temporary diagnostic shim. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Stubbed tests can miss startup behavior that occurs only in real dependencies. An application setting establishes intent; integration checks establish whether the full stack respects it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate generated evidence before copying it into a review workspace
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Shell output redirection can leave an empty evidence file when the generating script fails. Require a successful exit, non-empty output and expected report structure before copying the file into a review workspace. Prefer generating to a temporary file and promoting it only after validation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An empty file can look like a completed artifact to downstream steps. Fixing the generator later does not repair a copy already consumed by a reviewer, so the publication boundary must reject incomplete evidence immediately.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Gate artifact installation on explicit build success
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Install or publish generated artifacts only after explicitly verifying that their build and proof steps succeeded. Capture the build exit status before another command overwrites it, require any success marker to come from the current run, and validate the expected artifact. Do not infer success from reaching the next shell line. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Printing an exit code does not enforce it, and shell error handling depends on execution context. An explicit build-to-install boundary prevents failed validation from producing apparently approved inputs.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Store reusable test instruments in persistent workspace files
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep reusable test scripts and capture tools in persistent workspace files, reserving temporary storage for regenerable outputs. Temporary directories may be cleared during restarts or maintenance. Save test code, required configuration and reproduction instructions before relying on measurements. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Losing an output is inconvenient; losing the only script that explains how it was produced can undermine an investigation. Persistent test instruments let another developer reproduce results and help interrupted work resume without reconstructing the method.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check for system sleep before treating a timestamp gap as a hung probe
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A large wall-clock gap does not by itself prove that a test process is hung. System sleep can separate log timestamps while the probe has performed little active work; one investigation found only approximately 2.5 minutes of reported process runtime behind an apparent multi-hour wait. Check process activity, timer semantics and suspend history before terminating it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Different clocks and runtime counters handle suspension differently. Timing results that span sleep are unreliable for performance comparison, so rerun those measurements during an uninterrupted session.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Limit concurrent browser work and record the renderer actually used
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] On a memory-constrained machine, run one heavy process at a time and verify the actual WebGL renderer before interpreting browser results. Keep scratch files and captures on persistent disk, and avoid concurrent Chromium instances when memory is tight. A forced hardware code path can still render through SwiftShader; label the code path and renderer separately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Resource exhaustion can interrupt an entire verification run. Mislabelled software captures also create false confidence about hardware rendering, even when the application exercised the intended branch.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check temporary-storage backing before putting browser evidence and build copies there
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify whether temporary storage is RAM-backed before using it for build copies, browser captures or test evidence. On Linux or WSL, inspect the relevant mount and run free -h before launching memory-heavy browser work. Put important scratch artifacts in a confirmed disk-backed directory and serialize heavy processes when available memory is limited. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Temporary storage characteristics vary by machine; a familiar directory name does not establish persistence. Losing disposable build copies is recoverable, but losing comparison baselines and logs can force an expensive verification run to start again.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Avoid line comments that swallow trailing syntax in compact JavaScript
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Do not insert a // comment before closing syntax on a single-line JavaScript statement. Everything after the comment marker on that line becomes comment text, including brackets and parentheses. When patching compact scripts, insert a real newline or use a safely placed block comment, then run a syntax check. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A small explanatory edit can break the verification harness itself. After repairing it, rerun affected checks against the same build so a tooling failure is not confused with a product failure or an untested artifact change.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Long-lived processes can retain inherited flock descriptors and block queued jobs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A server started while a flock descriptor is open can inherit that descriptor and keep queued jobs blocked after the initiating script finishes. Inspect holders with lslocks -o PID,COMMAND,PATH and inspect the process tree before blaming a build that has not started. Restart the responsible server outside the locked section with the lock descriptor closed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The serialization mechanism can become the source of the stall. Restrict locked sections to finite jobs, and close the actual inherited descriptor; 9>&- applies only when descriptor 9 holds the lock.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Backgrounding an entire shell command list can make PID tracking miss the actual server
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] In a construct such as '( cd D && server & echo $! > pid )', the asynchronous job is the command list, so the recorded PID may identify a shell wrapper rather than the intended server. Establish the working directory first and launch the server with deliberate PID and descriptor handling. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Killing the wrapper may leave the server alive, including any inherited lock descriptor. Verify the process tree and lock holder instead of assuming that a saved PID guarantees control of every descendant.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use flock descriptor isolation for finite jobs and launch servers outside the lock
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] For finite commands, 'flock -o LOCK cmd' keeps the lock descriptor out of the executed command while the supervising flock process holds the lock. Launch long-lived servers separately, closing any inherited lock descriptor explicitly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Descriptor inheritance lets a child retain a lock beyond the useful lifetime of the serialized job. This isolation helps prevent that leak, but it does not make a never-ending command finite: running the server itself as the supervised command still keeps the supervisor waiting.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep persistent servers outside locks used for finite heavy jobs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Run finite heavy jobs with flock -o when child processes must not inherit the lock descriptor, and start persistent servers outside that lock. The supervising flock process can hold the lock while its finite command runs without passing the descriptor into descendants. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A server that outlives the intended job can otherwise keep queued work waiting indefinitely. Separating server lifetime from job serialization makes lock ownership easier to understand and diagnose.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check inherited lock descriptors when queued jobs stall
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A persistent server started inside a locked job can inherit the lock descriptor and block subsequent work after the parent task exits. Keep server startup outside heavy-job locks and use flock -o where appropriate to prevent descriptor inheritance. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A queue that appears slow may actually be waiting on an unrelated surviving process. Inspect the lock holder and process lifetime before increasing timeouts or launching additional jobs that will join the same blocked queue.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep long-lived servers outside locks intended for finite heavy jobs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use flock -o for finite heavy jobs when child processes must not inherit the lock descriptor, and start long-lived servers outside that lock scope. A development server launched from a locked job can otherwise keep later work waiting after the apparent parent task has finished. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A lock intended to serialize builds becomes a persistent blockage when its lifetime follows an unrelated background process. Separating server startup from finite jobs makes the resource boundary easier to understand and reduces confusing waits that resemble a deadlock.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use concise action-and-object labels for resource cards
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Write resource-card calls to action as a clear action followed by the content type, such as 'Read guide', 'Download brochure', or 'Watch video'. Keep a shared type-to-label dictionary and use a consistent fallback such as 'View resource'. Omitting unnecessary articles can make dense card grids easier to scan, but retain words needed for natural grammar and clarity. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A predictable label tells readers what will happen before they click and reduces editorial drift between featured cards and library results. Concision is a useful style choice rather than a universal prohibition. Ensure each link also has sufficient context for assistive technology when several cards share identical visible labels.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Localize metadata, formatting, forms and consent alongside page copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Localization should cover the complete user journey rather than only translated paragraphs. Set the document language per locale, publish consistent hreflang relationships for equivalent pages, and align social metadata with the page language. Choose a predictable URL strategy, such as locale subpaths, and use locale-aware date, number and currency formatting. Include navigation, form labels, validation messages and consent controls. Support right-to-left layout when required and have fluent reviewers assess meaning and tone. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Mixed-language error messages and incorrect formatting undermine an otherwise polished translation. Testing complete tasks in each locale also exposes text expansion, missing routes and layout assumptions that sentence-level review will miss.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use precise task language and track wording changes in evaluations
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe a task with the vocabulary that most accurately expresses its intended work. For an ordinary product review, concrete requests such as identifying failure modes may be clearer than dramatic metaphors. When testing wording effects, preserve each prompt version and change one factor at a time. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Ambiguous vocabulary can alter interpretation, but one successful rewording does not establish a routing mechanism. Clear language should improve communication without hiding material intent or changing the task unnoticed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Distinguish implemented, observed, and planned capabilities in public copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Public capability claims should distinguish what exists, what has been tested, and what remains planned. For a bicycle-repair co-op, an installed booking form, a successfully received booking, and a proposed repair-status portal are three different facts. Maintain a current evidence sheet and date-sensitive status checks before publication. Use specific, checkable statements instead of broad assurances. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Plans describe intent, while tests establish only the behavior they exercised. Collapsing those categories can make a polished page promise something visitors cannot use. Honest status language preserves credibility and gives future updates a clear evidentiary basis.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Settle positioning before propagating a tagline across a site
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat a tagline as a positioning decision that must be settled before it becomes shared page copy. For an invented neighbourhood bakery expanding from retail loaves into classes, reassess whether the existing phrase still describes the offering. A holding page can omit an unsettled tagline. Once wording is accepted, update shared lockups, guides, templates and copy checks together. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An inherited slogan can feel authoritative simply because it is embedded in design assets. Resolving the message early prevents stale positioning from spreading into every page and later being mistaken for an immutable brand rule.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose a consistent organizational voice without implying an unsupported team size
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Choose site-wide point of view deliberately and keep factual descriptions of the organization accurate. An invented ceramic studio might use its name or an organizational voice across service pages while stating plainly on About that one maker currently runs it. Record the voice rule in the editorial guide and review phrases that imply a larger team. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A durable voice can reduce future rewrites as an organization changes, but pronouns are not cost-free: readers may infer staffing or capacity. Consistency should support clarity without turning a future ambition into a present-tense claim.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build positioning around demonstrated differences and collect evidence beyond internal experience
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Positioning should connect a meaningful difference to observable evidence rather than treating the builder's experience as market validation. For an invented bicycle-repair co-op, a promise of understandable repairs could be supported by itemized estimates and photographed inspection notes. Ask one optional signup question about the visitor's repair problem to gather outside evidence. Keep future services clearly conditional. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Internal conviction can produce a coherent pitch without proving that strangers need it. A shared theme earns credibility when each page demonstrates it through a different concrete practice. Broad claims about reliability or transparency need examples, and cautious copy still needs enough substance to help someone choose.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Pair cautious capability claims with a concrete evidence-based upgrade plan
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe an unproven capability as an aim or design rule, and specify the test that would justify stronger wording. For an invented tide-pool field guide, distinguish a planned offline identification feature from one demonstrated on a device without connectivity. Record the current sentence, the required evidence and the exact copy change that evidence would unlock. Keep development status visible. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Softer wording need not abandon the central idea. An upgrade map makes caution actionable and prevents future editors from strengthening a claim merely because time has passed or implementation seems nearly complete.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate the first audience, current specialization and possible future applications
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe current specialization separately from the wider applications a system might eventually support. An invented seed library's catalog may initially serve vegetable growers while its underlying inventory structure could accommodate flowers or trees. State which collections and workflows are supported today; present broader uses as possibilities unless tested and committed. Distinguish the first audience from an exclusive eligibility rule. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A narrow launch audience can improve clarity without defining the system's permanent limits. Conversely, a flexible architecture does not prove readiness for every domain. Clear boundaries prevent both accidental exclusion and unsupported roadmap promises.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Lead product positioning with what people gain, then explain the safeguards
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Product positioning should state the useful capability people gain before listing safeguards or architectural virtues. Explain the task a tool enables, who can use it, and how it fits existing workflows. If interchangeable providers are part of the design, describe the concrete switching behavior and its limits rather than treating provider neutrality as a slogan. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Qualities such as auditability and durability help establish trust, but they may not explain why someone needs the product. Beginning with the user's purpose gives those supporting qualities a clear role and prevents technically accurate copy from remaining abstract.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Allow expressive brand language only where the plain meaning remains clear
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Expressive website copy should preserve a plain, testable meaning after one reading. For an amateur astronomy club, a phrase about discovering the night sky can introduce an observing session, but the same block should explain the equipment, experience level, and booking action. Make each metaphor correspond to a real activity, and keep factual claims within the available evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Personality and precision can reinforce each other. The useful test is whether a stranger can explain the offer without borrowing its metaphor; otherwise, decorative language is consuming attention that the reader needs for comprehension.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Support bold positioning with visible proof and an audience the product can currently serve
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A strong positioning claim needs observable proof and an audience that the current offering can serve. For a bicycle-repair co-op, explain a concrete service outcome, show how it is delivered, and distinguish available repairs from planned workshops. Evaluate alternative leads against comprehension, evidence, and support capacity. If the headline's proof cannot be shown, choose a narrower claim that can. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Ambitious positioning creates expectations about availability and assistance as well as capability. Connecting the lead to demonstrated behavior prevents a persuasive theme from promising an experience that the operation cannot yet provide.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Cold-test headlines without the context that makes them obvious to their author
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test headlines and taglines with readers who have not seen the strategy document. Show only the intended page fragment and ask what is offered, who it serves, and what each ambiguous term means. For a seed library, check whether 'share next season' communicates seed borrowing or sounds like a calendar feature. Prefer one coherent image family and a concrete description of the service. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Authors interpret shorthand through background knowledge that strangers do not have. A favorite line can fail because its metaphor suggests the wrong action, even when the underlying strategy is sound.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Lead with a recognizable problem solved rather than a list of common category attributes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Website openings should foreground a concrete benefit that readers recognize as solving a problem. For a tide-pool field guide, distinguishing 'not surveyed' from 'surveyed with no sightings' communicates a useful trust behavior more clearly than calling the guide comprehensive or intelligent. State availability plainly and test whether relationship language implies an endorsement that does not exist. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Familiar category attributes help readers orient themselves, but they seldom explain why this offering matters. One cold reader's reaction is a useful diagnostic rather than a universal verdict; use it to form and test sharper alternatives.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use crisp body copy and reserve brand flourishes for deliberate moments
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep explanatory copy crisp and concentrate expressive language in a few deliberate page moments. Let imagery, color, and naming establish much of the atmosphere; use a short flourish in a hero or closing only when the meaning survives without explanation. Describe integrations or compatibility precisely instead of suggesting partnership through vague relationship language. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers need different things from a memorable opening and a service explanation. Allocating flair deliberately preserves personality while keeping the practical offer easy to understand, and precise relationship wording avoids borrowing credibility from organizations that have not endorsed the work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give pages a clear middle with one or two expressive opening and closing moments
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A useful editorial starting point is one or two expressive moments per page, with clear explanatory writing between them. For a ceramic studio, a sensory opening can establish atmosphere and a warm closing can invite booking; the middle should explain class format, materials, accessibility, and what participants take home. Let the homepage describe the whole offering while individual pages carry service-specific detail. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A strong opening and close can make a page memorable without forcing readers to decode every paragraph. Treat the count as an adjustable design constraint, then check comprehension rather than enforcing it mechanically.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Put the strongest useful claim in the headline instead of burying it in supporting text
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A page's headline should carry its strongest supported, reader-relevant hook. If a neighbourhood bakery explains allergen handling clearly in the body, test whether that practical distinction deserves more prominence than a generic promise of exceptional baking. Pair any decorative heading with a concrete explanation in the same visual block. State availability clearly without repeating defensive status language throughout the page. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers often scan headings before deciding whether to continue. A distinctive fact hidden in supporting prose cannot help that decision, while repeated caveats can obscure both the offer and the actual limitation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Explain the capability added by a tool without claiming unmeasured performance gains
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe an enabling tool through the specific task it adds, and reserve performance claims for direct measurements. For an astronomy club's observation planner, explain that it combines a member's equipment list with observing notes rather than claiming it makes observations scientifically better. Distinguish demonstrated behavior from planned integrations and exploratory ideas. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A tool can extend what a user can accomplish without improving the underlying engine's measured quality. Naming the added capability creates a strong, bounded claim; borrowing results from unrelated studies would make the website sound more certain than its own evidence allows.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A technically distinctive feature is not automatically a useful headline
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Select headline claims for reader relevance as well as technical distinctiveness. Translate an implementation property into the consequence people experience, then test whether that consequence belongs in the lead or in supporting detail. Replace insider phrases such as 'shipped layer' with a direct description of what stays intact or changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Evidence tables can make an engineering achievement look like the obvious centerpiece even when readers consider it basic hygiene. A claim can be true, unusual, and still fail to explain the offering's main value; message hierarchy needs comprehension and task relevance alongside proof.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use architecture descriptions to orient technical readers without mistaking them for differentiation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Familiar architecture belongs in a 'what it is' explanation when it helps readers understand integration and operation. Explain components by function: a full-text index finds exact words, a vector index supports similarity search, and typed links represent relationships. State only the components verified in the implementation and approved for disclosure. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Technical readers need a recognizable shape before evaluating unusual behavior. Naming common components can provide that orientation, but common architecture alone does not establish a distinctive benefit; the lead still needs to explain the useful experience the implementation delivers.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check message hierarchy against the central product experience, not only isolated differentiators
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Website message hierarchy should reflect the central product experience while accurately separating internal use, public availability, and optional features. Ask whether an unusual supporting behavior has displaced the main reason someone would use the offering. Describe an internally working version as such without implying that it is publicly released, and keep optional additions visibly optional. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Review systems can overvalue whichever claim is easiest to distinguish from competitors. That can produce technically defensible copy that misses the offering's identity. Evidence checks and product understanding need to work together rather than compete for control of the lead.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate general availability notices from limitations that qualify a specific claim
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A general status notice can be centralized, but a limitation must remain beside the claim it qualifies. Use present tense for verified current behavior, 'is being built' for active development, and 'planned' or 'could' for future work. Place availability where readers can find it before acting, and preserve status context in standalone surfaces such as search descriptions and social cards. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeating status labels can clutter a page, but moving a crucial qualification to the footer can mislead. Consistent tense reduces repetition; it cannot replace an explicit explanation of an exception that changes what a headline means.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Scope approval and dependency claims precisely instead of using blanket statements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Product copy should specify installation dependencies, automatic behavior and which actions require approval. Verify automatic updates, learning, and maintenance separately before making broad claims. In an invented seed-library catalog, copy could explain that inventory totals refresh automatically, publishing new seed listings requires approval, and installation requires a database. Use a consistent image family and a headline grounded in a recognizable user problem. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Absolute safety language can hide meaningful differences between routine changes and gated actions. Precise scope helps readers understand what they can install, what it does automatically, and where they retain control.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Explain distinct collaboration models before choosing a metaphor for them
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe what each collaborator contributes before naming a partnership model. For an invented ceramic studio, distinguish hosting another maker's workshop from incorporating that maker's techniques into an existing class. Give each arrangement a concrete description, then test whether a shared label helps readers understand both. Compare optional taglines only after clarifying the offer. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A vague label can obscure reciprocal responsibilities or imply a purchase where joint creation is intended. Concrete descriptions help readers understand the offer without decoding a metaphor.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recheck explanatory copy when the underlying mechanism changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Revalidate public explanations whenever implementation changes the way a feature behaves. Compare each affected sentence with the new mechanism and distinguish design approval from deployed, observed behavior. For an invented astronomy club's observation archive, a separate panel of suggested identifications should be described as labeled suggestions beside confirmed observations, rather than as lower-ranked confirmed entries. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Old wording can remain superficially plausible while teaching the wrong mental model. A focused sentence-level review preserves accurate expectations and prevents planned behavior from acquiring the apparent certainty of a verified release.
