memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose precise feature verbs and consent wording that remains accurate over time
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Public copy should name the actual output of a feature and the actual scope of a subscription. For an invented tide-pool field guide, distinguish retrieving matching identification notes from generating a new identification. Describe newsletter topics accurately across the intended lifecycle; do not silently broaden a release-only subscription into general marketing. Check final copy against implemented behavior and the subscription promise. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Broad verbs invite readers to imagine capabilities that do not exist. Lifecycle-aware language avoids premature staleness, but durability must come from a clear initial promise rather than later reinterpretation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Write for the audience's existing capabilities and scope claims precisely
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Position a service around the intended audience's actual starting point and describe benefits with technically accurate terms. An invented bicycle-repair co-op addressing experienced riders should explain what its shared workshop adds rather than imply those riders lack basic tools. Distinguish open formats from ordinary text files, and scope access or network claims to the subsystem they actually describe. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A dramatic problem statement can alienate capable readers when it assumes ignorance. Precise terminology preserves the strongest supportable benefit and avoids absolute claims that optional integrations or different storage formats contradict.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build About pages around evidenced working principles rather than a career inventory
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An About page should connect relevant experience to how the organization works and what visitors can expect. For an invented neighbourhood bakery, explain how documented recipe trials inform consistency, how sourcing decisions shape the menu and how customers can commission work. Use a small amount of background to support those principles, and keep detailed offering proofs on their own pages. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A chronological inventory often makes visitors assemble the meaning themselves. Evidence-backed principles communicate character without inventing virtues, while a clear collaboration section turns that understanding into a practical next step.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Clarify affiliations when adjacent true statements could imply a false relationship
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Public copy should explicitly distinguish separate organisations when proximity could imply shared staff, ownership or services. In an invented example, two independently owned cafes share a coffee supplier; describe that relationship without implying shared ownership, staff or services. Maintain the clarification in a canonical fact registry and inventory every downstream copy. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Individually true sentences can combine into a misleading impression. A short, supported distinction is more useful than expecting readers to infer boundaries, and an actual inventory is more reliable than a remembered count of copies.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Pair credibility with a clear, truthful action visitors can take now
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A persuasive page needs a concrete next step that matches an offer actually available today. For a bicycle-repair co-op, explain whether visitors can book repairs, attend a workshop or only request updates, then align the call to action and FAQ with that scope. Confirm any new service commitment before publishing it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers may trust an organisation yet still leave because they cannot tell what to ask for. Fresh-reader feedback can expose this gap, but it should inform an authorized business decision rather than silently expand the offering.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat unverified evidence as a question and distinguish private trials from public availability
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Availability claims should distinguish private testing, limited distribution and public release. If an unverified note appears to contradict an availability claim, treat it as a question: trace its source and ask for confirmation before publishing either version. In an invented seed library, a small volunteer trial may coexist with a public service that has not opened yet. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Broad status language can become false through an overlooked exception. Preserving uncertainty prevents a weak lead from becoming a public assertion while still using it to improve the accuracy of the copy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Document unavailable dependencies separately from unconfigured features
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Capability descriptions should distinguish a configured dependency that is unavailable from a feature that was never configured. Build a behavior matrix covering active, absent and failed dependencies, then use it to check every affected claim and privacy disclosure. Describe fallback work separately from operations that produce no result. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Broad wording such as 'works automatically' can conceal meaningful failure states. Checking source facts as carefully as the final prose prevents repeated review cycles caused by ambiguous briefing material rather than by the writer's interpretation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate canonical display names from navigation styling and machine identifiers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Store canonical display names separately from navigation labels and stable machine identifiers. A bakery site can use title case in prose and breadcrumbs while styling navigation in capitals. Audit array-valued content, forms, generated metadata and machine-readable pages when changing display names; preserve submitted values and URL slugs. Use structural JSON edits and inspect the resulting diff. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reusing navigation text everywhere lets a visual casing choice leak into unrelated contexts. Separate name keys allow consistent presentation without duplicating spelling or breaking identifiers.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match visible cap height when different fonts must appear equally sized
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Match visible letter height rather than CSS font-size when two typefaces need comparable prominence. For a display serif and a sans-serif, measure each font's cap height at the same nominal size, then scale the face being adjusted by the reference cap height divided by its own cap height so visible capitals match. Verify the actual font files, weight and rendered text before applying the ratio. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Equal numeric sizes can produce unequal visual scale. Measurement explains why the eye reports a mismatch and supports targeted corrections without enlarging unrelated text throughout the site.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use softly shaped text veils when rectangular backplates disrupt artwork
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When text must sit directly on structured artwork, a rectangular legibility veil can reveal its own edges and interrupt the composition. Try an elliptical or radial veil feathered several rem beyond the words, or a glyph-following text shadow in the surrounding ground color. Verify contrast after the change and inspect at multiple widths. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The easiest background to implement can become an unintended card once rings or wisps cross its boundary. A proposed pixel-edge check should first distinguish accepted and rejected examples; visible background texture can otherwise dominate the measurement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check text-veil structure separately from the artwork beneath it
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Computed styles can verify a text veil's intended form when pixel-edge measurements are confounded by background artwork. Check for an unwanted box background or shadow, confirm the radial or elliptical layer, and measure its feather extent. A transparent stop about 4rem beyond the text box is a candidate bound requiring validation. Recheck text contrast, using 4.5:1 as the stated design target where appropriate. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] In one comparison, accepted and rejected veils had overlapping edge readings of roughly 23–42, so that statistic could not separate them. Structural checks and visual inspection answer different questions; a radial declaration alone does not prove an invisible veil.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe visible imagery plainly and make interaction instructions match the actual controls
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Image descriptions and interaction hints should name what the reader can actually perceive and operate. On an amateur astronomy club's abstract diagram, call a glowing control a light if it does not resemble a literal star. Describe share-card artwork without inserting promotional claims. Explain pointer, keyboard and touch behavior separately when they differ, including how a selection is held and cleared. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Familiar metaphors become misleading when the drawing or interaction changes. Precise nouns and short action instructions reduce the reader's need to experiment. Verify the wording against the implemented behavior on a preview, especially focus access, Escape handling and repeated taps.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Centralize resource labels and action verbs in one card presentation mapping
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Map each resource type to a display label and an action that accurately describes its destination. Keep related metadata together near the card view-model helper: video maps to Video and Watch the video, podcast to Podcast and Listen to the podcast, and a downloadable brochure to Brochure and Download the brochure. Provide a neutral Resource and View the resource fallback. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Centralized metadata prevents inconsistent wording across cards and avoids parallel dictionaries drifting apart. Choose verbs from actual behavior: a page that merely describes a file should not promise an immediate download, and unfamiliar content types still need intelligible actions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Map messaging strategy to concrete page elements and verify every proof point
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Connect each layer of a messaging framework to a specific website responsibility. Map the core narrative to hero copy, value themes to supporting sections, audience segments to relevant landing pages, format guidance to content templates, proof points to evidence, and language rules to editorial checks. For a bicycle-repair co-op, claims about turnaround or repair coverage should link back to verified service information. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This mapping prevents attractive pages from drifting away from the underlying offer. It also exposes unsupported statistics and inconsistent vocabulary before publication, making strategy review a practical content check rather than an abstract branding exercise.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make editorial exceptions narrow, explicit and testable
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An approved phrase that conflicts with a general writing rule should receive a narrowly scoped exception rather than disabling the rule globally. Record the exact phrase, permitted location and allowed occurrence count. Configure linting around that exception and keep surrounding copy subject to the normal standard. For example, a seed library might preserve a distinctive slogan once while avoiding repeated metaphor elsewhere. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] General lint rules cannot resolve every editorial decision. An explicit exception preserves intentional language without allowing one approved phrase to become permission for repetitive or vague writing across the site.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate audience needs by page while keeping the main offering easy to find
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give the homepage a clear primary task and route secondary audiences to dedicated pages. A bicycle-repair co-op could foreground repair booking and opening hours while placing its history, volunteer program and partnership information on an accessible About page. Keep those routes visible without making every audience compete for the hero section. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A site can serve several audiences without addressing all of them in every paragraph. Clear page roles reduce mixed messages and let visitors find supporting context without obscuring the service that brought them to the site.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep planned features clearly separate from available capabilities
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Present an unfinished feature as planned or experimental, with its current limitations, rather than giving it the prominence of an available offering. A neighbourhood bakery considering delivery could include a brief future-service note without placing delivery ordering in the primary navigation. Avoid names that conflict with existing services, and disclose material prerequisites before anyone commits to using the feature. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Navigation placement and naming communicate availability even when body copy contains caveats. Keeping speculative features subordinate preserves a clear account of what visitors can use today and avoids promises created accidentally by presentation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve conflicting writing instructions in a short precedence document before drafting
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A writing workflow should declare which instructions take precedence when brand, technical and editorial rules conflict. Record scoped decisions for terminology, spelling, voice, punctuation and approved exceptions in a compact document loaded before drafting. Preserve necessary technical terms when a broad banned-word rule would make the text inaccurate. Apply the same precedence during review and linting. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Without explicit conflict resolution, each page becomes a new argument about the rules. A stable precedence document reduces inconsistent corrections while keeping factual accuracy and the intended audience ahead of mechanical stylistic preferences.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give writers a focused evidence-led brief and reviewers a broader checking guide
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A writer's input pack should establish instruction precedence, audience, voice, page purpose and verified claims before supplying an exemplar. Keep the drafting pack focused, while giving reviewers the broader accuracy and acceptance guidance needed to challenge the result. Include all public text surfaces in the content plan: forms, error pages, alternative text, metadata and machine-readable descriptions as well as main page prose. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] More instructions do not automatically produce better writing. A coherent brief supports composition, while a separate review lens catches omissions without forcing every drafting decision through an oversized checklist.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Propagate factual corrections across every public representation of a claim
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A correction to a public claim should trigger a sweep of every surface that repeats or derives from it. Check body copy, FAQ markup, metadata, social previews and related pages. Maintain a site-wide evidence register so prominent claims use appropriate proof without repeatedly presenting the same example as independent evidence. Review placement again after rewrites, because accurate sentences can become misleading in a new context. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Correcting one paragraph leaves the defect alive if search results or structured data still repeat it. Review should close the whole class of inconsistency, with observable evidence stronger than impressive but uninformative scale claims.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat early positioning as a hypothesis with a specific audience and bounded claims
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Write early positioning as a testable hypothesis rather than established market proof. Choose an initial audience, describe the event that makes them seek help, identify their current workaround and state who the offer does not yet serve. For a ceramic studio, “beginner evening classes with small groups” is more concrete than claiming to transform creativity for everyone. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A narrow starting audience helps a small operation make clear choices without defining its permanent limits. Separate current capabilities, design aims and possible future offers. Where customer evidence is absent, explain the scope of internal evidence and admit limits instead of manufacturing social proof or broad assurances.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give writers a fact digest that distinguishes built, tested and planned capabilities
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build a public-copy fact digest with one claim per entry, a source, a status and a verification state. Distinguish implemented behaviour from behaviour exercised in realistic conditions, and separate both from planned or exploratory work. For a seed library, “reservation form built” should not become “members reliably reserve seeds” before the complete workflow is tested. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Writers cannot preserve caveats they never receive. Put material limits beside the facts they qualify, exclude private information before drafting and derive changing counts from their authoritative source. A concise digest reduces accidental promises and makes later copy reviews traceable to evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give cautious claims an explicit evidence threshold for future strengthening
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Pair every intentionally limited claim with a defined test that could justify stronger wording. For a tide-pool field guide, a claim that identification aids are designed for beginners could require novice field trials before becoming a claim about demonstrated identification accuracy. Specify participants, task conditions, success criteria, failures and the evidence to retain. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Cautious wording can become permanent through neglect if nobody records what proof is missing. An independent evaluator and an unstaged task reduce the risk of rehearsed demonstrations. Update all affected pages together after the test, and scope the new wording to the sample and conditions actually observed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Turn broad superiority claims into specific, demonstrated user benefits
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Product copy should explain the user, the task, and the demonstrated improvement before claiming superiority. For a seed-library website, describe whether visitors can find available seeds, understand borrowing rules, and reserve a collection slot. If setup is described as easy, identify the steps and prerequisites that actually exist. Keep planned conveniences visibly separate from available behavior. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Enthusiasm often compresses several unproven assumptions into phrases such as 'better for everyone' or 'no expertise required.' Concrete tasks make the promise understandable to strangers and expose the evidence needed to support a stronger claim.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe a specific difference without denying familiar foundations
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Explain a product's distinctive behavior while acknowledging the familiar category it belongs to. A bicycle-repair co-op might use an ordinary booking system but distinguish its service through a documented repair assessment and clear follow-up advice. Lead with that observable difference rather than asserting that nothing comparable exists. Separate the enduring service principle from the tools or suppliers currently used to deliver it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Honest category language helps readers orient themselves. Specific differences are easier to verify and maintain than sweeping novelty claims, and they remain meaningful when implementation choices change.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review copy through ordinary reader meanings, not internal definitions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check what a sentence implies to an unfamiliar reader, even when its words match an internal fact sheet. Separate permanent design boundaries from unfinished features, distinguish built from publicly available, and avoid extending one offering's capabilities to an entire organization. Established technical terms should retain their ordinary meanings. In a claim ledger, describe the proposition communicated by the copy rather than restating its evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Internal vocabulary can make inaccurate wording feel natural. An independent reader can catch category confusion, availability implications, and ambiguous failure language that a technically complete ledger misses.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use cold-reader belief tests to detect misleading implications
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Ask a reader who sees only the draft page to list what they believe it promises, then compare those beliefs with verified facts. Mark explicit statements separately from inferences. On a ceramic studio site, readers might infer that all classes are available now because several descriptions use present tense, even when enrollment is still planned. Investigate whether the misunderstanding originates in the copy or its source brief. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fact-aware reviewers can unconsciously supply missing context. A cold reader reveals implications created by tense, neighboring sections, unequal proof, and repetition. Sometimes the correct repair belongs in the underlying facts rather than another round of wording.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: State service scope and evidence boundaries explicitly
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Service copy should distinguish integration, customization, and replacement so readers understand what work is offered. For an amateur astronomy club, helping another group embed an observing calendar is different from rebuilding its entire website. Describe the component supplied and the work needed to fit it into the recipient's system. Internal use can support a modest experience claim without exposing private usage counts or participant details. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Vague collaboration language invites incompatible expectations. A precise service boundary connects the offer to a real capability, while restrained proof communicates experience without publishing unnecessary personal information.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Target the audience the current experience can actually support
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Choose the initial audience according to the expertise the current product requires. If installation and operation need technical knowledge, write for capable early adopters and describe beginner-friendly onboarding as future work until it exists. Replace insider shorthand with descriptions a stranger can restate. For a seed-library site, explain 'seed stewards' as people who collect, label, and replenish seeds when that role is unfamiliar. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Audience promises create practical expectations about setup and support. Clear sequencing lets a project serve today's users honestly while pursuing broader accessibility, and plain definitions prevent familiar team language from becoming a barrier.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve overloaded terms before treating a discussion as a decision
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define ambiguous terms before requesting or recording a consequential decision. Words such as 'engine,' 'platform,' and 'integration' can refer to different layers of a system. Restate each plausible meaning in concrete language and check which one the decision concerns. In public copy, distinguish compatibility with another service from an actual partnership or endorsement. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] People can agree enthusiastically while answering different questions. Making the ambiguity explicit preserves the useful parts of the discussion without inventing agreement. Precise relationship language also avoids implying commercial affiliations that the evidence does not establish.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Connect a technical behavior to a verified user benefit
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Explain who benefits from a feature and trace the behavior far enough to verify that benefit. For a tide-pool field guide, 'groups related observations' becomes useful when readers can actually discover those related observations while browsing. Check the full path from generation or processing to storage, retrieval, and display before promising the outcome. Keep limitations beside claims in independently shared excerpts. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A mechanism can run successfully without delivering anything a user encounters. Following the result to its point of use turns technical activity into credible value and exposes missing links that polished feature descriptions can conceal.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Lead with concrete distinctions and test what a stranger actually understands
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Put the most distinctive, verifiable benefit in the headline rather than burying it in supporting copy. Give a cold reader only the proposed text, then ask what works today, what remains planned, and which claims sound vague. Name the specific limits behind any promise of improvement. Consolidate repeated availability notices without obscuring status. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A writer knows the mechanism behind every phrase; a stranger does not. Concrete distinctions such as unavailable search versus an empty result communicate more than broad promises. Repeated qualifications can make honest copy exhausting while leaving its strongest evidence invisible.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Exempt factual disclosures from repetition rules and maintain one canonical wording
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Repeated factual disclosures should use a canonical shared include, even when surrounding copy follows an anti-repetition rule. Review whether editorial constraints force unnecessary paraphrases, multiply status phrases, or combine distinct capabilities into one claim. Correct the rule or source wording before commissioning another rewrite. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A blanket ban on repeated phrases can turn one accurate disclosure into several subtly different promises. Defensive density may be a tooling problem rather than a writer problem. Shared wording preserves meaning and lets reviewers spend attention on substantive claims instead of policing variants.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: When status disclosures move, audit the tense of every dependent claim
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Moving availability notices to a shared section requires a sweep of source facts, reusable includes, and claim wording throughout the site. Distinguish working components, incomplete integrations, and planned capabilities through accurate tense. Check the final input baseline and intended output files after any mid-draft fact changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Removing duplicate status text can improve readability, but it does not remove the obligation to communicate readiness. Old source wording often preserves assumptions from the previous placement rule, allowing polished copy to imply that unfinished features already work.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Explain a general platform through concrete task packages
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Make an abstract platform understandable by showing a few concrete packages of capabilities organized around recognizable work. For a ceramic studio's site, an event-publishing package might combine registration, reminders, and a public calendar, while a catalog package handles collections and availability. Explain which shared services each package uses and clearly label planned capabilities. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Visitors understand a coherent job more readily than an inventory of internal modules. Examples can also clarify what collaboration delivers, provided the illustration does not imply that a proposed package already exists or that its independence has been tested.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use cold readers to test availability, metaphors, and implied responsibility
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Ask cold readers to explain availability, key terms, and who acts on proposed changes using only the copy they would actually see. Probe whether second-person instructions imply a feature is already available, whether competing metaphors conflict, and whether a verb such as proposes leaves the decision-maker unstated. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Memorable wording can still produce the wrong mental model. A bakery's planned ordering service should not describe checkout as though visitors can use it today. Repeated confusion across independent readers is evidence to weigh even when a favorite line remains aesthetically appealing.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test reader beliefs and use precise limits as supporting evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate finished copy by asking a fresh reader what they believe, which statements persuade them, and what remains confusing. Compare those beliefs with the intended claims, especially around availability, data location, external processing, and guarantees. Use specific limits and named mechanisms where broad reassurance would conceal uncertainty. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A skeptical reader may trust a clearly bounded promise more than an ambitious slogan. Belief testing reveals contradictions between individually accurate statements and checks whether the page communicates the right overall picture, rather than merely containing all required disclosures.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Merge copy by known keys and require explicit exceptions for approved text
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A copy merge should reject unknown keys and preserve approved strings unless a specific revision is authorized. Populate pending slots with source provenance; report changes to approved slots as conflicts. Allow necessary exceptions by exact key and show old and proposed wording together. Keep structural fixes moving when they do not depend on unfinished wording, then apply later copy changes through the same controlled path. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Blanket overwrites can erase prior decisions, while blanket locks can obstruct legitimate corrections. Named exceptions preserve the distinction between accidental drift and intentional revision without forcing unrelated engineering work to wait.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review copy in rendered states, where individually true strings can become misleading
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review the complete visible message in each form state rather than approving strings in isolation. Success states may hide the original promise and leave a generic sentence that weakens or changes it. Consent wording must match the particular form, and bot-check errors must describe an action the visitor can actually take. Check whether retention rules allow promised future notifications to occur. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Meaning comes from composition and timing as well as individual sentences. A reusable consent slot can accidentally imply marketing consent on an ordinary contact form, while an automatic deletion deadline can silently contradict an open-ended notification promise.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Focus approval on explicit changes and preserve approved wording by default
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Present amendments to approved copy as an explicit comparison with a default that preserves the existing text. Show each changed passage in full, explain the decision it requires, and distinguish copy approval from implementation verification. Record unresolved dependencies and any consent-version or publication-date updates that follow approval. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Review attention is limited. A focused change report makes consequential revisions visible without requiring someone to rediscover them across an entire document. Preserving the existing version when a proposed amendment is not accepted prevents silence or an ambiguous response from becoming an unintended content change.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Merge approved copy atomically with explicit revisions and preserved originals
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A copy-registry merge should reject changes to approved text unless each revision is explicitly named. Validate the entire input before writing: fill pending slots, leave identical values untouched, and report other differences as conflicts. Provide a narrowly scoped revision option such as --allow-revise, preserve the original approved text in history, and exit nonzero on unresolved conflicts. Write only after the complete merge passes validation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Source-prefix refresh rules can silently bypass approval protection when several writers share a registry. An atomic merge preserves reviewed wording and prevents a partially applied update from becoming the new baseline.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prepare page copy with separate audits of implementation, approved language, and live behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before drafting a complex page, separately audit implementation truth, approved messaging, and live capability status. Assemble a public-safe fact digest, sensitivity classifications, and a denylist, then resolve gaps before writing a slot-based brief. Include figure labels and interactive readouts in the copy scope. Start a multi-page effort with the page whose facts and structure are clearest, and preserve reviewer independence when storing feedback. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These audits catch different failures: describing nonexistent behavior, contradicting approved language, and using present tense for unfinished work. A well-grounded first page also provides a useful example for later pages.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve conflicting source documents before turning facts into prose or diagrams
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build page claims and diagrams from a reconciled public fact register, not from an internal feature catalog. Compare approved strings, later decisions, status labels, unanswered questions, and illustrative documents for contradictions. Record which source supersedes which, and require factual support for every diagram label and readout. Treat internal explainers as research material until their claims pass publication review. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Attractive internal diagrams often contain speculative or sensitive concepts that public facts do not support. Resolving source drift before drafting prevents a polished page from giving unsupported capabilities the apparent authority of an approved visual.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Propagate fact corrections only to verified matching live copies
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Before propagating a canonical fact correction, verify that each target copy still matches the expected previous version. Compare hashes, update matching live copies, and stop for a merge when a target has diverged. Preserve review archives unchanged. Rerun content checks and identify approved strings that need explicit revision because the corrected fact changes their meaning. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Blind copying can overwrite a newer decision while appearing to synchronize documentation. Hash checks protect divergent work, and tracing the correction into downstream copy prevents a truthful fact register from coexisting with an outdated public promise.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Express editorial exceptions as narrow, testable allowances
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Editorial restrictions should allow justified exceptions only in explicitly defined contexts. For example, a ceramic studio might reserve a decorative term for one collection title while excluding it from general sales copy. Store the approved title centrally, permit it only in designated slots, and test both its valid use and a forbidden prose variant. Resolve contradictory source rules before drafting, and synchronize only matching live copies. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A blanket word ban can reject legitimate names, while a broad exemption defeats the rule's purpose. Narrow exceptions preserve intent and make enforcement predictable for writers and reviewers.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: State verified value without turning it into an unsupported uniqueness claim
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe a feature's demonstrated benefit without claiming it is first, only, or unique unless comparative evidence supports that claim. Verify the behavior before adding it to the public fact register, and keep flavor names confined to approved labels when they would obscure ordinary prose. Present unresolved design choices as concrete alternatives with consequences. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A useful capability does not need to be unprecedented to deserve attention. Separating value from uniqueness makes copy easier to defend, while clearly framed choices let reviewers decide without accidentally approving a stronger claim than the evidence warrants.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make a page brief executable with named copy slots and a public-safe fact subset
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define every copy slot in a page brief with an identifier, length budget, evidence source, and revision status. Include navigation text, figure readouts, and shared interface strings. Require one matching section per slot and test the validator with both valid copy and a deliberately broken example. Give the writer only publishable facts, not the full research dossier. Scope duplication checks to finished pages rather than their shared source material. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Slot-level validation turns completeness into a checkable contract. Separating research from authorized publication prevents a true but unapproved detail from becoming an unsupported public sentence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat showcase statistics, process diagrams, and release language as factual claims
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Audit figures and interface microcopy as rigorously as headline claims. Derive showcase counts from reproducible queries, register their scope, and require support for category labels and displayed relationships. Translate internal processing stages into accurate public explanations without inventing capabilities or implying unfinished work has shipped. Keep availability language consistent across status panels, notification forms, and navigation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A cautious paragraph can be undermined by an enthusiastic diagram or a small promise of release news. Internal explainers are useful leads, but their vocabulary, stale stages, and unsupported demonstrations need independent review before publication.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Map each public capability claim to evidence, release status and permitted wording
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain a claim register that connects each public capability to evidence, release status and wording boundaries. Separate built, being built, planned and possible features; distinguish storage support from a working search experience. Use the same supported process order in diagrams and prose. Review navigation labels, consent text and status messages alongside the main page. Define what each generated count measures, including its source table and filtering rules. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Research notes can be richer than the evidence approved for publication. A concise register gives writers a reliable ceiling while exposing the few unresolved questions that need investigation. Small interface strings can otherwise introduce promises the main copy carefully avoids.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve stakeholder intent while verifying terminology, compatibility and visible behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Translate stakeholder requests into verified claims rather than publishing their wording verbatim. Freely readable material is not automatically open source or licensed for reuse. Hardware requirements must reflect supported backends and installers, not a generic memory threshold. Check that each advertised input type reaches a usable result; email support does not imply chat-import support. Once factual questions are settled, review remaining wording in the actual page layout. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Stakeholders usually express the intended benefit, not a complete technical contract. Respecting that intent requires correcting terminology and narrowing unsupported implications. Seeing words with typography, spacing and neighboring sections also resolves ambiguities that another isolated writing round may miss.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use a cold-reader belief test to find false impressions created by individually true sentences
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test the fully rendered page with a fresh reader who sees no internal facts or explanatory notes. Expand all includes and include status messages, limits, captions and consent text. Ask what the service does, what is available now, what requires another service, what seems confusing and what evidence is convincing. Compare the resulting beliefs with supported facts. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Individually accurate sentences can combine into a false impression through omitted context, unclear pronouns or neighboring labels. A fact-informed reviewer may unconsciously supply missing explanations. Cold reading measures the understanding the page actually produces and can reveal that honest limits communicate more clearly than branding or unsupported longevity claims.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate unclear wording from uncomfortable truths when resolving review findings
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Resolve review findings by identifying whether the defect is ambiguity, missing context or an accurate limitation. Use explicit referents and consistent names for the same process. When independent readers identify the same phrase as confusing, prioritize that phrase for revision. Give closure reviewers complete evidence rather than arbitrarily truncated excerpts, and keep unreleased behavior tied to a launch condition. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reviewer may describe a negative impression that faithfully reflects the product's actual limits. Removing that impression would make the page less honest. Preserve the fact while fixing unclear causes, pronouns or scope. Agreement between a cold reader and a fact-informed reviewer is especially useful evidence of a wording problem.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Apply cold-reader comprehension checks to shared messaging as well as individual pages
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Cold-reader checks belong at both the shared-messaging level and the finished-page level. Give an unfamiliar reader only the material visitors will receive, then ask them to describe the offer, limits and expected next action in their own words. Compare those beliefs with the intended meaning, and repeat the check after substantive assembly or revision. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared messaging can spread one ambiguity across many pages, while page-specific context can introduce a new one. Testing both levels catches different failures. The useful result is not whether the reader likes the writing, but whether the writing supports an accurate understanding without private background knowledge.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe user-accessible capabilities separately from mechanisms that exist only in code
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Present-tense capability claims require evidence that the intended user can reach and complete the described action. Distinguish implemented mechanisms, tested workflows, unfinished interfaces and planned features. A backend permission mechanism does not justify saying users can approve requests when no usable approval path exists. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers interpret action verbs as promises about their experience. Unit tests and source inspection can establish narrower properties, but they cannot substitute for an end-to-end acceptance path through installation, interaction and observable results.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Write the strongest claim supported by the evidence, including its tense and scope
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Match each product statement to the scope and maturity demonstrated by its evidence. Use working, being built or planned deliberately; narrow broad terms such as software when a test covered only a supplied knowledge layer. Propagate amendments through active sources and rerun affected checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A smaller, precise claim gives readers something dependable to evaluate. Destination language presented as current functionality creates expectations the implementation cannot meet, while vague nouns can silently expand a modest test into an unsupported guarantee.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review limitation statements for capabilities they accidentally presuppose
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A limitation can imply that an unavailable capability already exists. Read clauses such as “while users work” or “when members book” for assumptions about the current product, even if the main sentence says something is unfinished. Record unresolved implications for independent review alongside mechanical check results. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Word-level validation can pass a sentence whose grammar invents an operating workflow. Treating writer questions as review inputs helps expose these assumptions without mistaking a clean lint report for a complete truth check.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Attach planned status to the unfinished relationship or feature, not an existing component
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A status qualifier must describe the exact thing that remains unfinished. On a ceramic studio's site, “Online class booking, planned” can be accurate when classes already exist but booking is unavailable; “Classes, planned” would misstate the offering. Read every label independently before publishing it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Mechanically adding a status word can create a false claim. Naming the unfinished action or integration preserves the distinction between an existing resource and a future way for visitors to use it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reordering an unordered list can reduce repeated phrasing without changing its meaning
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An order-sensitive repetition check may be satisfied by reordering genuinely unordered items. If a site uses a six-word repetition rule, inspect repeated lists before replacing precise vocabulary with weaker synonyms. Preserve the original order whenever it conveys priority, chronology or dependency, and rerun the check on assembled output. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Lexical variety is not always the best repair for duplication. A harmless change in list order can retain familiar terms, but mechanical compliance should never override meaning or make navigation less predictable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check what a sentence takes for granted, not only what it explicitly asserts
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Presuppositions can overstate product maturity even when the explicit limitation is accurate. For a seed library, “Members cannot yet reserve seeds while managing their online accounts” implies online accounts already work. If both features are planned, state that directly instead of embedding an unavailable workflow in a subordinate clause. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] No prohibited word is needed to create this error. A semantic review must ask what a reader must assume for the sentence to make sense, especially on pages describing unfinished services.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match the page's problem statement to the audience's existing capabilities
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A persuasive problem statement must remain true for its intended audience. An invented ceramic studio offering advanced workshops should not assume visitors lack basic pottery skills; it should explain the specific techniques or facilities the workshops add. Ask fresh readers what they believe, find convincing and still question. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Accurate feature descriptions cannot rescue a premise the audience rejects. When readers already solve the stated problem, revise the positioning or differentiation before polishing individual sentences.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check which actor owns each present-tense verb in a capability claim
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Present-tense verbs must describe behaviour supported for their grammatical subject. On a bicycle-repair co-op's site, “The booking system lets riders reserve a stand” promises a working reservation flow; a stored schedule alone does not support it. Describe the implemented capability directly and identify unfinished user actions as planned. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Writers can cite evidence for infrastructure while the sentence actually promises user activity. Asking who performs each verb exposes this mismatch and prevents a purpose phrase or polished headline from becoming an unintended availability claim.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve essential scope when microcopy must fit a strict length cap
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a capped label needs a factual qualifier, shorten less important wording before removing the qualifier. Check both word and character limits, such as six words and 40 characters, and record any substantive information dropped from a longer readout. Escalate an unresolved conflict between accuracy and fit as an explicit editorial choice. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Scope consumes space, but silently deleting it can widen a claim. Visible tradeoffs let reviewers assess what was lost instead of approving concise wording that promises more than the evidence supports.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure reader understanding separately from reader motivation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Cold-reader review should distinguish accurate understanding from persuasive value. Ask what is available, what remains planned, why the offer matters and what would motivate action. For a neighbourhood bakery, readers may understand a proposed subscription perfectly yet see no advantage over their current shopping routine. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Clearer, more truthful copy can improve comprehension without improving interest. Repeated audience objections suggest a positioning hypothesis to investigate; another wording pass alone may not resolve the missing benefit or comparison.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check the scope of qualifiers and the assumptions hidden in exclusions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Qualifiers such as “only” and exclusions such as “other than” can change a claim even when every individual word is supported. Compare “Only approved services may be reached” with “Requests to this service may go only to its listed address”: one restricts all destinations; the other restricts one request type. Check whether exceptions imply an existing permission. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Word-level matching cannot establish sentence-level truth. Readers follow grammatical scope, so review the complete proposition and its implied exceptions against the intended rule.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Put the main claim in the heading and review it together with the subheading
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A section heading should carry its main claim, while its subheading should clarify rather than redefine that claim. On a seed library website, a heading about creating community collections should not become an apparent offer of ready-made collections when paired with examples below it. Read the heading and subheading together, then read the heading alone. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Skimmers often miss body qualifications. If a line is accurate only after careful interpretation, its placement and surrounding copy can still produce the wrong belief.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give each feature its actual development status in mixed-status descriptions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A short feature list must preserve the status of each feature rather than implying that the whole offering is available. A bicycle-repair co-op might describe repair appointments as available, maintenance classes as being developed, and tool loans as planned. Keep those distinctions in the visible copy and supporting claim records. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Compression easily turns mixed readiness into a false promise. An honest list can establish scope, but a reader test must still determine whether it communicates a useful offer rather than disconnected features.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Terminology changes need repetition checks across all affected text pairs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Standardizing a term can create new repetition across headings, explanations and FAQs. After a terminology pass, rerun comparisons for every affected pair, including unchanged text that now matches a revised sentence. If a project uses a six-word overlap rule, distinguish necessary technical terminology from avoidable repeated phrasing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Consistent naming helps comprehension, while mechanical repetition limits can penalize that same consistency. Resolve the tension through clearer sentence structure or a justified rule exception, rather than substituting ambiguous names.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Name the offering on the first screen and lead with a meaningful distinction
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] The first screen should identify what the offering is and why the intended reader might care. For an amateur astronomy club, poetic language should accompany a clear description such as observing sessions or telescope workshops. Ask unfamiliar readers to identify the category and the most distinctive benefit before showing them the FAQ. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Metaphors and familiar feature lists can leave readers unable to classify the offer. Repeated confusion about category, terminology or unexplained limits deserves a structural fix rather than another decorative sentence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Attach publication constraints to source facts before drafting public copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Public-copy source records should state both what may be said and what identifying or unsupported details must be excluded. For a community workshop website, a fact about teaching experience can permit a general description while excluding private participant details and unpublished results. Check the resulting restrictions across pages, metadata and generated files. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Constraints separated from their facts are easy to lose during drafting. Keeping them together helps writers communicate useful evidence without converting a practice-focused page into a biography or leaking private context.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Ground the reason behind a position before asking a writer to explain it
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A brief should supply evidence for why a position was chosen, not merely require the writer to make it sound thoughtful. Place existing copy where its meaning fits: a broad philosophy may belong under a section heading while the main heading identifies the offering. Freeze the accepted source set for the drafting round. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Without a supported rationale, writers face a choice between empty assertions and invented motives. Clear evidence and suitable placement preserve useful language while allowing the page's structure to serve the reader.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Pair qualities with concrete work that demonstrates them
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Connect each claimed quality on an About page to observable work. An invented ceramic studio could demonstrate care through documented glaze tests or accessible workshop preparation. Make headings identify the subject and meaningful action, with supporting detail immediately below. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Abstract titles can sound impressive while communicating little about the organization. Evidence beside each claim lets readers assess the quality themselves and keeps the page specific and credible.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test credibility and the available offer as separate questions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A cold read should test both whether claims are believable and whether the visitor can take a useful next step. For a bicycle-repair co-op, readers might trust the repair experience yet find no bookable service or available workshop. Ask what they can inspect, use or request today, and compare their answers with actual availability. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Candour may strengthen trust without creating demand. An unclear or unavailable offer is a product or service decision; inventing a stronger promise in copy would conceal the real gap.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test universal connectives against every item they cover
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Phrases such as “either way,” “both” and “neither” must be true for every alternative they connect. A seed library might offer seed donations and borrowing; a closing sentence about returning seeds cannot automatically apply to both. Rewrite the common claim or describe each route separately when their obligations differ. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A connective can silently extend one branch's rule to another while every noun remains supported. Word coverage misses that logical change, so review the complete proposition against each listed option.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check semantic repetition after includes and shared content are expanded
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Read the fully assembled page to detect repeated meaning across headings, subheadings and included text. A position can appear three times even when its reusable block is included only once. Give each neighboring element a distinct job: state the point, explain it or provide evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Slot-level compliance cannot predict the reader's experience of a sequence. Repetition can make an otherwise reasonable position sound defensive, especially when several adjacent sentences open with the same denial or qualification.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Allowed citations must still support the actual claim
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A citation whitelist controls which sources may be used; it does not prove that an allowed source supports a sentence. Check the subject, relationship, scope and tense of each claim against its evidence. If the necessary source is outside the allowed set, narrow the claim or revise the source allowance explicitly. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Restrictive briefs can encourage writers to attach a permitted but irrelevant citation. A populated reference field looks complete while concealing an unsupported proposition, so citation presence and entailment require separate checks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check chronology before turning a list of events into a causal story
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A claim that one set of events led to another must agree with the underlying chronology and evidence of causation. An astronomy club's later outreach projects cannot explain its earlier founding merely because the two appear beside each other in a summary. Correct both the source summary and dependent copy when the connection is unsupported. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Narrative transitions make chronology feel natural even when it is wrong. Copy checks against a flawed summary preserve the mistake unless someone checks the original record.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Phrase-overlap thresholds do not establish that copy is meaningfully distinct
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Passing a fixed phrase-overlap threshold does not prove that two passages avoid repetitive wording or structure. A six-word rule can be defeated by inserting one word while leaving recognizable four-word runs and the same argument intact. Use overlap scans to locate candidates, then compare their meaning and role on the page. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A measurement can reward edits that satisfy its mechanics without improving the reader's experience. The remedy may be a better review criterion or a different purpose for the passage.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Sentence order frames a decision even when the facts stay the same
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Lead with the chosen purpose when explaining a deliberate strategy, then supply the constraints that informed it. A bakery can explain its focus on small seasonal batches before discussing limited oven capacity. Reversing those sentences may make the same decision sound like a reluctant fallback. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers interpret order as emphasis and often infer motive from the opening clause. Source notes preserve facts; their clause order need not dictate the public explanation, provided the rewrite does not invent intent.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check what definite descriptions imply about ownership and available choices
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Phrases such as “one of the planned workshops” imply an identifiable set, not merely a planning status. On a ceramic studio website, that wording could imply selection from the studio's programme when the intended offer is help developing a visitor's own workshop. State whose proposal is involved and distinguish its status from membership in a list. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Articles and possessives carry factual implications. A small grammatical change can alter the offer even when every prominent topic word remains accurate.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve pronouns and possessives again when moving sourced text
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Pronouns and possessives must be rechecked whenever a definition moves into a sentence with different participants. On an astronomy club's equipment page, “the member's mount” may refer to the lender or borrower depending on the surrounding wording. Name the relevant role explicitly when possession affects the arrangement. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Source accuracy does not guarantee contextual clarity. A supporting note may identify the intended possessor correctly while readers attach the phrase to someone else in the published sentence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Credibility does not replace a clear offer readers can act on
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A credible website still needs to state what visitors can obtain today and how to begin. For a seed library, distinguish current borrowing arrangements from a proposed delivery service and explain the next action plainly. Ask unfamiliar readers what they believe is available and whether they would contact the organisation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Evidence and candour can build trust while an ambiguous offer prevents action. Unsupported self-praise and grand comparisons consume attention that could instead clarify eligibility, availability and practical value.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Let the homepage explain roles and route readers to detailed evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A homepage can summarize offerings by purpose while leaving detailed proof to their destination pages. Maintain a simple register showing where major examples and evidence already appear. For a neighbourhood bakery, introduce bread orders, classes and wholesale supply through the needs they serve, then link to specifics. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeating every destination page's strongest passage makes the homepage crowded and the site repetitive. Clear roles help visitors choose a route without stripping availability qualifications from the summary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose homepage sections by visitor needs rather than a fixed template
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Include a homepage section only when it performs a distinct job for visitors. A tide-pool field guide might introduce identification, habitat and responsible observation, then route readers to detailed guides. Add an FAQ only if the page has real unanswered questions; any standalone answer must carry its necessary qualifications. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A template can pressure writers into redundant explanations or invented questions. A deliberate omission often produces a clearer page than filling a slot that has no useful content.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A reader's modal verb does not establish a provider's availability
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] “You could ask” describes a visitor's possible action and does not establish whether a service is available. State the provider's current offer directly, and label planned or unavailable alternatives separately. For a bicycle-repair co-op, distinguish repairs it currently accepts from a proposed tool-lending service. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Applying the same cautious modal to every option can erase important differences. Accurate qualification requires saying what exists now, not merely making every sentence sound less definite.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check what each trailing modifier appears to describe
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Place definitions and modifiers close to their intended subjects, and inspect competing attachments. On a seed library page, a phrase about returning borrowed equipment should clearly modify the equipment arrangement rather than nearby seeds or volunteers. Make the actor the sentence subject or repeat the relevant noun when necessary. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers often attach trailing phrases to nearby plausible nouns, although context also matters. Repairing one ambiguous sentence can introduce another, so reread every new clause rather than only the original problem phrase.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Avoid planting structural repetition through repair instructions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A repair instruction that points to another passage's construction can reproduce its structure even when the words differ. State the intended effect, such as making availability explicit, without prescribing the neighbouring sentence's grammar. Compare subject, action, clause order and ending across both passages. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Four-word overlap checks cannot detect every mirrored construction. Instructions should transfer the useful principle while leaving room for a structure suited to the new section's purpose.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use precise status instead of hedging every option with the same modal
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Uniform hedging can make an available service sound speculative while making an unavailable option sound accessible. Use present-tense offer language for current services and explicit status clauses for planned alternatives. Preserve essential definitions when shortening the answer, and test it without the surrounding page. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Caution is useful only when it matches the facts. Changing tense can improve one distinction, but it cannot by itself communicate every access condition, especially when the answer travels without a status banner.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review repeated fact order even when shared phrases disappear
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Lexical variation does not guarantee that two nearby passages serve different reading purposes. Compare the order of facts and sentence structure after removing shared four-word runs. A short FAQ may lead with the visitor's current need while a longer history section explains how the service developed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers can experience repetition through the same sequence of ideas despite different wording. Changing order should improve emphasis or usefulness, rather than merely adding filler to evade a phrase-matching check.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Change information placement when a rewrite needs a different construction
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A different sentence construction requires reconsidering subject, clause order and emphasis rather than swapping verbs. Place two candidate sentences side by side and label who acts, what information each clause carries and where the sentence ends. Move material according to the section's purpose, then check factual fidelity. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Clean n-gram results can coexist with nearly identical sentence frames. Structural comparison reveals echoes that word-run scripts miss and helps a rewrite become useful in its new context.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate every copy alternative and leave room below a hard word cap
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test proposed alternatives against the same word-count and content checks as the final copy. A 70-word ceiling is easier to maintain when the draft leaves a few words for later editing. Confirm whether the validator counts whitespace tokens, hyphenated terms, or another unit. Restore the chosen version after testing alternatives and compare it with the delivery file. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An unchecked fallback transfers uncertainty to the next reviewer. Small wording changes can exhaust the budget, so validation belongs after the final voice pass as well as before it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A semicolon does not reliably carry an availability restriction into the next clause
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Put an availability restriction inside the clause that describes the possible action. “The seed exchange is not open; members could request packets” can still suggest that requests are accepted now. “If the exchange opens, members could request packets” makes the dependency explicit. Check the reading without the surrounding page. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Keyword checks can confirm that a restriction exists while missing its scope. Readers may connect an unrestricted possibility to an earlier open invitation, recreating the misunderstanding the restriction was meant to prevent.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Put the limit before the possibility and preserve uncertainty the evidence does not settle
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Place a condition before a possible future action when readers could mistake it for a current offer. An invented ceramic studio might write, 'If evening workshops resume, visitors could reserve a place.' Test the sentence with fresh readers without first explaining its intended meaning. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Clause order influences initial interpretation. A reader seeking confirmation may be responding appropriately to an unresolved fact. Clear conditions matter more than eliminating every question through unsupported certainty.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check sentence structure as well as repeated word sequences
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An n-gram check cannot detect all repetitive sentence structures. Two sentences can share no four-word sequence yet both follow “opening modifier, subject, could become, one part of something.” Compare nearby sentences by modifier, subject, verb, and complement when structural variety matters. Apply this review to suggested wording as well as original drafts. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Text supplied by a brief can feel preapproved even when only its vocabulary was tested. Mechanical checks measure their defined pattern, not every form of rhetorical repetition.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Position conditions and timing words so they cover every intended action
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Put conditions and timing words before the actions they must qualify. “Visitors could later borrow field kits or download a survey pack” places both actions in the future more clearly than attaching “later” only to the final item. Use “if” when availability is uncertain; “when” or “once” can imply that it will happen. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Small changes in placement alter the apparent promise. A status sentence elsewhere cannot reliably repair an unrestricted action clause, especially when that clause is quoted alone.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep useful sentence structure when clarity justifies it and document the tradeoff
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate repeated sentence structure by its function, not merely its resemblance. A leading condition may be necessary to prevent a future possibility from sounding available now, even if another sentence also begins with a modifier. Compare the constructions, test alternatives, and explain why the clearest version remains. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Editing solely for variation can weaken meaning. A review that makes no changes can still be valuable when it records the alternatives considered and the concrete clarity or factual constraints that ruled them out.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use near-match scans during drafting when a project enforces cross-page wording limits
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a project rejects repeated six-word sequences, use a five-word near-match scan during drafting to expose fragile wording early. Compare against the approved corpus and keep the strict six-word check as the final gate. Give summary sections distinct roles so that variation comes from useful information rather than arbitrary synonym changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Waiting until the final pass can force hurried rewrites that damage meaning. Near-match scans are drafting aids for an explicit editorial constraint, not a universal requirement for good web copy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use explicit nouns and conjunctions when pronouns or participles blur the intended meaning
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Replace ambiguous pronouns and implied logical relationships with explicit wording. On a tide-pool guide, “Designed for beginners, the guide lacks offline maps” leaves the relationship unclear; “The guide is designed for beginners, though it lacks offline maps” states the concession. Check each “its” against plausible nouns in the preceding sentence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Read-aloud review can catch small semantic stumbles that scanners miss.
