Clear references and conjunctions reduce the work readers must do to infer whether a clause expresses cause, contrast, or qualification.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recheck meaning after small preposition changes in constrained copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A one-preposition substitution can change a sentence’s factual claim. “Built for the community garden” describes an intended destination or use; “built in the community garden” describes a construction location. When repetition rules force a paraphrase, identify what every location or purpose phrase now modifies. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Near-paraphrases feel safe because most words remain unchanged. Mechanical similarity checks do not establish semantic equivalence, so edits made to satisfy wording constraints need a separate reading for literal meaning.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A standalone card needs its purpose even when nearby copy already explains it
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A card that may appear independently must identify what its subject does, not merely offer a fresh technical detail. A bicycle-repair card describing “precision tools and a three-stage process” still needs to say whether it covers wheel alignment or brake servicing. Repeat essential nouns when needed, then vary the supporting facet. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A measurable novelty rule can crowd out an unmeasured clarity requirement. Test the isolated card first so that avoiding repetition does not erase the information that gives the detail meaning.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve modifier attachment when translating page copy into a factual proposition
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A claim ledger must preserve where modifiers attach in the sentence it represents. “A storage cabinet is being built in the studio” says where construction occurs; “A cabinet for storage in the studio is being built” specifies intended use. These are different claims even when they share the same nouns. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reviewer can accidentally repair the sentence while summarizing it, then validate that repaired meaning. Check the original grammar against the source and avoid shifting a location claim onto an activity whose location is unverified.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reread neighboring sentences after a fix because new noun order can change pronoun meaning
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After moving a phrase, check the next sentence for pronouns that may now point to a different noun. A ceramic studio description that ends with “the kiln” can make the following “it” seem to refer to the kiln rather than the studio. Repeat the intended noun or reorder the sentence when necessary. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A local fix changes the context around it. Grammar should make the reference easy to recover, but proximity alone is not a guarantee; test all plausible readings.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Lead standalone cards with the object or outcome before explaining the mechanism
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give a standalone card its object or outcome before adding a distinctive mechanism. For a seed library, “Seeds matched to local growing conditions through volunteer trials” explains the purpose more clearly than “A curated sequence of specialist assessments.” Essential nouns may repeat nearby copy without repeating whole sentences. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Novelty and standalone clarity are separate requirements. Overprotecting against repetition can remove the card’s meaning; restoring the object lets the technical detail become useful instead of merely sounding sophisticated.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test broad promises and problem statements against actual capabilities and reader knowledge
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review headline promises, pain statements, and status labels together against current capabilities. A bicycle co-op should avoid “every repair is impossible without us” when readers know practical alternatives, and “private use” may need clarification if it could mean an invitation-only service. Ask fresh readers when their understanding changes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated confusion points to a problem worth investigating, even when each sentence has prior approval. Broad promises can outrun narrow limitations, while exaggerated problems weaken trust among knowledgeable visitors.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review suggested replacement copy for privacy claims that expand through nearby wording
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A privacy claim can become misleading when adjacent wording extends it from local processing to hosted model use. Review proposed replacement sentences with the same care as published copy: identify the actor, operation, data and destination, then read the sentence alone and beside its neighbours. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Review findings are another source of copy, not an exemption from verification. A technically true statement about building a local index can imply that no passages leave the device during later answering unless its scope is explicit.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Evidence mappings must describe what the page actually says
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A claim ledger cannot supply a relationship that the visible page never states. For each evidence row, compare the proposition with the exact published phrase and check both directions: does the phrase support the proposition, and does the proposition omit anything the phrase implies? [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Review notes can quietly repair missing meaning in the reviewer's head. Readers do not see that repair. Navigation labels and footer context may help, but essential relationships should be stated where readers need them.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Re-read the new claim after fixing a misleading modifier
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Moving a location phrase can fix one ambiguity while falsely placing a hosted service on the reader's machine. After editing, identify exactly which noun or action the modifier now describes. If the evidence explanation must deny the sentence's natural reading, revise the sentence again. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Removing the original defect does not establish that its replacement is true. An elaborate disclaimer in an internal ledger often signals that the writer is defending wording that readers will reasonably misunderstand.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Scan drafts against briefs as well as other pages for borrowed sentence frames
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A six-word overlap scan against briefs and review findings can flag instructional wording that has slipped into published copy. Run it while drafting, inspect matches in context, and retell the underlying facts where the brief's purpose statement has become the sentence. Preserve necessary shared terminology. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] True, fluent instructions are particularly easy to copy without noticing. Comparing only published pages misses this source of repetition. The scan makes a write-from-facts rule observable, while human review prevents ordinary language overlap from becoming an automatic defect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Attach local-operation claims to the component that actually runs locally
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Describe a local workspace separately from the model or service it connects to. Attach location language directly to the component whose execution or storage location is verified, and state hosted or local model options independently when relevant. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Phrases about a model's home or workplace can imply local inference even when only the interface is local. A useful review question is whether the evidence explanation can restate the sentence without disclaiming its natural meaning. If it cannot, repair the public wording.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Scope privacy promises to a verified operation and remove unsupported extensions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Attach a no-send promise to the specific operation for which data movement has been verified. If indexing is local but later requests may send retrieved passages to a hosted service, avoid extending the promise across both operations. Explain downstream transfers wherever that use is offered. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Subtracting an unsupported clause can preserve a useful, accurate summary more reliably than adding every available fact to one sentence. Permission to cite a detail does not make that detail necessary in every summary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Put essential caveats near the claims that create readers' first impressions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A caveat at the bottom of a page may arrive after readers have formed an incorrect belief about availability or privacy. Ask fresh readers what they believe at successive points, including whether an offering is usable now and where processing occurs. Compare those answers with verified facts. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated misunderstandings after sentence-level repairs point toward placement, framing or persistent page chrome. A later correction does not erase the initial impression, and accurate fine print cannot reliably compensate for an expansive headline.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check tense against the meanings a page has already assigned to its nouns
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A sentence can be supported by a fact record yet imply an unsupported feature because the page has narrowed a noun's meaning. For example, a seed library page might define its catalogue as a future shared service, then imply that the service already exists through a later reference to catalogue access. Review nouns and tense across the whole page. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers carry definitions forward. Sentence-level entailment checks miss claims created by those accumulated associations, especially when current features and planned integrations share vocabulary.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use fresh readers across revisions to expose persistent misunderstandings
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use fresh-reader checks across revisions to identify misunderstandings that internal review can overlook. Keep audience assumptions and comprehension questions consistent, and give each reader the page without the team's explanatory history. Compare specific interpretations rather than relying only on general reactions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Familiar reviewers can unconsciously supply missing context. Independent first encounters reveal whether the page communicates on its own. Claim improvement only when comparable observations support it.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test an About page with readers who match its intended audience
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Include fresh-reader comprehension checks when revising an About page, using a consistent intended audience across rounds. Ask readers to explain who provides the service, what is offered and what action they can take, using only the page as evidence. Record misunderstandings and unanswered questions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Authors already know the organization and can overlook missing context. Audience-matched readers help reveal those gaps; comparable observations are needed before claiming a revision improved comprehension.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate replacement claims independently of the defect they were meant to fix
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review a replacement sentence as a new claim, checking its actor, action, location and qualifications against verified behavior. Use a fresh reader when the writer's intent is difficult to separate from the wording. Check both whether the original defect disappeared and whether the revision introduced another misleading implication. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A repair can move ambiguity to a different component. When an internal explanation contradicts the sentence's natural reading, revise the sentence again.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reserve status-bearing verbs so nearby repetition does not blur availability
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reserve a verb that signals unfinished work for that status wherever nearby repetition could weaken its meaning. Read the entire section as one paragraph, then count competing uses of the same verb. Give the maker a different verb and state a planned capability once. Add a targeted check for repeated status verbs across adjacent clauses. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Individually clear sentences can become muddy together. Section-level review preserves the distinction between something available now and something still being developed, without adding louder disclaimers.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recheck pronoun references whenever nearby nouns change
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Changing or reordering a noun requires reviewing the pronouns that follow it. Moving a plural noun nearer to “it” can reduce one source of ambiguity, but does not eliminate other singular candidates. Check subject continuity and meaning as well as proximity. When a relative clause could attach to the wrong noun, use an explicit phrase such as “a capability that is planned.” [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Small edits can silently change what a reader thinks a sentence refers to. Word order is economical, but explicit nouns are preferable when the intended reference remains uncertain.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give each page section a distinct job instead of repeating every product fact
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A short introductory card should state the essential category and status without repeating context already established nearby. On a seed-library site, a card might explain what a reservation service does while the surrounding section explains where collection happens. Retain necessary terminology even when a similarity checker notices a short overlap. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repetition can make a page feel padded and obscure the card's purpose. Changing accurate language merely to evade a word-count threshold improves the score while weakening the writing; review the overlap's function instead.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Change a duplicated sentence frame rather than swapping its main verb
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Rewrite a near-duplicate by changing its grammatical structure while preserving the supported claim and its status. For a bicycle-repair co-op, replace a repeated inventory-style promise with a sentence explaining the practical relationship between booking, tools and workshop access. Check the following sentence again if it contains a pronoun. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Substituting “gather” for “hold” leaves the same frame intact. Asking what the sentence must explain opens a different construction, but structural improvements can also create new antecedents that need review.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Explain pronoun clarity using meaning and salience, not number alone
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Pronoun review must consider grammatical number, subject continuity, semantic fit and nearby discourse together. Ending the preceding sentence with a plural noun does not remove a singular mass noun elsewhere in that sentence. Record why the intended referent remains strongest, and repeat the noun if competing interpretations remain plausible. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A correct conclusion supported by the wrong explanation is fragile. Later editors may preserve the supposed safeguard while changing the actual cues that made the reference understandable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat sentence-ending rules as proxies for pronoun clarity
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Ending a sentence with a plural noun or verb does not guarantee that the next sentence's “it” is unambiguous. Replacing a coordinated phrase with a clause can make an embedded singular noun more salient. Evaluate the main subject, parallel predicates, semantic compatibility and any explicit restatement that follows. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Mechanical rules are useful screening tools, but readers resolve references through several interacting cues. A rewrite can pass the proxy while changing the interpretation the proxy was intended to protect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test context-dependent wording again before reusing it as standalone copy
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Wording that is clear after an introduction may become misleading when extracted into an FAQ, card or search description. On a ceramic-studio site, “collect it where you learn” depends on readers already knowing which classes and collection location are meant. Review both the full page and the isolated passage. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Earlier context can resolve a sentence without making that sentence self-contained. Reuse removes those supporting cues, so compliance with a local wording rule cannot substitute for checking the reader's likely interpretation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Translate internal role labels into the page's established reader voice
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Internal labels such as “owner” must be checked before they enter visitor-facing copy. On a bicycle-repair booking page written in the second person, “the service owner chooses” could mean the operator even when the intended meaning is “you choose.” Search the whole page for reader-role nouns after importing an amendment. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Requirements often describe people in the third person, and writers can carry that voice into new slots. A single inconsistent noun can change who appears to control a decision.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recheck every bullet against its heading when product capabilities change
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A release update must check whether each bullet still belongs under its heading, even when its facts are accurate. A feature that has shipped no longer belongs unchanged beneath “Not available yet.” Review headings, bullets, status bands and data-flow explanations together. Use both a structured reviewer and a reader unfamiliar with the product. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reviewers and newcomers notice different problems: one may catch unsupported wording while another misreads the page's structure. Specific limitations build trust only when their grouping makes their meaning clear.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Put conditions before negative claims to prevent temporary contradictions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Put the condition before a negative claim when the claim is false outside that condition. For example, a bakery ordering page should say “For postal orders, same-day delivery is unavailable,” rather than starting with an unqualified denial. After rewriting a limitation, compare its main verb and polarity with nearby promises. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers interpret sentences as they unfold. A qualification at the end can arrive too late to prevent an apparent contradiction, especially when the opening repeats a familiar promise with the opposite meaning.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Shared copy needs explicit referents on every page where it appears
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Read reused copy in the vocabulary of each destination page and name the system or process its terms refer to. A seed library page linking to a separate reservation service should distinguish library membership registration from reservation-service setup. Use a specific noun when “its own setup” would still be ambiguous. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A sentence borrows context from its surroundings. Wording that is precise on its original page can point to the wrong process elsewhere, even when the copied facts have not changed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: After fixing a contradiction, inspect adjacent sentences for implied contradictions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A corrected sentence can still be contradicted by the contrast implied in a neighbouring sentence. Distinguish storage location from processing destination: saying one mode “keeps files on the device” may imply that another mode removes them, even when both retain a local copy. Review the whole comparison after changing a condition. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Attention naturally stays on the sentence that triggered the repair. Readers also infer meaning from contrasts, so the remaining defect may live in wording that is individually true but misleading beside the fix.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit repeated short phrases for conflicting meanings across a page
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check whether repeated phrases retain the same meaning across headings, FAQs, limitations and setup instructions. “Without a model” could mean no model installed, no model selected or no model available for a particular task. Name the relevant state explicitly when those distinctions affect behaviour. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Each sentence may be accurate in isolation while the page remains misleading. Readers carry definitions from one section into another, so inconsistent shorthand can make them dismiss a limitation that actually applies to their configuration.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recheck a summary's antecedent after inserting conditions or exceptions
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] After inserting a condition or exception before a summarizing sentence, check what that summary now appears to describe. On a seed library page, “This happens automatically” should clearly refer to a named renewal process rather than a newly inserted sentence about ineligible reservations. Move the exception or repeat the relevant noun. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Readers often resolve vague references against the nearest sentence. A factual amendment can therefore leave the original summary sounding illogical even though every individual statement remains accurate.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep the two branches of a conditional explanation adjacent
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Present both branches of a conditional claim in the same sentence or in adjacent sentences. A bicycle-repair booking page should explain what happens with a confirmed slot and without one before moving on to payment or collection details. During amendments, move existing text when needed instead of appending the missing branch wherever space remains. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separating a condition from its alternative forces readers to reconstruct the comparison. It also makes the later branch feel like an exception added after the main explanation was finished.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Do not let an evidence ledger silently clarify wording that remains ambiguous on the page
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When an evidence ledger adds words to make a published claim understandable, review the original wording for the same missing clarification. If a ceramic studio page says “This continues weekly” but its ledger says “The beginner class continues weekly,” the ledger may be resolving an ambiguity that visitors still face. Compare the recorded proposition with the exact displayed sentence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Internal evidence can accidentally make copy look clearer than it is. Readers see the page, so the page must carry the information needed to resolve its references.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Protect required terminology from stylistic rules against repetition
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Explicitly exempt required labels and technical terms from instructions to avoid repeating words. Give writing briefs a clear precedence order: factual meaning and required terminology outrank stylistic variation. Review preserved phrases word for word after editing. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A writer can satisfy a no-repeat instruction by dropping part of a term, leaving language that is awkward or changes meaning. Repetition is sometimes the clearest way to preserve a distinction. Conflicting instructions need an explicit priority rather than relying on the writer to infer which one matters more.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use fallback verbs that accurately describe retries, skips and disabled features
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Words such as “waits” imply future resumption and should not describe a feature that is permanently skipped in the selected configuration. Check fallback wording against every supported route, including routes where a capability is absent by design. Use “retries,” “skips” or “is unavailable” according to the actual behaviour. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Review tables can capture explicit propositions while missing promises embedded in verbs. Source notes may contain the same ambiguity, so copying them faithfully does not establish that the resulting explanation is true.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate canonical names from display labels and change structured copy safely
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Store canonical names separately from navigation labels so typographic treatments do not leak into prose or metadata. A ceramic studio might use uppercase collection labels in navigation while retaining normal name casing in descriptions, forms and structured data. Change only intended display fields through a structured transformation, leaving lowercase slugs, API values and provenance untouched. Walk both strings and lists beneath display keys. Check that unaffected fields remain unchanged and inspect generated pages after rebuilding. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Uppercase can work as a compact visual label while reading as shouting in a sentence. Separate name and label fields prevent one presentation decision from becoming an accidental data contract, and structured edits reduce the risk of damaging identifiers during a broad copy change.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit social-image descriptions and choose capitalization separately from shared label storage
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Include social-image alternative descriptions and context-appropriate label casing in a content completeness review. Check that descriptive text is actually emitted into metadata, and avoid treating an uppercase navigation string as the only canonical form of a name. Maintain readable wording for headings and structured data while applying display capitalization deliberately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Missing metadata can survive visual review because it is not visible on the page. Shared strings also spread presentation decisions into contexts where they may read poorly, so reuse meaning without blindly reusing formatting.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate font subsets on complete pages and preserve rendering features that affect layout
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Font subsetting should retain required characters, layout features, numeral styles and hinting where it affects rendering. Compare complete pages across representative routes and viewport widths after rebuilding fonts. Record the subset command so the result is reproducible. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Glyph samples can conceal changes to wrapping, alignment and page composition. File-size savings are useful only when the delivered fonts preserve the intended reading experience.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match perceived type size using cap height or x-height
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Match different typefaces by visible cap height or x-height rather than assuming equal CSS font-size produces equal apparent size. Two passages at 20 px can look substantially different. A measured cap-height ratio of 63/73 suggests an initial compensation factor of 73/63, followed by visual inspection of the actual text and font files. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Font metrics allocate space differently. Matching the property alone can leave a supporting passage looking unexpectedly small and weaken the intended reading hierarchy.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recheck captions whenever artwork changes its depicted objects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat an artwork revision as a reason to revalidate its captions, labels and surrounding claims. If a bicycle-repair co-op replaces a literal workshop diagram with abstract service shapes, copy describing benches or tools may become inaccurate. Propose the smallest truthful correction and follow the project's established copy-approval process where one applies. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Previously approved wording can become false without changing a single character. Reviewing image and text together prevents a polished visual update from quietly introducing a factual mismatch.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test text over artwork for glyph interference as well as contrast
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check that bright painted details do not intersect label glyphs, even when the text passes a contrast test. Inspect actual label boxes at responsive widths such as 1024 px and 390 px, and mask or reposition interfering peaks. Keep labels close enough to their own controls to preserve association, and verify changes in both wide and phone compositions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A tiny painted highlight can resemble an accent mark or extra stroke and turn a correct word into an apparent typo. Contrast measures alone do not capture that form of lost legibility.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inspect generated video directly and change one diagnosed variable at a time
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A favorable timing score cannot establish that a generated clip is visually usable. Inspect frames around entrances, exits, transitions, and the ending, then watch the complete clip. For continuous-shot prompts, attach timestamps to subject actions rather than new camera framings that may imply cuts. When diagnosing a failure, compare with a successful control and change one supported variable at a time. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A metric can overlook an empty frame or a subject disappearing at the crucial moment. Fixing the opening can also damage the climax, so local improvements still require whole-clip review.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Design web loops around cyclic motion, explicit encoding budgets, and a still fallback
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A seamless web banner needs motion that can return naturally to its starting state and a usable poster when animation is disabled. For a ceramic studio, a 10 s loop might show a subtle light cycle across a finished vessel. Test whether the generation tool accepts matching start and end frames before planning around that feature. A crossfade of duration F can seal a clip of duration D into a D−F loop. Encode H.264 with CRF 23 and faststart as a starting point; target video at most 10 MB and a WebP poster at most 300 KB. Remove audio with -an and verify with ffprobe. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Endpoint similarity alone does not prove a smooth seam. Watch the join, provide a pause control, and serve the poster for reduced motion or data-saving preferences.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep video and WebGL alternatives rooted in the same still and provide complete generation handoffs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Video and WebGL alternatives can share one approved still while remaining independently selectable for each visual region. For a generated loop, provide ingredient files, explicit reference labels, a prompt covering goal, input roles, scene, motion and constraints, plus duration and aspect ratio. A 10 s silent loop with matching start and end frames is a useful target; inspect the seam and prepare a crossfade fallback. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Matching source art preserves continuity when choosing between implementations. A complete handoff lets a human renderer work without reconstructing hidden assumptions, while a shared still also supplies a dependable fallback.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose render rounds around verified boundary frames and support per-clip durations
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A generated-video journey may require two render rounds when connector endpoints depend on the finished scene clips. Render scenes first, normalize and trim them, extract boundary frames, then supply those frames to the connectors. Store duration per clip instead of assuming one global length. For imperfect landings, compare candidate trims and try a baked 6–12-frame crossfade or a tuned runtime fade. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Requesting matching endpoints does not prove the model will deliver them. A start-equals-end probe can test whether all boundaries can be planned in advance. The browser implementation also needs Blob eviction, activation handling for each clip, posters matching decoded frames, per-scene mobile crops, preserved progress on resize and chapter jumps that avoid downloading skipped clips.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review raw passage clips separately from the assembled scroll experience
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A scroll story needs both a raw-clip review and a final review inside the interactive browser stage. Give each passage a self-contained prompt covering goal, input roles, scene, motion and constraints, with the palette repeated and the actual supplied frames described. Check raw clips for endpoint similarity, colour drift, camera continuity and unintended objects. Then scrub the assembled page forward and backward, checking seams, text placement and reading holds. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A clip can pass in isolation yet fail when seeking reverses or words overlap moving detail. Painted stops supplied at both ends can reduce render dependencies, but endpoint adherence still needs a probe. The final assembly medium is the browser, so its interaction must be part of the review.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Normalize video last so later processing cannot silently replace the intended GOP
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Finish colour matching and seam repair before the final web encode, then verify the encoded result again. A useful order is seam check, colour match, seam repair, normalization, repeated seam check, boundary extraction, contact sheet and media verification. Verify H.264, yuv420p, absent audio, faststart, GOP spacing, duration and bytes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Re-encoding after normalization can silently discard a scrub-friendly GOP-8 setting. Seam thresholds also need calibration: one sample set placed unrelated images near SSIM 0.62 and adjacent moving frames around 0.90–0.94, making 0.60 an inadequate repair floor. Example bands of at least 0.90 for pass and 0.75–0.90 for repair require local validation. Read structured verdicts because repairable and failed cases may share a nonzero exit code.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Calibrate white-paper checks after encoding and lift highlights without recolouring the artwork
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Measure white-ground video after its actual encode and decode path, using known-white and tinted controls. Useful diagnostics include p95 luminance, brightest-decile RGB spread, outer-edge brightness and per-channel white estimates. One calibrated pipeline used p95 at least 248 and tint spread at most 4, with values below 235 rejected. Its encoded white control measured about 253 rather than 255. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Codec and colour-conversion settings can change nominal white, so demanding exactly 255 may reject valid output. A per-channel knee LUT, for example beginning at 236, can lift measured paper toward white while preserving darker pigment. Verify that the artwork remains stable after re-encoding; these thresholds and the knee must be recalibrated for another pipeline.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Design stills and connecting motion together
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Author stop-image prompts and passage prompts as one production task with a shared storyboard and review criteria. Before painting a stop, establish how the camera arrives, where the next passage travels and which forms must remain continuous. Review the complete package, including ingredients, prompts and intended browser presentation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A striking still can be difficult to connect when its perspective, landscape or focal placement contradicts neighboring frames. Coordinating both media makes the seam a composition decision before it becomes a repair problem. It also prevents the video prompt from inventing a route through a scene that the image never provided.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit motion prompts against both portrait and landscape frames
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Measure focal-point positions in each aspect ratio before approving a passage's camera direction. A portrait crop can move the destination sideways even when the landscape version supports a forward drift. Check edge clearance too: a push-in may carry pigment across a paper margin only 2.5% deep. Verify every flagged discrepancy against the actual images. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Storyboard assumptions and prompt authors' self-reports are useful leads, not measurements. Also audit metaphorical vocabulary: waves, pours, drops and pools can encourage literal water in a scene meant to contain abstract light. Describe the intended material and motion directly, then confirm that the prompt agrees with both supplied endpoints before spending on renders.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use one representative render probe before releasing a batch handoff
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Gate a representative passage before rendering the full batch, even after its prompt package passes review. Choose a probe that exposes the difficult constraint, such as forward motion near a white paper border. Check endpoints, colour, margins and motion, then propagate any resulting prompt correction across the remaining handoff. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Storyboard review catches composition errors, prompt review catches contradictions, and an actual render exposes the generator's interpretation. These layers answer different questions. Keep unresolved judgments visible and map returned filenames to prompt identifiers without making harmless naming differences block ingestion. A clear pause after the probe prevents a correctable instruction from becoming a batch-wide defect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: A real render probe can expose prompt constraints that suppress the intended motion
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test the prompt strategy with one real passage before applying it across a large render batch. If the output is flat or choppy, inspect whether protective constraints prohibit the very motion the story requires. Revise the motion description, re-probe, then give each passage a distinct choreography consistent with its endpoints. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Preserving a white border or stable composition can become an accidental instruction to avoid movement. A prompt can pass a textual audit while producing lifeless footage. The probe tests the medium's interpretation and can save an entire batch of unsuitable renders. Keep the successful motion pattern and its limits available to the remaining prompts without copying identical movement everywhere.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate painted-image animation from interactive graphics overlays
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use image-to-video experiments for painted artwork and WebGL for responsive overlays when those roles preserve the intended aesthetic. For an invented ceramic-studio site, a short clip might animate light across a painted kiln scene while WebGL supplies interactive annotations beside it. Prepare a handoff with reference images, explicit asset roles, prompts and motion constraints after the static composition is stable. Google Flow/Omni is one candidate to evaluate; compare its output against the source artwork rather than assuming fidelity. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Rebuilding a painting in shaders can change its texture and composition. Separating artwork motion from interaction gives each technique a clear responsibility and makes reusable style decisions easier to evaluate.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Lock geometry at video-to-canvas seams and animate light within it
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a video background meets live graphics, preserve the shared boundary geometry throughout the entire clip. For an astronomy club's illustrated banner, animate light along fixed filaments if a canvas continues those filaments beyond the video edge. Build the handoff around GOAL, INPUT ROLE, SCENE, MOTION and CONSTRAINTS, including a locked-off camera, duration, aspect ratio and protected text areas. A 10 s clip can have subtle and livelier variants for comparison. Where the chosen tool supports matching start and end frames, supply the same plate; otherwise inspect any cross-dissolve for ghosting. Validate frame similarity and boundary positions separately, export H.264 and VP9 within an explicit budget such as 10 MB, and use frame 0 as the poster. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A seamless loop can still break its connection to neighbouring artwork. Keeping geometry fixed while light moves preserves that join; reduced-motion and data-saving modes should retain the still composition.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Compare a prerendered hero loop with live rendering using the same artwork and motion brief
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A silent video loop can be evaluated as an alternative to live WebGL using the same approved artwork and motion brief. Prepare a generation handoff with the reference image, a requested 10 s cycle, identical starting and ending composition, and explicit instructions for no text or audio. Treat these as requested output properties and inspect the generated result. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared art direction makes the comparison more meaningful. Matching endpoint images alone does not ensure a smooth loop; inspect velocity at the seam, responsive crops, transfer size, playback behavior, and the still fallback before choosing a delivery method.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Compare ambient motion and narrative motion as separate experiments
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test an ambient loop separately from a narrative loop when evaluating generated video against a live animation. For a ceramic studio, one clip might gently vary reflected light while another follows a single glow across a glaze sample. Structure prompts as GOAL, INPUT ROLE, SCENE, MOTION and CONSTRAINTS; supply separate wide and phone references and matching start/end frames when supported. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The two clips answer different questions: whether the medium preserves the painting, and whether it can execute a sequence without inventing objects. Compare cadence explicitly; a 10 s loop behaves differently from a 5.5 s live cycle.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate one anchored passage before adapting an entire video workflow for the web
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Prove one passage between two stills before investing in a complete generated scroll story. Create a manifest recording its start and end images, prompt, takes, trim window, duration and aspect ratio. The handoff should state who renders, where raw clips go and which normalized files the site consumes. Review the raw result before encoding. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Browser assembly introduces requirements that a conventional editing workflow may hide: stable boundary frames, compatible colour, silent output and reliable seeking. Useful processing stages include boundary-frame extraction, seam comparison, route-order contact sheets and short-GOP or all-intra encoding trials. Camera travel belongs in passages; locked-off motion belongs in loops. The initial probe determines whether endpoint adherence is adequate before either habit becomes a production assumption.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use a predictable package structure for motion assets and handoffs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give each motion package separate locations for source ingredients, raw renders, working files and finished web assets. Include a handoff document, storyboard and status record, with a shared index linking all packages. A filename pattern such as <prompt-id>_<aspect>_<take>_take<number>.mp4 makes variants identifiable without opening them. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A predictable structure tells contributors where to place downloads and tells builders which files are ready to use. When moving packages, update references and leave a redirect note where useful. Check that ingredient images are current before spending time or credits on rendering.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review raw video seams before encoding and calibrate similarity thresholds with real clips
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review raw passage clips against both endpoint stills before producing web encodes. Inspect key frames and a route sheet, measure structural similarity and colour drift, check for unexpected freezes or cuts, and inspect audio streams. Classify results as pass, repairable or requiring a fresh render. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The browser exposes joins directly, so a defective raw seam should not advance unnoticed. Best-matching trims, restrained baked crossfades or colour adjustments may repair small discrepancies. SSIM bands near 0.95 and 0.85 are only starting hypotheses until calibrated against representative visual judgments. A three-attempt escalation rule can prevent endless retries without diagnosis.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use camera travel for passages and a locked camera for anchored ambient loops
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Anchored scroll passages and ambient loops need different camera rules. A passage travels between start and end stills, with stable boundary moments, controlled orientation and a named transition medium such as mist. An anchored loop generally keeps the camera locked while light or small environmental details move. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Applying the loop rule to a passage produces a static transition with little sense of travel. Applying passage-style camera movement to a simple loop makes the wrap harder to hide. State the recipe before writing prompts so production and review assess the same intended behaviour.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Include JPEG-derived inputs when testing video colour-range normalization
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] JPEG-derived video inputs can retain full-range pixel formats unless the encoding pipeline explicitly normalizes them. For limited-range H.264 output, an observed fix ended the filter chain with scale=out_range=tv,format=yuv420p and supplied -color_range tv to libx264. Inspect the resulting media rather than relying only on requested flags. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Synthetic lavfi fixtures had passed while real JPEG-based input produced yuvj420p and failed verification. Add a representative JPEG-source case to the tests and keep final media verification at the end of the pipeline. Tests establish only the input states they actually exercise.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Compare short-GOP video with alternatives using real scrub behaviour and file sizes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] H.264 with GOP 8 is a useful candidate for scroll scrubbing when all-intra video costs substantially more without a clear visual benefit. One 720p, 8-second comparison measured GOP-8 files at 1.01 MB wide and 0.91 MB portrait, versus 2.87 and 2.71 MB for all-intra, and 1.98 and 1.68 MB for WebP strips. These are sample results, not expected sizes for other footage. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Test actual seeking and image quality on target devices before choosing. The tested H.264 settings used yuv420p, 24 fps, -g 8 -keyint_min 8 -sc_threshold 0, -an and +faststart. Review the complete storyboard before generating transitions so encoding choices and visual continuity serve the whole experience.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match camera direction to the subject's movement between endpoint images
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A subject that changes sides between endpoint images usually requires lateral camera movement or explicit subject movement, rather than a pure push-in or pull-back. Measure a recognizable anchor's pixel position in both images before writing the motion prompt. For a stationary subject, a camera move right generally makes the subject slide left. Check wide and portrait compositions independently. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Forward motion expands the scene around the viewing axis; it does not automatically explain a cross-frame relocation. Resolving this geometry before rendering prevents a probe from testing contradictory instructions instead of the model's endpoint adherence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Describe the visible scene and intended motion without inviting unwanted objects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Video prompts should describe the scene itself, using words whose visual associations match the intended result. Prefer 'the scene in the starting image' to wording that suggests a framed painting or webpage. Specify pale gold when orange fire is unwanted, and describe an upright, level camera positively. Treat words such as sea, chain and arc as possible instructions for water, linked objects or orbital motion. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A prompt can satisfy its literal wording while producing unwanted scenery. Handoffs should also explain how to assign start and end images through available frame slots when named-image references have not been verified.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit a complete render handoff and test one representative passage before batching
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A render handoff should specify endpoint images, aspect ratios, prompt variants, output mapping and a single first probe before authorizing a batch. Audit camera geometry against the actual stills, image compression, palette wording and any unverified frame-reference syntax. State lateral movement on the storyboard whenever focal subjects change sides. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A polished handoff can still contain a contradiction that wastes every subsequent render. One representative probe makes the package reviewable while changes remain cheap; resolving the findings in the handoff also prevents the operator from having to reconstruct decisions from scattered notes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check both video endpoints and explicitly remove audio from silent decorative media
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] For decorative video that must be silent, remove the audio track explicitly during encoding and verify its absence in the delivered file. Compare the opening and closing frames with their intended neighboring visuals, then repeat those checks after encoding. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A generation prompt does not guarantee media properties. Encoding can also change the appearance of transition boundaries, so acceptance checks must inspect the final asset.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve source masters and choose delivery resolution through device testing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep the highest-quality available source master separate from web delivery encodes, and choose delivery resolution by measured playback behavior. Compare 720p and 1080p derivatives on representative devices using scrub responsiveness, long frames, transferred bytes and page performance. If a source was upscaled from 720p to 1080p, record that provenance: larger dimensions do not restore native detail. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separate masters allow later encoding changes without repeated lossy processing. Shipping decisions should follow visible quality and device capability, while storage and transfer costs remain explicit rather than assuming that a larger master is free or inherently better.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inspect opening and closing video transitions independently
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check both ends of a generated video for changes in brightness, color, geometry and visual style. Combine automated comparisons with visual inspection, and check separately for abrupt cuts or frozen motion. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A convincing closing frame does not establish a smooth opening. Continuous motion and endpoint fidelity are distinct properties, and a single similarity score can conceal a visible mismatch.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Repair local endpoint drift with short blends and recheck after delivery encoding
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Local blends to the intended endpoint stills can repair passage seams without changing the grade of the entire clip. One repair approach searches the first and last 24 frames for good matches, trims there, then applies 8-frame blends, extending to 12 frames for stronger drift. Intermediate SSIM reached roughly 0.988–0.990; delivery encoding at GOP 8 and CRF 22 reduced measured similarity. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A global grade toward the opening may damage an already-correct ending. Inspect reported metrics when a repair misses its acceptance threshold, but preserve the failed gate until the output is reviewed or the threshold is deliberately recalibrated.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate transformed media and budget all assets needed for the page experience
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Check source video transitions, make any repairs, produce delivery variants and verify each final file's appearance and media properties. Budget the combined video and poster downloads for the complete page experience. Choose encoding and preload behavior for the intended browsers, connection conditions and device limits. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A small individual file does not establish an affordable total download. Cropping, resizing and compression can introduce new defects, so validation must follow each transformation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Probe the new visual constraint before commissioning a full storyboard
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a proven video method moves to a new visual ground, test that new constraint before generating the full asset set. Create one ordinary transition and one difficult transition, especially where scale or focal position changes sharply. Write both camera direction and expected scene displacement to avoid mixing conventions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Successful dark-background rendering does not establish behavior on white margins. Early probes can reveal whether clean-edge requirements constrain motion too strongly, while changes to composition are still inexpensive. Treat conservative scale limits as hypotheses to evaluate rather than permanent rules inherited from an untested storyboard.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Camera movement affects whether white margins remain clear throughout a passage
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Push-ins and strong vertical travel can move pigment into white top and bottom margins, while lateral travel or pull-backs may preserve them more easily. If every frame must retain white edges, start with sideways-dominant motion, at most 15% scale change and ample space around the still's forms. Verify the result rather than treating those limits as guarantees. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These constraints protect continuous paper margins but can flatten the motion. If the interface only needs clean endpoint images, allow more freedom mid-flight and evaluate stage masking separately instead of applying an unnecessarily strict all-frame rule.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Write passage prompts from the rendered stills rather than the intended storyboard
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Derive transition geometry from the actual endpoint images, including focal positions, wash boundaries and available text space. Measure a recognizable anchor in each still and record the camera movement required to connect them. Inspect wide and portrait images separately; generated compositions may shift a focal point or introduce an unintended eye-like shape, extra color or edge wash. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A storyboard describes intent, but the renderer receives pixels. Prompting against a discarded intention creates contradictions that can look like model failure. Update the handoff to describe what is painted before spending credits on the passage.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Overconstraining white-ground animation can turn a dimensional journey into a flat pan
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Prompts that emphasize a flat paper surface, fixed shapes, lateral sliding and explicit holds can suppress the dimensional motion a passage needs. A revised approach can describe luminous space, pigment at several depths, forward travel with a gentle curve and continuous blooming or curling motion. Test whether only endpoints require clean white margins before constraining every intermediate frame. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repeated caution words and preservation clauses can combine into a static clip even when each seems reasonable alone. Compare a revised probe before updating the batch, and check that richer motion does not introduce unwanted dissolves, duplicate objects or unreadable transitions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Apply visual constraints where the interface needs them and allow useful motion elsewhere
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Endpoint requirements should not automatically become restrictions on every frame of a transition. One white-ground probe retained clean first and last margins while pigment crossed the edges during forward travel: the outer 4% top/bottom region had endpoint fifth-percentile values of 249.3 and 247.3, with tint measures of 1.6 and 2.0. These measurements require a documented metric definition to reuse. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Protecting every intermediate margin can eliminate the motion the passage exists to provide. Validate the complete stage treatment, then vary choreography across passages while keeping palette and endpoint continuity consistent.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Track passage choreography explicitly to avoid repetitive motion across a sequence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Maintain a small choreography ledger that records each passage's camera move, depth cues and material behavior. Preserve a successful probe's exact prompt as a reference, then distinguish neighboring passages through meaningful movement changes rather than synonyms. Keep previous prompt versions so regressions can be traced. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A set of individually attractive clips can become repetitive when assembled. The ledger also separates internal metaphors from render instructions: a move nicknamed after a curtain or river need not mention that object in the prompt if it would introduce unwanted literal scenery.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Pair camera motion with depth cues and audit semantic regressions after prompt edits
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A camera instruction needs visible depth cues to avoid collapsing into a flat pan. Near motes passing the lens, overlapping wisps and changing occlusion can establish travel without excessive displacement of the main subject. Audit verbs as well as nouns: removing 'curtain' while retaining folding and drawing-aside behavior can still summon a curtain-like object. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Local prompt fixes can recreate earlier defects elsewhere, such as removing a pull-back and losing all depth. Recheck endpoint direction, motion variety and unintended object associations after each substantive revision, using the actual images as the reference.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Inspect contact sheets because seam and format checks miss semantic defects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Numeric seam checks and media-format validation cannot establish that generated video contains the right objects or motion. Review a contact sheet at 2 fps for every clip, then watch suspicious intervals at full frame rate. Look for tiling lines, unintended symbols, off-palette particles and shape changes that endpoint metrics can miss. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A technically valid clip can still communicate the wrong meaning halfway through. Keep raw, repaired and delivery-stage results distinct, and state whether a white-margin rule applies throughout the clip or only at endpoints; otherwise an intentional dark passage may be mislabeled as a defect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Fit centered canvas compositions to both dimensions with a minimum-based scale
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Size a centered canvas focal element with baseR = min(W * 0.46, H * 0.62) so its scale respects both available dimensions. Tune the coefficients to the artwork's actual bounds, including glow and motion. Pair container-relative text sizing with clamp(), and guard zero-size containers and invalid cell dimensions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An ultrawide stage becomes height-bound while a portrait stage becomes width-bound, reducing breakpoint-specific composition logic. Test narrow widths such as 375 pixels and ultrawide layouts; a minimum-based scale helps fitting but does not automatically guarantee every surrounding element remains visible.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build public visualizations from reproducible aggregates and review disclosure risks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Derive public visualization data through a reproducible, read-only transformation and review the resulting labels and aggregates before publication. An amateur astronomy club could export object counts by observation category and connect categories using a documented shared-property rule. Commit only the reviewed public dataset and record how counts and edges were computed. Verify source permissions separately from technical accessibility. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A graph can demonstrate useful scale without exposing underlying records, but aggregation alone does not guarantee privacy. Rare labels and combinations may reveal sensitive context, and an attractive connection needs a defensible meaning.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test float rendering, filtering, and blending as separate WebGL capabilities
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] WebGL2 float render-target support does not imply float filtering or blending support. A September 2026 survey snapshot reported EXT_color_buffer_float at 99.94% overall, but OES_texture_float_linear and EXT_float_blend at roughly 49% on iOS (as of September 2026; re-check before relying on it). Do not substitute WebGL1 extension statistics for WebGL2 evidence. Prefer a tested RGBA16F path for filtered or blended targets, reserve 32F for unfiltered, unblended state, and verify framebuffer completeness. Feature-detect shader compilation and scheduling helpers, with setTimeout or MessageChannel fallbacks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Capability ladders need separate checks for each operation. A static poster also provides visible content while rendering initializes, so first paint does not depend on a successful canvas boot.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit asset licences and measure the bundle produced by your actual scene
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify the licence and provenance of each shader, texture, and library before incorporating it into a WebGL site. Record the exact source version, licence text, attribution requirements, and whether commercial reuse is permitted; absent permission is not permission to copy. Trace mirrored assets back to an authoritative source rather than trusting a tutorial's description. For a 200 KB WebGL bundle budget, measure your production build with its actual imports and compression settings. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A permissive library does not automatically license every example bundled around it. Third-party bundle comparisons are useful leads, but different scenes and build settings can make their numbers unsuitable for your own budget.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prevent decorative graph connections from implying relationships the data does not support
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Decorative node-link figures must avoid accidental hubs and make the scope of each connection explicit. If a relation belongs to a group but its line visually ends on an individual node, explain that scope in accessible labels and the legend. Distribute endpoints among available members before reusing a node, provided this does not introduce crossings or enclosing shapes that imply further relationships. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A node carrying several lines appears important even when the data assigns it no special role. Text can clarify group-level meaning, but cannot reliably undo a strongly misleading drawing; revise the encoding if endpoint distribution and labeling are insufficient.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Size overlays using the displayed image scale and verify the rendered result
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Overlay marks that must visually match cover-fit imagery should derive their dimensions from the image's displayed scale. For a W by H box and w by h source, cover scale is max(W/w, H/h). Multiply source-relative mark widths by that scale; for SVG strokes, non-scaling-stroke can prevent an additional viewBox transform from distorting the intended width. Measure results in source-image pixels across viewport sizes, content states and raster resolutions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The image and overlay may scale through different coordinate systems. Matching them at one viewport hides drift after resizing or opening a disclosure. Geometric correctness is necessary, but fine marks also require enough raster resolution to preserve their apparent weight.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Account for canvas backing-store resolution when evaluating image-relative mark sizes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Correct image-relative geometry does not guarantee correct apparent mark weight on a coarse raster surface. Measure the actual backing-store pixels per CSS pixel, rather than assuming a DPR-2 screen produces a DPR-2 canvas. In one documented test family, fidelity deteriorated when a raster pixel represented roughly 1.4 source-image pixels; treat that as a local observation, not a universal cutoff. Increase resolution, use a suitable SVG fallback or explicitly report the limitation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Antialiasing can dominate a thin line's visible footprint. If a rule's registered failure condition occurs, withdraw its validated status; a narrower rule needs fresh, independent evidence rather than a retroactive exception.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate overlay scale correctness from raster limits and nominal stroke-weight choices
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Match overlay dimensions to cover-fit image scale, then evaluate raster resolution and nominal width as separate constraints. Use max(W/w, H/h) to convert source-image units into displayed units. For canvas, measure backing-store resolution directly. A nominal width of 1.1 source pixels leaves little headroom above a measured 1.0-pixel minimum: antialiasing can produce readings such as 0.94 despite correct scaling. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Choosing the right coordinate system prevents proportional drift but does not guarantee an absolute visual band. Resolution limits and width choices require their own evidence. When earlier guidance fails, preserve its useful mechanism as a narrower provisional claim instead of silently redefining what validated meant.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use exact segment intersection to keep animated paths clear of text
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use an exact segment-versus-padded-rectangle test when animated lines must avoid text boxes. Seventeen samples along a 265 px path leave roughly 16.6 px between samples, allowing a corner clip to pass unnoticed. Increasing to 33 samples reduces gaps but does not eliminate the defect. Use a slab or Liang-Barsky intersection method and a regression case that clips between the old samples. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A rare randomized failure can be a real geometric defect. Repeatedly rerunning it until green hides the probability rather than fixing the cause.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make exploratory visualizations understandable and usable on touch devices
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An exploratory visualization needs a clear subject, meaningful labels and discoverable interactions on both pointer and touch devices. For an astronomy club, group observations into labelled regions, explain selected items in plain language and expose pan, zoom and reset controls. Make tappable stars visibly interactive rather than relying on hover readouts. Inspect the initial static frame as well as the animated state. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Attractive imagery cannot explain its own data model. Real-phone review often reveals missing interaction cues and cramped labels that desktop inspection overlooks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use one semantic visualization stage with responsive layout data and accessible alternatives
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build an interactive graph around one semantic stage, responsive coordinate data and an accessible list of its contents. Provide keyboard movement, zoom and reset, touch selection and readable DOM callouts. Activate wheel zoom deliberately so the graph does not unexpectedly capture page scrolling. A seeded layout keeps screenshots reproducible. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shipping complete desktop and phone stages duplicates markup and increases document weight. A single stage also reduces the chance that labels, selections or accessibility behavior diverge between layouts while preserving a useful static fallback.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Derive connected visual coordinates from a shared source
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Derive coordinates for connected visual elements from one source rather than typing matching values in multiple places. If an illustrated stream ends at a vessel, calculate the vessel's center from the stream's final stage and assert the relationship in each layout. For regression checks, confirm that an injected defect actually takes effect before counting its failure as evidence. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Independent constants drift during responsive adjustments. Shared derivation turns alignment into an invariant, while verified fault injection ensures the test is checking that relationship rather than failing for an unrelated reason.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Derive both ends of an animated seam from the displayed artwork
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build continuous transitions between illustrations from measured boundary geometry at both ends. Extract crossings from each source image, map them through the displayed crop and test alignment at responsive widths with an explicit tolerance, such as 5 px. Avoid arbitrary connection caps that omit visible source strokes. Measure motion across enough of its cycle to capture slower swells. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Continuity becomes testable when endpoints come from the artwork rather than hand-tuned guesses. Larger displacement can still produce fewer changed pixels over a short interval if its timing becomes slower.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Close halo troughs with both an interior floor and a wider underlying glow
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A dark gap between a luminous core and its colored rim may require both a nonzero rim interior and a wider glow beneath it. In one calibration, interior values of 0.3/0.4 with fill 0.35 produced trough ratios of 0.652–0.686. Values of 0.35/0.5 plus an underlying halo at 1.15 times the rim radius and alpha 0.34 reached 0.732–0.763 while preserving the core color. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Raising only the rim floor can leave the layers perceptually disconnected. Measure the light between core and rim, and inspect the resulting shape across viewport sizes before adopting these example settings.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Give ring halos continuous interior light to avoid a bullseye appearance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A colored halo can read as a bullseye when its radial falloff contributes no light inside the rim. Start with a nonzero interior that rises continuously into the peak, such as [[0,0.35],[0.45,0.5],[0.68,1],[0.85,0.45],[1,0]], then adjust an underlying halo if a trough remains. One working configuration used halo radius 1.15 times the rim radius, alpha 0.34 and fill alpha 0.35. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A faint separate fill may not bridge the perceived gap. An example check required the trough to remain at least 0.7 of the rim peak along eight rays at widths 1440, 1024 and 390. Calibrate that criterion visually; it is not a universal lighting law.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Budget every additive light layer against the background brightness
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Additive glow tuned over a dark background can clip into a flat disc when it moves over pale artwork. Adjust every contributing layer against formation progress or available background headroom, including the rim. In one test, scaling only fill and halo left saturated areas of 1618/970/517 px; also scaling the rim reduced them to 776/400/228 px across three sizes. An example saturation cap was pi times (1.3 times core radius) squared. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An overlooked layer can consume the remaining headroom even after other layers are dimmed. Inspect the brightest forming frame and verify that reducing clipping does not make the subject disappear. The specific tuning remains scene-dependent.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reuse continuous halo profiles for hover pulses as well as static glows
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A centered halo profile with interior light can prevent hover pulses from reading as hollow rings. Give the radial falloff a nonzero interior and a smooth shoulder; if a dark trough remains, widen the underlying glow. Validate the pulse throughout its animation and across widths 1440, 1024 and 390. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A profile that works in one luminous element can guide another, but its old metric cannot automatically transfer. Inspect enlarged crops, compare against the previous ring-shaped effect, and calibrate any pulse-specific ring score to those examples before treating the reuse as verified.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prevent bullseye halos by carrying light continuously from the core into the rim
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A luminous rim needs light inside its radius to avoid reading as a bullseye. Replace zero-interior radial tables with a continuous shoulder, such as [[0,0.35],[0.45,0.5],[0.68,1],[0.85,0.45],[1,0]]. Measure the darkest trough between the core edge and rim peak; an interior floor alone may be insufficient.
