In one calibrated example, widening an underlying halo from 0.95 to 1.15 times the rim radius at 0.34 alpha, with fill at 0.35 alpha, raised the trough above 0.7 of the peak. Check multiple rays and viewport sizes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A faint separate fill does not necessarily hide the rim's own discontinuity. The 0.7 ratio is an example-specific acceptance threshold, not a universal law: confirm that the measured profile agrees with the intended appearance.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Document animation fidelity and performance tradeoffs with explicit acceptance criteria
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A faithful animation port may justify a performance exception only when the project explicitly accepts the measured tradeoff. Compare the implementation with its reference, use requestAnimationFrame, measure Lighthouse results and document any accepted score below 90. Byte-identical source establishes copying fidelity, not runtime correctness or acceptable performance. Preserve a static poster and pause rendering offscreen or when the tab is hidden. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Replacing a required animation with a static image can violate the design brief, while blindly copying it can harm usability. Explicit acceptance keeps both concerns visible and prevents a narrow exception from becoming a universal exemption from performance checks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prove animation ports with mechanical comparisons as well as visual inspection
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify a graphics-engine port by comparing constants and keyframes mechanically against its source. Assert equality for character ranges such as FF66–FF9D, term lists, ramp triples, gradient stops, breakpoints, and geometry values. Compare resolved values where textual formatting differs, and document intentional changes separately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A dropped glyph or reordered term can survive repeated visual code review in a 600-line engine. Mechanical checks expose those omissions, while live rendering checks remain necessary for timing, compositing, and actual pixel behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Preserve supported visual modes behind a clear flag when porting an animation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Retain a meaningful alternative visual mode behind one explicit flag when it remains a supported product choice. For an astronomy-club animation, a labels-on or labels-off option can share the same rendering engine without retaining the design tool's development controls. Keep the alternate branch understandable and verify it before later enabling it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Deleting a useful authored mode can force an unnecessary re-port. A small, deliberate switch preserves flexibility, provided the dormant path has a clear purpose and does not become unmaintained baggage.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Label curated diagrams honestly and keep private implementation topology out of public figure assets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A public explanatory diagram should distinguish a curated conceptual model from a faithful implementation graph. For a tide-pool field guide, group illustrated observations by habitat and explain what each connection means rather than implying unsupported ecological relationships. Provide an accessible HTML counterpart and review the underlying data asset for accidental disclosure. Opaque identifiers alone do not hide a revealing relationship structure. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Attractive graphs can imply stronger evidence than their source supports. Curating for comprehension is legitimate when the figure states its purpose and preserves the distinctions readers need, without exporting unnecessary private detail.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Package WebGL handoffs with visual intent, runtime limits, assets and executable acceptance criteria
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A WebGL handoff should describe both the intended experience and the conditions under which it must operate. Include a brief, assets with stated roles, reference stills, hardening requirements, porting notes and acceptance checks. Specify the layer stack, interaction behavior, reduced-motion mode, off-screen pause and responsive limits. Example project budgets might include a bundle ceiling of 200 KB and checks at widths of 1440, 1024 and 390 pixels. Keep text in HTML. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A screenshot cannot convey motion equations or failure behavior. Preserving the interaction logic alongside the visual references prevents a technically valid port from losing the design that made the original effective.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Research graphics techniques separately from the delivery critical path and verify reuse rights
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Graphics research should produce reusable findings without blocking unrelated page design work. Inspect interactive references in a browser, identify the underlying techniques and verify licenses before adapting code. Preserve required attribution and distinguish inspiration from authorized code reuse. Compare renderer options on the intended scene and devices rather than assuming a newer API will perform better. Monitor long research jobs for progress and define a bounded fallback when they stall. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Extensive research is useful only when its conclusions reach implementation. A separate research track protects delivery momentum, while license checks and scene-specific measurements prevent attractive demonstrations from becoming unsuitable production dependencies.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Study visual techniques separately from accessibility, licensing and hardware performance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate graphics references for rendering technique, production behaviour and licensing as separate concerns. Reducing pixel count can relieve fill-rate pressure; use DPR caps and lower-resolution effect buffers as hypotheses to test on target hardware. If ALIASED_LINE_WIDTH_RANGE reports [1,1], use screen-space quads or ribbons for thick threads. Bake complex backgrounds when only the foreground needs interaction. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Impressive demonstrations can still ignore reduced motion, visibility pauses, touch scrolling and frame-rate-independent easing. Software-rendered headless measurements cannot establish real-device frame rates. Inspect licences before adapting source; public availability is not permission. A production design needs readable HTML, lifecycle controls and measured device behaviour alongside its visual effect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose a graphics renderer from measured bundle and pixel costs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Choose a WebGL renderer by measuring the actual bundle and rendering workload, rather than counting particles alone. Raw WebGL2 with a small helper or OGL can suit a tightly scoped decorative layer. One teardown measured a tree-shaken three.js core at 176 KB gz against a 200 KB ceiling; that is a build-specific result, not a universal package size. Prefer per-star halo sprites and instanced thread geometry when full-screen bloom consumes too much fill rate. Treat SwiftShader results as software-rendering observations, not hardware performance predictions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Research is most useful when it exposes disagreements and missing measurements. Label proposed budgets as proposals and verify the chosen design on representative physical devices before publishing performance claims.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Re-derive animation recipes before trusting generated research
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify animation mathematics directly before adopting a research report's recipe. Orbital periods must share the intended repeat interval: a sequence that repeats after 900 seconds does not form a 120-second loop. Advecting particles through a periodic field does not guarantee that their accumulated positions return; applying periodic displacement to fixed rest positions can. A simple first-order spring does not supply the inertial overshoot of a second-order spring. Check color-space assumptions against the actual display pipeline. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A second source can reveal errors, but agreement is not proof. Small executable examples and direct source inspection resolve claims more reliably than copying plausible formulas from a polished synthesis.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Combine visual teardown, source checks, and device testing
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Turn a visual reference into an implementation plan by separating observed appearance, inferred technique, and verified measurements. Inspect the composition and interaction, prototype the smallest relevant effect, and check research claims against their sources. Measure the actual bundle and rendering behavior in a declared environment. Confirm hardware acceleration before interpreting frame results as device performance. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A convincing reference does not reveal its implementation budget or fallback behavior. Keeping observation distinct from inference prevents a teardown from becoming invented documentation and helps preserve the visual idea while choosing an appropriate technical approach.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Study interactive references by observing rendering, inputs, and fallback behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reverse-engineer interactive web techniques through read-only observation of rendering technology, input behavior, and resilience. Use Playwright and network inspection to identify likely libraries and whether the element uses Canvas2D, WebGL, WebGPU, SVG, CSS, or another runtime. Observe reduced motion, hidden tabs, off-screen behavior, and no-JavaScript fallback; measure frame behavior on stated hardware. Check licensing before reusing assets or code. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An impressive reference can hide weak accessibility or excessive rendering work. A useful teardown extracts mechanisms and constraints, then supports an independent implementation rather than copying a commercial site's code or appearance.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify each dependency and asset license before including it in a reusable pack
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Record the license for each exact library version and asset before including it in a reusable graphics pack. Inspect the source distribution or asset provenance rather than assuming an example page's code, textures, and dependencies share one license. Preserve any required notices and identify materials that cannot be redistributed. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Learning a rendering technique and shipping its implementation are different activities. Early license checks prevent an attractive demo from becoming an unusable dependency and make it clear which building blocks can travel with the pack and which require an independent implementation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Let evidence determine a diagram's density instead of filling every visual gap
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Every meaningful node, label, and relationship in an explanatory diagram should have a supported public claim behind it. For a seed-library map, build clusters from verified services and documented relationships rather than an internal wish list. If a cluster has little evidence, keep it modest, restructure the figure, or gather additional proof before adding nodes. Check source identifiers for obsolete numbering and keep unavailable capabilities visibly distinct. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Visual balance can pressure a designer to invent content. An empty region may expose a documentation or capability gap; decorative symmetry is not evidence that the missing claims are true.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check WebGL capabilities individually and keep the hero poster in HTML
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] WebGL2 support does not imply support for every floating-point rendering, filtering or blending operation. Historical survey figures reported roughly 99.9% support for EXT_color_buffer_float but about 49% for some float filtering and blending capabilities on iOS (as of October 2026; re-check before relying on it). Verify the API version and individual extensions; consider RGBA16F for supported filtered or blended targets and 32F for unfiltered state. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A wrong survey page can distort the entire fallback strategy. Browser scheduling APIs and canvas LCP eligibility also require current verification; a real HTML poster provides a dependable visible starting point.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit asset permissions and measure the actual renderer bundle before choosing a library
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Record license terms for each dependency, texture and code sample, then measure the production bundle for the intended scene. A bounded comparison reported about 13 kB gzip for OGL versus 127 kB for a minimal three.js application; these are build-specific observations, not universal package sizes. A WebGL budget of at most 200 KB makes that difference consequential. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Attractive examples can contain non-commercial or unlicensed material. Keep license evidence with the exact version, obtain permission where needed, and distinguish learning a technique from reusing its implementation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use spatial hierarchy to communicate readiness alongside explicit labels
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Concentric diagrams can communicate readiness by placing available items nearest the center and more speculative items farther away. For a seed library, inner items could represent seeds available today, with separate outer tiers for growing stock and proposed additions. Pair position with a clear legend and distinguish tiers through more than hue. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Spatial order gives readers a quick initial interpretation, but it must not replace explicit status wording. On phones, redraw the orbits and check target spacing; preserve the meaning even when the geometry changes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat every diagram connection as a factual claim that needs current evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Revalidate diagram edges whenever the underlying explanation changes, because an unlabelled connection still makes a claim. For an invented seed-library workflow, distinguish seed intake, inspection, storage and distribution; draw only relationships supported by the current process description. Record why each edge exists and remove or redirect it when its rationale becomes false. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Copy changes are conspicuous, while stale connections can survive unnoticed in an otherwise polished figure. Semantic review must cover topology as well as labels. Keep the source rationale beside the figure specification so future maintainers can check a connection without reconstructing the original design conversation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Turn diagram collisions into build failures instead of relying on screenshots
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Validate diagram geometry during the build so labels, targets, threads and readout regions cannot silently overlap. Reserve measured caption boxes in the layout solver and fail on collisions, including partially obscured interactive markers. Route mobile threads beside text and reserve readout space to avoid layout shift. Keep a text alternative aligned with the diagram's captions. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A shared geometry check can reveal defects on pages that earlier visual reviews missed. Test the checks with deliberately broken layouts rather than trusting a green report. Automated geometry still needs visual review for painted background objects, fallback-font wrapping and narrow-screen controls: these can remain wrong even when every solver constraint passes.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Convert visual findings into checks with explicit geometry and state coverage
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Turn repeatable visual defects into explicit layout constraints and verify that those constraints reject the old broken artifact. Useful checks include cluster separation, clearance from unrelated groups, endpoints attached to visible nodes and contrast across closed, open and pinned states. One layout improved its cross-cluster to within-cluster distance ratio from 0.94 to 2.24 and adopted a project-specific minimum of 2. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Concrete constraints make later regressions visible without requiring a reviewer to rediscover them. Match portrait selection to the content's 64rem breakpoint, measure coverage at real viewport shapes and keep a single text measure on compact layouts. Geometry checks do not eliminate judgement: scrims may remain visible as dark boxes, and shared marker-size changes can alter other figures. Inspect those effects before accepting the repair.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat a decorative doubled strand as one visual connection
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When two decorative filaments represent one connection, route and count them as a single visual thread. Keep them on the same side of intervening content, separated by about one core width at the apex, and converge on the same two endpoint markers. With a 1.6-unit core, a 4–8-unit offset is 2.5–5 core widths and can read as two separate lines. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Counting a decorative pair twice creates unnecessary endpoint and crossing constraints. Define the semantic object before adding geometry rules. This simplification applies only when the pair really represents one relation; genuinely distinct relationships still need an unambiguous representation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Scale vector overlays against the displayed raster image rather than only the SVG viewBox
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Match overlay stroke widths to the raster background's displayed scale when the SVG stage and background resize independently. Compute cover scale from the actual container as max(containerWidth/imageWidth, containerHeight/imageHeight), then apply proportional CSS-pixel widths with vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke. Starting proportions can use glow around 2 times the core and a secondary filament around 0.55 times the core. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Identical viewBox widths can look substantially heavier on mobile because the painting follows a different scaling rule. Use the same viewport basis as the art window, including lvh when applicable. A 0.85 CSS px stroke occupies 1.7–2.55 device pixels at DPR 2–3, so sub-CSS-pixel width is not automatically sub-device-pixel width. Validate the visible result at representative DPRs.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Validate diagram grouping, crossings and repeated shapes as well as clearance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Diagram validation should detect misleading visual grouping, not just overlapping boxes. Check that threads do not cross except at intended shared endpoints and that unrelated nodes are not enclosed by thread-bounded regions. In compact lanes, routing longer spans outside shorter ones can prevent shared-end crossings. Compare equal-sized clusters for unintended shape repetition; one project used a 12-unit RMS threshold after centring, best permutation and reflection. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Closure and similarity can communicate stronger relationships than labels or spacing. Turn observed failures into checks that reject known broken layouts, while keeping thresholds specific to the visual system. Emit layout values needed by CSS as custom properties from the solved data so duplicated literals cannot silently diverge.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match visual acceptance thresholds to measurement resolution and device pixel ratio
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Account for sampling resolution when a visual acceptance threshold approaches the measuring instrument's pixel size. Use a documented interpolation method for threshold crossings where appropriate, and state device pixel ratio and antialiasing assumptions. For a hypothetical line measuring 1.2 CSS pixels wide, a ceiling of 2.5 screenshot pixels becomes incompatible with that width above a device pixel ratio of approximately 2.08. Define whether enlarged selection halos are exempt. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Coarse measurements and mixed units can create false passes or failures. Explicit units, tolerances and rendering assumptions make acceptance results interpretable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate useful renderer-selection structure from unverified library claims
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate a renderer through fill-rate, bundle cost, initialization, feature needs and interaction latency before accepting a research report's library recommendation. Measure the actual production bundle; a core library that nearly consumes the total budget leaves little room for application code. Verify licenses, maintenance history, browser support and cited URLs independently. Half-float positions have 1.0-wide representable steps in the 1024–2048 range, so they cannot guarantee smooth subpixel motion there. Moving computation to a Worker does not guarantee zero interaction latency. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A report can offer an excellent decision framework while getting product details and numerical claims wrong. Keeping the framework and checking each factual dependency prevents confident prose from becoming architectural debt.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Render controllable threads with geometry and use baked halos for sparse glow
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use instanced signed-distance capsule quads for controllable thread widths and baked radial sprites for sparse star glows. Query native line-width support instead of assuming gl.LINES can produce wide strokes. Prefer DOM targets or CPU spatial indexing for modest interactive scenes to avoid synchronous GPU readback. Use separate link thresholds, such as forming within 100 px and breaking beyond 120 px, to prevent flicker near a boundary. MAX blending selects the strongest value rather than accumulating brightness, so it may not match the desired intersections. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Geometry, sprites and hysteresis give direct control without requiring a full bloom pipeline. Keep architecture decisions separate from unsupported benchmark timings in reference material.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use second-order motion for overshoot and keep useful formulas independent of engine choices
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use an underdamped second-order spring when a thread needs overshoot and settling; first-order smoothing alone cannot supply that behavior. For monotonic easing, use w = 1-exp(-dt/tau). A travelling highlight along a thread can use exp(-((u-v(t))/sigma)^2), with u as position along the thread. Perform lighting calculations in linear color and encode appropriately for display. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reference can contain useful mathematics even when its proposed engine and bloom pipeline exceed the project's budget. Separate the desired motion and light profile from the implementation stack, and remember that spring behavior still depends on damping, forcing and geometry.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Re-derive loop timing and shader math before trusting generated motion recipes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Create exact animation loops by evaluating periodic displacement from a fixed rest state rather than accumulating advection over time. For multiple periodic motions, calculate the least common multiple: periods of 30, 45, 60, 75 and 90 s repeat together after 900 s. Verify shader function provenance, buffer-size arithmetic and output color encoding independently. Linear color calculations still need the correct encoding when written to an sRGB display path. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Motion concepts can be visually persuasive while their mathematics is wrong. Re-deriving the small equations prevents drifting loop boundaries, unexpected memory costs and dark output without discarding the useful artistic idea.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Consider Canvas2D for modest sprite scenes and count actual rendering work
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate Canvas2D before choosing WebGL for a few hundred additive sprites without custom shader requirements. Small baked glow sprites, such as 32x32 px images, can supply light without post-processing. Keep essential labels and controls in HTML or SVG. Measure render invocations separately from requestAnimationFrame callbacks: a reference trace showed 57–60 callbacks per second while a timer-driven renderer executed 116 times per second. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A convincing visual effect does not require the largest rendering stack. Callback frequency can conceal duplicate work, and canvas-painted labels can conceal missing accessible content; inspect both the scheduler and the semantic interface.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Explore procedural filaments while accounting for engine and glow costs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Procedural particle fields can produce woven-looking filaments, but their engine and glow pipeline must fit the page budget. One reference technique respawned particles at fixed origins and advanced them through a cross-coupled sin*cos field, using a step of 0.4 and frequencies around 0.033–0.037. A blurred copy at one-eighth resolution supplied glow. A historical three.js r172 artifact measured approximately 176 KB gzipped before application code; measure the current build rather than treating that as a package constant. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The transferable asset is the field-and-respawn technique. Its visual appeal does not establish that low-resolution blur beats sprites for a particular scene, or that the surrounding engine is affordable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use damped springs and distance-weighted links for responsive ribbon motion
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An ensemble of damped second-order followers can create interweaving ribbon motion through lag and overshoot. A reference configuration used 50 followers, pull 0.1 and varying ease values of 0.6–0.8; these are implementation-specific starting points, not portable physical constants. Distance-based links can fade with 1-d²/r² inside radius r, use seeded acceptance, and trim endpoints by 30% to leave space around nodes. Adapt the motion to elapsed time or fixed simulation steps. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Variation between followers creates a richer response than identical first-order easing. Endpoint clearance and distance-weighted opacity help the resulting web remain readable rather than becoming a solid tangle.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Probe render-target formats and keep small GPU helpers explicit
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A compact WebGL renderer can use explicit shader, material and framebuffer helpers with runtime probes for supported render-target formats. A 4x4 framebuffer test can try R16F, RG16F, RGBA16F and an appropriate lower-precision fallback, checking actual completeness and required operations. Fluid pipelines commonly separate advection, divergence, pressure iterations, vorticity and input splats. Evaluate bloom, rays and simulation resolution as independent quality choices. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Small helpers can make the rendering path easier to inspect, but copying a demonstration wholesale also imports its flaws. A dt clamp at 1/60 can slow simulation time under load, touch handlers can trap scrolling, and borrowed code or textures require their own provenance and license checks.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose the simplest renderer that satisfies semantic and visual requirements
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Select rendering technology by required behavior, beginning with semantic HTML, SVG and CSS for meaningful content. Consider Canvas2D for modest sprite fields; raw WebGL2 with small helpers for instancing, custom shaders or specialized targets; OGL or twgl when lightweight utilities help; and three.js when scene graphs, asset pipelines or advanced effects justify its cost. Evaluate WebGPU separately when compute requirements warrant another capability and fallback path. Measure the exact shipped build. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A decision ladder keeps library familiarity from dictating architecture. Worker rendering does not eliminate initialization or DOM synchronization costs, and adding a framework solely to mount a decorative scene can exceed the value of the effect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep interaction state and meaningful targets in the DOM
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Let a DOM controller own selection, focus and accessible output while the canvas reflects that state visually. Use real buttons or links with generous targets, such as 48 px, and keep decorative canvas layers pointer-transparent. Hover and keyboard focus should preview the same information that activation pins; reserve readout space and let Escape restore the default state. Keep visual drift inside each fixed target's slack rather than moving targets every frame. For decorative fields, consider CPU spatial indexing before GPU picking. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A single semantic state model keeps the interface usable without graphics and avoids competing interaction implementations. Avoid synchronous GPU readbacks in frequent pointer handling, and limit live announcements so visual exploration does not become repeated screen-reader interruption.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use second-order springs for weaving and periodic displacement for exact loops
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Weaving needs a second-order spring, while an exact motion loop needs periodic displacement from fixed rest positions. For pointer easing, use p += (target-p)*(1-exp(-dt/tau)) with tau around 200 ms; this first-order response does not overshoot a stationary target. For weaving, integrate v += (w*w*(target-x)-2*zeta*w*v)*h and x += v*h at fixed 1/120 s steps, with zeta 0.6-0.9 for overshoot or 1 for settling. A local force can use dir*A*exp(-d*d/(sigma*sigma)), with A a few pixels. For divergence-free 2D flow, derive velocity as (dpsi/dy,-dpsi/dx). Make the noise input periodic using two extra coordinates, R*cos(2*pi*t/T) and R*sin(2*pi*t/T), then displace from rest rather than accumulating advection. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Smooth following, weaving and seamless looping are different requirements. Choosing the correct motion model prevents a convincing description from becoming animation that never crosses or never returns to its starting frame.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Share one halo profile between the static poster and GPU sprites
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Generate static and animated halos from one shared profile so their appearance matches when the canvas appears. Store gradient stops, core radius and sigma as data, then produce both an SVG radialGradient and a baked sprite, such as a 32 px PNG or a Canvas2D-generated texture. Draw sprites on instanced quads when point-size limits or clipping would affect the result. Hover can change brightness and radius without adding a bloom pass. Avoid live per-node SVG blur for interactive figures. When translating a CSS blur measure into device pixels, account for DPR: device sigma = CSS stdDeviation * DPR. Compare sprites with a blur pass on the actual scene rather than assuming a universal particle-count crossover. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A shared profile prevents the poster-to-canvas transition from changing the artwork. Baked glow also gives direct control over shape and spread without committing the page to a full post-processing pipeline.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose blending and dithering for the actual background and output colour space
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Match blend modes, alpha conventions and colour handling to the background before tuning a GPU overlay. Additive blending with ONE,ONE suits luminous sparks on dark grounds; premultiplied over with ONE,ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA suits translucent threads. Over-blending still saturates and does not guarantee unclipped highlights. For bounded nonnegative glow RGB, alpha=max(r,g,b) can support a premultiplied overlay; verify the resulting composite. Use premultipliedAlpha consistently and avoid an additional CSS mix-blend-mode unless deliberately required. Static blue-noise dither around ±1/255 can reduce dark-gradient banding without temporal shimmer. Read colours from CSS tokens through getComputedStyle. On white backgrounds, use darker over-blended marks because additive light has little visible range. Compare the canvas and SVG through the same output colour pipeline. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These choices determine whether an overlay belongs to the artwork. Incorrect alpha or colour conversion can defeat careful palette matching, while animated dither can make an otherwise still panel appear restless.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build graph layouts once and share their coordinates with the live renderer
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Compute node-link layouts at build time and let SVG and WebGL consume the same emitted coordinates. If randomness is needed, use the same seeded algorithm, such as SplitMix32, in every implementation; matching seeds across different generators is insufficient. Runtime randomness can remain limited to decoration. For portable thick threads, use instanced signed-distance capsules rather than assuming gl.LINES supports the desired width. Capsules can provide round caps, Gaussian edges, draw-in progress and travelling highlights. For a spatial illustration, consider a relative neighbourhood graph; for a factual graph, preserve its actual relationships. Runtime proximity links can fade as 1-d*d/(r*r), with 100/120 px entry/exit thresholds to reduce flicker. Keep SVG draw-in to manageable path counts using pathLength="1". [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared geometry prevents the live layer from rearranging the poster. Explicit link selection and stable thresholds preserve readable paths instead of creating a constantly changing tangle.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep a versioned licence ledger for borrowed graphics code and assets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Record the licence and required notices for each exact version of graphics code or asset before incorporating it into a distributable project. Track the source location, version, licence file, modifications and attribution obligations separately for libraries, shaders, textures and examples. Inspect repository files rather than assuming an example has the same licence as its host framework. Resolve conflicts between package metadata and repository licensing before copying. Missing licensing is not permission to redistribute. Copyleft material requires a compatibility review rather than a blanket assumption that it is either unrestricted or unusable. Preserve required copyright, licence and NOTICE files when adapting permitted material. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A rendering layer often combines many small borrowed pieces. A ledger makes their provenance reviewable and prevents an attractive snippet or texture from introducing distribution obligations nobody noticed.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose the renderer only after defining the visual requirement and resource budget
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Select the least complex renderer that satisfies the required visual behaviour within an explicit page budget. Compare HTML and SVG, Canvas2D, raw WebGL2 with a helper, lightweight libraries and full scene engines before adopting a GPU stack. Define limits for frame time, DPR, overdraw, particle count, compressed JavaScript, shader compilation and render-target memory. Include startup and fallback behaviour in the comparison, not just the steady-state scene. A figure needing labels and a few highlighted paths may remain primarily SVG even if one decorative layer uses WebGL. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Engine choice influences every later implementation decision. Establishing requirements and budgets first reduces the risk of building an elaborate rendering system that the page cannot load, operate or maintain comfortably.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Let semantic controls own interaction state while the canvas follows
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep selection, focus and activation state in semantic DOM controls, then let the canvas render that state. Define how temporary hover previews differ from pinned selections, and provide equivalent keyboard and touch behaviour. Choose hit testing appropriate to the figure rather than defaulting to synchronous GPU readback. Use elapsed-time pointer easing for gentle following and second-order springs when overshoot is part of the intended motion. Keep ambient displacement bounded so a moving target does not escape interaction or obscure its label. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This division preserves a usable interface when graphics are disabled or paused. It also prevents visual effects from becoming a second, conflicting state machine that disagrees with focus, selection or accessible descriptions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make lighting data shared between CSS, SVG and the live canvas
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define colour and halo parameters once and derive each rendering layer from that shared data. Read CSS design tokens for palette values, generate SVG gradients and GPU sprites from the same halo profile, and document the alpha and colour-space conventions at their boundary. Use static dither where dark gradients visibly band. Select blending for the background: luminous addition can suit dark artwork, while marks on white generally need darker over-blended colour. Compare the actual first canvas frame with the poster at matched size and DPR. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Separate hand-tuned implementations tend to drift. Shared lighting data makes the transition predictable and turns a visual mismatch into a specific rendering problem instead of another round of subjective palette adjustments.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Design node-link figures for legibility before adding atmospheric motion
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build node-link figures around readable grouping, explicit relationships and accessible navigation before adding animation. Emit stable coordinates at build time, use deliberate line geometry and check effective contrast after dimming. Distinguish decorative proximity links from relationships asserted by the data. Evaluate the figure at its actual display size, including label collisions, crowded crossings, visual hierarchy and target spacing. Provide keyboard navigation and a textual relationship view. Recompose mobile layouts when desktop geometry becomes too dense. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Stars and glowing threads can make unrelated items appear connected or make real relationships impossible to trace. Legibility checks keep atmosphere subordinate to the figure's purpose and help the static and animated versions communicate the same information.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Package visual handoffs with behaviour, assets, constants and acceptance checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A graphics handoff should include a brief, assets with stated roles, a visual reference, lifecycle requirements, porting notes and acceptance checks. Identify which constants determine the appearance and compare them explicitly after a port. Preserve the mathematics while removing development-only machinery. Specify sizing independently of a single aspect ratio, suspend work when off-screen, and reset elapsed-time tracking when resuming. Keep experimental behaviour behind a real shared switch whose disabled path is also tested. Include reduced-motion and static references alongside the animated target. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A screenshot describes appearance but omits the behaviour that keeps it stable. A structured handoff gives another builder enough information to reproduce the visual without silently dropping fallback, timing or interaction constraints.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Let animated connections follow real relationships
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Restrict animated connections in an explanatory graph to relationships the underlying data actually supports. On a seed library site, an animated link might connect a seed variety to a compatible planting season rather than choosing arbitrary endpoints for visual variety. Randomize endpoint selection or direction only within allowed relationships. When animated lines replace static ones, hide only their duplicates; keep structural grouping visible. Preserve the complete relationship view in the static fallback and provide a textual equivalent. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Visitors naturally interpret a visible connection as a claim. Constraining decoration to truthful relationships makes the motion quietly informative and prevents a visually attractive effect from teaching a false model.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure animation range and per-frame movement over a window long enough to capture slow motion
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate slow animation with both movement range and frame-to-frame steps over a sufficiently long window, such as 12 s. A 4 s pixel-difference check can report less movement after amplitude increases by 1.4x if the animation also slows down. Compare equivalent phases or complete cycles when possible. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A short difference window can reward speed while missing larger excursions. Separating range from step size helps distinguish deliberate, expansive motion from jitter and prevents a misleading score from driving the art direction.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use masked texture displacement to make painted artwork interactive without introducing new pigment
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A velocity field can animate painted artwork by displacing texture UVs without adding color. For a tide-pool field guide, restrict displacement to water and exclude labels and illustrated specimens. Start the effect on mouse or pen input, provide a still experience for reduced motion and touch, and let it settle before sleeping. A recorded prototype used three initialization macrotasks of 3–8 ms and stopped after 7 s without pointer activity. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Displacement can preserve the artwork's palette while making it responsive. A sweep changed 18.9% of a sampled patch versus 2.1% in a control, with luminance-histogram L1 distance 0.075; these are diagnostic observations, not proof of identical color or acceptable GPU cost. Real-GPU frame cost remained unmeasured.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Encode packed RGB masks losslessly to preserve independent channels
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use lossless encoding for textures that pack independent masks into RGB channels. Lossy WebP with 4:2:0 chroma subsampling can contaminate decoded channel values, allowing an effect to cross boundaries that should remain protected. A displacement mask can therefore affect nearby decorative elements even when the source mask is correct. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Image compression optimized for visual similarity does not preserve the numerical independence of data channels. Inspect the decoded mask used by the renderer, and treat packed masks as data assets rather than ordinary photographic images.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use mipmaps when painted textures render smaller than their source resolution
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Generate mipmaps and use LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR when painted textures are substantially minified. In one recorded phone comparison, this reduced the frame-zero p99 pixel-difference metric against the still image from 19 to 14. Keep the comparison viewport and reference rendering consistent when evaluating the change. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A first-frame mismatch can come from texture sampling rather than animation logic. Fine watercolor detail is especially vulnerable to minification aliasing, so inspect filtering before rewriting scene behavior or compensating with changes to the artwork.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Design lighting for pale artwork with selective masks and probes that exclude moving objects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Lighting over pale artwork needs selective masks and a falloff designed for a bright background. Modify the pixels that should hold light rather than the entire rectangular sprite. A dark-scene halo with intensity 0.07 at 60% radius may become nearly invisible on white. Measure illumination with a ring just outside the object, scaled to its size. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Bright backgrounds leave little room for additive light, while whole-sprite adjustments can reveal pale rectangles. In one test, a disc probe confused 2.6 px of object bobbing with illumination and selected the wrong object at four of five stops. Probe placement must separate lighting from movement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Benchmark unrolling small uniform-array loops in full-screen fragment shaders
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Small uniform-array loops in full-screen fragment shaders are candidates for measured unrolling on software renderers. In one five-iteration workload, replacing loops with straight-line helpers and individual vec4 uniforms changed throughput from 15 to 23 fps. Check output equivalence and measure the target renderer before adopting the rewrite. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A short source loop executes across many fragments, and compiler handling can dominate its cost. Fewer than roughly six elements is a useful investigation threshold from this example, not a universal rule; code size and hardware compiler behavior can change the tradeoff.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Replace fragile texture distortion when simulation artifacts undermine painted artwork
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Low-resolution fluid displacement can visibly damage painted artwork through texture folding, mask seams, input discontinuities, and abrupt resets. A recorded prototype used 72/48-texel simulation resolutions, event-discrete splats, a 0.05 UV offset clamp, lazy initialization, and a hard clear after 7 s. A replacement used translucent light, stateless particles, a critically damped pointer spring, and an approximately 400 ms influence fade. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Displacement exposes numerical artifacts directly in recognizable brushwork. An overlay avoids geometric tearing, though it still needs color and compositing checks. Choose the technique by visual continuity, not by simulation sophistication.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Composite watercolor elements with multiply when white should leave the background unchanged
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Watercolor elements prepared on white can blend into painted backgrounds using multiply, where white leaves the underlying image unchanged. Normalize the photographed or generated paper tone before compositing so uneven paper does not become a visible rectangle. Test the result over the actual destination artwork rather than only a white preview. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Translucent pigment often integrates more naturally through darkening than through a hard alpha key. Multiply preserves soft washes, but it also darkens underlying detail, so it suits pigment-like elements rather than every object or lighting effect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build reveal animations from the idle state to avoid a handoff pop
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define a reveal animation as the idle deformation plus a reveal mask so its final state naturally matches ongoing motion. Reassemble layered artwork in its original painting order and compare it with the flat reference. One recorded reconstruction differed by a mean of 1.3 pixel levels and used a crossfade over the final tenth of the reveal. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Independently authored reveal and idle animations require matching position, shape, and phase at the handoff. Sharing the underlying state removes much of that coordination and leaves the crossfade to absorb small compositing differences.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Simplify motion into one continuous action and compare replacements against proven behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Prefer one continuous motion when intermediate stages add visible hesitation without adding meaning. For an astronomy club illustration, particles could converge directly on a target over 1.5 s, using substantial trails and smooth fades instead of forming a temporary ring first. Remove redundant shaking when a stronger animation already communicates activity, and verify that traveling highlights follow their actual paths. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] More animation can weaken coherence through competing movement and abrupt handoffs. Keep the previous implementation available for comparison: a replacement may improve one effect while degrading path fidelity or timing elsewhere.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Remove an unnecessary motion phase when easing cannot repair a visibly awkward transition
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A single converging trajectory can eliminate jerk introduced by switching between swirl and inward-motion phases. One implementation used radius r0(1-p), with p = 1-(1-s)^2, appearances within 0.3 s, and the final arrival at 1.5 s. A 0.5 s advected ribbon supplied visual texture independently. Recorded checks found zero outward frames and speed jumps of 0.13%, compared with 18.4% previously. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These are example measurements, not universal targets. The useful diagnosis is structural: an unwanted phase may need removal rather than more smoothing.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep effects that outlive a cycle on an independent clock
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Shortening an animation loop can truncate effects whose lifetime extends beyond the loop boundary. One timing design combined a 0.55 s hold, a 3.0 s run, and a 0.5 s restart gap; a 1.4 s response glow began at 86% of the run. Tracking that glow on an absolute clock preserved its fade across restarts. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Before resetting cycle time, identify every effect still alive. Update screenshot windows to the new schedule and verify the actual end-to-restart gap at desktop and mobile widths.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build the fallback still from shipped textures to avoid a visible animation handover
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reconstructing the static fallback from the same textures used by the live renderer reduces first-frame mismatch. For composite pixel P, background F, and alpha a, the premultiplied foreground contribution is P-(1-a)F; straight-alpha storage requires corresponding conversion where alpha is nonzero. Keep colour space and compositing conventions consistent. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Ordinary cutouts over an inpainted background can change the picture at activation. One reconstruction measured a mean difference of 0.94 colour levels, illustrating why the shipped composite should be tested rather than assumed identical.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Expand displacement protection masks by the full sampling reach
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A displacement effect must be suppressed around protected details, not only directly on them. Expand the protection mask by the maximum displacement reach and account for filtering. In one failure, nearby pixels sampled painted stars from 9 px away, producing visible smears by 5 s despite masking the star cores. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Sampling moves information across mask boundaries. Protecting only destination pixels misses the source pixels that neighboring fragments can pull into motion, so test thin lines and highlights throughout the animation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Remove pale background contamination when extracting dark elements from light artwork
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Dark painted elements on a light background may need opacity derived from their darkness relative to the local paper. A simple circular cutout can carry an opaque pale patch that becomes obvious when the element moves over coloured washes. Inspect extracted sprites against several representative backgrounds. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A cutout that looks clean in its original position may contain background colour rather than useful foreground detail. Darkness-based keying can help with suitable artwork, but preserve intentional light highlights and verify the resulting edges.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Resolve crop offsets before converting image labels into geometry
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Convert image coordinates into rendering coordinates only after accounting for each element's crop offset. Record the original image dimensions, crop origin, scale and destination bounds, then draw a debug overlay to compare the resulting polygon with the artwork. A missed crop offset can displace an edge by 100 px. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Coordinates that look precise can still describe the wrong reference frame. An overlay exposes the mismatch immediately and prevents repeated adjustments to otherwise correct geometry.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use seeded variation and reduce pointer-oriented effects on touch devices
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep animated variation inside defined visual constraints and expose a deterministic seed for testing. For a gathering effect, select 2–5 source regions within an artwork mask, vary them between cycles and start the next gathering 1.5 s after arrival, with a timing tolerance of one frame. Compare haze density or luminance at a 390 px phone width. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Bounded randomness keeps a loop varied without breaking its meaning. Effects designed to respond to a pointer can become persistent visual noise on touch devices, so their mobile intensity should be intentionally reduced and verified.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prevent colour clipping when extracting feathered layers from painted backgrounds
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Un-matting a feathered layer requires enough alpha to keep reconstructed colour channels within their valid range. For normalized composite colour P, background F and alpha a, the recovered premultiplied colour P−(1−a)F must lie between 0 and a. For 0<F<1, raise alpha to at least max(1−P/F,(P−F)/(1−F)) across channels; handle endpoint backgrounds separately. Combine overlapping soft masks with screen union, a+b−ab. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Insufficient alpha causes clipping and coloured bands, while max-based mask union can expose seams. Inspect the composited artwork as well as difference maps.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure light prominence at reading scale rather than by peak pixels
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Compare decorative and interactive lights after blurring at the intended reading scale, rather than ranking their single brightest pixels. A 3 CSS px blur can capture spatial prominence that a 1.5 px blur misses; calibrate the scale against the actual composition and display mapping. Require the test to reject an undamped background known to overpower the controls. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A broad painted glow can dominate a tiny interactive point despite having a lower peak value. A test that ignores apparent size can approve precisely the hierarchy failure it should detect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Put path wavering in the angle to guarantee inward convergence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] To guarantee that a path only approaches its centre, use radius r(s)=r0×(1−smoothstep(s)) for s from 0 to 1 and place wavering or braiding in the angle. With nonnegative r0 and monotonic progress, radial distance cannot increase. Verify that later coordinate transforms preserve the intended metric. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Adding a perpendicular Cartesian offset can push part of an otherwise inward path outward. Separating radius from angle makes the convergence property structural, reducing reliance on trial-and-error tuning or sparse frame sampling.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use overlapping radial lights to soften hard-edged animated paths
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a strip renderer produces a hard tube instead of a soft veil, try overlapping radial lights along the path. A chain of 64 samples is a concrete starting point; tune spacing, falloff and intensity for the displayed size, then check blending and rendering cost. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Path geometry alone does not determine the material impression. A box-shaped cross-section remains rigid even on a graceful curve, while overlapping soft profiles can suggest dispersed dye or light. Excess overlap can also create hot spots, so inspect the full animation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Evaluate additive accent colours against their composited background
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Additive gold light can lose its gold appearance over pale luminous backgrounds, so inspect the composited result rather than the source colour. Place a two-colour marker over darker artwork, reduce the underlying glow or reconsider the blending method when hue distinction matters. Measure the visible colour region at the intended display scale. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Adding light to already bright channels pushes the result toward white. A correctly specified gold rim can therefore disappear perceptually, undermining a colour-coded interaction even though the shader uses the expected values.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat unverified stream-lighting values as hypotheses rather than reusable presets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test whether a luminous stream's broad body carries its light before adopting numerical settings from a rendering experiment. A bright narrow center can make additive radial lights resemble a neon tube. Exploratory values of about 0.12 for the body, 0.015 for the center and 0.15 for the front taper were not independently verified and are not established presets. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Plausible parameter stories can be recorded before the resulting image is properly reviewed. Preserve the visual diagnosis, but keep speculative values labelled so later work does not mistake a generator's explanation for demonstrated craft.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure composited color instead of trusting an unverified alpha multiplier
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Judge additive color from the composited image rather than assuming an alpha multiplier will preserve the source hue. An exploratory claim that gold required about 2.5 times a violet stream's alpha was contradicted by artifact review; proposed annulus alpha near 0.6 was likewise not established as a reusable setting. A criterion such as R > B + 12 needs a declared channel scale and sampling region. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Background color, clipping and overlapping bloom all affect perceived hue. Retaining rejected values as warnings is useful; presenting them as recipes would propagate a failed assumption.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Account for downward-increasing coordinates when choosing a shader animation's phase sign
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] In a coordinate system where y increases downward and k is positive, sin(y*k - t) moves bands downward while sin(y*k + t) moves them upward as t increases. Confirm the texture coordinate convention before implementing rising light or scrolling wave effects. Check a simple visible band before layering in noise and glow. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A copied formula can be algebraically valid yet move in the opposite visual direction. Reasoning from a constant-phase point exposes the sign error before complex styling makes it harder to diagnose.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Normalize additive light chains for spacing as their path length changes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Normalize additive light chains for actual sample spacing instead of keeping both light count and alpha fixed as path length changes. A chain of 64 lights at alpha 0.12 can accumulate excessive brightness where samples crowd together. Evaluate the entire path and account for true arc length when placing samples. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Additive overlap changes with spacing: compressed segments can become blobs, while stretched sections can look tubular or reveal individual beads. Treating spacing and intensity together makes the visual result less dependent on path length and viewport geometry.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use spacing-aware alpha to control brightness accumulation in additive light chains
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat sample spacing relative to light radius as a primary control for additive-chain brightness. An approximate overlap model gives axis alpha proportional to alpha × 2R/spacing. Keep spacing a stable fraction of radius by adapting sample count, or scale each light's alpha by min(1, spacing/(k × R)). A proposed gate is maximum-to-median added luminance no greater than about 1.5 across supported viewports. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fixed count and alpha can produce saturated short segments, tubular long segments or visible beads. This model is provisional: if normalized short segments still exceed the proposed ratio, revisit the sampling, overlap assumptions and brightness measurement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Space lights by true arc length rather than an eased path parameter
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Space additive lights by true arc length when an eased path parameter crowds samples near the ends. After positioning the samples, normalize alpha for their spacing. A provisional implementation report measured peak-to-median luminance falling from 1.85 to 1.32 with arc-length spacing, while a radial-distance-only adjustment remained at 1.72. These values describe that experiment, not universal expectations. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Equal steps in a parameter do not imply equal distances on the rendered curve. Correct placement addresses bright endpoint blobs at their source instead of compensating for them with arbitrary dimming.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Tune brightness inside both visibility and glare limits with margin for variation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Tune a light's intensity against both a visibility floor and a glare ceiling, leaving margin from each boundary. In a provisional experiment, an 8× multiplier reached 0.606% against a 0.6% bright-area cap. A 6.5× multiplier reportedly kept the visibility score at least 0.21 while bright-area coverage stayed at or below 0.45%. The score definition and image conditions must accompany these numbers. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Increasing brightness can solve one gate while breaking another. A setting comfortably inside the feasible range is more reliable than one that passes only on a favorable frame.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Combine arc-length spacing and alpha normalization to reduce additive-chain hotspots
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Combine equal spacing by true arc length with spacing-normalized alpha when drawing additive light chains. In one reviewed comparison, this combination reduced the chain's peak-to-median luminance from 2.71 to 1.32. Retain a deliberately defective fixed-spacing or fixed-alpha variant to demonstrate that the brightness gate detects the old failure. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Correct sample placement and controlled overlap solve different parts of the problem. Applying only one can leave crowding or excessive accumulation, while testing their combined effect ties the visual improvement to a reproducible measurement.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use true arc-length spacing and radius-relative alpha scaling for additive soft-light chains
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Space additive soft lights evenly by true arc length and scale each light's alpha by min(1, spacing/(0.35*radius)). In the reviewed setup, a maximum-to-median luminance gate of 1.5 separated accepted chains from deliberately defective variants: defective ratios were 2.71 and 2.27, while corrected ratios were 1.32 and 1.22. Revalidate the threshold for different light profiles and backgrounds. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Eased curve parameters crowd samples where motion flattens, and fixed alpha amplifies the overlap. Combining geometric spacing with intensity normalization addresses both the placement error and the resulting brightness accumulation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test a continuous interior falloff when ring halos appear hollow
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A provisional fix for a bullseye-like halo is to carry light inside the ring's own radial profile, rising continuously toward its peak. Compare this profile against a hollow ring with a separate low-alpha fill, keeping the remaining scene unchanged. The hollow-ring approach had remained visually unsatisfactory across repeated reviews; the integrated interior profile was still untested. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Layering a faint disk beneath a sharp annulus may preserve the very contrast boundary that causes the target-like appearance. Treat the continuous profile as a testable proposal, not a validated universal fix.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build continuous ring halos with interior light and an underlying glow
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A ring halo may need both a continuous interior falloff and a glow beneath the ring to avoid a bullseye appearance. In one calibrated test, an interior floor alone produced trough-to-rim ratios of roughly 0.66–0.71; adding an underlying halo reached 0.73–0.76 at viewport widths of 1440, 1024 and 390. The test sampled 8 rays with a 0.7 minimum ratio. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A bright rim separated from its core reads as an outline. Keep a revised rule provisional until it survives evaluation beyond the round that changed its test.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Budget additive glow against background brightness throughout its formation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Additive glow needs a brightness budget that accounts for the background and every layer during formation. A glow that looks soft over dark sky can clip into a roughly 50 px white disc over pale mist. Scaling layers by formation progress or background darkness is a candidate remedy that requires visual validation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Core, halo, fill and rim accumulate light together. Adjusting only the most obvious layer may leave another layer responsible for the hard disc.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Include the rim when reducing additive glow clipping
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reducing additive clipping requires budgeting every contributing layer, including the rim. In a 1440 px viewport comparison, a clipping measure fell from 1781 pixels to 1618 when only halo and fill were scaled, then to 776 when the rim was scaled too, below the example cap of 962.6. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A thin, bright rim can still dominate accumulated light over a pale background. Inspect layers individually and together throughout formation instead of assuming the broad halo is the sole cause.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Animate painted highlights with masked opacity layers while preserving the initial still
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Subtle painted motion can be built from 3 copies of a highlight layer under 3 static masks, cycling their opacity in sequence. Start every highlight copy at zero opacity so the initial frame matches the underlying still. This can create shimmer or falling-light effects without adding WebGL logic. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Restricting movement to light preserves the painting's composition. Opacity animation can use compositing, but confirm actual browser behaviour and layer costs; also provide a reduced-motion state that retains the complete static image.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Combine painted cutouts and CSS highlight motion without expanding the WebGL renderer
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Illustrated navigation cards can combine background-keyed alpha masks with CSS highlight animation while leaving an existing WebGL renderer unchanged. For a neighbourhood bakery, extract loaf illustrations from related artwork, blend their edges into the page painting, and animate only selected highlights. Verify the cards at widths such as 1440, 1024 and 390. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reusing visual language can make navigation feel integrated. Keeping this motion in CSS avoids new renderer logic, but image bytes, compositing costs and interaction clarity still require checking.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure visible text descendants when a wrapper uses display:contents
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A display:contents wrapper has no layout box, so text-protection effects must measure its visible descendants. Collect the actual text-bearing elements and use their individual rectangles when masking or dimming artwork behind copy. Avoid replacing separated text regions with one large enclosing rectangle. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A zero-sized wrapper can disable protection, while an oversized combined rectangle unnecessarily fades artwork in open gaps. Measuring the rendered text preserves both legibility and the composition.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Recheck animated color visibility after moving artwork beneath text
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Repositioning artwork beneath a text column can hide an essential part of its animated color sequence. After a layout change, inspect every required color across complete cycles and relevant viewport sizes, including regions affected by text-protection masks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A composition can satisfy static placement requirements while losing a color during motion. Testing the interaction between layout and animation catches omissions that a single screenshot or an isolated renderer test will miss.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reroute animated color paths when text masks obscure them
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a text mask hides a required animated color, reroute that color through an uncovered region before moving the focal object. In one wide-layout test, a color appeared in only 2 of 3 cycles; the failing cycle measured a visibility ratio of 0.01–0.08 against a 0.15 requirement. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Placement and color visibility can both remain valid constraints. Adjusting emission origins or paths can satisfy both without weakening the threshold or undoing the layout.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate scene-specific interaction behavior from shared sprite handling
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A scene-specific effect can bypass shared sprite behavior by using a distinct semantic target and a scene-owned implementation. Ensure the target does not accidentally match the renderer's generic sprite identifiers, then load its effect from the scene's own chunk. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] This can preserve shared renderer behavior and unrelated route payloads while allowing a different interaction treatment. Verify that identifier separation is deliberate and documented, since an unexplained naming workaround would be fragile.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Fix missing animation content in the planner before changing visibility thresholds
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Repeatedly missing animation content calls for a planner fix rather than a weaker visibility threshold. In one visual check at 1024 px width, the second cycle produced only 10 px of gold with a reported gold-to-violet ratio of 0.00 across 3 runs. A concrete planning constraint was to make the gold path at least 0.6 times the violet path in every cycle. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Repetition helps distinguish an actual absence from a measurement problem. Adjusting the threshold would conceal the missing visual role instead of restoring the intended composition.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test radial smoothing for visible bands in swirling effects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Bands that follow a swirling eddy can be addressed by smoothing across its radial direction. Treat this as a targeted correction: inspect whether the unwanted variation crosses the radius, then compare the result against the original at the intended display scale. The available observation does not establish a universal blur radius or kernel. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Directional artifacts call for directional investigation. An indiscriminate blur can erase useful structure along with the bands, while a correction aligned with the defect offers more control over the visual tradeoff.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reduce visible noise-grid structure with smoother interpolation and broader haze falloff
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Visible rounded-square chunks in procedural haze can come from the noise lattice rather than the painted art. A useful correction combines quintic interpolation, lower-frequency octaves, wider smoothstep edge bands and lower opacity per overlapping sheet. Recheck the animation across the full viewport rather than judging one still frame. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Artistic adjustments alone may leave a mathematical artifact intact. Quintic interpolation improves derivative continuity but does not guarantee invisible structure; frequency, opacity and overlap still matter. Verify both visual quality and the remaining graphics bundle budget after the shader change.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build the static hero first and reveal WebGL only after a successful frame
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A decorative WebGL hero should progressively enhance a complete static design. For an amateur astronomy club, a bounded 70–85vh sky illustration can introduce the site while the reading sections remain calm and legible. Place the fallback beneath a transparent canvas and keep semantic content above both. Reveal the canvas only after a successful rendered frame. Defer initialization until appropriate visibility or interaction, respect reduced motion, provide a pause control where needed, pause hidden-tab work, and handle context loss by restoring the fallback. Observe container size and cap mobile rendering budgets. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The illustration must survive script failure and unavailable graphics hardware. A restrained animated opening preserves atmosphere without making the entire reading experience depend on continuous motion or GPU availability.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify research claims separately from whether their links resolve
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A live research link does not establish that its source supports the associated WebGL claim. Audit link availability, claim support, attribution, and unresolved evidence separately. For reduced motion, check whether documentation actually covers the canvas animation rather than only surrounding DOM effects.
