Treat inaccessible sources and ambiguous implementations as unsettled, and define an explicit reduced-motion fallback for your own site. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Research summaries can combine real URLs with incorrect interpretations. Independent verification prevents attractive examples from becoming false accessibility assurances or unjustified implementation requirements.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat persistent header animation as a recurring load and usability cost
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Animated headers need stricter restraint because their cost and distraction recur across the site. Keep navigation reachable during scrolling and assess atmospheric effects in the rendered page. For a subtle sky treatment, alpha around 0.3 can be a starting point, but test contrast and legibility against the actual background. Provide static and reduced-motion behavior and avoid loading expensive effects before they are useful. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Small decorative choices become significant when every page repeats them. Reversible prototypes help judge atmosphere, while explicit loading and accessibility constraints keep decoration from competing with navigation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Persist an explicit motion choice with narrowly scoped session storage
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A motion preference can be stored in sessionStorage only after the visitor changes the control, using one documented key and no transmission. Handle unavailable storage gracefully so pausing still works in memory. Describe the behavior accurately and keep any automated storage exception limited to that component and purpose. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A narrow preference mechanism is easier to understand and audit than unrestricted storage. Its technical scope does not by itself establish legal consent requirements, and adding a consent banner later does not automatically resolve every privacy obligation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep composition-dependent overlays synchronized with the image actually displayed
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An overlay derived from one image composition should draw only while that composition is displayed. Subscribe to media-query changes in both directions, and verify currentSrc or a reliable source identity before rendering. Reevaluate after image loading because a media-query event can precede completion of the source change. Test wide-to-narrow and narrow-to-wide resizing, including repeated crossings, and ensure ordinary resizes within one composition do not cause unnecessary teardown flashes. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Landscape hotspots, masks or continuation lines become incorrect when a portrait source replaces the image beneath them. A boot-time width check passes initial testing but cannot protect a visitor who rotates a tablet or narrows a window.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Exercise every graphics tier and distinguish software fidelity tests from real-GPU evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a test browser selects a software fallback, explicitly exercise other graphics tiers before claiming their behavior is covered. Prefer a test-only tier override; where interception is necessary, document what it changes. Confirm the active tier through application state, backing-store dimensions and any later stand-down decision. Run fidelity probes in both paths and compare them with real-device results before assuming equivalent rasterization. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A fallback-only test suite can leave the visitor-facing code path untouched. Forcing a tier exercises its logic, but software-rendered timing remains software-rendered timing, and headless operation alone does not establish which graphics backend is active.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep image-derived overlays synchronized with the displayed responsive source
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] An overlay derived from one image composition must draw only while that composition is displayed. Subscribe to its media query in both directions: tear down when it stops matching and rebuild when it matches again. Before drawing, verify currentSrc or source dimensions against the image used to derive the geometry. Test resize crossings in both directions and confirm that a deliberately boot-only implementation fails. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Responsive image selection and overlay activation can drift when configured separately. A correct initial render does not prove that seams, masks or hotspots remain aligned after resizing.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify that live enhancement starts even when the fallback already looks complete
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Test live-layer activation separately from the appearance of a static fallback. Verify that every supported figure variant enters its intended rendering path, produces motion when enabled and stops when paused. Include a deliberately skipped activation case that the test must reject. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A polished still can hide a missing animation indefinitely from screenshot checks taken at rest. Progressive enhancement needs two proofs: the baseline remains useful without scripting, and the enhanced path actually runs when its prerequisites are satisfied.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Investigate rendering-path differences when a report conflicts with automated probes
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] When a visitor reports missing motion but a probe sees animation, compare the rendering paths and persisted state before dismissing the report. Check hardware versus software rendering, device-tier selection, reduced-motion settings, pause state, viewport and deployed version. Record which path each probe actually exercised. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Headless software rendering may follow different code from a physical browser. Conflicting observations narrow the investigation; they do not establish that either observer is mistaken. Clarifying whether motion is absent or merely too subtle can prevent an unnecessary renderer fix.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate software-rendering checks from hardware compatibility evidence
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Use software rendering for suitable browser graphics checks, verify which rendering mode the browser selected and validate hardware behavior separately. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Software rendering can establish functional behavior, but it does not establish hardware performance or driver compatibility. Test reports should state the rendering mode so conclusions remain within the evidence.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep a complete static design beneath WebGL and stop animation when motion is disabled
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat WebGL as an enhancement over a complete static design. Place the fallback at z-index 0, the canvas at z-index 1, and real content at z-index 2. Start the canvas transparent and reveal it only after a successful rendered frame. When reduced motion is requested, preserve the static design and stop animation scheduling. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Failed graphics initialization should leave a usable, visually complete page. visibility:hidden can preserve layout space, but it does not stop requestAnimationFrame; JavaScript must halt the loop. Choose hiding behavior according to whether the canvas participates in layout.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Load optional WebGL after the page is usable and preserve a static fallback
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat a decorative WebGL layer as progressive enhancement that may fail without affecting page content. Initialize after its container exists and has measurable dimensions, reuse an existing compatible loader, and handle script and renderer failures. Keep text above the canvas and match the canvas clear color to the static background to prevent a black flash. Prefer a bundled or self-hosted dependency under a self-only script policy. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] CMS script ordering and blocked third-party CDNs can otherwise break initialization. Pin a tested version rather than assuming an old release is universally compatible, and measure its compressed cost against the layer budget; a 30 KB budget may rule out a full rendering library.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Reset animation clocks when resuming a canvas that was fully paused off-screen
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Fully pause an off-screen animation loop and reset its clock before resuming. Use IntersectionObserver to stop scheduling requestAnimationFrame callbacks while the canvas is outside the viewport. On re-entry, set lastT = performance.now() before requesting another frame, and clamp elapsed time with a bound such as Math.min(40, t - lastT). [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Stopping the loop avoids unnecessary background work. Without the clock reset, the next frame can apply the entire paused interval and jump abruptly, even when the original animation logic was otherwise preserved.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make the no-runtime experience useful before adding browser computation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Design a useful fallback before loading an optional browser runtime. Put equivalent terminal instructions and any required downloadable files in the initial HTML, then enhance the page when the runtime becomes available. Test CDN blocking, JavaScript disabled, WebAssembly unavailable, and a throttled connection separately. Ensure failures reveal actionable instructions rather than an indefinite spinner. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A user under time pressure needs a dependable route to completion. Rendering fallback content before JavaScript runs also covers failures that JavaScript itself cannot detect or repair.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep decorative WebGL optional and test interaction performance beyond initial page load
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Decorative WebGL should enhance a usable static page and stop consuming resources when it is not visible. Layer static fallback below canvas and real HTML content above it; reveal the canvas only after successful initialization. Consider interaction-triggered startup, antialias:false and a DPR cap of 1.5 where visual testing supports them. Use sprite halos rather than many live blur filters. Test hover behavior at 4× CPU throttling, keyboard focus, reduced motion and context loss. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A Lighthouse target of 90 or higher does not establish smooth interaction. Avoid hover-driven live announcements, preserve keyboard parity and make animation optional so visual polish does not obstruct reading or navigation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify graphics capabilities, citations, and asset licenses independently
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build graphics fallbacks from runtime capability checks and observed frame behavior rather than GPU-name lists. Check required texture filtering, blending, shader extensions, and scheduling APIs individually; provide a fallback when each is absent. Keep a static visual available while the first usable frame loads, and handle WebGL context loss. Separately verify the exact licenses of libraries, textures, and copied examples. A reachable article is not permission to reuse its assets. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Research summaries can combine correct architecture advice with stale compatibility tables, misattributed quotes, and incorrect license labels. Fetching the underlying sources turns those uncertainties into concrete implementation decisions. Support percentages and bundle comparisons remain tied to their sampling dates and measurement methods.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check rendering, filtering, and blending capabilities separately
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat float render-target support, linear filtering, and blending as separate capabilities when choosing a WebGL pipeline. Verify that references describe the intended WebGL version and test the formats and operations the renderer actually needs. Do not infer all required behavior from a broadly supported color-buffer extension. Provide a fallback for unsupported combinations. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A reassuring support statistic can conceal a narrower operation with substantially different availability. Separating capability checks prevents an apparently safe architecture choice from failing on real devices, and avoids carrying a corrected research conclusion forward as an established fact.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep artwork, optional motion, and readable content in separate layers
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build decorative web scenes as a static image base, an optional motion layer, and accessible HTML or SVG content above both. An astronomy club could use a responsive AVIF/WebP picture as first paint, with either a silent 10-second loop or a later WebGL enhancement. Reduced-motion or Save-Data preferences should retain the still. Keep text and meaningful controls outside the canvas, and document whether a rendering mode is implemented or merely reserves a slot. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Layer separation lets motion evolve without rewriting page content. The static composition remains usable before enhancement loads and when animation is unavailable or unwanted.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify research claims and build accessibility independently of showcase reputation
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Treat research summaries as leads to verify, and do not infer accessibility from a site's visual reputation. One bounded audit classified 66 claims as 47 confirmed, 14 contradicted and 5 unsettled; only 2 of 6 showcase sites documented reduced motion for their WebGL layer. These are sample findings, not population estimates. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Working links do not establish factual accuracy, and missing documentation does not prove missing implementation. Build a complete static presentation and explicitly test reduced motion rather than borrowing confidence from an impressive example.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Build the complete static figure and shared checks before adding visual effects
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Make each figure complete in HTML or SVG before adding WebGL, animation or decorative lighting. Build shared components, deterministic layouts, legends, reserved readout space and accessible HTML data equivalents first. Establish Playwright, axe and Lighthouse checks before producing individual pages. Commission mobile artwork alongside desktop artwork and measure contrast under the actual text. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A shared foundation prevents several pages from accumulating separate interaction and accessibility hacks. Static completeness also preserves the experience when scripts fail, motion is reduced or the graphics layer cannot initialize.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep art geometry stable when disclosures open beneath calibrated overlays
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Visual size constraints must hold in every visible interaction state, including open disclosures. If an overlay uses a project-specific floor of 5 image-space pixels at half maximum for markers of magnitude at least 0.72, opening a panel must not silently invalidate it by resizing the cover image. A reliable structure holds the art at its closed height and places expanded content below on a matching band. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Changing container height changes cover scale and can break measurements that passed at rest. Prefer separating the expanding content from the art box over repeatedly retuning markers. Check the new join: a practical target is CIE76 deltaE at most 3, or a feathered fade of at least 48 px with luminance steps no greater than 5% per 8 px. Treat these as design constraints to verify, not universal perceptual laws.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Translate ambient-motion requests into geometry, accessibility and execution budgets
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Specify ambient graphics as measurable visual behavior with explicit loading, motion and accessibility limits. A candidate brief can require image-to-canvas seams within 2 CSS px and 6 degrees across 768–1920 px widths, with crossings mapped through the live cover transform. Keep star drift within 2.5 CSS px of fixed hit targets. Budget a transient link as roughly 1 s forming, 1–1.6 s attached and 1 s fading; allow only one forming at once. For text, test the darkest backdrop against max(4.5:1, 0.75 times its white-background contrast). Suggested project budgets are a 2 KB gzipped loader, 30 KB gzipped graphics payload, DPR capped at 1.5 and per-frame JavaScript within 2 ms at 4x CPU throttle. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] These are acceptance targets, not proven device performance. Load after page load and idle on visibility, stop hidden or off-screen loops, honor reduced motion, provide one pause control and restrict meaningful links to real relationships.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep static content intact while proving graphics startup and loop behavior
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Build decorative graphics as an optional layer over a complete static page, with explicit startup and pause behavior. Reserve layout space with aspect-ratio, keep content separate from the canvas, and combine requestAnimationFrame with visibility and intersection checks. Hiding a canvas with CSS does not stop its JavaScript loop. A roughly 200 ms fade can follow a verified first frame. Treat a fallback trigger such as five startup frames averaging over 33 ms as a project heuristic requiring validation. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Attractive output does not prove reliable lifecycle behavior. Source-check accessibility claims and renderer assumptions, and avoid presenting an uncited timing heuristic as a universal standard.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Choose graphics boot triggers by purpose while retaining load and motion safeguards
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Delay optional graphics until user intent or until a decorative section becomes visible after page load and an idle opportunity. Interactive scenes can wait for Play or Explore; ambient scenes need a visibility trigger if they are meant to appear without interaction. Cap DPR with Math.min(devicePixelRatio, 1.5), describing it correctly as a ceiling. Start intersection testing around 0.1 and tune it to the layout. Prefer static dither when temporal noise would introduce unwanted movement. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The purpose of delayed startup is to protect useful content and responsiveness. Changing the trigger can preserve that purpose if loading budgets, reduced-motion behavior, pause controls and first-frame checks remain explicit.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Query line-width support and preserve normal touch scrolling
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Query ALIASED_LINE_WIDTH_RANGE before relying on native wide lines, and preserve vertical page scrolling around graphics. A measured range of [1,1] means native lines offer only width 1 in that context; use capsule quads or other geometry for controllable thick threads. Nested translucent geometry can approximate glow where its overdraw is acceptable. Use touch-action: pan-y for horizontally interactive regions that must retain vertical scrolling, and avoid indiscriminate touch preventDefault calls. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Desktop visuals can conceal both rendering limitations and mobile interaction failures. A graphic that looks correct but traps page scrolling has broken the site's primary navigation behavior.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Prove the first live frame before revealing an optional canvas
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep the static design visible until the canvas has rendered a frame consistent with it. Place an aria-hidden, pointer-events:none canvas above the artwork and below meaningful DOM content, initially at opacity 0. Request only needed context features; context failure leaves the static design intact. Share layout seeds and halo definitions, and define displacement so d(0)=0. After rendering and allowing paint opportunities, fade the canvas in over roughly 200 ms. A one-pixel readback can be a limited sanity check, not proof of complete frame correctness. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Black flashes and geometry jumps expose the handoff. A matching first frame makes the enhancement unobtrusive, while an always-present DOM equivalent preserves content when graphics fail.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Gate decorative graphics startup on intent or visibility after load
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give optional graphics an explicit boot policy that protects page loading and respects user preferences. Interactive scenes can load on pointer entry or keyboard focus; on touch, keep the initial handler small and defer heavy work until after a paint. Ambient scenes can import when visible after load and an idle opportunity. Framework hydration directives alone do not prove that all these conditions hold. Candidate budgets are a 2 KB gzipped loader and 30 KB total graphics payload. Skip graphics fetching under reduced motion or Save-Data and provide a shared pause control. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A navigation audit may never exercise delayed startup. Measure that boot path directly so deferred work is not merely hidden from the audit.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Design context-loss recovery around a persistent static fallback
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Handle WebGL context loss by stopping rendering and restoring the static presentation immediately. In webglcontextlost, call preventDefault when restoration is intended, cancel the loop and expose a lost state. On webglcontextrestored, rebuild programs and resources from retained source data or reloadable assets, then repeat first-frame validation before fading in. Defer expensive recovery while the page is hidden. Exercise both paths with WEBGL_lose_context where available. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Context recovery is a lifecycle requirement, not an exceptional polish task. Planning resource reconstruction from the beginning avoids blank graphics regions and makes failure behavior testable without sacrificing meaningful page content.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Use a pausable clock and elapsed-time motion across refresh rates
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Drive animation from elapsed time on a pausable requestAnimationFrame clock rather than fixed per-frame increments. Stop when off-screen or hidden, reset the previous timestamp before resuming, and use easing weights such as 1-exp(-dt/tau). A per-frame retention factor k at 60 Hz becomes k^(60dt). Candidate safeguards include analytic dt capped at 0.1 s and spring integration at 1/120 s substeps with at most 1/30 s simulated per frame; document dropped-time behavior. Stop settled loops when motion falls below a threshold. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Frame-based constants change apparent speed across displays, while stale timestamps cause jumps after pauses. Re-measure container size after resize and page restoration, and preserve touch scrolling rather than coupling animation controls to blanket event cancellation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bake the heavy artwork and reserve live rendering for a purposeful interaction
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Keep complex static artwork baked and animate only the layer that benefits from live interaction. Use scroll position to update uniforms while a controlled animation loop handles rendering. Provide a static tier for unsupported or unsuitable rendering environments, and retain the poster until a valid first frame has painted. Recover from context loss and test restoration on mobile browsers. Keep text and controls in HTML rather than rendering essential interface content inside the canvas. Choose quality tiers from capability and observed behaviour rather than relying only on renderer names, which may be unavailable or obscured. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] An impressive visual reference is evidence of art direction, not proof of production robustness. Selective animation preserves the strongest visual idea while leaving room for accessibility, recovery and a complete fallback.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Review WebGL layers for fallback, timing, input and rendering failures
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review a WebGL layer as part of a usable page, including startup, fallback, motion timing and input behaviour. Check that performance evidence identifies hardware or software rendering; the canvas stays hidden until a valid frame; DPR and antialiasing have explicit budgets; and animation uses elapsed time rather than per-frame increments. Test reduced motion, a pause control for persistent automatic movement, ordinary touch scrolling, context loss and off-screen suspension. Keep meaning in HTML or accessible SVG, and verify contrast after opacity multiplication. Inspect particle shapes, blur costs, random-seed stability, colour conversion and exact-loop boundaries. Bundle dependencies deliberately and review the deployed content-security policy. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Many graphics failures occur outside the shader: a premature reveal, trapped scroll or hidden text can undermine an otherwise polished effect. A repeatable review list catches these integration failures before visual approval is mistaken for production readiness.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Audit an existing hero by preserving useful safeguards and replacing fragile lifecycle code
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Review an existing animated hero feature by feature before reusing it on another page. Useful safeguards can include antialias:false, a DPR cap of 1.5, baked particle sprites, transparent clearing, reduced particle counts, hidden-tab suspension and a static layer that survives renderer creation failure. Check lifecycle gaps independently: eager startup, revealing the canvas before a valid frame, missing off-screen suspension, frame-dependent rotation, unseeded layouts and absent context-loss recovery. Replace a rotation increment such as 0.00045 per frame with an elapsed-time model calibrated to the intended speed. Provide an accessible pause control for persistent automatic motion and inspect faint threads for information loss. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Reuse should preserve demonstrated strengths without inheriting every historical shortcut. A visually successful effect can still have fragile startup and accessibility behaviour that only becomes obvious when it is deployed more widely.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Treat graphics lifecycle and fallback behaviour as production acceptance criteria
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A production canvas needs explicit rules for startup, first-frame reveal, suspension, recovery and fallback. Keep the static page complete, start the live layer only when its trigger and scheduling conditions are met, and reveal it after a valid frame. Handle context loss, resize, hidden tabs, off-screen sections and restoration from the browser's back-forward cache. Support reduced motion, user-controlled pausing and ordinary touch scrolling. Serve assets through a deployment arrangement compatible with the site's security policy. Test these transitions directly, including unsupported rendering and initialization failure. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A working animation in a fresh desktop tab covers only one lifecycle path. Production hardening keeps the page usable when a mobile browser suspends resources, a visitor changes preferences or the GPU layer cannot start.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Translate expressive motion requests into geometry, readability and fallback checks
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Turn an expressive animation brief into measurable constraints for seams, motion, text clearance and fallback behaviour. For a bicycle-repair co-op's animated route illustration, define permitted connections and keep at least two candidate routes per permitted relationship across target widths. Example seam tolerances are 2 px and 6 degrees; enforce them throughout the animation rather than only at rest. A visibility check might require free points to move at least 3 CSS px during any 3 s window. Protect text at every phase and through a 50 px scroll sweep. Cap a tall canvas backing store to the viewport at min(DPR,1.5), and avoid fetching layers that mobile layouts never draw. Test the entire page with the effect disabled. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Concrete constraints preserve the desired movement while making collisions, unreadable phases and resource waste reviewable. A tested off switch keeps an experimental layer from becoming a dependency of the underlying page.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Budget scroll-triggered startup and make accordion state visible before first layout
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Apply startup budgets to scroll-triggered graphics and initialize deep-linked accordion state before it can shift the rendered page. A useful graphics acceptance target is no main-thread task over 50 ms under 4x CPU throttling, checked at 1440x900 and 390x844. Build heavy candidate pools after the first frame in slices capped at 30 ms, and cache by layout signature. Measure actual task duration because scheduling an idle callback does not guarantee short work. For accordions, place a small hash opener immediately after the markup when appropriate, then verify initial layout and later hash navigation. A four-point icon needs a non-equivalent rotation, such as 45 degrees, rather than 90 degrees. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Deferring work until a section appears can merely move a stall into the visitor's scroll. Likewise, a late accordion opener or visually identical icon can undermine an otherwise correct component.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test that reused live graphics actually initialize when optional inputs are absent
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Reusing a graphics component requires a test that its live layer initializes successfully with the new page's optional inputs. A gradient lookup can fail on an empty stop list when one figure omits a halo present in the original. Because a static SVG remains visible, screenshots and accessibility checks may still pass. Define behaviour for missing gradients, validate inputs and assert a documented live-state signal after a valid frame, such as data-gl="live". Also verify that genuine initialization failure preserves the fallback. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A resilient fallback can conceal a broken enhancement. Checking both successful initialization and graceful failure prevents a component from appearing reusable while silently losing its intended interaction on the first variation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Check live layers after their runtime shutdown window
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Verify that a decorative layer remains active after its runtime budget has had time to disable it. In one observed implementation, approximately 3,000 Gaussian dabs per frame triggered a shutdown rule: a median frame gap above 70 ms over 40 frames. The layer appeared at 2 s, disappeared after approximately 4 s, and was absent at 6 s. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Successful startup proves only that initialization worked. A later state probe distinguishes sustained rendering from a layer that quietly disables itself, and should also confirm that the static fallback remains usable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure and split scroll-triggered startup work independently of frame rendering
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A scroll-triggered canvas or WebGL layer needs an explicit startup task budget in addition to its steady-frame budget. Target no main-thread task above 50 ms under 4x CPU throttling. Split context creation, shader work, buffer upload and geometry preparation across tasks; yield using setTimeout or MessageChannel, and feature-detect scheduler.yield before using it. Defer work unnecessary for the first frame and reject geometry candidates with bounding boxes before fine sampling. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A below-the-fold layer may initialize outside Lighthouse's navigation measurement window, while a frame trace begins after the expensive setup. Install a long-task observer before page code runs, scroll to the layer, and observe approximately 12 s. Compare equivalent runs against the previous build and report the longest task and blocking time. A good navigation score cannot establish that later scrolling stays responsive.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Include deferred rendering startup in performance acceptance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Performance acceptance for deferred decorative rendering must include the interaction or scroll position that starts it. Measure initialization separately from steady animation, split expensive setup across bounded tasks, and confirm that the static fallback remains usable throughout startup. Check input responsiveness during activation on representative devices. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A layer can pass initial navigation checks because it has not started, then block input when the visitor reaches it. Testing the actual activation path establishes whether startup is responsive as well as whether the final animation runs smoothly.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Every event-driven WebGL pass must establish the rendering state it needs
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A WebGL pass triggered by an input event must explicitly establish its required state, including its VAO and blending mode. In one failure, a simulation inherited another layer's VAO binding and blending configuration, leaving its velocity field at zero. Binding its own VAO and calling gl.disable(gl.BLEND) restored the pass. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Shared contexts retain state from whichever operation ran last. Event-driven work can execute between normal animation passes, so assumptions about the previous frame are fragile. Explicit pass setup makes correctness independent of execution order.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test compile-time shader variants when uniform-disabled paths remain expensive in software rendering
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Compile-time shader variants can reduce software-rendering cost when uniform-disabled branches remain expensive. One SwiftShader experiment measured 13 fps with uniform-false branches and 26 fps after removing them; scene-specific defines plus a separate glow program measured 19.5 fps. These results describe that workload and do not establish how every driver executes branches. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A renderer with a 70 ms stand-down threshold may disable an effect because of test-environment costs. Validate both the fallback behavior and the intended hardware path, and distinguish software-renderer observations from general GPU claims.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Apply fallback-to-live visibility rules across every responsive composition
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A static fallback can obscure a working WebGL layer when its visibility rule applies only above a breakpoint. In one failure, the still image remained above the canvas on phones because the hide-when-live rule started at 48rem. Check stacking order and fallback visibility at every layout variant, including failed initialization. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A breakpoint-specific repair can leave the same defect elsewhere. Treat fallback handover as a component-wide behavior, and hide the still only after the replacement layer is ready.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify that shared live layers support every figure variant before depending on them
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A polished static fallback can conceal a live renderer that silently skips an unsupported figure variant. Inspect initialization guards and exercise each component variant before a page depends on animation. Record an observable ready state and verify that supported figures actually advance after initialization. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Screenshots alone may approve a fallback that looks complete while the intended enhancement never runs. Keep unsupported variants explicit and test fallback quality separately from live-layer activation so either outcome is understandable.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Start live decorative additions at zero visibility
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A live layer added over a complete static illustration should begin with zero contribution from new decorative elements. Set their initial opacity or intensity to zero, then introduce them gradually after the handover. Compare the static image with the first live frame, including small bright features. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A particle at its initial position can still alter the artwork before motion begins. This produces a visible startup jump even when the element is described as decoration rather than content.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Match browser graphics validation to the claims being made
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Define which browser graphics checks establish functionality and which require representative hardware. Record the rendering mode used, and include hardware validation before making compatibility or appearance claims that depend on it. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A passing test in one rendering environment does not establish equivalent behavior in another. Explicit coverage boundaries make remaining uncertainty visible.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Measure halo continuity with radial samples and geometry-bounded centring
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A radial brightness test can distinguish a continuous halo from a disconnected bullseye when its sampling geometry is controlled. In one calibration, the minimum brightness between core and rim along 8 rays had to reach at least 0.7 times the rim peak; rejected examples measured 0.31–0.33 and accepted examples 0.73–0.76. Limit automatic recentring to 0.5 times the feature radius. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A search that reaches the rim can select the wrong centre and invalidate the comparison. These thresholds are calibration examples, not universal aesthetic laws.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Bound visual-test recentring by the feature radius rather than a fixed pixel distance
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A visual test that searches for a nearby bright centre should keep that search within the subject's own geometry. At a 390 px viewport, a 12 px search radius exceeded a 10.5 px rim radius and could lock onto the rim, reversing a colour comparison on the same frame. A 0.5R search cap prevented that failure in follow-up checks. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Fixed pixel distances become unsafe as features shrink. Because the artwork also changed between runs, the cap's independent effect was not fully isolated.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Verify that an excessive-brightness test actually produces excessive light
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] CSS brightness() can saturate near-white pixels, making it ineffective for constructing a strongly over-bright test case. In one visual test, brightness(3) produced only about 1.5 times the measured effect. Two additive clones using plus-lighter produced a substantially stronger result and triggered the ceiling check. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The requested multiplier is not the delivered perturbation. Measure the altered output before concluding that an acceptance gate can detect excessive brightness.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Test subtle animation with both a visibility floor and an intensity ceiling
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] A subtle-motion requirement needs an upper bound as well as a lower bound on its visible effect. In one frame-difference calibration, accepted animation measured mean 0.86–0.96 and p99 14–17; an excessive variant measured mean 3.4–3.8 and p99 74–87. Ceilings of mean 1.5 and p99 30 separated them. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A visibility-only check rewards stronger motion indefinitely. These example thresholds belong to their capture and measurement procedure, not every animation.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Freeze animation time to isolate the onset of an interaction
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Freeze ambient animation time and capture before and after an interaction to isolate its onset response. A custom paused state must still permit redraws when interaction state changes; an HTML data attribute alone does not implement that behavior. One comparison measured an abrupt response at 35–45 intensity levels and an eased response at 0 at onset. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Holding background motion constant removes unrelated differences and makes interaction jumps easier to detect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Fit image scale to distinguish a growing sprite from an added glow
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Estimate the scale that best aligns high-pass-filtered inactive and active frames to distinguish geometric growth from glow changes. Fit the zoom around the interaction target while holding capture conditions constant. In one test, the best-fit scale was 1.22 for a growing sprite and 1.00 after replacing the growth effect. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] A brighter object can feel larger without changing geometry. The fit supplies evidence about structural scaling, though alignment quality and filtering still need inspection.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Keep paused canvas layers covered unless they are updated for the current scroll position
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Making a foreground section transparent can expose a stale canvas frame when the background animation stops updating offscreen. During component migration, verify the animation's visibility lifecycle, drawing bounds and coordinate mapping before removing an opaque cover. An apparent visual gap may be deliberately hiding a frozen layer. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] The retained frame can look plausible while being offset from the current scroll position, making the defect easy to miss in a still screenshot. Either keep the cover, hide or clear the inactive canvas, or redraw it before exposure; test the boundary while scrolling in both directions.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Make decorative controls discoverable without overwhelming the illustration
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Give interactive objects visible focus, hover and touch affordances that fit the illustration. A seed-library diagram might use a soft halo around selectable seed packets while keeping labels readable and nearby groups spatially distinct. Consolidate repeated status language only when a prominent shared caption remains unambiguous. Retain accessible instructions if decorative on-screen hints are reduced. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Removing interface clutter can improve an artwork, but visitors still need to recognize actions and understand availability. Subtle presentation succeeds only when those meanings remain easy to discover.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.

memories.summary: Separate detectable motion from motion that feels fluid
memories.content: [OBJECTIVE] Evaluate animation with both motion measurements and perceptual review. When movement exists but feels weak, test a controlled amplitude increase such as 1.3–1.5x alongside smoother easing and an adjusted swell duration, while preserving the original rest frame. Observe the full cycle rather than a single short sample. [SUBJECTIVE/WHY] Saying that a scene is not animated may mean its motion is too subtle to read. Pixel differences establish that something changes; they do not establish that its rhythm, strength or fluidity communicates the intended effect.
memories.source_context: A web-development lesson in the webdev pre-seed pack.
